title: Defining specialised expertise in dental education
abstract: Dental education is a broad, multifaceted, and interdisciplinary scholarly field encompassing key domains, including curriculum design, teaching and learning, assessment, leadership, programme evaluation, and educational research. However, the definition of expertise in dental education remains ambiguous. In many settings, individuals are recognised as “ dental education experts ” or “ dental educationists ” primarily based on teaching experience and educational contributions, sometimes without formal academic preparation in education. While experience provides valuable practical insights, it may not fully equip dental educators with the theoretical and methodological foundations required for contemporary educational practice. This paper reflects on the evolving nature of dental education and argues that expertise should be understood more broadly than teaching experience alone. It highlights the key domains that require specialised knowledge in education. Drawing on developments in medical and health professions education, this paper emphasises the growing role of academic qualifications in education to support educational competence and leadership in dental education. While experience remains indispensable, this paper emphasises formal postgraduate academic preparation as an important foundation for specialised expertise in dental education, complemented by continued educational practice, scholarship, faculty development, and institutional support.
authors: Galvin Sim Siang Lin; Chan Choong Foong

title: Deformable CT-US Registration via Anatomy-Aware Implicit Neural Representations
abstract: Slice-to-volume registration between ultrasound (US) and preoperative computed tomography (CT) imaging would enhance many minimally invasive interventions, for example by locating soft tissue structures intra-operatively that are discernible in CT. While optical tracking enables initial rigid registration, contact from the probe induces soft tissue deformations that inhibit accurate alignment. In this work, we introduce a deformable CT-ultrasound registration framework that incorporates anatomical priors derived from CT to improve registration under deformation. Rigid registration is first established using a robot-assisted optical tracking system, after which a deformable transformation is estimated using a sinusoidal implicit neural representation (SIREN) optimized per frame. Tissue stiffness is approximated from CT-based HU values and used as spatially varying regularization, suppressing deformation in rigid structures such as bone while allowing more flexibility in soft tissue. Two additional constraints capture the physics of probe contact: a contact-zone displacement prior that drives the displacement field to compress tissue below the probe face, and a fan-geometry regularization term based on beam direction and convex transducer field of view. Model parameters are optimized with a normalized gradient field (NGF). The proposed approach improves alignment over rigid initialisation by 17% and outperforms classical deformable baselines while maintaining near-zero topological folding.
authors: Agnieszka Łach; Magdalena Wysocki; Feng Li; Mohammad Farid Azampour; Benjamin D. Killeen; Felix Ginzinger; Mathias Braun; Phil Steininger; H. Deutschmann; Nassir Navab

title: Delayed dual-tracer sentinel lymph node biopsy after nipple-sparing mastectomy with implant-based reconstruction
abstract: Objective: to present a clinical case of delayed dual-tracer sentinel lymph node biopsy using technetium-99m radiocolloid and indocyanine green fluorescence in a patient who previously underwent nipple-sparing mastectomy with immediate implant-based breast reconstruction, and to analyze the technical feasibility and early perioperative safety of the procedure. Material and Methods. This article presents a clinical case of delayed sentinel lymph node biopsy after previous nipple-sparing mastectomy with immediate implant-based breast reconstruction. The report is descriptive and was not intended to assess diagnostic accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, or the false-negative rate of the technique. A 40-year-old woman with a history of right nipple-sparing mastectomy and immediate implant-based reconstruction underwent delayed axillary sentinel lymph node biopsy for staging regional lymphatic basin. Preoperative lymphatic mapping was performed using periareolar subcutaneous injection of 50 MBq 99m Tc-Nanocoll, followed by lymphoscintigraphy and SPECT-CT. On the day of surgery, indocyanine green was injected intradermally at four periareolar points. intraoperative detection was performed using a near-infrared fluorescence imaging system, MARS, version 2.0.0.7, 2024, and a handheld gamma probe. The primary procedural endpoint was technical success, defined as intraoperative identification and excision of at least one sentinel lymph node. Results. Preoperative lymphoscintigraphy and SPECT-CT demonstrated radiotracer uptake in two right axillary lymph nodes. Intraoperatively, both sentinel lymph nodes were successfully identified and excised using combined gamma-probe detection and fluorescence guidance. Concordance between radioactive and fluorescent signals was observed in both removed nodes. Histological examination showed no metastatic involvement. No intraoperative or early postoperative complications were recorded. The implant, mastectomy flaps and nipple-areolar complex remained viable, with no evidence of ischemia, infection, implant exposure or reconstructive failure. Conclusion. In this clinical case, delayed dual-tracer sentinel lymph node biopsy was technically successful and was not associated with early perioperative complications. These findings indicate the principal technical feasibility of the procedure in this specific clinical situation, but they do not allow assessment of diagnostic accuracy, reproducibility, or oncological safety.

title: Delineating precise surgical resection areas: recent advances in NIR-II fluorescence imaging molecular probes
abstract: Precise delineation of surgical resection margins is a pivotal determinant of oncologic surgery outcomes, with R0 resection serving as the gold standard for maximizing local control and long-term survival. However, intraoperative identification of tumor boundaries remains challenging. Conventional tools such as frozen section pathology offer limited field coverage, are labor-intensive, time-consuming, and may yield sampling errors, particularly in anatomically complex or highly infiltrative lesions. Near-infrared II (NIR-II, 1000-1700 nm) fluorescence imaging has emerged as a transformative modality for real-time intraoperative navigation. Leveraging reduced photon scattering, minimal tissue autofluorescence, and deeper penetration compared with NIR-I and other optical approaches, NIR-II imaging enables high-contrast visualization of tumor margins while preserving adjacent normal structures. Over the past decade, the molecular probe landscape for NIR-II imaging has rapidly evolved-from early non-specific small molecules and inorganic nanomaterials to the latest generation of targeted agents designed to bind tumor-specific biomarkers. These advances have facilitated more accurate tumor-normal tissue contrast in a range of surgical contexts, including glioma, hepatobiliary malignancies, colorectal cancer, and head-neck tumors. Several first-in-human and ongoing clinical trials have demonstrated the feasibility, safety, and intraoperative utility of NIR-II molecular probes. Nevertheless, issues related to regulatory approval, probe pharmacokinetics, real-time quantitative imaging, and integration with multimodal surgical systems remain to be addressed. This review summarizes current concepts of precise surgical resection margins, outlines the origin and principles of NIR-II fluorescence imaging, and provides an in-depth discussion of targeted molecular probe development, preclinical and clinical progress, and their role in tumor margin delineation. Finally, we highlight existing limitations and future opportunities for translating NIR-II probes into routine surgical oncology practice.

title: DentalGEN: a large-scale controllable generative AI framework for automated dental crown restoration
abstract: Dental crown restoration addresses a global public health burden, yet is constrained by a slow, variable, and labor-intensive manual design process that limits access to high-quality treatment. Here we introduce DentalGEN, a large-scale controllable generative artificial intelligence framework for automated dental crown restoration. DentalGEN is the first framework capable of designing a patient-specific crown while simultaneously satisfying morphological, functional, and aesthetic criteria. Its core is a novel multi-view diffusion model that leverages explicit control mechanisms to incorporate clinical constraints directly within the generative process. This approach enables the integrated synthesis of view-consistent geometry and texture, achieving a level of precision and integration unattainable with prior automated methods. Evaluated on the largest reported multi-center dataset, DentalGEN’s designs achieved clinical scores statistically equivalent to those of human experts in blinded assessments, while outperforming state-of-the-art methods by 70% in Hausdorff Distance. Furthermore, a clinical proof-of-concept study demonstrated the feasibility of integrating DentalGEN into a supervised scan-design-manufacture paradigm, reducing active design time by over 90%. DentalGEN represents a crucial step in bridging the translational gap for generative AI in dental restoration, paving the way for more accessible, accurate, and efficient dental care.
authors: Jiamin Wu; Ying Liu; Yanning Chen; Yuqiang Zhang; Jiaying Gu; Yuan Liu; Mengxun Li; Wenping Wang; Yuanfei Fu; Zhiming Cui; James Kit Hon Tsoi; Dinggang G. Shen

title: Design and Comparative Evaluation of Two Low-Cost Analog RF Transmission Approaches for a Wireless Capsule Endoscopy Prototype
abstract: Abstract Capsule endoscopy provides a pain-free, non-surgical alternative to conventional gastrointestinal (GI) tract examination, yet its high commercial cost restricts adoption in resource-constrained healthcare environments. This paper presents the design and comparative evaluation of a low-cost wireless capsule endoscopy prototype built entirely from commercially available analog components. Two radiofrequency (RF) transmission solutions are implemented and compared: Solution 1 employs the MC1373 TV modulator integrated circuit (IC) configured as a 67.25 MHz carrier generator, while Solution 2 uses a discrete-component NPN transistor (2N2222) Colpitts-type oscillator circuit tuned to 61.2 MHz. Both solutions share a common miniaturized analog CMOS camera (8×8 mm, 600 TVL, CVBS output) and a custom-wound 0.1 µH air-core inductor forming the LC tank resonator. Breadboard prototyping, Proteus-based PCB design, and physical fabrication were performed for both solutions. Solution 1 produced a stable RF carrier confirmed on an oscilloscope but encountered video reception failure on available digital television receivers due to PAL/NTSC format incompatibility. Solution 2 successfully delivered clear real-time wireless video on an analog PAL television receiver, with a fabricated PCB footprint of 25×25 mm satisfying the esophageal lumen size constraint. The work provides a documented engineering baseline for low-cost capsule endoscopy development in developing-country contexts and identifies PAL/NTSC format incompatibility as a critical design constraint not previously reported in the prototype literature for this region.
authors: Ali Amir; Muhammad Ahmad

title: Development and internal validation of a deep learning system for criterion-specific assessment of preclinical dental soap carvings: a multi-rater study
abstract: Preclinical dental morphology education, assessment of soap-carving exercises may be influenced by inter-rater variability and the workload associated with manual evaluation. This study developed and internally evaluated an artificial intelligence (AI)–based deep learning system for criterion-specific assessment of soap carvings and examined its agreement with an averaged multi-rater reference standard. A total of 280 soap-carved maxillary left permanent central incisors (Fédération Dentaire Internationale [FDI] tooth 21) were photographed in five standardized views (1,400 images). Three educators independently scored each specimen on ten morphological criteria using a 0–10 scale. Inter-rater reliability was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs), and mean ratings formed criterion-specific averaged multi-rater reference scores. Specimens were partitioned into a development set ( n = 224) and an internal hold-out test set ( n = 56). A ResNet50-based multi-output regression model was trained using five-fold cross-validation across three random seeds and two-stage transfer learning. Performance was evaluated using mean absolute error (MAE), root mean squared error (RMSE), coefficient of determination (R²), Spearman’s rank correlation, ICC, Bland–Altman analysis, and bootstrap 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) was qualitatively examined in eight hold-out specimens. Average-measure ICCs among educators ranged from 0.849 to 0.994 across the ten criteria. On the hold-out test set, the ensemble achieved a macro MAE of 1.204 (95% CI, 1.059–1.374), macro RMSE of 1.584 (95% CI, 1.371–1.799), and macro R² of 0.223 (95% CI, 0.023–0.348). Criterion-specific Spearman correlations ranged from 0.297 to 0.560, while absolute-agreement ICCs between AI predictions and averaged multi-rater reference scores ranged from 0.309 to 0.429. Criterion 10 had the lowest MAE (0.709), whereas Criterion 9 had the highest (2.029). Bland–Altman mean biases were small, with variable limits of agreement. Grad-CAM showed heterogeneous activation patterns. The findings demonstrate the feasibility of a ResNet50-based approach for criterion-specific assessment of soap carvings, while highlighting substantial variability in criterion-level performance. Absolute agreement with the multi-rater reference standard was heterogeneous and does not support interchangeability with educators assessment or autonomous summative grading. The approach may support human-supervised formative assessment, though prospective external validation is required before implementation.
authors: Göknur ÖZTÜRK; Özlem Kara; Hasan Efe Purmut; Mehmet Berk Birdal; Aysun Sezer

title: Development of software for use of dental mannequins in virtual environments or virtual reality and the metaverse
abstract: This research aims to present an interactive tool called OdontoSim 3D, which simulates dental procedures, providing an immersive educational experience, allowing risk-free practice for patients, and improving clinical skills. The use of detailed 3D models and features such as zoom and rotation enabled accurate analysis. The virtual system offers advantages over the use of physical mannequins, such as the elimination of clinical risks and cost reduction. The repetition of procedures and real-time interaction with three-dimensional models improved student learning. The software also showed scalability, allowing expansion to more complex procedures.

title: Diabetic Retinopathy Detection in Retinal Fundus Images Using Sequential Convolutional Neural Network
abstract: Diabetic Retinopathy (DR) is a dynamic, incurable microvascular condition of diabetes mellitus that produces floaters, blurred vision, trouble seeing colors, and occasionally permanent blindness. Therefore, systematic discussion and review of related approaches and findings are necessary for DR detection. The analysis and identification of various ophthalmologic conditions, including arteriosclerosis, glaucoma, hypertension, DR, and choroidal neovascularization, are the main uses of fundus images of the retina. By examining retinal fundus images, the Computer-Aided Detection approach helps ophthalmologists identify such anomalies. Deep Learning is a developing and highly promising method that is used by machines to learn features of certain objects and recognize patterns, and due to the increase in the amount of data collected in the medical field, it is becoming a great option to be implemented in the field. Thus, this study will provide a thorough analysis of the issues related to retinal vessel segmentation, evaluating various extraction techniques and providing a brief example of quantitative performance metrics for retinal vessel segmentation, such as sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy, among others. Sequential Convolutional Neural Network is employed here for the classification of the APTOS fundus image dataset for the detection of Diabetic Retinopathy.

title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Two Multimodal Artificial Intelligence Systems Versus Dental Students in Endodontic Radiographic Classification
abstract: Objectives: Multimodal artificial intelligence (AI) systems are increasingly used to support image interpretation in dentistry, but evidence regarding their diagnostic performance on endodontic radiographs remains limited. This study compared the diagnostic accuracy of two general-purpose multimodal AI systems with that of undergraduate and postgraduate dental students and evaluated whether image cropping influenced AI performance. Methods: Fifty anonymized periapical radiographs were retrospectively selected, with 10 cases in each of five predefined endodontic diagnostic categories. Reference diagnoses were established by consensus between two experienced endodontists. ChatGPT version 5.2 and Gemini version 3 independently classified each case using both full-size and tooth-cropped images and a standardized prompt. Twenty-five fifth-year undergraduate dental students and 20 postgraduate students in clinical endodontics classified the full-size images. Overall and category-specific accuracies were calculated, and agreement with the reference standard was assessed. Results: Overall accuracy was highest among postgraduate students (84.9%), followed by undergraduate students (78.7%). Gemini achieved accuracies of 72.0% with full-size images and 82.0% with cropped images, whereas ChatGPT achieved 68.0% and 50.0%, respectively. Cropping significantly reduced ChatGPT accuracy (p = 0.0117) but did not significantly affect Gemini performance (p = 0.3018). Diagnostic accuracy varied substantially across categories. Agreement with the reference standard for the AI systems ranged from 50.0% to 82.0%. Conclusions: Diagnostic performance depended on the evaluator, AI system, image format, and diagnostic category. Postgraduate students showed the highest overall accuracy, while AI performance was heterogeneous and did not consistently exceed that of trained human observers. General-purpose multimodal AI may support supervised radiographic interpretation and education, but it should not replace comprehensive clinical assessment or professional judgment.
authors: Andrea Spinelli; Emanuele Charles; Maria Giovanna Gandolfi; Carlo Prati; Fausto Zamparini

title: Diagnostic Performance of Claude AI Sonnet 4.6 in Interpreting Conventional Intraoral Periapical and Digital Radiovisiographic Images: A Retrospective Comparative Study
abstract: Background: Multimodal artificial intelligence and vision-language models are increasingly being evaluated for medical image interpretation. Recent radiology studies indicate that these systems can generate clinically relevant diagnostic suggestions, while performance varies according to model, task, and imaging context. Dental radiographic applications, particularly direct comparison of conventional intraoral periapical (IOPA) and digital radiovisiographic (RVG) images, require further evaluation. Aim: To evaluate and compare the diagnostic performance of Claude AI Sonnet 4.6 in interpreting conventional IOPA radiographs and digital RVG images. Materials and Methods: A retrospective comparative observational study was conducted on 100 intraoral radiographic images comprising 50 conventional IOPA radiographs and 50 RVG images. Eligible images were of acceptable diagnostic quality and had a confirmed reference-standard diagnosis. Each image was uploaded individually to Claude AI Sonnet 4.6 using a standardized prompt. The AI-generated diagnosis was compared with the clinician-established reference diagnosis. Prompt requirement and processing time were recorded, and data were entered into Microsoft Excel and analyzed using SPSS. Results: Sixty images (60%) represented the mandible and 40 (40%) the maxilla. Claude demonstrated 79% overall diagnostic concordance when full or partial agreement was considered. No statistically significant difference in diagnostic agreement was observed between RVG and IOPA images (p=0.908). RVG images required fewer prompts than IOPA images (mean 1.53±0.50 versus 2.13±0.57; p<0.001). Mean processing time documented was 15.4±5.5 seconds for RVG and 21.64 ± 1.91 seconds for IOPA. Conclusion: Claude AI Sonnet 4.6 demonstrated moderate diagnostic concordance across both conventional and digital intraoral radiographs. The findings support further evaluation of multimodal AI as a clinical decision-support technology, while emphasizing the continued need for expert clinical and radiographic interpretation.

title: Digital Transformation and Multidsciplinary Treatment Approaches in Orthodontics
abstract: Digital transformation in orthodontics refers to the digitization of patients’ clinical, photographic, radiological, and surface data; the integration of these data within a common digital environment; and the management of the workflow from diagnosis to retention based on these data. Intraoral scanners, digital models, cone-beam computed tomography, three-dimensional cephalometry, virtual treatment setups, clear aligner systems, artificial intelligence, and remote monitoring platforms contribute to making orthodontic decisions more measurable, reproducible, and shareable. Nevertheless, it should be recognized that digital tools do not inherently guarantee clinical success and that data quality, biological boundaries, operator supervision, and the sequencing of multidisciplinary treatment are decisive determinants of outcomes. This chapter addresses digital diagnostic and record-taking methods in orthodontics, intraoral scanning, three-dimensional and artificial intelligence-assisted cephalometric assessment, digital treatment planning, clear aligner workflows, and teleorthodontics. In addition, decision-making and treatment sequencing are discussed in multidisciplinary clinical situations involving impacted teeth, endodontically treated teeth, patients with periodontal problems, missing teeth, and orthodontic preparation before prosthetic treatment. The monitoring of biological risks, particularly root resorption, using digital data; the limitations of digital orthodontics; and the future transition toward personalized treatment models are also evaluated. The fundamental approach is to use digital technology not as a substitute for clinical examination, but as a decision-support system that addresses the appropriate clinical question and strengthens communication among specialists.
authors: Ali Kağan Özen

title: Direct access to treatment by dental hygienists in Ireland: a survey of dental practitioners’ perspectives
abstract: Objectives The public can directly access dental care by a dental hygienist (DH) in many countries internationally. Research has shown that allowing DHs to work under direct access (DA) improves oral health outcomes, increases service efficiency, and expands access to preventive care. Currently, DA to a DH in Ireland is not permitted. The purpose of this study was to gain a better knowledge of the views of dentists in Ireland in relation to the provision of treatment by DHs under DA in the future. Methods A cross-sectional survey was used on a convenience sample of Irish dentists. The quantitative data were analysed using descriptive and inferential statistics, and a thematic analysis was undertaken on the qualitative data. Results Seventy-five dentists completed the survey. Most had experienced working with a DH at some time (97%). Many respondents (65%) felt positive or very positive about the introduction of DA in Ireland. Overall, most respondents felt that all groups of the population (general population, children, people with disabilities, the elderly, people in nursing homes) would benefit from the introduction of DA; the highest perceived benefit was in nursing homes (71%). Conclusions While the concept of DA to DHs was broadly welcomed by dentists practising in Ireland, some reservations and concerns do exist. DA was seen as both an opportunity and a challenge. DA has potential to strengthen the dental care system in Ireland, but its success will depend on thoughtful implementation, updated training pathways, clear regulatory guidance, and alignment with broader workforce planning.
authors: Sviatlana Anishchuk; Siobhán Kelleher; Donna Paton; Seren Truter; Wenda Thomas; Janet Williams Oshun; Catherine Waldron

title: Do Earth-Trained Humanoid Controllers Walk on the Moon? Gravity, Terrain, and Soil Transfer
abstract: The Moon changes gravity, terrain, and soil at once. Learned locomotion has studied reduced gravity on rigid ground and granular terrain mostly at Earth gravity, but not humanoids under both, generalist-controller transfer, or the Earth cost of lunar adaptation. On a simulated Unitree G1, we train 12 policies with one recipe, varying gravity, terrain geometry, and ground contact (rigid or three-dimensional resistive force theory, 3D RFT), and including Earth-to-Moon fine-tuning and gravity randomization. We test them at both gravities on rigid ground and 3D RFT, and at their training gravity on three held-out soil models. We also test the frozen SONIC, a released generalist humanoid controller, at both gravities on rigid ground only. Gravity transfer is asymmetric. Earth-trained policies keep 0.64 to 0.75 survival at the Moon on flat rigid ground, Moon-trained and fine-tuned policies cannot stand at Earth, and SONIC survives at most 0.10 at the Moon. Rough training lifts combined-tile survival from 0.53 to 0.98 at Earth and 0.80 to 0.99 at the Moon. In 3D RFT, soil training helps on Earth sand, on tiles and for rough-trained policies also on flat sand. On the stiffer lunar soil it helps only flat-trained Earth policies at Earth and changes the survival of Moon-trained policies by at most a few hundredths. In the sampled rollouts of the held-out soil models, Moon-trained policies keep most of their rigid-ground progress on lunar regolith at the low G1 foot pressure, with per-seed progress ratios of 0.84 to 1.39 apart from one seed with a short rigid reference. A gravity-randomized policy trained on rough 3D RFT terrain has a seed-mean survival of at least 0.84 at Earth and 0.96 at the Moon on every key test cell up to 20 degrees. Lunar results are simulation predictions conditional on the contact model and soil stiffness.
authors: Guillem Casadesus Vila; Sri Aditya Deevi; Grace X. Gao

title: Double-balloon enteroscopy in different age groups: indications, findings, diagnosis, and treatment
abstract: Double-balloon enteroscopy (DBE) is an essential diagnostic and therapeutic modality for small-bowel disorders. Most prior studies on age-related differences in DBE involved limited age groups and small cohorts. We evaluated age-specific differences in the indications, findings, therapeutic interventions, and complications of DBE in a large single-center cohort. We retrospectively analyzed 817 patients who underwent 1101 DBE procedures between January 2006 and January 2023 at a tertiary center. The patients were grouped as young (18-44 years), middle-aged (45-64 years), and elderly (≥65 years). Demographics, indications, endoscopic and pathological findings, interventions, and complications were compared among groups. Bleeding was the most frequent indication in elderly patients, whereas diarrhea, abdominal pain, inflammatory bowel disease, and polyposis syndromes were more common in younger patients. Inflammatory lesions and polyps predominated in younger patients, whereas vascular lesions and tumors were more frequent in elderly patients (P < .05). Diagnostic interventions predominated in young and middle-aged patients, whereas therapeutic interventions were more common in the elderly (P < .001). Benign and malignant neoplasms were more common in the elderly, whereas celiac disease and polyposis syndrome were more common in younger individuals (P < .05). The overall complication rate was 2.6%, with a higher but nonsignificant rate of anesthesia-related complications in the elderly (P = .11). DBE is safe and effective in all age groups. Age was significantly associated with clinical indications and endoscopic findings, and recognizing these patterns can guide more targeted use of DBE and improve diagnostic accuracy.

title: Dual-Rate Force-Image Control with Model-Based Orientation Limits for Robotic Ultrasound
abstract: Robotic ultrasound couples a high-rate contact-force loop with slower, delayed image feedback, so image-guided ultrasound probe rotation can perturb contact force before the resulting image response is observed. We derive a closed-form orientation-rate limit that bounds the modeled rotation-induced estimated-force excursion over a finite horizon while accounting for disturbance rejection by the fast force loop. The limit depends on local contact stiffness, force-loop gains, a conservative rotation-to-force gain bound, the excursion budget, and the prediction horizon. We implement this model in a dual-rate controller with timestamp-based delay reconstruction and joint-torque-based force estimation, and evaluate it on a curved gelatin phantom using paired controller comparisons and component ablations. Relative to unconstrained image guidance, the proposed rate-limited controller reduced first-second root-mean-square (RMS) estimated-force error by 0.40 N while increasing cue-convergence time by 0.94 s. A fixed rate cap near the analytically predicted ceiling produced no resolvable difference in force error and converged 0.32 s faster, indicating that the principal practical value of the model is the rate-design rule rather than online prediction. Delay reconstruction had no resolvable effect at the tested latency. A single-subject popliteal scan demonstrated feasibility, although the image cue was noise-limited on heterogeneous tissue.

title: EBV-CAN: Vision--Language Grounding for Contact-Aided Endoscope Navigation
abstract: Flexible endoscopes exploit structural compliance to traverse narrow lumens, pipes, and cavities, where navigation involves distributed environmental contact. This compliance makes tip motion depend on the evolving support configuration. We present external bird's-eye-view contact-aided navigation (EBV-CAN), a vision-language policy that combines one initial global static bird's-eye image with evolving endoscopic observations and motor state. Three supervised semantic queries locate the tip, next waypoint, and instructed target on the cached global image; their residual representations predict bending and insertion commands. We introduce the Vision-Language Contact-Aided (VLCA) dataset, linking 517 demonstrations and 75k action samples to 958k spatial entries and 93k remaining-route records. On 50 held-out episodes, tip-coordinate and waypoint localization reach 97.5% and 94.8%. Swapping the target instruction under identical observations changes target attention and motor output across 17 dual-target episodes. Across 1,920 physical trials of eight policies trained under a shared protocol, EBV-CAN achieves 183/240 successes (76.25%) under automatic blue-area scoring. Gated recurrent unit behavior cloning (GRU-BC) achieves the lowest matched-task offline mean absolute error (MAE), 0.056, and 1/240 physical successes, establishing distinct rankings for action imitation and task completion. Successful multi-guide executions and representative failures connect spatial progress, steering transitions, and visibility to physical navigation.
authors: Chi Kit Ng; Shuchang Liu; Jinsong Lin; Yidong Zhang; Xizi Wang; Ho Yin Chim; Hongliang Ren

title: EFFECT OF PHARMACIST-LED EDUCATIONAL INTERVENTION ON DISEASE KNOWLEDGE AND HEALTHRELATED QUALITY OF LIFE AMONG PATIENTS WITH INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE: A PROSPECTIVE OBSERVATIONAL STUDY FROM SOUTH INDIA
abstract: Background: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), comprising ulcerative colitis (UC) and Crohn's disease (CD), is a chronic, relapsing, immune-mediated gastrointestinal disorder that imposes a substantial physical, psychological, and socioeconomic burden on affected individuals.The recurrent nature of the disease, coupled with prolonged treatment requirements and frequent disease exacerbations, significantly compromises patients' health-related quality of life (HRQoL).Adequate disease-related knowledge is considered a critical component of successful disease management, as informed patients are more likely to adhere to prescribed therapies, participate actively in self-care practices, and achieve improved clinical outcomes.Despite the growing prevalence of IBD, patient awareness regarding disease pathology, treatment strategies, lifestyle modifications, and long-term complications remains inadequate, particularly in developing countries.Therefore, educational interventions may play an important role in improving patient knowledge and quality of life.Objective: The present study aimed to evaluate the impact of a structured clinical pharmacist-led educational intervention on disease-related knowledge and health-related quality of life among patients diagnosed with inflammatory bowel disease.Additionally, the study sought to identify demographic and disease-related factors associated with patient knowledge and quality-of-life outcomes.Methods: A prospective observational study was conducted among 74 patients with confirmed diagnoses of inflammatory bowel disease attending gastroenterology departments of selected tertiary care hospitals in Andhra Pradesh, India, between October 2025 and January 2026.Disease-related knowledge was assessed using the validated Crohn's and Colitis Knowledge Score (CCKNOW), while health-related quality of life was evaluated using the Short Inflammatory Bowel Disease Questionnaire (SIBDQ).Baseline assessments were performed during the initial hospital visit.Subsequently, individualized patient counselling and educational leaflets were provided to improve disease understanding and self-management practices.Follow-up assessments were conducted after 4-5 weeks using the same validated instruments.Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS version 16.0.Paired t-tests, chi-square tests, and one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) were applied to determine differences between pre-and post-intervention outcomes, with statistical significance established at p < 0.05.
venue: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology

title: EVALUATION OF THE ROLE OF FECAL CALPROTECTIN AS A BIOMARKER OF ENDOSCOPIC DISEASE ACTIVITY IN PATIENTS WITH CROHN’S DISEASE
abstract: Introduction: Crohn's disease is a chronic inflammatory bowel illness with transmural inflammation and diverse clinical manifestations. Accurate assessment of disease activity is required to guide treatment and improve patient outcomes. This study assessed the diagnostic efficacy of fecal calprotectin as a biomarker of endoscopic disease activity in patients with Crohn's disease undergoing biologic therapy.Methods: We conducted this prospective cohort study of 70 patients at Baghdad Teaching Hospital/Medical City between January 2024 and January 2025. We measured disease activity using the Simple Endoscopic Score for Crohn's Disease (SES-CD). We classified endoscopic activity as remission (0-2), mild activity (3-6), moderate activity (7-15), or severe activity (?16). Results: Among the 70 patients, 51 (72.8%) were in remission, while 19 (27.2%) had active disease after treatment. Active patients had significantly higher post-treatment fecal calprotectin levels than those in remission (367.89 vs. 111.83 ?g/g, P < .001). ROC analysis showed an area under the curve of 0.835 (P < .001). A fecal calprotectin cutoff of ?148.5 ?g/g resulted in 89.4% sensitivity, 70.6% specificity, 53.1% positive predictive value, and 94.7% negative predictive value. Conclusion: Fecal calprotectin effectively detects endoscopic disease activity in patients with Crohn's disease. Its high sensitivity and negative predictive value suggest it could be useful as a noninvasive monitoring tool, but the results should be interpreted in the context of this single-center investigation.

title: Effects of Generative AI–Supported Virtual Reality Dental Skill Training on Learning Performance, Visual Behavior, and Cortical Activation Among Dental Students: Stratified Randomized Controlled Trial
abstract: BACKGROUND: The rapid advancement of AI, particularly generative AI (GenAI), is reshaping educational paradigms. However, its utility in preclinical digital medical skills education remains insufficiently explored. OBJECTIVE: This study aims to investigate whether GenAI‑assisted training yields superior performance relative to traditional instruction in virtual reality (VR)-supported preclinical dental skill education. METHODS: A total of 123 eligible students from a top‑tier Chinese university completed the trial. Participants were stratified by baseline theoretical scores and randomly assigned within each stratum into two arms: the GenAI-assisted group (n=62) received ChatGPT guidance without human tutoring, with research assistants monitoring AI outputs solely for safety and error checking; the teacher-led control group (n=61) received on-site instructor guidance. Both groups underwent standardized VR-based dental skill training for 7 days. Assessments included dental operative skill examinations, functional near-infrared spectroscopy recording, continuous eye-tracking monitoring, visual-spatial ability tests, and questionnaires measuring self-regulated learning, learning emotions, and engagement. RESULTS: =3.88, Cohen d=0.70; P<.001). For secondary outcomes, the GenAI‑assisted group also demonstrated significantly lower cognitive‑load indicators (mean 0.180, SD 0.136) than the control group (mean 0.346, SD 0.150; P<.001), accompanied by more efficient visual attention allocation patterns and stronger activation in prefrontal cortex, motor cortex, visual association cortex, and temporoparietal junction brain regions. The GenAI‑assisted group showed better performance across low (P=.003), medium (P=.004), and high (P=.004) level visual-spatial ability tests. Among low-achieving participants, the largest between-group difference in self-regulated learning was found in favor of the GenAI-assisted group (P=.02). Better scores were also observed for the GenAI‑assisted group in learning enjoyment, as well as behavioral, emotional, and cognitive engagement. CONCLUSIONS: Students randomized to GenAI-assisted training had higher immediate operative scores than students receiving teacher-led instruction. Secondary cognitive, behavioral, and neurophysiological findings were exploratory and pointed toward a link between GenAI exposure and variations in skill‑acquisition metrics among dental students receiving VR-based training. The results offer preliminary insights regarding the potential integration of GenAI into preclinical dental skill education. title: End-to-end framework integrating generative AI and deep reinforcement learning for autonomous ultrasound scanning.
abstract: Cardiac ultrasound (US) is among the most widely used diagnostic tools in cardiology for assessing heart health, but its effectiveness is limited by operator dependence, time constraints, and human error. The shortage of trained professionals, especially in remote areas, further restricts access. These issues underscore the need for automated solutions that can ensure consistent, accessible cardiac imaging regardless of operator skill or location. Recent progress in artificial intelligence (AI), especially in deep reinforcement learning (DRL), has gained attention for enabling autonomous decision-making. However, existing DRL-based approaches to cardiac US scanning lack reproducibility, rely on proprietary data, and use simplified models. Motivated by these gaps, we present the first end-to-end framework that integrates generative AI and DRL to enable autonomous and reproducible cardiac US scanning. The framework comprises two components: (i) a conditional generative simulator combining Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) with Variational Autoencoders (VAEs), that models the cardiac US environment producing realistic action-conditioned images; and (ii) a DRL module that leverages this simulator to learn autonomous, accurate scanning policies. The proposed framework delivers AI-driven guidance through expert-validated models that classify image type and assess quality, supports conditional generation of realistic US images, and establishes a reproducible foundation extendable to other organs. To ensure reproducibility, a publicly available dataset of real cardiac US scans is released. The solution is validated through several experiments. The VAE-GAN is benchmarked against existing GAN variants, with performance assessed using qualitative and quantitative approaches, while the DRL-based scanning system is evaluated under varying configurations to demonstrate effectiveness.

title: EndoVLA-OOV: Language-Conditioned Out-of-View Target Acquisition in Robotic Endoscopy
abstract: The scan-then-revisit workflow of upper gastrointestinal endoscopy requires bringing a previously observed suspicious region back into view for closer inspection. Acquiring such targets requires translating anatomical and appearance descriptions into camera motions from partial observations of a confined, deformable environment. We present EndoVLA-OOV, a language-conditioned vision-language-action policy for out-of-view target acquisition in robotic endoscopy. The policy adapts a pretrained backbone to continuous two-degree-of-freedom distal bending commands and combines initial, intermediate, and current images to guide search. To support policy learning, we provide an open-source VLA dataset containing 1,050 episodes across six tasks and approximately 262k observation-action pairs. Physical evaluation spans wet-lens and low-light conditions, two unseen stomach phantoms, and cross-embodiment transfer to an unseen ex-vivo environment. In the cross-embodiment evaluation, the full-data policy achieves 93.3% target acquisition success (28/30). In a controlled training-data comparison, expanding the corpus from 312 to 1,050 episodes increases acquisition success from 40.0% to 90.0% under the same model, training, and test configuration. Instruction and observation interventions further support the use of language and temporal context in the evaluated acquisition tasks. These results support language-guided endoscopic revisitation across the evaluated environments and robot embodiments and demonstrate the benefit of expanded task-specific demonstrations.

title: Endoscopic Endonasal Approaches to Anterior Cranial Base Meningiomas: Indications, Limitations, and Surgical Decision-Making
abstract: Endoscopic endonasal surgery (EES) has fundamentally changed the management of anterior skull base meningiomas by enabling access to many lesions through a direct minimally invasive corridor that avoids traditional transcranial exposure. Improvements in endoscopic optical technology, surgical instrumentation, and skull base reconstruction have steadily expanded the range of tumors that can be treated through an endonasal approach. Even so, EES is not appropriate for every lesion, making thoughtful patient selection and surgical team experience the most important determinants of surgical success. This review explores where EES fits in the contemporary management of anterior skull base meningiomas, including olfactory groove, tuberculum sellae, and planum sphenoidale meningiomas, with particular attention to its indications, limitations, and situations in which EES may not be appropriate. Evidence comparing endoscopic endonasal and transcranial approaches for anterior skull base meningiomas is reviewed, with attention to how tumor anatomy, oncologic objectives, and individual patient characteristics influence the choice of approach. A major consideration is how surgical morbidity can be minimized without compromising oncologic and safety outcomes. Current strategies to protect critical neurovascular structures, reduce the risk of cerebrospinal fluid leakage, and improve skull base durability, including advances in vascularized reconstruction techniques, are discussed. Emerging outcome data and the evolving learning curve associated with EES are also reviewed. Rather than presenting EES as a universal solution, the evidence points toward a patient-centered approach in which operative strategy and clinical decision making is guided by tumor characteristics, anatomy, and surgical goals.

title: Endoscopic and Robotic Minimally Invasive Breast Surgery (MIBS) for Benign Breast Lesions: Our Experience of 80 Cases and Descriptive Comparison
abstract: Objective: Minimally invasive breast surgery (MIBS) via an extramammary approach offers an alternative to conventional open lumpectomy, eliminating breast scarring and improving psychological outcomes in patients with benign breast lesions.While endoscopic MIBS (EMIBS) has been described, data on robotic MIBS (RMIBS) are sparse.We analyzed the clinical and cosmetic outcomes of EMIBS and RMIBS.Materials and Methods: Eighty patients undergoing MIBS for benign breast lumps were divided into endoscopic (n = 40) and robotic (n = 40) groups.Primary endpoints included cosmetic outcomes [evaluated via Patient and Observer Scar Assessment Scale (POSAS) and BREAST-Q], total operative and docking times, and complications, which were statistically analysed (IBM SPSS Statistics version 30).Results: Groups were comparable in age (p = 0.325), lesion size (median 2.0 vs. 2.75 cm; p = 0.247), and number of lumps (median 1 in both groups; p = 0.165).Operative time analysis showed that operative time was significantly longer in the robotic group (median 150 vs. 95 minutes; p<0.001).Complications were minor, self-resolving, and comparable across both groups (Fisher's exact p = 0.647).Cosmetic outcomes (at 1 month) were comparable between the two groups: median POSAS score 2 and median BREAST-Q score 88 (breast-conserving therapy module, satisfaction with breasts subscale).A subjective reduction in physical strain on the surgeon was noted in the robotic group; no objective ergonomic measurements were performed. Conclusion:We demonstrate the feasibility and safety of both approaches for benign breast lesions, with comparable and favorable cosmetic outcomes, and with the robotic platform offering subjective improvement in ergonomic strain, especially in difficult-to-access medial quadrants.These findings are hypothesis-generating and require validation using instruments such as NASA-TLX or the Borg CR-10 scale in larger studies.

title: Evaluating Wi-Fi HaLow for Next-Generation Capsule Endoscopy
abstract: Capsule endoscopy is limited by its wireless link: insufficient throughput restricts image resolution and frame rate, whereas high-rate radios typically use higher carrier frequencies that experience greater attenuation through tissue. This work evaluates Wi-Fi HaLow (IEEE 802.11ah), a sub-GHz Wi-Fi standard, as an image link for capsule endoscopy. Across all tested combinations of modulation and coding scheme and bandwidth, the saturation TCP throughput reached 15.55 Mbps, and the fastest configuration also achieved the lowest energy per bit. Through power optimization strategies, the combined power consumption of the HaLow module and microcontroller at 1 frame per second (FPS) was reduced from 101.70 to 14.00 mW, which is comparable to that of Bluetooth Low Energy systems. In a simulated in vivo setting, the default rate control selected the highest tested MCS and bandwidth, indicating sufficient link quality; this configuration also had the lowest measured power in both the 1 FPS mode (13.59 mW) and the 30 FPS mode (174.21 mW). The capsule-to-receiver latency was 20.68 ms for a 24 KB frame, while the receiver-to-capsule latency was 4.77 ms for a command; this low-latency bidirectional communication supports real-time detection and manipulation for next-generation capsule endoscopy.
authors: Ziyao Zhou; Chen Shen; Tiancheng Cao; Hen-Wei Huang

title: Evaluation of Personas and Daily Activity Maps to Inform Clinical Care and Socially Assistive Robot Training and Design for Persons With Dementia: Mixed Methods Study
abstract: Background: Over 55 million people worldwide are living with dementia, resulting in significant caregiving demands and caregiver burden. Socially assistive robots (SARs) are increasingly being explored to reduce caregiving workload and improve the quality of life for persons with dementia; however, their effectiveness depends on person-centered design grounded in a comprehensive understanding of the target population. Personas and their corresponding daily activity maps (DAMs) are user-centered design tools that provide a holistic understanding of the personal, medical, emotional, and life trajectory of persons with dementia, enabling SARs to engage in contextually relevant and empathetic interactions. Despite their potential, these tools have not been formally evaluated for dementia care and digital health technology development. Objective: This mixed methods study aimed to explore the perspectives of professional and family caregivers, health care providers, and robot designers on the quality and use of personas and DAMs in clinical practice and digital health design. Methods: Using purposive sampling, 15 stakeholders involved in dementia care or digital health design were interviewed via Zoom (Zoom Communications, Inc) between March and April 2025 to evaluate a subset of persona-DAM pairs using a modified 12-item version of the Persona Perception Scale (PPS), adapted for dementia care contexts, across 5 domains: Credibility, Completeness, Clarity, Willingness to Use, and Empathy. Participants subsequently provided qualitative perspectives through semistructured interviews, reflecting on their ratings and offering suggestions for improvement. Results: Fifteen participants with a median of 9 (IQR 4-15) years of experience in dementia care evaluated 9 persona-DAM pairs. Overall evaluation-level median PPS scores were 4.79 (IQR 4.45, 4.91) for personas and 4.76 (IQR 4.45, 4.94) for DAMs. For both personas and DAMs, the highest-rated domains were Clarity, Credibility, and Willingness to Use (all median 5.00), suggesting stakeholders perceived the tools favorably and were willing to use them. Empathy scores (personas: median 4.67, IQR 4.25-5; DAMs: median 4.83, IQR 4.33-5) highlighted the need for greater cultural, ethnic, and religious representation to foster culturally sensitive interventions. Completeness was the lowest-scoring domain (personas: median 4.50, IQR 3.94-5; DAMs: median 4.38, IQR 4-5), representing the most quantitative improvement suggestions. Qualitative analysis revealed 3 major themes: (1) improving human-robot interaction training through greater knowledge of the personal context of persons with dementia; (2) comprehensive assessment of clinical history and functional capacities as essential for the provision of safe and effective interaction; and (3) perceived design utility: translating person-centered knowledge into actionable tools. Conclusions: This study provides early-stage exploratory evidence that personas and DAMs are perceived as clinically and technically relevant tools for dementia care, complementing existing clinical documentation through a holistic, person-centered view, and serving as human-centered design tools for developing personalized digital health solutions.

title: EviGround-CT: Sentence-to-Volume Grounding for Verifying LLM-Generated Chest CT Reports
abstract: Chest computed tomography (CT) reports generated by large language models (LLMs) can describe positive findings that lack localized evidence in the scan. We propose EviGround-CT to verify these findings after report generation. A deterministic extractor identifies positive finding sentences, and a 3D grounding model predicts an evidence mask for each sentence. Using the full sentence retains anatomical location, laterality, and descriptive modifiers in the grounding query. We evaluate report generation on CT-RATE, and grounding and verification on a held-out 100-case ReXGroundingCT subset. Using the available annotations, sentence-grounded verification raises evidence-supported precision (ESP) from 0.263 to 0.365 across 137 extracted in-scope positives, compared with category conditioning. The corresponding unsupported positive finding rate falls from 0.737 to 0.635. The paired case-level bootstrap ESP difference is +0.102 (95% confidence interval: [0.028, 0.181]). The predicted masks associate individual report statements with spatial evidence that can be inspected alongside the CT.
authors: Ziyuan Li; Juncheng Ni; Feng Li

title: Explainability-informed patient-disjoint evaluation of deep learning for plus disease in retinopathy of prematurity with an ophthalmologist reader study
abstract: Background: Plus disease is a treatment-relevant sign of retinopathy of prematurity, but fundus images from the same infant may differ in image quality, posterior-pole coverage, and visible vascular severity. We evaluated deep-learning classification using a patient-disjoint design, within-infant variability, and an ophthalmologist reader study. Methods: The primary analysis included 732 Phoenix ICON fundus images from 38 infants, assigned exclusively to a 634-image development pool or a 98-image hold-out set from eight previously unseen infants. Five pretrained convolutional neural networks were evaluated at the image level. Hold-out predictions were grouped by infant and laterality to characterize descriptive within-infant variation. A historical secondary analysis used a random image-level partition without enforced patient separation and was considered exploratory. Two ophthalmologists independently graded 30 unique isolated images for inter-observer analysis; 10 were presented twice, resulting in 40 presentations for intra-observer repeatability. Results: DenseNet121 achieved an image-level ROC-AUC of 0.929; however, infant-equal-weighted image-level ROC-AUC was 0.905 and leave-one-infant-out ROC-AUC ranged from 0.838 to 0.989, demonstrating sensitivity to the small clustered hold-out cohort. At a development-defined threshold of 0.0184, sensitivity increased to 98.0%, while specificity decreased to 46.8%. Within-infant probability variability was observed across all five CNN architectures. Ophthalmologists 1 and 2 assessed 14/18 and 17/18 plus-reference images, respectively, as Healthy. Exact three-category inter-observer agreement was 26/30 (86.7%), and both reproduced the same severity grade for all 10 repeated images. Conclusions: Patient-disjoint evaluation revealed substantial uncertainty in image-level performance and variability among images from the same infant. Cluster-aware analyses showed dependence on the small hold-out cohort, while the development-defined operating point demonstrated a marked sensitivity-specificity trade-off. The reader study showed that an examination-derived reference label and the diagnostic evidence visible in an isolated image are not equivalent, despite high inter-observer agreement and complete categorical repeatability. Because examination identifiers were unavailable, within-infant analyses were interpreted descriptively and not as infant or examination-level diagnostic performance. Clinically useful systems should assess image quality, select informative views, and integrate evidence across multiple images and both eyes. External prospective multicentre validation is required before clinical implementation.
authors: Rouhollah Kian Ara; Jan Kubíček; Sumit Kaushik; Kristýna Maršolková; Juraj Timkovič

title: F2D-RetinaNet: a feature-to-decision dual-path network with fractional operators for retinal disease detection and grading
abstract: Visible pathological abnormalities and vascular integrity help diagnose retinal diseases. This paper introduces a unified feature-to-decision framework that first extracts vasculature and enhances lesions. First, this study proposes the fractional anisotropic diffusion–based hybrid enhancement (FADHE) method that selectively amplifies lesion contrast and vessel visibility in the green channel using long-memory fractional diffusion dynamics. Second, this study introduces a fractional Hessian-based attention U-Net (FHAU-Net), a multi-scale vessel segmentation model that leverages fractional Hessian responses across eight fractional orders and attention-guided skip connections to capture fine vessel structures. Finally, this work designs a dual-branch disease grading model, F2D-RetinaNet, which jointly processes the enhanced image and vessel map to learn lesion-related and vascular feature representations for the recognition and grading of retinal diseases. The FHAU-Net model achieved a Dice coefficient of 0.8987, a sensitivity of 0.9084, an accuracy of 0.9804, and a specificity of 0.9876 across the unified test set, which contains variations in resolution, acquisition site, camera type, and imaging conditions. The F2D-RetinaNet is evaluated for Diabetic retinopathy (DR) detection, DR grading, and multiclass retinal disease classification tasks. Extensive testing and comparisons to the baseline procedures support the reliability of the proposed methodology on the datasets evaluated here.

title: Feasibility-guaranteed link adaptation and agentic semantic communication under imperfect CSIT via deep unfolding
abstract: We present a feasibility-guaranteed framework for task-oriented semantic communication and link adaptation under imperfect channel state information at the transmitter (CSIT). The framework characterizes semantic rate, task distortion, and an operational semantic-capacity measure that jointly captures finite-blocklength effects, CSIT uncertainty, and probing overhead. To support adaptive transmission, an agentic controller first generates nominal decisions for pilot allocation, feedback budget, transmit power, payload blocklength, coding rate, and semantic joint source–channel coding (JSCC) parameters. These decisions are then processed by a model-driven deep-unfolded projection layer that maps the nominal action onto the feasible set while preserving differentiability for end-to-end policy learning. The unfolded architecture embeds iterative primal–dual updates and explicitly enforces power, latency, blocklength, rate, energy, and reliability constraints. A multi-agent realization separates information acquisition from payload adaptation while sharing the projection module to maintain coordinated feasibility under rapidly varying channels. The principal novelty lies in combining causally ordered probing and payload agents with a state-dependent deep-unfolded projection and deterministic terminal restoration, thereby converting policy-generated mixed-domain decisions into instantaneously feasible semantic transmission actions under imperfect CSIT. Numerical evaluations over time-varying fading and interference conditions show that the proposed design reduces semantic NMSE by up to approximately 30% and increases task-success probability by up to 9 percentage points relative to the strongest competing baseline, with the largest gains observed under severe CSIT mismatch and stringent resource budgets.
authors: A. Mohajer; Asad Mirzaei; M. Darabi; X. Fernando

title: Fed-ADApt: Federated Anytime Depth Adaptation for Resource-Aware Medical Image Segmentation
abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative training of medical image segmentation models without sharing raw patient data, yet existing approaches assume a homogeneous compute budget across institutions, limiting participation of low-resource sites. We propose Fed-ADApt, a depth-adaptive federated framework for UNet-based segmentation that jointly addresses low-compute training and inference. Fed-ADApt integrates multi-depth supervision with hierarchical depth-wise aggregation, allowing each site to train according to its local compute budget while contributing to a global model that supports dynamic depth selection at deployment. We evaluated Fed-ADApt on multi-site 2D retinal fundus disc segmentation and 3D brain tumor segmentation. Across both tasks, federated collaboration substantially improves robustness under domain shift. Fed-ADApt matched the full-resource FedAvg performance in 3D and achieved competitive 2D performance with a 4.7% average Dice reduction, while reducing average inference cost by 19.5% in 3D and 34.5% in 2D and substantially reducing training cost by 98% at the most constrained sites. Importantly, Fed-ADApt enables low-resource institutions that cannot train full-capacity models to participate in federations while maintaining competitive global performance under a favorable accuracy to efficiency trade-off. By considering training and inference compute budgets, Fed-ADApt provides a practical and equitable solution for federated medical image segmentation across heterogeneous clinical and edge-enabled imaging environments.
authors: Abhijeet Parida; Zhifan Jiang; Pooneh Roshanitabrizi; Austin Tapp; María J. Ledesma‐Carbayo; Syed Muhammad Anwar; Ziyue Xu; Marius George Linguraru; Holger R. Roth

title: FedFound: Federated Foundation Model for GI endoscopy imaging
abstract: Gastrointestinal (GI) endoscopy is essential for identifying abnormalities and enabling early diagnosis, thereby improving diagnostic accuracy and facilitating timely clinical intervention. While deep learning has shown promise in supporting GI diagnostics, most models require carefully labeled datasets that are costly to acquire and limited in scope. Foundation models offer a paradigm shift by learning general-purpose representations that can be adapted for diverse tasks, addressing data scarcity and variability. However, training such models on medical imaging data remains challenging due to privacy regulations, security concerns, and fragmented digital infrastructures that prevent centralized data aggregation, even as hospitals collectively generate vast amounts of endoscopic data. To overcome these barriers, we propose a federated learning (FL) framework for GI foundation models, allowing data to remain local while collaboratively training a shared model. We extensively evaluate multiple FL algorithms under both homogeneous and heterogeneous settings across three clinically relevant downstream tasks-classification, detection, and segmentation. We further evaluate our framework with a larger number of clients and across diverse pretraining strategies to assess its scalability and robustness. Our results demonstrate consistent performance gains, underscoring the potential of Federated Foundation Models to enable clinically validated AI applications and support secure, regulation-compliant deployment in real-world gastroendoscopy practice.
authors: Alina Devkota; Annahita Amireskandari; Joel R. Palko; Soban A. Maan; Shyam J Thakkar; Tapan Khan; Xiajun Jiang; Donald Adjeroh; Binod Bhattarai; Prashnna Gyawali

title: Force-Torque Classification of Reference-Profile-Defined Drilling States During Robot-Assisted Dental Implant Osteotomy
abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate whether force-torque features can classify three predefined, reference-profile-defined operational drilling states during robot-assisted implant osteotomy under specimen-level separation. Materials and Methods: Thirty porcine hemimandibular specimens underwent 180 robot-controlled osteotomies under three drilling conditions. Axial force (Fz) and drilling torque (Mz) were sampled at 1000 Hz, segmented into 100-ms windows with a 50-ms step, and represented by 42 time-, frequency-, and wavelet-domain features; 23 features were selected using training-only ANOVA ranking and correlation pruning. Specimens were separated into training, validation, and held-out test sets (18/6/6). Linear support vector machine (SVM), random forest (RF), and XGBoost were evaluated against predefined depth-indexed operational reference profiles; a same-acquisition CBCT rule served as an imaging comparator. Results: The dataset contained 92,675 overlapping windows. On six held-out specimens (36 osteotomies; 18,496 windows), XGBoost achieved 93.0% accuracy (specimen-clustered 95% CI, 92.0-94.0%), 82.9% balanced accuracy, and 85.6% macro-F1. RF and SVM accuracies were 90.5% and 88.8%, respectively. The CBCT rule achieved 92.3% accuracy but lower balanced accuracy (80.1%) and transitional recall (51.1%). XGBoost transitional recall was 59.6%, increasing to 73.0% in a weighted sensitivity configuration at the cost of lower overall accuracy. Accuracy decreased from 94.1% away from class boundaries to 75.6% in boundary-adjacent windows. Conclusion: Force-torque features differentiated the three predefined reference-profile-defined drilling states under specimen-separated evaluation. XGBoost achieved the highest classification performance, with errors concentrated primarily in transitional and boundary-adjacent windows. Keywords: robot-assisted implant osteotomy; force-torque sensing; reference-profile classification; drilling-state classification; XGBoost; specimen-level validation .
authors: Jiaqiang Li; Yangdong Wu; Yao Wang; Min Shao

title: Force–Vision Multimodal Measurement of Model-Equivalent Elastic Parameters for Soft Tissue Modeling
abstract: In robotic manipulation, robot-assisted surgery, and other contact-rich interactions with deformable bodies, reliable prediction of contact force and deformation requires rapid determination of the effective mechanical parameters governing the soft-tissue model. However, these model-equivalent properties are difficult to obtain directly from physical interaction, particularly for human soft tissue with substantial variability in geometry and mechanical response. This work presents a force-vision multimodal framework for rapidly identifying effective elastic and contact-model parameters from measured force and deformation. The human breast is selected as a representative validation object because of its high compliance, pronounced geometric variability, and sensitivity of its deformation response to mechanical properties and contact conditions. A six-axis force/torque sensor and an eye-in-hand RGB-D camera provide time-synchronized measurements of three-dimensional contact force and surface-marker displacement. A finite-element contact model maps the probe pose and a parameter vector to the measured responses, while a multiobjective Bayesian optimization procedure identifies the parameter set under a limited simulation budget. Experiments using three breast-tissue-mimicking phantoms with different geometries and stiffnesses yield normalized force and displacement residuals of 4.93%-6.00% and 7.18%-12.33%, respectively, within 55 model evaluations. Force and displacement provide complementary constraints, and the Bayesian solver achieves residuals comparable to particle swarm optimization with a 5.5-fold reduction in the number of finite-element evaluations. Held-out indentation and controlled posture-change tests further support the predictive consistency of the identified model-equivalent parameters within the experimental protocol. The proposed framework provides an approach for rapid parameter identification of deformable-tissue contact models, with potential to support more consistent reproduction of contact force and deformation in soft-tissue simulation and future sim2real robotic manipulation with force-vision feedback.
authors: Le Zhang; Yi Liu; Ziyu Liang; Dapeng Yang

title: From Accuracy to Reliability: What Prevents Artificial Intelligence from Being Clinically Reliable for Periapical Lesion Detection? A Review
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly deep learning, has shown potential in detecting periapical radiolucencies on dental radiographs. However, accuracy on a retrospective research dataset does not guarantee clinical performance. This narrative review explores the discrepancy between algorithmic accuracy and real-world clinical reliability, including dataset representativeness, spectrum and selection bias, cropped-image evaluation, lesion size and anatomical complexity, reference-standard uncertainty, domain shift in imaging systems, external validation, explainability of AI, and the limited integration of radiographic AI with clinical information. Recent systematic reviews report high pooled diagnostic performance, but consistently cite substantial heterogeneity, risk of bias, limited prospective evidence, and insufficient external validation. The argument for this review is that the next phase of research should change the question from 'Can AI detect a periapical lesion?' to 'Can AI reliably detect an unexpected lesion in an unselected clinical image and improve the clinician's decision?' Clinical reliability should therefore be viewed as a multidimensional concept incorporating technical performance, generalizability, calibration, interpretability, workflow compatibility, and impact on clinician and patient outcomes. A staged framework of internal validation, external validation, prospective clinical validation, human-AI evaluation and post-deployment monitoring is proposed. AI should be regarded as an adjunctive second reader and decision-support tool rather than an autonomous diagnostic replacement.
authors: Priyanka Sharma

title: From Engraftment to Vision: Defining Evidence of Functional Success in Retinal Cell Replacement Therapy
abstract: Retinal graft survival and post-treatment visual improvement do not, alone or together, demonstrate functional cell replacement. Apparent benefit may reflect material transfer, trophic rescue, residual host function or procedural and measurement effects. This critical narrative review uses a structured PubMed search covering January 2020 to August 2026, supplemented by seminal studies, to assess retinal pigment epithelium (RPE), photoreceptor, retinal sheet or organoid, and retinal ganglion cell (RGC) transplantation. We separate mechanistic attainment, downstream outcomes and claim-specific causal confidence. Authentic RPE replacement requires donor epithelial function across the host interface, without new synapses. Photoreceptor replacement requires donor phototransduction and transmission to host retinal circuitry; composite grafts additionally require identification of the active donor components. RGC replacement requires both retinal afferent integration and functional reconnection with appropriate central targets. Selected photoreceptor studies demonstrate persuasive local physiological coupling, but durability, donor necessity and generalisability remain incompletely established. Human evidence principally supports feasibility, safety and graft-associated anatomy, rather than convincingly donor-mediated visual restoration. We propose a non-linear evidence framework in which outcomes cannot substitute for secure donor provenance, cell-specific function or host-graft coupling. Spatial concordance, durability, controls, disease-model relevance and experimental unit should qualify every claim.
authors: Georgios D. Panos; Theo Empeslidis; Eleftherios Chatzimichail; Lorenzo Motta; Z Gatzioufas; Winfried M. K. Amoaku

title: From Freehand Demonstrations to Autonomous Robotic Ultrasound: An Anatomy-Anchored Learning Framework
abstract: Ultrasound imaging is highly operator-dependent, motivating robotic systems that reproduce expert scanning skills consistently. These skills involve coordinated interpretation of anatomical landmarks, ultrasound images, and probe-tissue interactions that are difficult to encode in hand-designed control strategies. Imitation learning offers an alternative, but its observation and action representations should reflect the anatomically structured nature of scanning. We propose an anatomy-anchored imitation-learning framework that combines anatomy-guided probe placement with learned ultrasound navigation. The placement module identifies a task-specific anatomical starting point from external visual observations and establishes the initial probe pose as the reference frame for scanning. A flow-based policy then generates scanning motions from anchor-relative probe poses, ultrasound images, probe-mounted camera views, and contact forces, while a termination head predicts task completion. This avoids continuous reliance on third-person vision and reduces dependence on the robot-patient configuration. A handheld acquisition platform enables multimodal demonstrations to be collected during natural freehand scanning without a robot. On 16 unseen participants, task success reaches 96%, 94%, 88%, and 94% for kidney, gallbladder, and liver standard-plane acquisition and radial artery sweeping, respectively. Compared with a fine-tuned pi_0 model, success on the abdominal tasks improves by 10-42 percentage points, with lower time-to-target, peak contact force, and trajectory jerk. Ablations support the complementary roles of anatomical anchoring, egocentric vision, and force feedback. End-to-end trials with automatic placement achieve 90-100% success, and the policies transfer without retraining to a second robot with 83-100% success.

title: From Prompts To Masks: Assessing Gemini Image Models for Tooth Segmentation on Panoramic Radiographs
abstract: Introduction and aims Tooth-region segmentation on panoramic radiographs supports annotation, region-of-interest extraction, and dataset triage, but conventional approaches require task-specific training labels. Although vendor-hosted multimodal models can follow natural-language prompts, their pixel-level reliability in dental radiographs remains unclear. This study assessed the accuracy, false-positive behavior, and run-to-run stability of two Gemini Image models for prompt-based tooth-region masking. Methods Ninety-six panoramic radiographs from the Tufts Dental Database (32 permanent dentition, 32 mixed dentition, 32 edentulous) were standardized to 2880 × 1472 pixels. Each image was submitted five times to Gemini 3 Pro Image and Gemini 3.1 Flash Image using a fixed text-to-mask prompt. Permanent- and mixed-dentition outputs were evaluated using mean Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) and intersection over union (IoU); edentulous outputs were evaluated using specificity, false-positive (FP) area ratio, and no-mask rate. Bootstrap 95% confidence intervals and Holm-corrected paired permutation tests were used for inference. Results In the pooled permanent- and mixed-dentition group, both models achieved a mean DSC of 0.883; mean IoU was 0.794 and 0.795 for Gemini 3 Pro Image and Gemini 3.1 Flash Image, respectively. Permanent dentition favored Gemini 3 Pro Image numerically (DSC 0.905 vs 0.896), whereas mixed dentition favored Gemini 3.1 Flash Image (DSC 0.871 vs 0.861). For edentulous radiographs, specificity and FP area ratio were comparable between models, and the no-mask rate was numerically higher for Gemini 3 Pro Image (76.3% vs 63.8%). No comparison remained significant after Holm correction, and k-of-5 analysis revealed variable run-to-run stability. Conclusion Prompt-based tooth-region segmentation yielded clinically plausible outputs without task-specific training, but dentition-dependent performance, target-absent false positives, and limited reproducibility support expert-supervised rather than autonomous use. Clinical relevance Expert-reviewed annotation support, dataset triage, and human-in-the-loop preprocessing are more appropriate than stand-alone clinical segmentation.

title: From Repetition to Reform: Confronting Academic Redundancy in Dental Education
abstract: Introduction: Why This Conversation Matters NowModern dental education was built on a vision of continual improvement.Nearly over a century ago the great visionary William J. Gies said, What we want is a better class of better dentists, because the world is, I believe, suffering from a lack of good dental service more than from any bodily ailment of which we have any knowledge .This insightful vision has helped shape the foundations of modern dental education; the profession faces a different but related challenge: How to preserve educational rigor and institutional memory while ensuring that accumulated curricular and organizational structures remain responsive to contemporary learners and professional needs.Calls for transformation in dental education are not new.The American Dental Education Association (ADEA) Commission on Change and Innovation in Dental Education identified the need to reconsider traditional educational approaches and promote deliberate change in response to evolving societal, professional, and educational demands [ 1,2 ].The Commission's work also highlighted concerns about curricular complexity and educational environments that may be expensive and dissatisfying for learners [ 2 ].Yet curricular renewal remains challenging.New knowledge, technologies, expectations, and educational priorities are often added to existing structures, while fewer mechanisms exist for systematically determining what should be integrated, reduced, or retired.

title: From pain relief to mucosal grief: A comprehensive review of NSAID enteropathy.
abstract: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) are essential for their analgesic, anti-inflammatory and anti-pyretic properties. However, their extended use can lead to NSAID enteropathy, a frequently underdiagnosed condition of the small intestine. This pathology manifests as mucosal damage, ulcerations, strictures and increased intestinal permeability, potentially resulting in complications such as bleeding, protein loss and nutrient malabsorption. Modern diagnostic technologies, particularly capsule endoscopy, have revealed that small-bowel injury affects up to 70% of chronic NSAID users, although many patients remain asymptomatic. This comprehensive review explores the epidemiology, underlying mechanisms, clinical manifestations, diagnostic approaches and treatment strategies for NSAID enteropathy, while emphasizing the growing importance of increased clinical awareness and continued research into preventive and therapeutic interventions, especially as long-term NSAID use becomes more prevalent in our aging global population.
