title: From task-specific networks to foundation models in diabetes care: a critical review of opportunities, evaluation gaps, and safety frontiers
abstract: Artificial intelligence in diabetes care has historically relied on task-specific supervised learning, such as bespoke networks for retinopathy grading, kidney disease prediction, and glucose forecasting. The emergence of foundation models (FMs: large models pretrained on broad data, typically with self-supervision, and adapted to many downstream tasks) is displacing this paradigm across diabetes-relevant modalities: ophthalmic models such as RETFound, pretrained on 1.6 million retinal photographs, have been reported to outperform task-specific networks on retinopathy grading and systemic disease prediction, especially when labeled data are scarce; transformer-based time-series models are replacing long short-term memory (LSTM) pipelines for continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) forecasting; clinical large language models (LLMs) such as Med-PaLM and GPT-4 attain expert-level scores on medical question-answering benchmarks; and generative models supply synthetic CGM and electronic health record (EHR) data. This review provides a critical, modality-organized synthesis of this transition. We (i) formalize a three-era taxonomy: rule-based risk scores (era I), task-specific deep learning (era II, 2016–2020), and foundation models (era III, from 2021), and map the diabetes literature onto it; (ii) survey foundation-model architectures, pretraining objectives, and adaptation strategies across retinal imaging, CGM, longitudinal EHR, and multimodal data; (iii) expose an evaluation crisis: benchmark contamination of LLM medical evaluations, a near-universal absence in the literature we reviewed of external and prospective validation for retinal and CGM foundation models, miscalibration under dataset shift, and, to our knowledge and within the reviewed literature (January 2016–December 2025; negative findings are time-sensitive), the absence of any randomized evaluation of a foundation model in a diabetes workflow; and (iv) analyze safety risks: hallucinated insulin-dosing advice, automation bias, inherited algorithmic inequity, and privacy exposure during adaptation. We conclude that the decisive open problem is no longer representation learning but grounded, calibrated, causally informed deployment, requiring contamination-resistant evaluation, prospective trials, and hybrid architectures coupling foundation-model representations with treatment-effect estimation.
authors: M. Nanda Kishore; C. Navaneethan

title: From validation to public health impact: implementing equitable AI-enabled diabetic retinopathy screening
abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) remains a preventable cause of vision loss as diabetes prevalence rises worldwide. Artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled retinal screening has progressed from retrospective validation to prospective and real-world deployment, with recent reviews showing high diagnostic performance across fundus photography, smartphone-based systems, and autonomous platforms. Yet diagnostic accuracy alone does not ensure public health benefit. Population impact can be lost when eligible people are not reached, images are ungradable, results are delayed, referrals are incomplete, treatment capacity is insufficient, or disadvantaged groups face financial, geographic, or digital barriers. Unlike reviews centered mainly on diagnostic accuracy or economic performance, this Mini Review reframes AI-enabled DR screening as a population-health intervention spanning detection through completion of effective eye care. We synthesize evidence on diagnostic validity, implementation, economics, referral completion, care cascades, patient-centered outcomes, equity, and governance. We argue that effectiveness and cost-effectiveness are properties of the complete screening-to-treatment pathway, not the algorithm alone, and propose a four-domain framework encompassing technical validity, service integration, population impact, and equity and sustainability. Future research should prioritize comparative implementation studies and outcome sets that capture screening reach, gradability, referral completion, treatment initiation, time to treatment, avoidable vision loss, vision-related quality of life, acceptability, costs, and subgroup equity. The policy question is no longer whether AI can detect DR, but whether health systems can translate automated detection into equitable completion of effective eye care at scale.

title: Fundus torsion in strabismus: Measurement, clinical interpretation, and emerging imaging approaches.
abstract: Fundus torsion is an important but underused anatomical marker in strabismus evaluation, particularly for cyclovertical disorders. Unlike subjective cyclodeviation testing, fundus-based assessment provides an objective reference based on retinal landmarks, though it remains influenced by image acquisition, head position, ocular anatomy, and measurement conventions. We synthesize the anatomical basis of ocular and fundus torsion, contemporary qualitative and quantitative assessment methods, and disease-specific evidence across superior oblique palsy, pattern strabismus, pediatric and adult strabismus, and surgical follow-up. The review emphasizes 3 clinically important issues: the frequent dissociation between objective fundus torsion and subjective cyclodeviation, the need for method-specific interpretation using reproducibility and minimal-detectable-change data, and the importance of avoiding isolated treatment decisions based on anatomical torsion alone. Recent optical coherence tomography-based and artificial intelligence-assisted approaches may improve measurement consistency and scalability, but current evidence supports their use as adjunctive tools rather than autonomous decision systems. Fundus torsion should therefore be interpreted within a multimodal clinical framework that integrates motility findings, sensory status, age, chronicity, fixation behavior, and surgical history. Treatment options include observation and symptom relief in selected patients, inferior oblique weakening for associated overaction, and torsion-directed surgery for persistent symptomatic excyclotorsion; comparative evidence remains limited. Prospective comparative treatment studies are a clinical research priority. Standardized acquisition protocols, explicit reporting conventions, age- and population-specific normative data, externally validated automated methods, and prospective studies linking torsional change to symptoms and functional outcomes are needed to strengthen the clinical utility of fundus torsion assessment.

title: Generative Artificial Intelligence in Dentistry: Clinical Applications, Evidence, Limitations, Ethical Considerations, and a Framework for Responsible Implementation
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI), including large language models (LLMs) and multimodal foundation models, is increasingly being used in dentistry, dental education, and scientific research. Unlike conventional predictive AI, which is generally developed for defined classification or prediction tasks, GenAI can produce new text, images, summaries, and other outputs from user prompts. In dentistry, potential applications include patient communication, clinical documentation, education, literature synthesis, and selected forms of decision support. These applications are accompanied by important risks, including hallucinated information, bias, privacy breaches, fabricated references, and automation bias. This narrative review summarizes recent evidence on GenAI in dentistry, with emphasis on the distinction between assistive use and autonomous clinical decision-making. Recent systematic, scoping, and narrative reviews describe applications in dental education, oral and maxillofacial surgery, implant dentistry, endodontics, and other areas, but the available evidence remains heterogeneous and prospective clinical validation is limited. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) may improve evidence alignment by linking language models to curated external sources, although dental-specific evidence remains early. Based on the reviewed literature, responsible implementation should be task-specific and should include data minimization, verification of outputs, human accountability, documentation, and ongoing monitoring. A seven-stage framework is proposed: define the task, assess risk, protect data, verify output, retain human decision-making, document relevant AI use, and monitor performance. At present, GenAI is best regarded as an assistive technology that can support, but should not replace, professional dental judgment.

title: Genetic Algorithm-Based Weighted Ensemble of Deep CNN Models for Dental Disease Detection
abstract: Accurate categorization of dental imagery is crucial to facilitate early identification and efficient treatment strategizing in dental healthcare. This investigation aspires to establish a multiclass dental pathology classification framework employing a Genetic Algorithm (GA)-based weighted ensemble of deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architectures. The resources used in this scholarly inquiry comprise a publicly accessible dental image repository encompassing four categories: caries, calculus, discoloration, and hypodontia, sourced from diverse clinical and web-based sources. The proposed methodology implements transfer learning by fine-tuning three pre-trained CNN frameworks, specifically ResNet50V2, EfficientNetB4, and EfficientNetB5. Each foundational model is trained autonomously, and their predictive probabilities are amalgamated via a weighted ensemble approach. A Genetic Algorithm is utilized to autonomously ascertain the optimal ensemble weights by maximizing the macro F1-score, thereby ensuring equitable performance across all pathological categories. Experiments were executed utilizing varying training epochs to assess model convergence and generalizability. The experimental findings reveal that the GA-based ensemble attained optimal efficacy at a configuration with a maximum of 300 training epochs, with an accuracy of 98.71%, a precision of 98.62%, a recall of 97.66%, and an F1-score of 98.12. A minor reduction in performance at elevated epochs indicates the emergence of overfitting. Compared with individual CNN models and non-optimized ensemble methods, the proposed framework exhibits enhanced robustness and more consistent class-wise classification. These results underscore the efficacy of metaheuristic optimization in advancing ensemble deep learning for dental disease classification. Prospective research should concentrate on validation utilizing larger multicenter clinical datasets, exploration of alternative optimization algorithms, and real-time clinical implementation.

title: GeoCM-Pose: geometry-aware monocular dental 2D/3D registration benchmarked against reference-assisted methods
abstract: Abstract Objective. To develop GeoCM-Pose, a geometry-aware monocular dental 2D/3D registration method that predicts metric model-to-camera 6DoF pose from one image under weak texture, repetitive anatomy and partial visibility. Approach. GeoCM-Pose comprises cross-modal adaptation (CMA) and geometry-aware pose regression (GAPR). CMA uses fixed-Gaussian frequency separation and a high-frequency structure-preservation module with multi-scale edge extraction, spatial–channel gating and cross-resolution refinement. GAPR uses a ResNet-50/U-Net to predict dense object-coordinate maps; hierarchical geometric feature aggregation and geometry-aware channel refinement feed decoupled unit-quaternion and translation heads. Joint 20-point pose-matching and dense-coordinate losses train the network. The study comprised 30 in vitro training cases, five in vivo validation cases, five in vivo internal-test cases, 10 fully held-out Teeth3DS+ dental surface models and a 200-frame benchmark generated from a single three-dimensional dental model. Main Results. GAPR/V0 generated pose estimates for all 200 query frames, with median reprojection, rotation and translation-vector errors of 2.156 px, 1.252° and 0.653 mm, respectively, and a <5 px pass rate of 91.5% across all attempts. It used no inference-time reference-image bank. At R01, scale-invariant feature transform and ORB generated 85/200 and 89/200 valid estimates, with <5 px all-attempt pass rates of 40.5% and 40.0%; at R20, each generated 197/200 valid estimates, with pass rates of 98.0% and 95.5%. Thus, conventional performance increased with the available reference bank, whereas GAPR/V0 provided complete query coverage from a single image without inference-time reference images. Median GAPR/V0 inference latency, including image I/O, was 11.459 ms. Significance. GeoCM-Pose integrates CMA, dense object-coordinate supervision and metric pose regression for monocular dental 2D/3D registration. Further case-level evaluation using intraoral endoscopic images acquired from independent patient cases and additional image domains, together with robot-integrated experiments, is required to assess generalisation and system-level performance.
authors: Z. Frank Qiu; Jingang Jiang; Jie Pan; Xinrui Cheng; Qunsong Qiu; Jiawei Zhang; Jingchao Wang; Guang Yu

title: Giant Brunner's gland hamartoma: the surgical management of complex cases.
abstract: Brunner's gland hamartoma (BGH) is a rare, benign tumour composed of mucin-secreting glands within the duodenal submucosa. Lesions typically range from 0.5 to 1.0cm and are usually managed endoscopically, with larger tumours occurring infrequently. This case involves a 74-year-old woman presenting with syncope. Diagnostic investigations revealed a massive BGH with a 10cm pedicle, accompanied by significant iron deficiency anaemia and intussusception. Although there are no formal, universally established guidelines, literature favours endoscopic removal because of reduced bleeding, a shorter hospital stay and lower cost. However, open surgical resection proved more appropriate owing to the lesion's size and complexity. This case highlights the challenges of managing giant BGHs and supports open surgical intervention when standard methods are unsuccessful.
authors: P Sen; T Broquetas; M Pera
venue: Annals of the Royal College of Surgeons of England

title: Global research trends in interventional bronchoscopy: a bibliometric analysis of publications from 2005 to 2025
abstract: Abstract Background The field of interventional bronchoscopy (IB) has experienced rapid advancements over the past two decades, evolving from a predominantly diagnostic modality into a highly technological specialty encompassing use of endobronchial ultrasound (EBUS), electromagnetic navigation bronchoscopy (ENB), robotic-assisted bronchoscopy (RAB), transbronchial cryobiopsy, airway stenting, and image-guided interventions. Although there have been emerging advancements in the practice of IB, no global research studies have comprehensively evaluated trends in the field. Objective To analyze the global scientific output, collaboration patterns, influential contributors, and thematic evolution of IB research from 2005 to 2025. Methods The bibliometric analysis was performed using Scopus database. Studies related to IB published from January 2005 to December 2025 were identified using predefined search strategy. Records were identified using the predefined search terms. The dataset was then cleaned by removing similar but non-relevant terms, and eligibility was restricted to research articles and conference papers, with review articles, book chapters, and other document types excluded. No language restriction was applied. Data were analyzed using the Bibliometrix and Biblioshiny packages in R. Results A total of 18,019 records were identified, of which 652 eligible publications were included, comprising 609 original research articles and 43 conference papers, with no language restriction. Publication output increased markedly after 2020. Zaroulidis P was the most productive author, while the United States, China, Japan, Germany, and the United Kingdom were among the leading contributing countries, with Nagoya University as the most productive institution. Highly cited studies mainly focused on airway stents and tracheal prostheses, bronchoscopic lung volume reduction, diagnostic and image-guided bronchoscopy, and procedural sedation and safety. More recent highly cited studies increasingly addressed robotic, computational, and artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted bronchoscopy. Randomized and comparative clinical trials are relatively limited but included EBUS-TBNA and ENB for diagnostic strategies, bronchoscopic lung volume reduction, airway stenting, hybrid EBUS, radial EBUS, and AI-assisted bronchoscopy. Research themes progressively shifted from diagnostic and imaging applications toward therapeutic, navigational, robotic, bioengineering, and AI-enabled approaches. Conclusions In conclusion, IB research has transitioned from predominantly diagnostic and imaging-based techniques (EBUS-TBNA and navigational bronchoscopy), toward therapeutic, robotic, image-guided, bioengineering, and AI-assisted interventions. Emerging bioengineering, and AI-assisted technologies hold promise for IB but require clinical validation.
authors: Tawseef Ahmad; Tauqeer Ahmad; Fazal Mustaan; Jamil Ur Rahman; Muhammad Esa

title: Grounded ophthalmic AI beyond the electronic health record trap: a critical narrative review
abstract: Electronic health records (EHRs) show that health information technology can digitise clinical work while increasing documentation burden, workflow rigidity and professional burnout. Artificial intelligence (AI) may enter a deeper layer of medicine than the EHR because it can draft summaries, interpret images, recommend follow-up and influence decisions. This critical narrative review uses ophthalmic vision-language models as a concrete case study. Diabetic retinopathy screening AI and lesion-level deep learning have achieved important successes in defined tasks, but clinical interpretation is not classification. A sentence such as ‘hard exudates have increased in the macula’ requires localisation of the fovea and macula, lesion segmentation, longitudinal registration, change quantification and faithful language generation. We argue that the unresolved informatics challenge is grounded in clinical interpretation: the auditable translation of images into finding-location-change triples that remain inspectable by clinicians. The article proposes a three-layer architecture: globally standardised objective observation, explicit local policy and workflow adaptation and clinician-authored AI operations governed by safety gates. Customisation should not be monetised as bespoke vendor work; it should be a safety function built into procurement, audit and lifecycle regulation. The three-layer architecture is a conceptual governance framework derived from published evidence rather than a prospectively validated implementation, and we specify the observable failure modes and metrics that would refute it. Ophthalmology illustrates the broader design principle for medical AI: automation should make evidence more visible, not convert care into another opaque information-processing layer.

title: Harnessing gastrointestinal motility for advancing diagnostics and therapeutics
abstract: Gastrointestinal (GI) motility plays a fundamental role in digestion, metabolism, immunity, and drug absorption. Yet, many current diagnostic and therapeutic devices designed for the GI tract overlook its dynamic mechanics, compromising their effectiveness and reliability. In this review, we provide a comprehensive overview of GI motility metrics, current devices and their limitations, and how a deeper understanding of motility can improve device design. We also highlight sex-specific differences in GI motility and their implications for clinical translation. We offer a perspective for a new approach that embeds standardized motility metrics into device development, thus improving diagnostic accuracy and personalizing therapies. By emphasizing physiology-guided design principles, future ingestible devices could adapt in real time to individual motility patterns, thereby transforming patient care.
authors: Shonit Nair Sharma; Akash A Pai; Noah J. Selda; Xiangang Huang; Nimrat Kaur; Wei Tao; Jeffrey M. Karp; Yuhan Lee

title: Herbal and Natural Products for NSAID-Induced Small Intestinal Injury: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
abstract: Objectives: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), including aspirin, are widely used medications that frequently cause small intestinal injury (enteropathy). Conventional proton pump inhibitors do not prevent this injury and may exacerbate it through dysbiosis. Herbal medicines and natural products offer potential therapeutic benefits, but synthesized clinical evidence remains limited. Thus, this study will systematically evaluate the efficacy and safety of herbal medicines and natural products for preventing NSAID-induced small intestinal injury. Methods: MEDLINE, Embase, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and the China National Knowledge Infrastructure will be searched to identify articles published since inception, without restrictions on publication date or language. Randomized controlled trials involving adults aged ≥ 18 years receiving NSAIDs will be included. Two reviewers will independently perform study selection, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment using the RoB 2 tool. If appropriate, a meta-analysis will be conducted. The primary outcome will be mucosal injury, objectively assessed using video capsule endoscopy or measures of intestinal permeability. Secondary outcomes will include symptoms and adverse events. Results: This study will synthesize the current clinical evidence on natural interventions for NSAID-induced enteropathy. Conclusion: The findings will inform the management of small intestinal injury and guide future research.
authors: Ji Hye Hwang; You-Kyung Choi

title: HiRNet: A Hierarchical-Refinement-Guided Hybrid Retinal Vessel Segmentation Network for Smartphone-Based Fundus Images
abstract: Smartphone-based fundus photography provides a low-cost and convenient approach to retinal screening and follow-up examinations. As a fundamental step in fundus image analysis, retinal vessel segmentation plays an important role in the diagnosis and monitoring of retinal diseases. However, existing methods often exhibit limited performance on smartphone-based fundus images. This limitation mainly arises from the significantly lower image quality that affects the clarity and detail of the retinal vessels, making accurate segmentation more difficult. To address these challenges, we propose a hierarchical-refinement-guided hybrid network (HiRNet), which incorporates a hybrid CNN-Transformer feature extractor to jointly model local vascular structures and global contextual information. Specifically, consecutive asymmetric dilated convolutions capture multi-scale local features, while multi-path dilated attention enhances contextual representations across different receptive fields. In addition, a hierarchical context information transmission module is introduced to progressively integrate features from different resolutions during multistage upsampling, thereby improving vessel continuity and boundary delineation. Experiments on RVD, DRIVE, and CHASE_DB1 demonstrate the effectiveness of HiRNet. On the smartphone-based RVD dataset, HiRNet obtains the highest mean sensitivity (58.36%), specificity (97.81%), accuracy (95.83%), F1-score (58.39%), and AUC (95.16%). The improvements in sensitivity, accuracy, F1, and AUC over the strongest competing methods are statistically significant. HiRNet also obtains sensitivity values of 82.73% and 82.13%, accuracy values of 95.59% and 95.98%, F1-scores of 82.76% and 80.37%, and AUC values of 98.83% and 97.90% on DRIVE and CHASE_DB1, respectively. These results indicate that HiRNet provides a relative improvement on the challenging domain of smartphone-based fundus images while maintaining strong performance on conventional fundus datasets.
authors: Yuqing Yin; Liang Niu; Suyan Li; Yifan Mu; Xiao Xu; Yan Wang

title: High Accuracy Fingerprint Recognition on FPGA Using a Dual Path Lightweight CNN
abstract: Abstract This paper addresses the increasing demand for reliable identity verification in various applications and highlights the importance of biometric features such as fingerprints due to the limitations and potential distrust of identification cards. Given the strong performance of neural network-based methods, this work focuses on convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for fingerprint image classification and identification, with an emphasis on efficient hardware implementation on field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs). A lightweight CNN architecture is proposed that achieves higher accuracy compared to prior approaches while operating directly on raw images without pre-processing. The proposed model is evaluated under two data augmentation scenarios, achieving accuracies of 70.3% and 63.1%, respectively, outperforming previous studies. The network response time per sample is 77.9 ms on GPU and requires approximately 483 KB of memory for parameter storage. The architecture is implemented on a Xilinx Virtex-7 FPGA using VHDL, utilizing 70% of available resources. The FPGA implementation consumes 28.72 W of power and operates at a maximum frequency of 108.6 MHz.
authors: Abdolah Amirany; Belal Jahannia; HAMED Dalir

title: High-Precision RCM Motion for Ophthalmic Robotics via Hierarchical QP Control and Authority-Guided Recovery Planning
abstract: General-purpose manipulators can position ophthalmic instruments under a software Remote Centre of Motion (RCM). However, at some reachable configurations that are nonsingular for the tip task alone, the RCM and tip-tracking objectives conflict and the servo oscillates. We formalise this failure as a constraint-induced task singularity: the RCM-projected tip Jacobian loses rank while the unprojected tip Jacobian stays well conditioned. Thus, the effective tip authority collapses although the target remains reachable. We present a high-precision RCM servo architecture with built-in singularity recovery: for each commanded target, an authority-guided planner selects a well-conditioned arm configuration that reaches it and plans an RCM-consistent route, executed by a fixed hierarchical-QP controller. On a 200-scenario kinematic benchmark, the complete nominal-and-recovery protocol reaches 128/128 near-singular targets and 71/72 near-joint-limit targets (100% and 99%, respectively), with the software-RCM residual below 0.142 mm. On a physical 6-DOF arm it executes across four RCM entry points, with a worst-case kinematically reconstructed RCM residual of 178 μm and a median tip-regulation error of 32μm, within the 200μm control requirement adopted for the ophthalmic task.
authors: Huanyu Tian; Adriana Namour; Lingyun Zeng; Zicong Wu; Sebastien Ourselin A; Lyndon da Cruz; Christos Bergeles

title: How does hard magnetic soft matter deform?
abstract: Abstract Hard Magnetic Soft Materials, i.e., elastomers seeded with hard magnetic particles, convert magnetic energy into complex motion and have become central to the design of untethered soft robots, biomedical devices, and, in general, for enabling fast, wireless actuation. Their behavior depends critically on how the surrounding soft matrix deforms and transmits torque to each magnetized inclusion, yet there is no consensus on the correct mapping between macroscopic strain and microscopic motion. Competing models predict conflicting particle rotations and magnetic responses under identical loads. Here, we construct counterexamples that show the key shortcomings in these models, and then establish a first-principles framework that leads to an optimal deformation mapping. The resulting closed-form law unifies conflicting models and shows that they are, in fact, simply different limits of our general approach. Our work permits the rational design of magnetically actuated soft devices and a unified view of deformation in magnetic soft matter, and broadly, in similar architectured materials.
authors: Daniel Katusele; Carmel Majidi; Liping Liu; Pradeep Sharma; Kaushik Dayal

title: Human-Centered Robotics for Surgery
abstract: Surgical ergonomics is influenced by many aspects associated with posture, vision, hand motion, and haptic feedback. Specific ergonomics aspects can induce long-term effects in the surgeon directly affecting the performance. One of the major disadvantages of Minimally Invasive Surgery (MIS) remains the non-ergonomic design of the entire surgical environment. This condition results in a significant reduction in the quality of interventions and discomfort for the medical operator. Modern teleoperated surgical robots offer an optimized console, in which the surgeon can operate in a seated position with specific arm support and a 3D view of the operating site. The da Vinci surgical console offers ergonomic improvements over standard endoscopic surgery. Modern robotic platforms stand beyond the da Vinci System, offering more advanced ergonomic solutions in terms of haptic feedback and visual perception. Due to the introduction of more advanced technology, surgery has changed, resulting in increased system complexity at the technical, human and organizational levels, which may lead to higher variability of patient outcomes due to new error pathways. Adopting a proactive approach enables the prior identification of critical factors and the design of safer socio-technical systems, thanks to a multi-level perspective. This chapter addresses the fundamental elements of surgical ergonomics, considering the factors that affect performance and healthiness during traditional procedures, with specific reference to MIS and microsurgery. This baseline is then compared to the use of surgical robots by evaluating the effect of design decisions on operator ergonomics. In addition, studies propose proactive methodologies that assess the personal and organizational factors of surgical performance in this complex socio-technical system.
authors: Rocco Moccia; Raffaella Mancino; Emanuele Ruffaldi; Massimiliano Simi; Rossella Onofrio; Fanny Ficuciello

title: Humanoids for Robot-Assisted Surgery: Bimanual Base Placement and Tool-Mount Optimization via Capability Maps
abstract: Rapid advances in humanoid robotics have motivated growing interest in the application of humanoids for healthcare and clinical tasks. However, it remains unclear how close contemporary humanoids are to meeting the kinematic demands of robot-assisted laparoscopic surgery. In this work, we address the question of optimal robot positioning through a quantitative analysis of workspace and robot setup configurations. We present a capability-map-based robot setup framework that optimizes humanoid base placement and tool mounting orientation to maximize bimanual humanoid reachability while accounting for tool-tip kinematics and remote-center-of-motion (RCM) constraints. We evaluate three humanoid platforms spanning different body dimensions and kinematic redundancy on workspace reachability for three representative general surgery procedures: cholecystectomy, inguinal hernia repair, and sleeve gastrectomy. The proposed joint optimization of base placement and tool mounting consistently outperforms base-only optimization and heuristic baselines. For cholecystectomy and inguinal hernia repair, which are characterized by relatively small and minimally overlapping workspaces, humanoid reachability approached 90%. For the larger, overlapping multi-port arm workspace of sleeve gastrectomy, humanoids yield substantially lower coverage. These results quantify the near-term promise of humanoids for selected laparoscopic procedures and clarify key limitations that must be addressed for broader deployment.
authors: Peihan Zhang; Zekai Liang; Florian Richter; Nikita S. Thareja; Ryan C. Broderick; Shanglei Liu; Michael C. Yip

title: Hybrid deep feature fusion framework with maximum entropy based selection for accurate diabetic foot ulcer diagnosis from enhanced and segmented medical images
abstract: Abstract Diabetic foot ulcers (DFU) pose significant risks, including delayed wound healing, infection, and, in severe cases, amputation. Early diagnosis is critical to mitigate these risks and enhance patient outcomes. Manual assessment may be affected by inter-observer variability and workflow delays, which motivates the investigation of AI-assisted methods for DFU image classification. In this study, several hybrid artificial neural network (ANN) strategies were developed incorporating features from various convolutional neural network (CNN) models for diabetic ulcer image diagnosis. The use of feature selection algorithms, specifically principal component analysis (PCA) and maximum entropy score based selection (MESbS), enhanced the discriminatory power of the models. Image quality was improved by using fused filters - average and Laplacian - to enhance the images and highlight the features of the diabetic ulcer and highlight the boundaries of the lesion. The geometric active contour (GAC) algorithm facilitated isolation of damaged areas from healthy areas. AlexNet, MobileNetV2 and VGG16 models processed these regions and extracted deep feature maps. These maps are later combined to create global feature vectors, namely, AlexNet-MobileNetV2, MobileNetV2-VGG16, AlexNet-VGG16, and AlexNet-MobileNetV2-VGG16. The fusion of features from multiple CNN models gives rise to high-dimensional vectors, prompting the application of PCA and MESbS for feature selection. The proposed hybrid strategies demonstrated strong diagnostic performance on the evaluated dataset. Among the evaluated configurations, the AlexNet-MobileNetV2-VGG16-ANN model with MESbS achieved the highest performance, reaching an AUC of 99%, sensitivity of 99.7%, accuracy of 99.5%, precision of 99.5%, and specificity of 99.75%. These findings suggest that combining complementary CNN feature representations with feature selection may improve DFU classification under the evaluated experimental conditions.
authors: Elham Ali; Ebrahim Mohammed Senan; Narmine El Hakim; M. Attique Khan; Ibrahim Abdulrab Ahmed; Omaia Mohammed Al-Omari; Suliman Mohamed Fati

title: Image-enhanced autonomous navigation in intestinal robotics: a threshold-triggered approach combining dark-area localization and morphological contour guidance short title: enhancing visibility and navigation precision in confined spaces.
abstract: Robotic endoscopy offers a potential route to autonomous gastrointestinal navigation. However, autonomous intestinal navigation is hindered by non-rigid lumen deformation and visual degradation from specular reflections, which compromise accurate perception and stable control. We propose a threshold-triggered, vision-driven framework incorporating Navier-Stokes-based highlight suppression. Algorithmically, the system is governed by a threshold-triggered mechanism that acts as a conditional perception gate, dynamically alternating between a lightweight 'dark-area guidance' algorithm for approximately centered navigation and a more detailed 'contour-based guidance' pipeline for corrective steering. The switching policy avoids executing highlight suppression and morphological contour processing in every frame. In phantom-based trials, the system achieved an average speed of 3.10 cm s<sup>-1</sup>on the triangular path. Highlight suppression increased the proportion of frames with normalized center error below 0.1 from 65% to 71%, below 0.2 from 95% to 97%, and below 0.3 from 98% to 100%. The adaptive mechanism decreased runtime by approximately 2% compared to continuous contour processing. Although this absolute reduction was modest, it recovered approximately 89% of the runtime difference between the contour-only and dark-area-only baselines. These phantom-based results support conditional perception allocation while keeping average processing time close to that of lightweight navigation.
authors: Wang S, Yuan J, Deng H, Deng H, Yue X, Zhang T, Chen S, Chen H.

title: Imaging biological tissue at extended depth using swept-source visible-light OCT
abstract: Abstract We present a swept-source visible-light optical coherence tomography (SS-vis-OCT) system with twice the imaging depth of prior SS-vis-OCT and improved sensitivity for imaging biological samples, achieving shot-noise-limited operation. Because second-harmonic generation is limited by the booster optical amplifier’s output power, the visible-light SS power is capped at 450 µW. Increasing it further would require a more powerful, but costlier, amplifier. Instead, we reduce the receiver noise floor by selecting a balanced detector with NEP approaching the thermal (Johnson–Nyquist) limit. Real-time numerical k-linearization increases the effective number of linear-in-wavenumber samples per sweep, further improving SNR and extending the imaging range. Together, these improvements yield a sensitivity of 89 dB and an imaging depth of 9 mm in air or 6.5 mm in tissue, enabling full anterior-segment imaging of ex vivo porcine eyes.
authors: Weijia Fan; Roman V. Kuranov; Menglin Shi; Fengyuanshan Xu; Junfang Zhang; Hao F. Zhang

title: Impact of AI‐Assisted Endoscopy on Secondary Review and Referral Decisions in Gastric Cancer Screening: A Multicenter Real‐World Study
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted endoscopy may support gastric cancer screening, but its impact on structured secondary human review remains unclear. We evaluated secondary review modifications and referral decisions before and after AI implementation. METHODS: This retrospective multicenter study included 5013 screening esophagogastroduodenoscopy examinations performed before (n = 2021) and after (n = 2992) AI implementation. The primary outcome was secondary review modifications. Secondary outcomes included referral for further diagnostic evaluation. Multivariable logistic regression analyses adjusted for age, sex, Helicobacter pylori eradication status, prior-year endoscopy, and endoscopist experience were performed. Interaction analyses according to endoscopist experience and inverse probability of treatment weighting analyses were conducted. No external reference standard was available to verify secondary-review modifications or referral decisions. RESULTS: Secondary review modifications increased from 1.2% in the pre-AI period to 3.7% in the AI period (p < 0.01). A significant interaction was observed between AI implementation and endoscopist experience (p for interaction < 0.01), with increased modifications primarily among nonexpert endoscopists. Cancer-related modifications remained uncommon but increased after AI implementation (0.6% vs. 0.2%, p = 0.04). Referral rates decreased from 4.9% to 2.8% (p < 0.01), and AI implementation was independently associated with lower odds of referral (adjusted OR = 0.53; 95% confidence interval = 0.36-0.77). CONCLUSIONS: AI-assisted endoscopy was associated with lower referral rates; however, secondary review modifications persisted after AI implementation, particularly among nonexpert endoscopists. These findings describe workflow changes and do not establish the clinical validity of the modifications or the appropriateness of referral decisions.
authors: Sachiyo Onishi; Seiji Adachi; Masahito Shimizu

title: Impact of Data Augmentation on Confidence Calibration in Melanoma Classification
abstract: Accurately quantifying the predictive uncertainty or improving model calibration plays an important role in medical image classification, in particular in melanoma diagnosis, where accurate uncertainty quantification can have significant implications for patient care. One of the methods for calibration improvement is data augmentation. In addition, data augmentation as a method for synthetically increasing the size of the dataset has been proven to improve the performance of models trained on imbalanced datasets. However, the impact of data augmentation, as a transformation of a part of the original data, on calibration of models trained on imbalanced datasets, in particular in melanoma classification is under-explored. We train neural networks on SIIM-ISIC 2020 melanoma classification dataset under two conditions: with and without data augmentation, and compare the differences in AUC and expected calibration error (ECE) in both scenarios. Our results shows improvements in uncertainty calibration using different augmentation methods.
authors: Morgan May; Simon J. Caton; Pierpaolo Dondio

title: Implementing AI-supported Screening for Retinopathy of Prematurity in Low-resource setting on a Relatively Small Set of Data: A Retrospective Cohort Study
abstract: Background: Context-adapted screening programs supported by AI-enabled teleretinopathy of prematurity (ROP) systems are essential to improve access, efficiency, and early diagnosis in underserved settings, particularly for often overlooked diseases such as ROP. This study aims to evaluate the diagnostic performance of an AI-based model for detecting and classifying ROP using wide-field retinal images and assess its relevance for neonatal screening systems in limited and middle-income countries (LMIC). Methods: This retrospective cohort study analyzed 5531 RetCam II images from 950 preemies (2018–2023) at Eye World Hospital, Giza, Egypt. Images were graded using international classification of ROP (ICROP) 3rd edition by a trainee and confirmed by a vitreoretinal consultant. A CNN-based model was developed to classify ROP stage, zone, and severity after augmentation up to 8500 images. Performance was assessed using standard metrics. Results: A total of 5531 RetCam II images from 950 preemies were analyzed. The AI model demonstrated good performance in detecting advanced ROP, particularly treatment-requiring stages (stages 4 and 5 and type 1 ROP), with high precision and recall. Overall classification accuracy was 66%. Performance was lower in early-stage disease and in differentiating closely related subtypes, particularly aggressive type ROP (A-ROP) and early stages. Conclusion: The CNN model based on 5531 RetCam II images, augmented up to 8500 images, shows good performance in detecting advanced ROP but limited sensitivity for early stages. Constraints include small, imbalanced data and reduced generalization. The system is intended for triage and decision support in tele-ROP screening, not autonomous diagnosis. Future improvements require larger multicenter datasets, better class balance, and advanced architectures with transfer learning to enhance early detection accuracy and clinical reliability.

title: Improved diagnostic model for gastrointestinal disorders through novel masking and semantic segmentation
abstract: The integration of advanced computing techniques, such as computational intelligence, in disease classification and prediction through medical imaging has become a prominent practice within the field of computer vision. A critical aspect of this process is precise image segmentation, which helps identify and isolate relevant areas in medical images, thereby streamlining the analysis and enhancing the accuracy of predictions. Among various segmentation methods, semantic segmentation, which assigns class labels to each pixel, has proven particularly effective. In this study, we introduce the U+EfficientB0 Net model, specifically designed to segment gastro-intestinal images, including dyed-lifted polyps, polyps, and ulcerative colitis. The proposed work is different from traditional EffeicientNetB0 encoder as it utilizes Decoder-guided Adaptive Skip Refinement (DASR) module for feature refinement before combining the features obtained from encoder with the features obtained through decoder. Utilizing advanced computing techniques like computational intelligence for disease classification and prediction through medical imaging is a prominent practice in computer vision. Precise image segmentation is crucial as it identifies relevant areas, streamlining analysis, and bolstering prediction accuracy. Semantic segmentation, assigning class labels to each pixel, proves especially effective. This study introduces the (U+EfficientB0) Net model specialized in segmenting gastro-intestinal images, notably dyed-lifted-polyps, polyps and ulcerative colitis leveraging the Kvasir-Seg dataset for polyps and while corresponding masks for dyed-lifted polyps and ulcerative colitis are generated using pixel-based annotation approach. Trained on a thousand images supervised by medical experts, proposed model achieved remarkable accuracy (92.89%) and dice coefficient (80%). Additionally, the study presents a classification approach using DenseNet-121 that uses the predicted segmented images as input and its performance is compared with similar model’s using non-segmented image and achieved better results (Accuracy 99.63) over segmented images in earlier epochs.

title: Information-based Unified Design Framework for NMR Magnetic Tracking System
abstract: Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) magnetic tracking offers a promising alternative to magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based localization for medical robotic guidance. However, scalar field measurements and field-aligned marker moments constrain position and orientation tracking, requiring careful configuration design. We present a unified information-based framework that uses local covariance analysis to evaluate receiver geometry, marker separation, and external source configuration in on/off-board NMR tracking. Numerical evaluation shows that planar-array precision depends jointly on receiver count and geometry, with triangular lattice arrays achieving the lowest best-case position uncertainty among the evaluated layouts for 9--20 receivers. Two spatially separated, field-aligned markers enable device-axis tracking, with predicted angular uncertainty below $2^\circ$ at the evaluated workspace center for suitable marker separations. We further establish point-dipole source--receiver duality, unifying the analysis of on/off-board NMR tracking. These

title: Integrating Local and Global Feature Learning for Retinal Disease Detection: An EfficientNetB3-ViT Hybrid Model
abstract: Undiagnosed ocular conditions in initial phases can progressively impair vision, potentially leading to critical visual dysfunctions. Fundus imaging has enabled the identification of several retinal disorders, notably diabetic retinopathy, glaucoma, and age-related macular degeneration. However, manual evaluation of these images is both time-consuming and dependent on expert judgment. In this context, artificial intelligence-based automatic diagnosis systems have become an important need in the field of medical image analysis. In this study, deep learning-based models were compared for multi-class eye disease detection from fundus images, and a unique hybrid model was proposed. In this study, current deep learning architectures, including EfficientNetB3, DenseNet-121, ResNet-50, MobileNetV2, and ViT, were employed. All models were independently trained and tested, and their effectiveness was evaluated using commonly employed classification metrics. Additionally, a hybrid model based on EfficientNetB3 and ViT was designed, combining the strengths of Transformer and CNN architectures. All models were subjected to hyperparameter optimization using the GridSearch method, allowing for a fair comparison. The results obtained showed that the hybrid model successfully learned both local and global features in fundus images and exhibited higher performance compared to other models. In this context, the developed system has the potential to be integrated into future clinical decision-support systems.
authors: Onur Ceylan; Anıl Utku

title: Integrating Machine Learning, Deep Learning and Robotics for Intelligent Information Management and Decision Support
abstract: Machine Learning, Deep Learning, and Robotics are revolutionizing the landscape of intelligent information management and decision support, connecting data processing, predictive analysis, and autonomous action. This review discusses the conceptual background, technological architectures, and application areas of integrated intelligent systems. It brings together the latest advances in machine learning, deep learning, robotic perception, autonomous control, reinforcement learning, digital twins, edge AI, federated learning and human-in-the-loop decision support. The review also compares the machine learning, deep learning, robotics, and integrated approaches in terms of accuracy, scalability, adaptability, computational efficiency, explainability, and real-time decision making. These technologies are increasingly becoming relevant in the healthcare sector, in manufacturing, in supply chains, in the finance sector, in cybersecurity, in smart cities, in agriculture, and in environmental monitoring. While significant strides have been made, there are still numerous challenges to address, such as data quality, privacy, security, interoperability, computational complexity, transparency, and trust. Multimodal intelligence, foundation models, Distributed learning, and Self-learning robotics are expected to become increasingly common in future intelligent systems. In summary, learning, reasoning, and robotic execution, when integrated, provide a strong basis for trustworthy, adaptive, explainable and human-centric decision support in real-world complex environments and retain the effectiveness of human involvement in the decision process and the responsibility of system governance.
authors: B. Nagarajan; Dr. Vipulkumar Kishorbhai Patel; Dr. Gurunadham R; Dr.G. Naga Chandrika; Dr Bansari Thakkar; Ei Thandar Soe

title: Intelligent System for Celiac Disease Detection Based on Deep Learning
abstract: Abstract In this study authors explore the application of deep learning techniques for the early detection of celiac disease through the analysis of medical imaging and clinical data. We used the convolutional neural networks (CNNs). The proposed model exhibits promising accuracy in identifying patterns indicative of celiac disease from diverse images of a big database. The integration of deep learning in celiac disease diagnosis holds the potential for enhancing early intervention and improving patient outcomes, marking a significant advancement in medical diagnostics. The proposed approach elucidates the intricacies of celiac disease and implements a robust Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model for accurate image classification. Achieving an average accuracy of 96%, this method promises enhanced diagnosis and management, paving the way for personalized healthcare interventions with significant improvements in patient outcomes and quality of life.
authors: Souhir Sghaier; Nasser Alsharif

title: Internal Validation of a YOLOv8 Model for Classifying Temporomandibular Joint Disc Displacement With Versus Without Reduction on Open‐Mouth Proton‐Density‐Weighted MRI
abstract: BACKGROUND: The temporomandibular joint (TMJ) disc plays an important role in maintaining normal joint function. However, disc displacement is a common condition that can lead to pain, restricted jaw movement and chronic TMJ dysfunction. OBJECTIVE: To develop and evaluate a deep learning model capable of autonomously localizing the TMJ region from magnetic resonance (MR) images during mouth opening using the You Only Look Once (YOLO) v8 framework, and to discriminate between TMJ disc displacement with reduction (DDwR) and disc displacement without reduction (DDwoR). METHODS: This study included 237 patients (48 males, 189 females; age range, 19-83 [mean, 44.73 ± 18.3] years) who underwent MRI examination at our hospital for suspected TMJ disorders and were diagnosed with disc displacement based on imaging findings. After exclusion, 439 proton density-weighted MR images during mouth opening were preprocessed and divided on a patient basis into training (280 images), validation (71 images) and test (88 images) datasets. The TMJ region was manually annotated using LabelImg, including the condyles, articular disc and articular tubercle. The YOLOv8 deep learning model was trained for 200 epochs to localize the TMJ region and classify DDwR or DDwoR. RESULTS: The YOLOv8 model achieved promising results for the detection and classification of TMJ disc displacements. The performance metrics were a precision, recall and F1 score of 0.983, 0.988 and 0.987, respectively, indicating a high accuracy in detecting and identifying disc displacement patterns. CONCLUSION: The YOLOv8 deep learning model demonstrated promising performance in automatically localizing and classifying TMJ disc displacement from MR images.
authors: Kotaro Ito; Hirotaka Muraoka; Satoshi Tokunaga; Kohei Otsuka; Tomohiro Komatsu; Yuta Kohinata; Shoya Hirohata

title: Intestinal Diseases in Men and Women: Etiology, Diagnosis, and Therapeutic Approaches
abstract: Background/Objectives: Intestinal diseases constitute a significant global public health issue and encompass a broad spectrum of inflammatory, functional, and infectious disorders, including inflammatory bowel disease (Crohn’s disease and ulcerative colitis) and irritable bowel syndrome. In recent years, increasing attention has been paid to sex-related differences in epidemiology, clinical course, diagnosis, and treatment outcomes. Methods: A structured narrative review was conducted using the PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science databases to identify publications addressing sex-related differences in the epidemiology, pathophysiology, diagnosis, and treatment of intestinal diseases. The aim of the study was to examine sex-based differences in the etiology, diagnosis, and treatment of intestinal diseases. Results: The development of intestinal diseases is determined by the interaction of genetic, immunological, hormonal, microbial, and environmental factors. Sex-related differences were identified in disease prevalence, clinical course, and progression and are associated with hormonal regulation, immune response characteristics, and gut microbiota composition. Diagnosis of intestinal diseases is based on a combination of laboratory biomarkers, endoscopic, and imaging techniques, and diagnostic accuracy may vary according to biological sex. Video capsule endoscopy, balloon-assisted enteroscopy, and advanced imaging methods, including computed tomography colonography, improve the evaluation of small bowel diseases, whereas chromoendoscopy, colonoscopy, and cross-sectional imaging play important roles in the assessment of colonic disorders. Treatment includes pharmacological, dietary, microbiota-based, endoscopic, and surgical approaches. Current evidence suggests that biological sex may influence treatment response, adverse event profiles, and clinical outcomes; however, the available evidence remains limited or inconsistent for several therapeutic strategies, highlighting the need for further sex-specific clinical research. Conclusions: Sex-related differences should be considered to improve diagnostic accuracy, optimize treatment strategies, and support individualized clinical management. Although evidence remains limited in several areas, current findings support the integration of biological sex into clinical decision-making. Further research is needed to establish sex-specific diagnostic and therapeutic approaches.
authors: Erik Shorabaev; Amankeldi K. Sadanov; Saltanat Orazymbet; И.А. Ратникова; Baiken B. Baimakhanova; Алтынай Мамбаева; Mira Azhakhmetova; Yelena Shorina; Gulzakira Xetayeva; Maimakova Akmaral; Aziza Assylbekkyzy Kudaibergen; Aknur Turgumbayeva

title: Intracellular accumulation of AAV6 genomes governs microglia reactivity and the inflammatory response in retinal gene therapy
abstract: Adeno-associated viral (AAV) vectors possess immense potential for gene therapy applications. However, microglia can mount an immune response against AAV vectors. Yet, microglia are therapeutic targets since they play a driving role in the progression of neurodegenerative diseases. Thus, it is critical to understand the cellular processes driving the microglia-mediated immune response against AAV vectors. To this end, we modelled AAV6 induced inflammation upon retinal gene therapy in minipigs. Upon AAV6 administration, the IBA1+ cells demonstrated a morphological transition to the amoeboid form, indicating microglial reactivity. We also observed the invasion of peripheral immune cells in the retina. To elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms, we transduced human iPSC derived microglia-like cells (iMGLs) in vitro with AAV6 and AAV8 respectively. Only AAV6 transduced iMGLs exhibited morphological features and a transcriptomic signature of microglial reactivity. The magnitude of intracellular AAV6 viral genomes was significantly higher as compared to the AAV8 condition. The elevated levels of intracellular AAV6 genomes induced a DNA damage response in AAV6-transduced iMGLs, which is a key feature of neuroinflammation-linked microglial reactivity. Thus, our work highlights the impact of intracellular viral genome accumulation on microglial reactivity and its implications for retinal gene therapy associated inflammation.

title: Intrinsically photosensitive retinal ganglion cells: Context-Dependent resilience and vulnerability
abstract: Retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) exhibit marked heterogeneity in their susceptibility to injury and disease. Intrinsically photosensitive retinal ganglion cells (ipRGCs), a small subset of melanopsin-expressing RGCs involved in non-image-forming visual functions, have emerged as a particularly informative example. In multiple experimental models, ipRGCs show relative resistance to acute insults such as optic nerve injury, excitotoxicity, and mitochondrial dysfuinction. In contrast, functional alterations and degeneration have been reported in aging and in neurodegenerative conditions including Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease. This apparent discrepancy suggests that ipRGC survival may depend on the nature and duration of the underlying stress. In this review, we summarize current evidence on ipRGC resilience and vulnerability across a range of experimental and pathological contexts. We discuss candidate mechanisms that may contribute to these responses, including sustained activity, calcium handling, metabolic specialization, neurochemical interactions, and gene expression programs. We also consider the role of subtype-specific diversity within the ipRGC population in shaping these outcomes. Finally, we examine the potential of ipRGCs as biomarkers of disease and as a source of insight for neuroprotective strategies. Together, these observations support the view that ipRGC behaviour reflects an interaction between intrinsic cellular properties and the context in which they are engaged.
authors: Arianna Cella; Ludovic S. Mure

title: Investigation of ciliary body inner diameter in Chinese myopic adults using ArcScan Insight® 100
abstract: Background Ciliary body inner diameter (CBID) was recently reported as a new parameter for Implantable Collamer Lens (ICL) sizing. This study aimed to characterize CBID in Chinese myopic adults using the novel ArcScan Insight 100 very high-frequency ultrasound biomicroscope, identify its associated ocular anatomical factors, and assess its influence on Implantable Collamer Lens (ICL) size recommendations. Methods In this cross-sectional study, 107 myopic eyes of 58 Chinese adults were enrolled. Anterior segment parameters, including CBID, were measured using ArcScan Insight 100. Linear mixed-effect models (LMMs) were fitted to identify determinants of CBID while accounting for inter-eye correlation. The relative contributions of independent variables were evaluated using part R 2 . ICL sizes calculated via the Reinstein formula (incorporating CBID) were compared with those from the STAAR OCOS formula (based on white-to-white diameter). Results The mean CBID was 10.80 ± 0.48 (range 9.76 to 11.97) mm. Multivariate LMM analysis revealed that wider CBID was independently associated with younger age ( P = 0.045), lower crystalline lens rise (CLR, P = 0.011), wider sulcus-to-sulcus diameter (STS, P < 0.001), and smaller STS lens rise (STSL, P = 0.017). Part R 2 analyses identified STS (part R² = 0.595) as the dominant contributor, explaining 59.5% of CBID variability. ICL sizes recommended by the Reinstein formula differed significantly from OCOS-based sizes ( F = 4.672, P = 0.010), with 49% agreement. Conclusions ArcScan Insight 100 allows direct measurement of CBID using a standardized protocol. In Chinese myopic adults, CBID was normally distributed and was mainly associated with STS. The Reinstein formula, which incorporates CBID, resulted in different ICL size recommendations for half of the eyes compared to the traditional WTW-based method. These findings demonstrate that incorporation of CBID can alter preoperative ICL size recommendations, though its direct effect on postoperative vault prediction requires future surgical validation.
authors: Lei Luo; Xindi Wang; Qianrong Hu; Yan Cai; Linjuan Yang; Yu Zhang; Shimin Tan; Yimeng Fan; Zhao Liu; 康前雁; Shengjian Mi

title: Investigation of gear design parameters for soft-gear-driven self-propelled colonoscopy robot.
abstract:
Purpose

Colonoscopy is the most effective method for colorectal cancer screening; however, successful insertion requires a high level of operator skill and may cause patient discomfort or injury. To address these challenges, self-propelled colonoscopy robots that generate propulsion at the distal tip have been actively investigated. In our previous work, we developed a self-propelled colonoscopy robot using a worm-gear mechanism; however, the use of rigid gears posed a potential risk of excessive contact force on the colonic wall.

Methods

In this study, we propose a self-propelled colonoscopy robot enabled by soft gears that combine compliant contact with gear-based power transmission. By reinterpreting the crawler-based propulsion concept as a soft spur gear driven by a worm-gear mechanism, the proposed design allows elastic deformation of the gear teeth under load, providing adaptive traction through compliant deformation of the gear teeth. Gear parameters were optimized using gear-design software, and four soft-gear configurations were fabricated to investigate their propulsion characteristics.

Results

The prototypes were fabricated using stereolithography 3D printing and evaluated using a colonoscopy training model. The robot achieved a maximum propulsive speed of 9.6 mm/s and a propulsive force of 1.5 N in straight sections. Gears with larger modules produced higher propulsion performance. In addition, the proposed coaxial double-worm-gear architecture enabled traversal of curved sections of the colon model under manual steering.

Conclusion

These results demonstrate the mechanical feasibility of using soft gears as a propulsion mechanism for self-propelled colonoscopy robots. Although the evaluation was limited to a colonoscopy training model, the proposed design demonstrated stable propulsion in a colonoscopy training model while maintaining compliant contact with the intestinal wall. The simple and compact mechanical structure provides a promising proof of concept for future minimally invasive robotic endoscopy, although further ex vivo and in vivo validation will be required.
authors: Osawa K, Duan K, Ueda A, Nakadate R, Arata J, Nagao Y, Akahoshi T, Eto M, Tanaka E.

title: KASID Guidelines for Diagnosis and Monitoring of Inflammatory Bowel Disease: 2026
abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is characterized by heterogeneous disease presentations and clinical courses. Accurate diagnosis and appropriate disease monitoring play an important role in improving long-term outcomes by preventing misdiagnosis and unnecessary treatment; enabling early detection of disease progression, treatment failure, and disease-related complications; and facilitating timely adjustment of treatment strategies. The Korean Association for the Study of Intestinal Diseases (KASID) developed guidelines for the diagnosis and monitoring of IBD in adults, reflecting the Korean clinical setting, to support clinical decision-making and improve the quality of patient care. To develop these guidelines, existing international clinical practice guidelines and expert consensus statements were comprehensively reviewed, along with updated evidence relevant to each clinical topic. Final recommendations were established through expert consensus using a modified Delphi process. These guidelines address major clinical areas in the diagnosis and monitoring of IBD, including initial diagnosis and baseline assessment, assessment of disease extent and activity, disease monitoring in ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease, nutritional assessment, and colorectal cancer surveillance. These guidelines are intended to support individualized clinical judgment and should be applied flexibly, taking into account not only individual patient characteristics and clinical circumstances but also available resources, access to diagnostic and monitoring modalities, regulatory requirements, and reimbursement policies.

title: Large-area reflection suppression for structured-light three-dimensional reconstruction of specular surfaces
abstract: Abstract The inherent physical constraints of polishing tools lead to positioning and repeatability errors in industrial robots, which compromise polishing accuracy by deviating the actual dwell time from its theoretical value. A structured light detection technology, as a high-precision non-contact measurement technology, provides a promising solution for the on-machine positioning of polished workpieces. Nevertheless, the strong specular reflection of metal workpieces tends to cause large area overexposure in the captured fringe images, thereby inducing the loss of three-dimensional point cloud data. An algorithm combining the improved Retinal-cortex theory (Retinex) and mask-aware transformer (MAT) deep learning is proposed to suppress the influence of large area surface reflection on measurement to address this issue in this study. The process involves adaptive aperture adjustment to obtain images within an optimal grayscale range, followed by Retinex-based strong-light suppression and MAT-based inpainting to recover missing fringe information in overexposed areas. Validation experiments are conducted on high-reflective aluminum alloy plates based on a structured light measurement system calibrated with an accuracy of 0.01 mm. The results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm can effectively recover missing surface-data holes in the point cloud with an average growth rate of 3.92%, eliminate overexposed regions and compensate for underexposed areas, providing a novel solution for the on-machine inspection and localization of polished workpieces. It is of great significance for improving the deterministic polishing accuracy of robots.
authors: Shaojie Zheng; Ying Liu; Ziqi Han; Haihong Ai; Kun Wang; Zhanshan Wang

title: Laser‐Assisted Transoral Robotic Supraglottic Laryngectomy
abstract: ABSTRACT Objective To describe the operative setup, safety principles, and stepwise technique for laser‐assisted transoral robotic supraglottic laryngectomy using a flexible CO 2 laser system. Methods This operative video demonstrates laser‐assisted transoral robotic supraglottic laryngectomy performed with the da Vinci SP platform. Key technical steps include laser‐safe airway management, transoral exposure with a Feyh–Kastenbauer retractor, robotic docking, flexible CO 2 laser fiber placement through a distal drop‐in guide, aiming‐beam confirmation, noncontact laser dissection, coordinated bedside suction and bipolar hemostasis, and en bloc specimen delivery. Results The technique allows controlled transoral access to the supraglottic larynx with three‐dimensional visualization, precise noncontact laser incision, and preservation of uninvolved glottic and subglottic structures. A deliberate sequence of inferior, lateral, and superior release facilitates exposure of the pre‐epiglottic space, specimen mobilization, and margin‐oriented en bloc resection. Conclusion Laser‐assisted transoral robotic supraglottic laryngectomy combines the precision of CO 2 laser surgery with the visualization and dexterity of single‐port robotic surgery. With appropriate patient selection, strict laser safety, and a standardized team‐based workflow, this technique can support precise en bloc resection, reliable margin assessment, and preservation of uninvolved laryngeal structures.

title: Learning-Enhanced Observer for Sensorless Task-Null-Space Compliant Control
abstract: This paper presents a novel framework integrating a robust wrench observer with a hybrid pose and force controller for physical Human-Robot Interaction (pHRI). In pHRI tasks, robots are expected to perform task-space motions robustly while remaining compliance with human disturbance, which proposes distinct control objectives. Most existing approaches focus mainly on either robustness or compliance and rely on force sensors for real-time tracking. To address these limitations, we propose a novel framework with the following key contributions. Firstly, a neural network (NN) is trained to improve the observer performance by compensating for system friction and unmodeled dynamics. Secondly, a task-null-space decomposition is applied to separate the joint velocity and reduce the effect of the human disturbance on the observer. Finally, a hybrid pose and force controller is introduced to achieve the end-effector pose and force tracking. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides robust and accurate wrench estimation while maintaining reliable pose and force tracking performance. The proposed approach offers an effective solution and framework for pHRI without the need of force/torque sensor measurements which can be applied to many robotic manipulator platforms which do not have force/torque sensors.
authors: Nuo Chen; Ya-Jun Pan; Onur Toker

title: Lesión de Dieulafoy yeyunal causante de hemorragia digestiva severa
abstract: Introduction: Dieulafoy lesion is an exceptional cause of severe gastrointestinal bleeding in pediatric patients, with few international reports and no prior publications in Latin America. We believe this case, diagnosed and managed at our institution, provides valuable insights for the national and regional pediatric community, emphasizing the importance of timely diagnosis and a multidisciplinary approach in these potentially life-threatening emergencies. Severe gastrointestinal bleeding with hemodynamic compromise in the pediatric age group represents an uncommon emergency, with cases caused by a jejunal Dieulafoy lesion being extremely rare.Case presentation: a 13-year-old adolescent presented with profuse lower gastrointestinal bleeding (hematochezia) accompanied by hemodynamic compromise. An emergency laparoscopy was initially performed, ruling out suspected Meckel diverticulum. Esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD) was normal, and colonoscopy was inconclusive due to poor visualization secondary to blood clots. Mesenteric angiography localized the bleeding site in the jejunum and enabled successful embolization. Subsequent rebleeding occurred, and the lesion was definitively diagnosed via video capsule endoscopy. Jejunal resection with end-to-end anastomosis was performed. Histopathological examination confirmed the diagnosis of a Dieulafoy ulcer. The patient had a favorable recovery, with no bleeding recurrence at the two-year follow-up.Conclusions: establishing the etiology of severe lower gastrointestinal bleeding with hemodynamic compromise can present a significant diagnostic challenge.

title: Letter to the Editor: Reconsidering water based boosters for small bowel capsule endoscopy
abstract: Ferreira et al ’s in the World Journal of Gastrointestinal Endoscopy conducted a prospective, multicenter, quasi-randomized trial comparing three intraprocedural booster regimens for small bowel capsule endoscopy: Polyethylene glycol, polyethylene glycol with ascorbic acid, and still water. The study has several strengths including the prospective, multicenter design with efforts to minimize confounding, use of the validated Small Bowel Cleansing Assessment and Report scoring system with excellent interobserver agreement, and assessment of patient tolerability. Key limitations include quasi-randomization, unequal group allocation, a wide non-inferiority margin, and the lack of formal confidence interval-based analysis. In agreement with recent studies such as the PrepRICE trial, the CROHN PREP trial, and a recent umbrella meta-analysis, the findings suggest that booster timing may matter more than the agent used, though reduced cleansing in the distal small bowel with water remains a concern. Future non-inferiority trials are needed before water-based boosters can be adopted as standard practice.
