title: Variable Admittance Control of Symmetric Teleoperated System for Percutaneous Surgery With Reliable Interaction Force Perception
abstract: BACKGROUND: Teleoperated percutaneous surgery offers significant clinical value by improving needle targeting accuracy and minimising radiation exposure to surgeons. Intuitive control and precise force perception in such teleoperated needle insertion robotic systems are critical for optimising curative effects and ensuring patient safety. METHODS: In this study, we propose a symmetric master-slave robotic system integrated with an adaptive variable admittance approach to provide an intuitive human-robot interaction. A new variable admittance control algorithm for a symmetric teleoperation system is proposed to guarantee the reliable interaction force perception during constrained percutaneous operation. RESULTS: The intuitive human-robot interaction is achieved by an adaptive variable admittance scheme that utilises the time derivative of the human applied force to assess human intentions. CONCLUSIONS: The proposed control scheme enables smoother and higher precision master slave robot movement, thereby enhancing operational safety and procedural reliability.

title: Virtual Chromoendoscopy Enhancing Visualization of Parasite Anatomical Landmarks: A Case Report
abstract: Cestodes are parasitic flatworms transmitted through fecal-oral transmission. Some patients may present with nonspecific gastrointestinal symptoms. Endoscopic identification of intestinal helminths is uncommon and may pose a diagnostic challenge. We describe the endoscopic findings of intestinal cestodiasis and highlight the role of advanced endoscopic imaging techniques in its in vivo recognition. We report the case of a patient with no significant medical history who presented with recent-onset intermittent gastrointestinal symptoms, including abdominal distension and bloating. Laboratory tests and computed tomography enterography showed no abnormalities. Using magnification and virtual chromoendoscopy, detailed visualization of a parasite attached to the terminal ileal mucosa was achieved. Colonoscopy revealed a thin helminth adherent to the terminal ileal mucosa. Virtual chromoendoscopy enhanced visualization of characteristic anatomical structures. This case highlights the diagnostic value of advanced endoscopic imaging techniques and underscores their usefulness for recognizing uncommon intestinal infections during routine colonoscopy.
authors: Andrés E. Guevara-Zavala; Sofía Mariño-Velasco; Jordan Bayne; Joel Omar Jáquez-Quintana; Héctor J. Maldonado-Garza; JA Gonzalez-Gonzalez

title: Vision–Language Models in Ultrasound Imaging: A Comprehensive Review
abstract: Ultrasound vision-language models (US-VLMs) must interpret operator-dependent images and dynamic examinations while linking visual evidence to clinical language. This review synthesizes 32 formally published studies identified through a three-database search. We apply an operational three-axis taxonomy: the interaction axis identifies the primary image-text computation, the learning axis records ultrasound-specific training objectives, and grounding granularity specifies the finest documented visual-linguistic correspondence. Study-level assignments and rationales make these distinctions reproducible. We compare task-specific results without ranking models across incompatible cohorts, endpoints, and metrics. Dataset analysis separates acquisition volume from independent clinical diversity, and a seven-domain risk-of-bias appraisal identifies limitations in reporting of patient-level partitioning and development-test overlap. We also distinguish retrospective performance, including external-cohort results, from evidence that assistance improves clinical decisions or workflows. Current systems support diverse ultrasound tasks, but clinical claims require evidence grounding, uncertainty assessment, and validation matched to the intended use.
authors: Zeyuan Tang; Shukang Zhang; Huanjun Wang; Wei Shao; Wentao KONG; Daoqiang Zhang; Peng Wan

title: Visual Characteristic Classification of Peritoneal Carcinomatosis Tumors in Laparoscopic Images Using Chained Convolutional Neural Networks and Region of Interest Extraction
abstract: Peritoneal tumor characterization during laparoscopy relies on surgeon-assigned visual characteristics that vary between observers. Automated methods have not addressed these five individual characteristics. A chained Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) was developed to classify Color, Adherant, Mucinex, Nodulaire, and Retractile from tumor Regions of Interest (ROIs). Cramér's V, mutual information, and Random Forest (RF) predictability were used to determine which labels provided context, and later classifiers received soft probabilities from earlier classifiers. The method was evaluated on a private dataset of 3,432 tumor instances using three ROI methods (Box-ROI, Black-Fill-ROI, and Mean-Fill-ROI) with ResNet50 and VGG19-BN backbones. Macro F1 was the primary metric, supported by the Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUROC) and the Area Under the Precision-Recall Curve (AUCPRC). The best aggregate configuration combined Black-Fill-ROI with chained classification, achieving a mean Macro F1 of 0.7347 and a mean AUROC of 0.8611. Mucinex achieved the highest single-target Macro F1 of 0.8332. For Color, Mean-Fill-ROI achieved the highest independent Macro F1 of 0.7408, whereas Box-ROI achieved the highest chained Macro F1 of 0.7992. Adherant remained difficult despite class weighting. Its independent AUCPRC was higher with Mean-Fill-ROI than with Black-Fill-ROI (0.242 compared with 0.094). Chaining improved Macro F1 in 7 of 15 target-ROI comparisons. The variation across targets shows that ROI design and chaining require target-specific validation. The classifier is intended to support consistent surgical documentation and review rather than autonomous diagnosis.
authors: Hilmi Zharfan Rachmadi; Agus Budi Raharjo; Diana Purwitasari; Frédéric Dumont; Emilie Thibaudeau; Cédric Dumas

title: Vulvar Crohn's disease in children: Diagnostic challenges and therapeutic implications from a literature review
abstract: Vulvar Crohn's disease (CD) is a rare and frequently under-recognised extraintestinal manifestation in children and may precede gastrointestinal symptoms, leading to significant diagnostic delays. We report the case of a 13-year-old girl with a 3-year history of chronic vulvar swelling, erythema, and fissures, initially misdiagnosed despite extensive investigations. Vulvar biopsy ultimately revealed non-caseating granulomatous dermatitis consistent with metastatic CD, and a subsequent endoscopic evaluation confirmed colonic CD. Due to severe and refractory vulvar involvement, treatment with anti-tumour necrosis factor-α (anti-TNF-α) therapy was required, with dose intensification necessary to achieve disease control. Furthermore, we performed a narrative review of the literature and identified 56 paediatric cases of vulvar CD. In most patients, vulvar manifestations preceded the diagnosis of intestinal disease and were frequently independent of gastrointestinal disease activity. Vulvar swelling was the most common presentation, often painless and isolated. Diagnosis was based on a combination of clinical, endoscopic, radiological, and histological findings. Gastrointestinal evaluation played a central role, while pelvic magnetic resonance imaging was essential to exclude contiguous fistulising disease. Vulvar biopsy was performed in most cases but may not be required when CD is confirmed endoscopically and alternative diagnoses have been excluded. Reported treatment ranged from topical therapies and antibiotics to systemic immunomodulators and biologics, with frequent need for escalation to anti-TNF-α therapy in refractory cases. Early recognition and a multidisciplinary approach are essential to prevent irreversible tissue damage and optimise long-term outcomes in affected children.
authors: Silvana Ancona; Matilde Tagliabue; Rosaria Celano; Francesca Laura Boggio; Veronica Boero; Francesca Musto; Giulia Naspi Catassi; Giulia D’Arcangelo; Marina Aloi
venue: Journal of Pediatric Gastroenterology and Nutrition

title: Waveguided, Self‐Sensing Sheath–Core Liquid Crystal Elastomer Fiber Actuators
abstract: Soft actuators capable of operating in confined and hard-to-access environments, while providing integrated self-sensing capabilities, are highly desired for next-generation robotic systems. Here we report a waveguided sheath-core optical fiber actuator consisting of a liquid crystal elastomer core encased in a conductive sheath of carbon nanotubes/carbon black. Near-infrared light guided through the fiber actuator drives reversible contractions of up to 38% and enables a load-bearing capacity of up to 320 times the actuator's own weight. Arrays of these fibers enable independent optical addressing of individual actuators, allowing programmable multimodal gripping in confined environments. The conductive sheath simultaneously serves as a strain sensor, providing real-time monitoring of actuation states via changes in resistance. By integrating photothermal actuation and self-sensing into a single fiber architecture, this work establishes a multifunctional platform for soft robotic systems operating in spatially confined environments.
authors: Hailong Wei; Cheng Zhou; Zhoutao Li; Zhixin Wang; 高福廷; Yuwei Tian; S.H. Chon; Hyun Kim; Ye Xiao; Guanggui Cheng; Zhongqiang Zhang; Xinghao Hu

title: Wearable 3D Transmitter for Omnidirectional Wireless Energy Delivery for Microrobot.
abstract: Capsule robot has emerged as a non-invasive and painless diagnostic tool for gastrointestinal examination. However, the growing demand for high-definition video and advanced functionalities significantly increases power consumption, while the capsule's compact size imposes stringent battery constraints. Wireless power transfer (WPT) offers a promising solution to overcome this energy bottleneck. This paper presents a wearable three-dimensional transmitting coil (3DTC) and a one dimensional receiving coil (1DRC) to enable omnidirectional and uninterrupted wireless charging for capsule robots. By acquiring attitude data from the capsule, the magnetic field of the wearable 3DTC is adaptively controlled to maximise receiving efficiency despite changes in the capsule's position and orientation. The capsule's built-in thermal and charging management circuits monitor the device's temperature, battery voltage, and stop charging when necessary to ensure safety. Beyond demonstrating a maximum received power of 1690 mW and a peak efficiency of 16.09%, this work further examines a range of practical challenges including, the effects upon the flexible coil bending in garment, charging robustness under various capsule motions, and thermal safety. These evaluations contribute to safer, more efficient, and more sustainable ingestible biomedical devices.
authors: Heng Zhang; Chi-Kwan Lee
venue: IEEE transactions on biomedical circuits and systems

title: Wearable Sensors for Monitoring Haemodynamics, Tissue Perfusion, and Motion in Microgravity: Systematic Review
abstract: This systematic review protocol outlines the methodology for identifying and synthesising studies that measure haemodynamics, tissue perfusion, or motion in microgravity environments. The data will evaluate the clinical feasibility and baseline metrics for an Autonomous Ultrasound & NIRS Rig designed for orbital redistribution assessment (Headward Fluid Shift Monitor) (AURORA-HFSM). The search strategy targets database literature from 2015 to 2026 across PubMed and the Cochrane Library. Screening, data extraction, and quality assessment (utilising QUADAS-2 and WEAR-BOT tools) will be conducted independently by a four-reviewer team using Rayyan.
authors: Sakina Hassan

title: When Every Test Fails: Multifocal Grade 1 Ileal Neuroendocrine Tumors Causing Transfusion-Dependent Obscure Overt Gastrointestinal Bleeding.
abstract: Small bowel neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) rarely present as obscure overt gastrointestinal bleeding (OGIB), causing significant diagnostic challenges. We report a 56-year-old man who presented with OGIB that required approximately 50 units of packed red blood cells during a 6-week hospitalization. Multimodal evaluation, including computed tomography angiography, tagged red blood cell scan, video capsule endoscopy, computed tomography enterography, provocative mesenteric angiography, balloon enteroscopy, and octreotide scan, failed to identify a source. Exploratory laparotomy identified 3 mid-ileal nodules with histopathology revealing well-differentiated grade 1 neuroendocrine tumors. Bleeding resolved following resection. This case highlights the diagnostic and therapeutic role of surgical exploration in refractory OGIB.
authors: James Mo; Suraj Suresh

title: When Imaging is Negative: Endoscopic Diagnosis of a Secondary Aortoduodenal Fistula
abstract: Aortoenteric fistula is a life-threatening aortic graft complication with a narrow opportunity for treatment. We present a patient with aortobifemoral bypass who developed recurrent anemia and melena. Despite previous upper endoscopy and colonoscopy, computed tomography angiogram, and tagged red blood cell scan, his symptoms were persistent. Capsule endoscopy showed blood in the duodenum. Push enteroscopy revealed graft erosion in the duodenum, confirming aortoduodenal fistula. He underwent aortobifemoral graft excision, and resection of the third portion of the duodenum with end-to-side duodenojejunostomy, highlighting the importance of endoscopy in timely diagnosis of aortoenteric fistulae.
authors: Avneet Kaur; Ayushi Shah; Anand Gupta; Muhammad Nauman Jhandier

title: Zero-shot classification of bleeding, angiectasia, and normal mucosa in video capsule endoscopy by general-purpose multimodal models
abstract: A diagnostic accuracy study measuring how well current general-purpose multimodal models, given no task-specific training and no worked examples, assign video capsule endoscopy frames to one of three categories: fresh blood, angiectasia, and normal clean mucosa. Frames are drawn from the publicly available Kvasir-Capsule dataset by two-stage stratified sampling at the level of the source recording. The primary outcome is macro-averaged F1. Predictive values are recalculated across the range of frame-level lesion prevalence met in clinical reading; calibration of stated confidence and the rate of declining to answer are treated as outcomes; and a prespecified probe tests whether the models recognize the provenance of the images they are shown. This project holds the protocol and the analysis code, registered before any model was queried.
authors: Ahmed Salman

title: Zero-shot performance of a general-purpose vision-language model for pediatric appendicitis diagnosis.
abstract: General-purpose vision-language models can analyze medical images without task-specific training, but their value for pediatric abdominal ultrasound is unknown. To investigate the zero-shot performance of a general-purpose vision-language model to diagnose pediatric appendicitis using multimodal inputs, including images, report text, and clinical information. In this retrospective study, diagnostic capabilities of Llama 4 Maverick were evaluated on the Regensburg Pediatric Appendicitis Dataset. Five experiments were conducted using the following inputs as well as input combinations: images only, ultrasound report text only, images and ultrasound text, images and clinical data, entire multimodal input. Reference standard of appendicitis was defined based on histopathology in patients who underwent surgical resection and on clinical follow-up in patients managed conservatively. Performance was assessed at the patient level using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, negative predictive value, and F1-score. Area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) was evaluated secondarily as a measure of discrimination. Of 782 patients, 294 met inclusion criteria; based on data availability, four experiments are conducted using 293 patients and in the fifth experiment, 284. Images-only experiment showed very low specificity (13.5%) and had the poorest discrimination (AUROC, 0.567). Ultrasound report text improved classification performance, with specificity increasing to 63.5% while maintaining high sensitivity; discrimination was also strong (AUROC, 0.883). Adding images to ultrasound text or combining all available inputs did not yield further meaningful improvement. Differences between images-only experiment and text-containing experiments were statistically significant (P≤0.002). Zero-shot visual interpretation of pediatric abdominal ultrasound by a general-purpose vision-language model is inadequate for safe appendicitis diagnosis. Performance is driven primarily by a structured sonographic imaging report, supporting a role for such models as text-based decision support tools rather than autonomous ultrasound image interpreters.
authors: Ceren Altintas Mese; Ismail Mese; Tugba Akinci D'Antonoli

title: [Point of care ultrasound: terminology, professional roles and protocols].
abstract: Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) is an imaging modality performed and interpreted by the treating physician at the bedside, with immediate integration of findings into clinical decision-making. Its rapid expansion in emergency medicine, critical care, and resource-limited settings has significantly improved diagnostic and therapeutic timeliness. However, this growth has highlighted the need to clearly define its scope of practice, standardize protocols, and distinguish POCUS from comprehensive consultative echocardiography. This review outlines the historical evolution of POCUS, from early trauma applications to structured protocols for shock, dyspnea, and cardiac arrest, and its current role in cardiopulmonary and hemodynamic monitoring of critically ill patients. Recent international guidelines are summarized, emphasizing POCUS as a distinct and complementary clinical tool rather than a replacement for formal imaging. Finally, future perspectives involving artificial intelligence and robotic ultrasound technologies are discussed, addressing their potential benefits and associated educational, organizational, and ethical challenges.
authors: Simona Giubilato; Francesca Musella; Carlotta Sorini Dini; Francesco Piroli; Nicola Gasparetto; Serena Guasti; Roberta Della Bona; Daniela Zabbia; Francesca Campanella; Salvatore Petrina; Roberta Rossini; Paolo Trambaiolo; Fabrizio Oliva; Federico Nardi; Massimo Grimaldi; Benedetta De Chiara

title: iPSC-derived RPE as a context-of-use defined NAM framework for RPE-centered drug-induced retinal toxicity assessment
abstract: The retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) is essential for outer retinal homeostasis and a key target for drug-induced retinal toxicity. However, conventional preclinical models, including immortalized cell lines and animal systems, may incompletely recapitulate human RPE biology because of limited representation of specialized RPE functions and species-specific differences in retinal physiology. Induced pluripotent stem cell-derived RPE (iPSC-RPE) has emerged as a candidate human-relevant platform for New Approach Methodology (NAM) development, with the potential to improve mechanistic relevance by reproducing key structural and functional features of native human RPE. Its translational utility depends on a clearly defined context of use (COU), reproducible differentiation and functional characterization, and benchmark-based frameworks for future assay qualification and validation. This review evaluates the potential of iPSC-RPE as a COU-defined NAM framework for RPE-centered drug-induced retinal toxicity, with particular emphasis on toxicities in which RPE dysfunction represents a primary or mechanistically important component. We summarize differentiation strategies and critical quality attributes that may inform future assay qualification, evaluate disease-modeling evidence supporting physiological relevance, and discuss applications in ocular safety assessment, including chloroquine/hydroxychloroquine-, MEK inhibitor-, and anti-VEGF-associated retinal effects. We further discuss limitations, including cellular immaturity, donor-to-donor variability, incomplete microenvironmental modeling, and the limited validation of long-term exposure paradigms. Current evidence supports mechanistic concordance for selected RPE-centered toxicities, whereas prospective predictive performance across diverse compounds and clinically relevant exposure conditions remains to be established. Further COU-specific qualification and prospective validation will be required to establish the reliability and decision relevance of iPSC-RPE for defined ocular toxicology applications.
authors: Weixiao Ding; Longjun Gu; 董田甜; Minjun Xiong; Chen Wang; Chunlei Ji; Juan Lv; Xuefeng Zhang; Xinjiang Gong

title: “Integration of Embedded AI and Medical Heat Pipes in Robotic Neurosurgery: A Novel Framework Based on Elmas’s Thermodynamic Theory”
abstract: Objective: This study presents an interdisciplinary framework that autonomizes the thermal management of high-temperature laser ablation and ultra-low-temperature cryoprobe applications, which represent opposing thermal poles in robotic neurosurgery operations. The thermal sensitivity of neural tissues and the risk of permanent neuron damage developing at temperatures above 43°C necessitate a micron-level stable thermal control. Accordingly, the study aims to optimize surgical robots both in terms of hardware and software. Method: The theoretical foundation of the study is based on the principles of “ELMAS’s Thermodynamic Theory”, the “5th Law of Thermodynamics”, and “Bio-Robotic Resonance” developed by Asst. Prof. Dr. Emin Taner Elmas. In the hardware layer, dual-phase medical heat pipes integrated into the tip of the robotic arm (end-effector), having a diameter of 0.8 mm, flexible, and containing sintered copper powder micro-capillaries with water-graphene nano-fluid, were utilized. In the software layer, an embedded artificial intelligence (AI) engine supported by machine learning models was developed, capable of real-time data processing from micro-sensors on the heat pipe and performing digital twin-based live thermal mapping (HUD). The validation of the system was designed with a 5-step validation protocol encompassing computerized thermal modeling, synthetic gel tests, ex-vivo organ tests, in-vivo animal experiments, and preclinical human simulation. Findings: The integration of the micro-heat pipe provided passive cooling without requiring an external energy source, thereby suppressing peripheral heat dissipation (thermal dissipation) during laser operations and maintaining healthy neural tissues within a stable range of 37°C - 38°C. In cryoprobe applications, it acted as a passive heat barrier, creating reverse thermal gradients along the probe shaft, protecting healthy tissues along the entry path while performing instantaneous shock freezing cycles (freeze-thaw) at the target tumor site. The predictive algorithms of the AI engine predicted the thermal saturation at the tissue border milliseconds in advance and successfully activated the haptic lock (fail-safe) mechanism that applies resistance to the surgeon’s master control arms at critical thresholds. Conclusion: The developed autonomous thermal management architecture elevates surgical robots beyond being merely devices that produce mechanical motion into intelligent protective shields that thermally sense the tissue. The integration of Dr. Elmas’s medical thermodynamics equations into robotic software demonstrates at a preclinical level that a micron-level precise, autonomous, and thermally safe hybrid surgical platform can be established for brain tumor resections. [1-111]
authors: Emin Taner ELMAS
venue: Biomedical Journal of Scientific & Technical Research

title: 3D-printed microneedles in biomedical applications: Versatile approaches and clinical potential
abstract: Microneedles (MNs) are micron-scale structures that can painlessly penetrate the skin barrier to facilitate drug delivery, biomarker sampling, and biosensing. Although conventional molding techniques allow large-scale production, they have inherent limitations in rapidly and precisely customizing geometric structures—parameters that critically determine MN biomedical functionality and performance. As a next-generation manufacturing paradigm, three-dimensional (3D) printing offers novel opportunities for the development of personalized and intelligent MNs, leveraging its high precision, design flexibility, and integrated fabrication capabilities. This article reviews different types of MNs and their geometric characteristics, systematically summarizes the applications, advantages, and limitations of mainstream 3D printing technologies in MN fabrication, and focuses on recent research advances in 3D-printed MNs for drug delivery, biomarker extraction, and biosensor construction. Furthermore, it provides an in-depth overview of the application potential of 3D-printed MNs in treating various diseases. The article also discusses the emerging integration of 4D printing and artificial intelligence within this domain. Finally, we summarize and propose directions for future research.
authors: Ziqing Su; Sheng Cheng; Weiwei Chen; Menghui Liu; Peng Gao; Liang Xu; Xingliang Dai

title: A COMPLEX MÜLLERIAN ANOMALY MISDIAGNOSED AS FIBROID UTERUS: A CASE REPORT
abstract: We report a 47-year-old woman who had never been pregnant and had suffered from primary infertility. She also had chronic pelvic pain and irregular menstrual periods. She had several uterine abnormalities, including a complete septate uterus, a duplicated cervix, and a longitudinal vaginal septum, with primary infertility. Her diagnosis included a large endometrial polyp and submucosal fibroids in the uterine cavity. This has been reported in only a few cases. The ultrasound diagnosis revealed a single uterine body with a single endometrial cavity and uterine fibroids but missed other diagnoses of two separate cervical canals, a double cervix, or separate vaginal canals, and a large endometrial polyp. The patient opted for definitive treatment and declined fertility preservation, leading to a total abdominal hysterectomy and removal of the uterine corpus, both cervices, and the vaginal septum. She was discharged five days after surgery and recovered. There are three clinical aspects to this case. First, imaging techniques (ultrasonography and MRI) should be used to diagnose and classify atypical Müllerian duct anomalies (MDAs) before applying a classification system. Second, in hysteroscopic septal resection, treatment should be individualized based on age, disease severity, and reproductive status. For younger women who wish to conceive, hysteroscopic septal resection is generally the most appropriate option, and hysterectomy is usually the last resort for suitable candidates. Finally, a multidisciplinary approach is necessary to deal with congenital anomalies that are complicated by acquired uterine pathologies. The diagnostic and surgical plan is required for such a patient to achieve optimal outcomes.
authors: Dil Sahi Roka; Priyanka Gharti Magar; Krishna Kumar Sah; Sandeep Shrestha; Lijing Liu
venue: World Journal of Biology Pharmacy and Health Sciences

title: A European algorithm and strategy for management of chronic postoperative inguinal pain (EurA-CPIP)
abstract: Background: Chronic postoperative inguinal pain (CPIP) is a disabling complication affecting 8%-17% of all patients after inguinal hernia repair. It is a complex pain condition with several pathophysiological mechanisms involved, including neuropathic pain, inflammation, and mechanical effects (e.g., mesh or scar tissue). Management remains inconsistent, probably due to limited high-quality evidence, heterogeneous approach, and insufficient standardisation of outcomes. This study aimed to develop EurA-CPIP, a multidisciplinary treatment algorithm and prospective data-collection platform designed to support consistent phenotyping, step-up management, and standardised outcomes across centres, creating an iterative platform for future hypothesis-driven research and multicentre trials. Methods: An international multidisciplinary working group from European tertiary referral centres developed the European Algorithm and Strategy for Management of Chronic Postoperative Inguinal Pain (EurA-CPIP). Development was informed by the evidence synthesis underpinning the updated international HerniaSurge guidelines and a critical appraisal of previously published CPIP algorithms. A pragmatic step-up algorithm was designed, integrating pharmacological, interventional, surgical and supportive treatments, with prospective outcome registration and planned data-driven revision on a regular basis. Results: EurA-CPIP provides a multidisciplinary algorithm with entry at multiple levels depending on prior treatment attempts. The concept is to begin and, if needed, advance from conservative measures such as systemic medication and topical therapy, to more invasive treatments such as trigger point injections, and ultrasound-guided nerve blocks; predefined investigational add-ons (radiofrequency, cryoneurolysis, botulinum toxin A) are embedded after documented block response. Multidisciplinary team review precedes escalation to more invasive interventions such as surgery. A supportive and rehabilitative coping trajectory is integrated early on. Standardised outcomes include patient-reported pain outcomes, functional impairment, psychological factors, analgesic use, and patient global impression of improvement. Conclusion: EurA-CPIP is a pragmatic consensus-based strategy intended to harmonise and improve specialised CPIP care while utilising existing and developing emerging therapies. Future research should investigate pathophysiology and intervention effects within this step-up algorithm.
authors: K. G. Andersen; T. W. K. van der Meer; Nadine van Veenendaal; N. B. Foss; M. J. A. Loos; M. Miserez; M. Pawlak; R. M. H. Roumen; T. Naddaf; M. Togsverd-Bo; M. W. Stadeager; E. K. Aasvang; Willem A. R. Zwaans

title: A Multi‐Axis Plantar Load Measurement Platform for the Assessment of Foot Disorders: Comparison of Patients With Psoriatic Arthritis to a Healthy Control Cohort
abstract: BACKGROUND: Accurate assessment of plantar loading, including shear forces, is crucial for understanding foot pathologies such as dactylitis in psoriatic arthritis (PsA). Existing devices predominantly measure plantar pressures, neglecting important shear stresses which may initiate dactylitis. This study presents a novel multi-axis plantar load measurement platform to address this gap. METHODS: The study utilised a newly developed plantar load measurement system, comprising a Hall-effect-based magnetic sensing array, custom data logging electronics, and tailored data processing software. The system's efficacy was evaluated in a pilot feasibility study involving patients with PsA with no, current, or previous dactylitis, and healthy controls. Participants walked barefoot on the platform, capturing plantar shear and pressure data. FINDINGS: Shear stresses were notably higher in the second to fourth rays compared to other regions, particularly in the left foot, aligning with the hypothesis that repetitive local trauma might initiate dactylitis in PsA. However, no consistent differences in stresses were observed between diagnostic groups, likely due to small sample sizes and gait alterations associated with pain. A marked asymmetry was observed between the right and left feet, suggesting dominant-foot placement effects. INTERPRETATION: The new platform demonstrates potential clinical utility in capturing comprehensive foot-loading profiles, including critical shear stresses previously under-assessed. Although the current pilot study was limited in number, the results support the theory that local mechanical stresses may contribute to PsA-related dactylitis. Future larger-scale studies are needed to clarify these findings and overcome limitations related to altered gait patterns due to foot pain.
authors: D. A. Jones; Lefan Wang; Max Houghton; Jennifer Jones; Richard A. Wilkins; Heidi J. Siddle; Graham Chapman; Ali Alazmani; Peter Culmer; Philip Helliwell
venue: Journal of Foot and Ankle Research

title: A PROSPECTIVE OBSERVATIONAL STUDY ON MANAGEMENT OF ESOPHAGEAL CARCINOMA WITH MINIMALLY INVASIVE IVOR-LEWIS ESOPHAGECTOMY AND ITS OUTCOMES IN A TERTIARY CARE CENTRE IN CENTRAL INDIA
abstract: Introduction: Esophageal cancer is a life threatening malignancy with abysmal survival, even for subjects under therapeutic care.Minimally invasive surgery like minimally invasive Ivor Lewis esophagectomy, which is commonly performed for treating esophageal cancer, has a favourable impact in perioperative morbidity and enhances short term recovery compared to traditional open surgery through thoracotomy.The present study was performed to evaluate the outcomes and complications of minimally invasive Ivor-Lewis esophagectomy (MILE) for esophageal cancer. Methods and Materials:A prospective observational study of 20 patients, with histologically proven adenocarcinoma of lower esophagus and posted for minimally invasive Ivor-Lewis esophagectomy, was performed in Department of General Surgery of Government Medical College and Hospital, Nagpur for a period of 18 months (From August 2022 to January 2024).Results: In this study, predominantly patients were females (60%) in the age group of 61 -70 years, with a mean age of 64.04 ± 5.15 years.All patients experienced dysphagia (100%), and more than half also reported weight loss, odynophagia, and retrosternal pain.Approximately 40 % of patients were diabetic.Additionally, 60% of patients had hypertension, with 20% of those also having diabetes.Around half of patients were smokers (50%).Patients predominantly classified as ASA status II (60%), while the remaining 40% were classified as ASA status III.Predominantly, 60% of patients were classified under the T3 category, while the majority were classified under the N1 category (80%).Majority of patients had duration of surgery 4-5 hours (40%) with mean duration was 4.5 ± 1.72 hours.Among all patients, 40% experienced bleeding in the range of 151 to 200 mL, with a mean blood loss of 176.8 ± 40.07 mL.Among patients with complications, 10% experienced early postoperative bleeding, chyle leak, anastomotic leak, or conduit necrosis, while 60% had no complications.The most common length of stay was 6 days, experienced by 40% of patients, with a mean duration of 6.6 ± 0.97 days.Around 30% patients did not survive, while the remaining 70% survived.
authors: Dr. Kartik Sharma
venue: Indian Journal of Health Care Medical & Pharmacy Practice

title: A compact star-shaped microwave resonator sensor with a deep S-band transmission notch for liquid discrimination
abstract: A compact planar microwave resonator based on concentric star-shaped conductive paths is investigated for S-band liquid discrimination. The sensor occupies 20 × 25 mm 2 and is fabricated on Rogers RT5880 ( ɛ r = 2.2 , tan δ = 0.0009 ). Full-wave simulation and two-port vector-network-analyzer measurements show a dominant unloaded transmission notch at approximately 3.34 and 3.33 GHz, respectively, corresponding to a resonance-frequency deviation of about 0.30%. The measured notch reaches approximately −55 dB, while the simulated response is about −44 dB. Three edible oils were then evaluated using the same fixture and sample-holder arrangement. Olive, canola, and coconut oil produced distinct resonance signatures at approximately 3.23, 3.40, and 3.33 GHz, respectively, with a total resonance span of about 170 MHz and a minimum inter-sample separation of about 70 MHz. Electromagnetic-field and surface-current distributions show that the concentric star boundaries create localized capacitive regions and an extended current path, providing a physically consistent basis for dielectric perturbation. A first-order coupled RLC model is introduced to interpret the transmission-notch mechanism. Because the present three-oil dataset is not a calibrated monotonic permittivity series and repeated loading statistics were not recorded, the paper does not report a universal dielectric sensitivity, statistical limit of detection, or biomedical diagnostic performance. The demonstrated result is therefore stated conservatively as frequency-domain discrimination of the investigated liquids, with repeatability, temperature-dependent calibration, and controlled dielectric standards identified as the next validation steps.
authors: Md. Shakhawat Hossen; Muhammad Amir Khalil; Mohamad A. Alawad; Abdulmajeed M. Alenezi; Mohamed Ouda; Phumin Kirawanich; Mohammad Tariqul Islam

title: A flexible silicone elastomer/copper oxide nanocomposite for current-mode X-ray dosimetry: Synthesis, characterization, and performance evaluation
abstract: Flexible, polymer-based nanocomposite dosimeters have attracted growing interest for radiation monitoring in diagnostic radiology because of their mechanical conformability and potential for low-cost, large-area fabrication. While silicone-based detectors loaded with heavier metal oxides have previously been explored, the dosimetric behavior of room-temperature-vulcanizing (RTV-2) silicone elastomer reinforced with copper oxide nanoparticles — which differs from these systems in both filler chemistry and cure mechanism — has not been systematically characterized. In this work, a flexible silicone/copper oxide nanocomposite was fabricated and evaluated, for the first time, as a current-mode X-ray dosimeter. Copper oxide nanoparticles were synthesized by a simple precipitation method and incorporated into the silicone matrix at weight fractions ranging from 0 to 36.4 wt percent. Structural and chemical characterization confirmed the formation of phase-pure, monoclinic copper oxide nanoparticles with an average crystallite size of 27–29 nm, dispersed within the amorphous silicone network as submicron aggregates (mean Feret diameter 253 ± 86 nm within the composite, from 121 measured particles). Under 60 kV diagnostic X-ray irradiation, the nanocomposite exhibited a stable, nearly linear photocurrent response over a dose-rate range of 2.8–12 mGy/min. Among the compositions evaluated, the sample containing approximately 27.6 wt percent copper oxide showed the best overall dosimetric performance, with a sensitivity of 0.102 ± 0.014 nA/(mGy/min) and a noise-limited detection threshold of 0.25 mGy/min; given that the composition-dependent variation in photocurrent (∼11%) is comparable to the measurement uncertainty, this composition is best regarded as a favorable rather than a definitively optimized formulation. The enhanced sensitivity relative to the unfilled matrix is attributed primarily to the higher photon-interaction probability associated with the increased effective atomic number introduced by the copper oxide phase. The devices showed good short-term repeatability, with a relative standard deviation of 1.01% over repeated irradiation cycles, and a signal-to-noise ratio exceeding 90 at an applied bias of 400 V. These results indicate that silicone/copper oxide nanocomposites constitute a cost-effective, mechanically flexible platform for low-energy X-ray dosimetry, with performance comparable to other polymer–metal oxide systems reported in the literature.
authors: Farideh Keyvani; Leila Gholamzadeh; Shahryar Malekie; Sedigheh Kashian

title: A highly reproducible, safe cranial window surgery for targeted in vivo manipulations in the adult zebrafish telencephalon
abstract: Experimental surgery is one of the most fundamental fields of biomedical research, recreating clinical conditions on living organisms similar to clinical patients, to facilitate the design of novel therapies. For modeling neurological and psychiatric disorders, the majority of operative techniques mandatorily include craniotomy for consecutive interactions with the open brain. The most wide-spread methodology involves stereotactic surgery in rodents, implementing a specific head holder, attached to the coordinate table, providing the precise animal head positioning according to the brain structures topology. Despite the high efficiency, such systems require complex instrumental skills and long procedure duration per animal even for simple implantation protocols. Hence, novel alternative model species could be a valuable supplementary tool for such manipulations. Therefore, the zebrafish (Danio rerio) fits perfectly, due to its low cost, easy husbandry, rapid development, optic transparency, and high genetic and physiological similarity to rodents and humans. Furthermore, the everted zebrafish telencephalon provides excellent accessibility to critical mammalian-like structures involved in emotion processing and cognition. However, conventional avian- or rodent-inspired craniotomies in adult zebrafish often trigger inadvertent disruption of the brain vessels network, resulting in high operative mortality. A novel, geometry-driven, non-lethal cranial window protocol preserving neurovascular integrity and ensuring 90-100% post-operative survival is presented to overcome above mentioned limitations. This rapid, simple, and high reproducible technique opens new avenues for precise region-specific in vivo neurosurgery, high-throughput psychopharmacological screening, and neurostimulation in a powerful non-mammalian model species
authors: Konstantin N. Zabegalov

title: A motion vector sensor-enabled 3D spinal morphology monitoring suit for intelligent scoliosis identification
abstract: Abstract Early identification of scoliosis is highly significant for timely intervention and efficient management of the disease. However, conventional static screening approaches rely heavily on subjective assessments, resulting in limited diagnostic accuracy and insufficient continuity. Here, we propose a motion vector sensor-enabled 3D spinal morphology monitoring suit for intelligent identification and continuous monitoring of scoliosis. By orderly aligning elastic conductive fibers, highly anisotropic soft meshes are customized and achieve dual responses to motion amplitude and direction. The sensors exhibit a minimal directional resolution of 2° while maintaining a linear response up to 100% strain. The suit integrates motion sensors positioned at symmetrical body locations to quantify 3D spinal motions via precise measurement of skin-surface deformation amplitude and direction. Dynamic scoliosis identification is achieved through machine learning-powered kinematic symmetry evaluation of 3D spinal motions. The system demonstrates accuracies of 100% for scoliosis detection, 97.7% for curvature degree quantification, and 93.37% for curvature location identification, rigorously validated on a multi-center dataset from four hospitals and one school-based screening program. This work provides a radiation-free alternative for scoliosis screening, with potential to facilitate lifelong monitoring and management of the condition.
authors: Yue Zhang; Liangxu Xu; Guilin Chen; Hongjun Liu; Xuan Zhao; Chao Yao; Haonan Si; Mao Lin; Yue Wang; Bingwu Wang; Xiangjie Yin; Jing Yuan; Guixing Qiu; Zhihong Wu; Terry Zhang; Xiaojuan Ban; Qingliang Liao; Nan Wu

title: A new fluidic MEMS-based mercury ion sensor for water sources
abstract: Mercury detection is essential for ensuring the safety and environmental responsibility of clean energy technologies. This sensor can be used to detect mercury in water sources to remove the toxic pollutant from water effectively. Our proposed sensor addresses this demand by accurately detecting mercury ions through its mass-sensitive properties. The novelty of this sensor stems from two key aspects: first, the incorporation of a highly mercury-sensitive gold layer on the active area to enhance its capabilities and specificity to mercury ions; and second, its unique integration with a digital microfluidic system without any pump and microchannel. This system is fully compatible with microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) technology and can be used in conjunction with, or as part of, clean energy systems. This integration is crucial as it facilitates the delivery of deionized water droplets containing mercury ions to the sensing area. The sensor employs comb-drive electrodes to actuate its resonator in an in-plane mode, which causes its surfaces to slide parallel to the liquid interface. This leads to the mass and stiffness changes in the central resonator and consequently, a measurable frequency shift. Finite element analysis of the mechanical behavior of the sensor demonstrated a quality factor of 651 at a resonance frequency of 351.96 kHz for the resonator. Furthermore, the sensor exhibits a high sensitivity of approximately 105 Hz/ppb, highlighting its potential for trace mercury detection.
authors: Mahnaz Mehdipoor; Reza Hadjiaghaie Vafaie; Sahar Zinatloo‐Ajabshir

title: A proof-of-concept in Blu-ray based nanoplasmonic platform for label-free detection of complement activation (sC5b-9) in Myasthenia Gravis
abstract: Aquesta tesi presenta el desenvolupament i validació d’un biosensor nanoplasmònic altament sensible, ràpid i sense etiquetes, dissenyat per a la detecció i quantificació del complex terminal soluble del complement (sC5b-9) en mostres de sèrum de pacients amb Miastènia Gravis (MG). El dispositiu es basa en la ressonància de plasmó superficial (SPR) utilitzant una nanorreixeta fabricada a partir de discos Blu-ray, un enfocament econòmic i escalable que permet obtenir superfícies amb una periodicitat òptica per a la generació d’efectes plasmònics locals (LSPR). L’objectiu principal ha estat desenvolupar una plataforma capaç d’oferir una alternativa més ràpida i sensible que les tècniques convencionals com ELISA o RIPA, reduint alhora el volum de mostra i la complexitat del pretractament. La biofuncionalització de la superfície amb cys-Protein G ha assegurat l’orientació òptima dels anticossos, millorant l’eficiència de reconeixement de l’anàlit. Per tal d’operar amb matrius complexes com el sèrum, s’ha optimitzat una estratègia antifouling combinant PLL-PEG i BSA, que ha reduït significativament les interaccions inespecífiques. El biosensor ha assolit un límit de detecció (LOD) de 0,015 ng/mL, posicionant-se com una eina competitiva respecte als mètodes tradicionals. Les proves amb mostres reals han demostrat que el sensor detecta activació del complement en pacients amb MG seropositius per AChR, mentre que no s’ha observat activació en casos positius per MuSK, reflectint les diferències immunopatològiques conegudes entre subtipus de MG. Aquests resultats indiquen que el sensor pot constituir una eina valuosa per al monitoratge de l’activació del complement i per al seguiment de teràpies dirigides, com els inhibidors del complement. Tot i que actualment el sistema opera amb sèrum diluït, la integració futura amb microfluídica podria permetre l’anàlisi directa del sèrum i el desenvolupament de dispositius portàtils de diagnòstic al punt d’atenció. En conjunt, aquesta tesi estableix una nova aproximació per al monitoratge ràpid i sensible de biomarcadors del complement en malalties autoimmunes, amb potencial extensió a altres patologies mediades pel complement.
authors: Maria Jose Ugarte Orozco
venue: Tesis Doctorals en Xarxa (Consorci de Serveis Universitaris de Catalunya)

title: A quasi-zero stiffness triboelectric vibration sensor for high-fidelity vibration characterization
abstract: Triboelectric nanogenerator-based vibration sensors offer a promising solution for large-scale, distributed vibration monitoring in mechanical equipment and civil infrastructure. However, their performance is often compromised by inherent structural resonance, which introduces frequency-dependent sensitivity and distorts broadband vibration waveforms. In this work, we present a quasi-zero stiffness triboelectric vibration sensor (QZS-TEVS) that extends the post-resonance operational region towards ultralow frequencies, facilitating high-fidelity broadband vibration characterization. Specifically, an ultralow resonant frequency is realized via the QZS characteristic of the tailored harmonic curved beam. This strategic resonance shift broadens the flat-response bandwidth, thereby effectively suppressing resonance-induced distortion. The QZS-TEVS exhibits a nearly constant displacement sensitivity of 0.31 V/μm over 10-300 Hz, with a frequency measurement accuracy of 99.98%. Furthermore, the QZS-TEVS achieves precise reconstruction of arbitrary vibration waveforms. This work shifts the design paradigm from resonance-driven energy maximization to high-fidelity characterization and provides a high-precision scheme for self-powered, multidimensional condition monitoring within the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT).
authors: Zhengyu Li; Xingyu Chen; Liye Zhao; Jiawen Xu

title: A responsivity theory of call timing patterns in bat echolocation
abstract: ABSTRACT Background The temporal patterning of bat echolocation is extensively characterised, but a general mathematical account linking call timing to acoustic propagation, relative motion, and behaviourally selected information remains incomplete. Results We present the responsivity framework, which represents each call event as a delayed active-sensing cycle comprising an acoustic acquisition interval and a subsequent behavioural interval. Their proportional relation is described by the responsivity coefficient, k r , connecting call timing to effective anchor distance, relative velocity, call duration, and the selected echo window. Analytical derivation, call-by-call simulation, internal validation, and comparison with field recordings show how the framework generates hyperbolic call-rate–distance relationships, shifts approach timing with echo-window selection, and places the terminal buzz at the near-target limit of the same timing process. Responsivity and kinematics have separable terminal effects: k r constrains terminal update density and attainable call rate, whereas closing velocity determines the time available within the terminal region. A buzz-readiness state precedes the complete expression of buzz, and transient sonar strobe groups emerge under multi-target anchor allocation without an explicit grouping rule. Field recordings show broad correspondence with simulations in the organisation of movement, call timing and call duration, and illustrate conditional evaluation of acquisition-window and anchor assumptions. Conclusions Responsivity theory provides a process-based descriptor of echolocation timing and a diagnostic framework for hypothesis generation and empirical testing. The framework identifies the measurements needed to test how selected acoustic information governs subsequent call timing.
authors: Ravi Umadi; Uwe Firzlaff

title: A wearable closed-loop insulin micropump toward a miniaturized artificial pancreas for diabetes
abstract: The application of a fully autonomous artificial pancreas faces fundamental constraints from the bulky mechanical drives of conventional insulin pumps and the spatially separated glucose sensing unit. Herein, we report a wearable closed-loop insulin micropump that enables a miniaturized artificial pancreas for diabetes treatment. It seamlessly integrates an electrochemical micropump with an optical glucose-responsive microneedle (MN) sensor. The core actuation module features a novel semi-dry sandwich electrode configuration combined with a highly elastic latex membrane and a groove-type epoxy sealing architecture. This structural paradigm shift effectively eliminates bulk fluid flow and ensures robust hermeticity for precise, electrolysis-gas-driven, microliter-scale dosing with a precision of 0.5 μL. For continuous glucose monitoring, a polyvinylpyrrolidone/polyvinyl alcohol (PVP/PVA) hydrogel MN array functionalized with 9-anthracene boronic acid (9-ANB) is employed. The specific binding of interstitial glucose triggers measurable fluorescence quenching, which is precisely digitized by an integrated XYZ true-color sensor (detection range: 0-600 mg/dL). Comprehensive in vitro and in vivo evaluations demonstrate the platform's predictable, programmable delivery kinetics and excellent biocompatibility. In type 1 diabetic mouse models, a smartphone-controlled system by autonomously and effectively suppressed postprandial glycemic spikes, maintaining glycemic fluctuations within 25 mg/dL. This highly integrated, miniaturized design offers a compelling paradigm shift for next-generation, patient-friendly diabetes management systems.
authors: Ziyu Kuang; Xiangbin Kong; Tan Cao; Rui Lin; Zhihe Long; Tianyou Jiang; Xianchun Jin; Xinyu Xue; Zhangzhi Zhao; Meihua Chen

title: AI-Powered Personal Tutors as a Scalable Solution to the 2-Sigma Problem in Pharmacy Education
abstract: Background: The “2 Sigma Problem”, where individualized tutoring outperforms conventional instruction by two standard deviations, remains a persistent challenge in large-enrollment pharmacy courses. Generative AI tutors, constrained to instructor-verified content, offer a scalable, equitable approximation of personalized support. Methods: Four course-specific AI tutors were deployed across first-year (P1; n = 108–119/cohort) and third-year (P3; n = 98–108/cohort) Doctor of Pharmacy cohorts (Fall 2024–Spring 2026) using ChatGPT-4o and PlayLab with retrieval-augmented generation. Effectiveness was evaluated through longitudinal grade analysis, American Association of Colleges of Pharmacy proficiency outcomes, satisfaction surveys, and anonymized interaction log analysis. Results: Engagement was heterogeneous across curricular formats: 15-week P1 courses supported sustained weekly usage for foundational concept reinforcement, whereas 4-week P3 modules exhibited lower, targeted utilization focused on rapid self-assessment. In P1 Biochemistry, tutor integration was associated with longitudinal cohort exam improvements. The overall targeted metabolism exam mean rose from 74.0% (Fall 2023, no AI) to 81.4% (Fall 2024, AI tutor) and 83.6% (Fall 2025, AI tutor), with active users (n = 16, 85%, Fall 2024) outperforming non-users (n = 16, 79.3%, Fall 2024) by 5.7 percentage points, and with higher mean scores observed across progressively higher usage tiers. AACP proficiency means increased from 77.9% to 82.1%, exceeding the 80% benchmark. In P1 Physiology and P3 modules, cohort performance remained consistently high (83.7–88.2%), maintaining AACP benchmark proficiency across all observation cycles. Student perceptions were positive regarding conceptual clarification and adaptive explanations. Conclusions: Curriculum-aligned AI tutors represent a viable strategy for approximating individualized instruction in pharmacy courses. Course-specific AI tutors demonstrate feasibility across PharmD curricula, functioning as continuous retrieval-practice tools in foundational sciences and as targeted self-assessment aids in accelerated modules. Educational benefits and adoption dynamics are moderated by curricular pace, subject complexity, and assessment structures, highlighting key considerations for broader health sciences implementation.
authors: Maria Victoria Tejada-Simon

title: ALGORITHMIC SECOND OPINIONS IN PRIMARY CARE DERMATOLOGY: TRUST DYNAMICS AND AUTOMATION BIAS ACROSS SKIN LESIONS AND ERUPTIONS
abstract: Dermatological complaints constitute a significant portion of primary care consultations, encompassing a broad spectrum from infectious exanthems and inflammatory rashes to malignant neoplasms. The recent integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into primary care settings promises to bridge the diagnostic accuracy gap between General Practitioners (GPs) and board-certified dermatologists. However, the socio-technical dynamics of how GPs calibrate trust in AI diagnostic suggestions remain poorly understood. This study investigates human-computer interaction, focusing on diagnostic confidence and automation bias, when physicians are provided with an AI-generated "second opinion." Utilizing an explanatory mixed-methods design, 50 clinicians—comprising 25 GPs (Novices in specialized dermatology) and 25 Dermatologists (Experts)—evaluated a curated dataset of 40 diverse macroscopic and dermoscopic clinical cases, including viral rashes, fungal infections, inflammatory dermatoses, and skin tumors. To assess automation bias, the AI assistant was programmed to provide deliberately incorrect diagnostic prompts in 20% of the cases. Quantitative results demonstrate a profound experience-based divergence. GPs, operating under higher diagnostic uncertainty, exhibited severe automation bias, frequently overturning correct initial diagnoses to align with erroneous AI prompts. Conversely, dermatologists demonstrated resilient diagnostic confidence but exhibited instances of algorithmic aversion, often rejecting the AI entirely due to its "black box" nature. The findings emphasize that deploying AI in primary care requires shifting focus from algorithmic accuracy to human-centered interface design, specifically integrating Explainable AI (XAI) paradigms to ensure safe and synergistic clinical decision-making.
authors: Jakub Klepacz; Radosław Swędrak; Zuzanna Dobrakowska
venue: International Journal of Innovative Technologies in Social Science

title: Abnormal behavior perception in elderly care scenarios based on multimodal generative adversarial networks
abstract: In view of the limitations of the existing elderly care anomaly perception methods, which mostly rely on single visual mode and shallow stitching multi-source sensing features, such as insufficient accuracy of long-time progressive anomaly recognition, easy mode collapse of multimodal training, and insufficient utilization of non visual sensing information, this paper proposes a multimodal wgan GP anomaly perception method combining CNN-LSTM spatio-temporal double branch coding. The framework integrates five kinds of heterogeneous sensor data, including vision, inertial IMU, bed pressure, physiological signs and environmental audio, and adaptively allocates the weight of each mode to complete the cross modal feature alignment based on the dual attention of space and time; The shared generator based on the fusion of spatial and temporal two-way sub generators only learns the distribution of normal behavior, and uses multimodal attention discriminator to distinguish the true and false features; Wgan GP gradient penalty and modal imbalance correction item were introduced to stabilize the confrontation training, and the weighted reconstruction error and discriminant confidence were fused to construct a joint abnormal score. Four core abnormalities, including falling, falling out of bed, long-term wandering and physiological index disorder, were identified by dynamic threshold. The experimental results show that the AUC roc of the complete model in this paper can reach 0.978 ± 0.003, the F1 score is 95.64 ± 0.47%, the false positive rate is 2.13 ± 0.24%, and the false negative rate is 3.05 ± 0.30%; Ablation experiments showed that F1 score decreased significantly after removing inertia, bed pressure or audio modes, which confirmed that such non visual modes had complementary contributions to information, and the complete model had stronger scene adaptability and engineering landing value. Not applicable.
authors: Xinbo Zhao

title: Accelerator-based BNCT as a drug–device regimen: system engineering, clinical evidence, and regulatory considerations
abstract: Boron neutron capture therapy (BNCT) is a binary, tumor-selective radiotherapy modality that combines preferential delivery of boron-10 to tumor tissue with neutron irradiation to generate high-linear energy transfer particles in situ . The field has undergone a defining transition from reactor-based neutron sources to accelerator-based BNCT (AB-BNCT), enabling hospital-based deployment, broader clinical translation, and renewed global interest in indications with substantial unmet needs, particularly recurrent head and neck cancers and gliomas. However, AB-BNCT is intrinsically a drug–device regimen, requiring coordinated evaluation of the boron agent, neutron irradiation system, and dedicated treatment planning software, supported by end-to-end quality management, commissioning and routine quality assurance, and postmarket surveillance. This review summarizes the system-engineering foundations and current global landscape of AB-BNCT. We outline the therapeutic principle and key subsystems, including accelerator neutron sources, beam shaping assembly, patient positioning and setup, beam/dose monitoring, treatment control, and Monte Carlo–based BNCT treatment planning. We synthesize clinical evidence from reactor-era feasibility studies, accelerator-era registration programs, and emerging real-world evidence, including the Japanese Phase II registration study reporting an objective response rate of 71.4% in patients with unresectable recurrent or locally advanced head and neck cancer and subsequent nationwide postmarketing evidence. We also compare regulatory classification and approval pathways across the European Union, United States, Japan, and China. Finally, we discuss regulatory considerations relevant to the evaluation of BNCT devices in China. Continued advances in boron agents, accelerator engineering, and standardization, together with accumulated regulatory experience, may support broader clinical implementation of AB-BNCT. Further accumulation of evidence integrating beam physics, dosimetry, and clinical outcomes may facilitate cross-jurisdictional understanding and the continued clinical development of AB-BNCT.
authors: Zehua Wang; Yue Wang; Yan Jiang; Qing Zhang; Xiaofang Gu; Lu Liu

title: Access To Healthcare For People With Disabilities: A Case Study Of Mulimira Zone, Bukoto I, Kampala
abstract: Despite Uganda’s progressive legal and policy commitments to disability rights, persons with disabilities in many urban communities continue to face significant barriers to accessing healthcare. This study examined access to healthcare for persons with disabilities, using Mulimira Zone, Bukoto I, Kampala as a case study, guided by objectives establishing patterns of healthcare utilization, identifying physical, communication, attitudinal, and economic barriers, assessing health worker perceptions and practices, and exploring coping strategies. A descriptive cross-sectional mixed-methods design was adopted, drawing on a total population sample of 50 persons with disabilities/caregivers and 15 key informants, using structured questionnaires, in-depth interviews, a focus group discussion, and facility observation. Descriptive results showed high physical access barriers (mean = 3.40) and severe communication barriers among deaf respondents (mean = 4.56), alongside moderate-to-high economic barriers (mean = 3.44). All four barrier domains were significantly and negatively correlated with healthcare utilization, with economic barriers showing the strongest association (r = −0.641, p < 0.01). Regression analysis showed the four barrier domains jointly explained 57.1 percent of the variance in healthcare utilization (R² = 0.571), with economic barriers (β = −0.398) and physical barriers (β = −0.312) as the strongest significant predictors. Path analysis revealed that physical and communication barriers exert significant indirect effects on utilization through their influence on economic burden (β = 0.481 and 0.296 respectively), with a total effect of physical barriers on utilization of −0.503 compared to a direct effect of −0.312. The study concludes that healthcare access barriers for persons with disabilities in Mulimira Zone are multidimensional and interlinked, with physical and communication barriers compounding economic burden, and recommends facility infrastructure retrofitting, sign language interpretation services, disability-inclusive health worker training, targeted transport/cost subsidies, and strengthened community-based monitoring.
authors: Walusimbi Joshua; Oumo Gideon
venue: Metropolitan Journal of Academic and Applied Research

title: Adaptive Robotic Skill Transfer System
abstract: Abstract Adaptive robotic skill transfer concerns the reuse of learned behaviour across machines, tasks and operating environments while preserving interpretable performance boundaries. This monograph develops a research architecture in which task representations, embodiment adapters, uncertainty estimates and independent execution controls jointly determine whether a transferred skill may operate. Ten research themes connect the supplied bibliography to five chapters on foundations, statistical explanation, machine learning, scalable engineering and sectoral governance. The analysis distinguishes transferable task structure from robot-specific actuation and separates adaptation performance from evidence of safe execution. Twenty-five mathematical models formalize distinct research questions, including representation alignment, causal transfer effects, calibration, scheduling, provenance and deployment value. The proposed evaluation programme uses grouped experiments, held-out embodiments, explicit resource budgets and staged physical validation. Its implementation pathway combines a versioned skill registry with local runtime supervision, auditable adaptation and reversible release procedures. Manufacturing, logistics, assistive systems and field robotics illustrate how environmental and institutional conditions alter transfer requirements. The central conclusion is that useful transfer must be demonstrated as a conditional improvement over credible baselines, with failure recovery and responsibility included in the comparison. The book offers research protocols and a technical invention disclosure for further implementation and examination; it does not report completed robotic experiments. Keywords adaptive robotics, skill transfer, embodiment adaptation, imitation learning, reinforcement learning, causal inference, uncertainty quantification, domain shift, digital twins, safety supervision, multimodal fusion, edge intelligence, continual learning, federated learning, reproducibility, model governance, provenance, scheduling, human oversight, industrial automation, research design, assurance
authors: Murali Krishna Pasupuleti

title: Adductor Longus Tendon Repair and Lengthening for the Treatment of Core Muscle Injury: A Step‐by‐Step Surgical Technique
abstract: Core muscle injury is an increasingly recognized condition that causes groin pain, most commonly in young, active adults. Multiple surgical interventions have been described, including rectus abdominis repair and/or adductor longus lengthening, generally reserved for recalcitrant cases. This article presents a step-by-step guide to an open adductor longus repair and lengthening. By performing an anatomic tendon repair combined with controlled lengthening at the musculotendinous junction, this approach aims to minimize recurrence while providing sustained pain relief.
authors: Roger Quesada-Jimenez; Talha Syed; Alexandra M. Assimos; William M. Moore; Andrés Maldonado‐Rosales; Etan P. Sugarman; Benjamin Gilbert Domb

title: Advanced Drug Delivery Systems: Barriers and Emerging Strategies for Clinical Translation
abstract: Advanced drug delivery systems, including nanoparticles, liposomes, hydrogels, and hybrid composites, promise substantial improvements in targeted therapy and reduced systemic toxicity, yet their clinical translation remains limited. We conducted a systematic literature review covering publications from 2016 to 2025, employing a structured extraction framework across nine domains to evaluate platform design, biological barrier penetration, and translational outcomes. Our analysis reveals that hybrid composite systems consistently face greater manufacturing scalability constraints and regulatory ambiguity compared to single component platforms such as liposomes and lipid nanoparticles, which have achieved Phase III trials and market approval. Smart stimuli responsive hydrogels in chronic inflammatory diseases demonstrate improved therapeutic indices through reduced systemic exposure and enhanced local efficacy, although formal ED50 or TD50 values were not reported in primary studies. Living drug delivery systems pose higher immunogenicity risks than biomimetic alternatives, with standardized testing protocols existing for synthetic coatings but lacking quantitative acceptable ranges. Multi scale computational modeling, including a physiologically based pharmacokinetic model for blood brain barrier penetration, achieved strong validation with a correlation coefficient of 0.848, indicating improved translational feasibility. Chemical modification of natural polymers, particularly hyaluronic acid, yields route dependent improvements for example, thiolation produced a twenty fold increase in mucosal deposition, while sulfation enhanced transdermal bioavailability ten fold. The primary contribution of this work is a comprehensive synthesis identifying cross cutting translational barriers manufacturing complexity, regulatory uncertainty, and incomplete immunogenicity validation that inform future development priorities. These findings underscore the necessity for standardized characterization protocols, advanced computational modeling to bridge in vitro and in vivo performance, and strategic chemical modification approaches tailored to specific administration routes.
authors: Nucky Indra Praja; Callista Putri Nabila
venue: Journal of Regenerative Medicine and Molecular Innovation

title: Advanced piezoelectric nanogenerators for next-generation self-powered nano-bio sensors
abstract: Abstract Two-dimensional (2D) material-based piezoelectric nanogenerators (PENGs) are emerging as efficient energy-harvesting devices that convert mechanical stimuli into electrical energy. Owing to their tunable electronic, mechanical, and structural characteristics, 2D materials, including TMDs, MXenes, h-BN, etc, offer significant advantages in flexibility, durability, and low-power operation, making them highly suitable for next-generation self-powered systems. This review systematically highlights recent advances in 2D material-based PENGs, emphasizing fabrication strategies, performance optimization, electromechanical coupling enhancement, and their applications in self-powered nano-biosensors. The interdependence between material properties, device architecture, and measurement conditions is comprehensively analyzed to establish robust structure-performance relationships. Furthermore, critical challenges, including low output power, signal instability, integration complexity, and the lack of standardized evaluation protocols, are systematically analyzed. Emerging strategies to enhance energy-harvesting efficiency, signal reliability, and device scalability are also highlighted. Overall, this review establishes a unified framework for the rational design and advancement of high-performance 2D PENGs, providing key insights for their practical implementation in portable, wearable, and autonomous self-powered systems.
authors: Abhay Singh; Manish Sharma; Rajesh K. Gangwar; Ajeet Kumar Kaushik; Sanjeev Kumar K. Sharma

title: Advancements in optical fiber coatings and functionalization for chemical and biological sensing applications
abstract: Recent advances in optical fiber engineering have enabled the transformation of conventional fibers into sophisticated platforms for chemical and biological sensing. Innovations in coating technologies-incorporating polymers, metals, nanoparticles, and hybrid nanocomposites, have significantly enhanced light-matter interactions at the fiber interface, thereby improving analytical sensitivity and performance. Polymeric coatings provide chemical tunability and mechanical flexibility, while metallic films enable plasmonic-based refractive index sensing with high responsiveness. In parallel, the integration of nanoparticles and nanocomposite materials introduces tailored optical properties and multifunctional behavior, expanding the capabilities of fiber-based sensing systems. Complementary surface functionalization strategies, including self-assembled monolayers and molecular imprinting have further advanced the field by enabling the controlled immobilization of biorecognition elements such as enzymes, antibodies, and aptamers. These approaches confer high selectivity and stability, facilitating the development of next-generation optical fiber sensors for the detection of gases, volatile organic compounds, biomarkers, pathogens and genetic targets. This review summarizes recent progress in coating materials, surface functionalization methods, and optical transduction mechanisms for fiber-optic chemical and biological sensors. Particular emphasis is placed on the relationship between coating morphology, sensing performance, and practical challenges including coating instability, signal drift, reproducibility, and operation in complex sample environments. Emerging trends in distributed sensing and artificial intelligence-assisted signal processing are also discussed as promising directions for next-generation intelligent optical fiber sensing systems.
authors: Maxwell Ogochukwu Ojukwu; Jonas H. Osório; Júlio César Ugucioni; Fabiana S. Felix

title: All-fiber wireless auscultation garment for cardiopulmonary diagnostics
authors: Qianyi Li; Ziang Li; Xiaoyu Zhang; Hakan Akgün; Swetika Chaturvedi; Hooi Khee Teo; Kamalesh Anbalakan; David Sim; Kenneth Michael Chew Yun Chi; Kee Thai Yeo; Derek John Hausenloy; Tural Khudiyev

title: Amortized Feedback Planning: Turning Model-Based Rollouts into Executable Policies
abstract: Closed-loop planning accounts for future observation-dependent actions but can be expensive to repeat at deployment. Bellman-gradient (BG) refinement differentiates conditional rollouts through an existing actor, corrects the current action, and stores the result in an executable policy. A backward sweep reuses deployed future feedback; full-horizon rollouts in an identified Gaussian belief model need no learned value critic. A nonlinear error recursion links quadratic continuation error, local correction, and policy storage. A controlled non-LQG example exhibits second-order policy accuracy with consistent storage, while ideal affine LQG admits exact backward recovery. In nonquadratic thrust, BG reduces actor cost by 2.47-3.20% and remains within 0.13-0.53% of the tested feedback MPC; original policies execute in 5-6 microseconds in a seed-0 native audit. With matched storage, BG attains competitive plant costs at about one ninth (arm) and one sixtieth (docking) of feedback-teacher-plus-student construction time on one GPU, excluding shared learning and node preparation. Richer common maps substantially narrow some student-BG gaps. These results expose the roles of learned feedback, local correction, and storage in executable control.
authors: Jeonggyu Huh

title: Artificial Intelligence Models for Early Disease Detection Using Clinical Data
abstract: In a variety of chronic and acute diseases, earlier detection of disease is a major determinant of better patient outcomes, better treatment costs savings and reduced mortality.The current diagnostic process, mostly manual, manual interpretation of clinical data, is limited by the capacity of the human mind, by inter-observer variability and by the amount of data produced by modern healthcare systems.Artificial Intelligence (AI) that leverages machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) capabilities has become a rapidly evolving technology that can help uncover patterns within very large, heterogeneous and high-dimensional clinical datasets, well in advance of what traditional methods could accomplish.In this research paper, a thorough investigation of AI models for early disease detection from medical data, such as laboratory results, electronic health records (EHR), vital signs, and medical image metadata is conducted.We examine the theoretical underpinnings of important classifiers like Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machines, Random Forests, Gradient Boosting methods, Artificial Neural Networks, Convolutional Neural Networks and Long Short-Term Memory networks and compare their performances using the metrics: accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC).A systematic procedure of data acquisition, data preprocessing, feature engineering, model training, model validation and interpretability is suggested and illustrated using simulated experiments.The results show that ensemble and deep learning algorithms (especially XGBoost and CNN) are more accurate at forecasting than traditional statistical models, but they are less interpretable and more demanding in terms of resources.The paper also highlights these issues of data privacy, class imbalance, explainability of AI models, and clinical integration, and proposes directions for future research such as federated learning, explainable AI, multimodal data fusion for early disease detection, among others.
venue: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology

title: Artificial Intelligence for Clinical Competence Assessment Compared with Human Examiners: A Systematic Review and Exploratory Meta-Analysis of Agreement, Reliability, And Validity
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being used to assess clinical competence, yet its measurement performance relative to human examiners remains uncertain across professions, tasks, and assessment formats. This systematic review and exploratory meta-analysis evaluated agreement, association, reliability, validity, score differences, classification performance, and human-human benchmarking for AI-based assessment of human clinical competence. Searches identified 29 eligible reports representing 27 independent studies across medicine, dentistry, nursing, pharmacy, and paramedicine. Owing to substantial heterogeneity in measurement methods, most outcomes were synthesized narratively. Two independent studies reported Spearman correlations and were included in an exploratory random-effects meta-analysis despite differing substantially in clinical assessment context using Fisher z transformation and restricted maximum likelihood estimation. The pooled AI-human association was ρ = 0.82 (95% CI, 0.55-0.93). The two correlations were numerically similar (I² = 0%), but between-study heterogeneity could not be estimated reliably because only two studies were available. This estimate should be interpreted cautiously as a cross-context summary of association rather than a common clinical effect. Direct agreement varied markedly across studies, and favorable correlations or reliability estimates sometimes coexisted with systematic score differences or disagreement near decision thresholds. Performance appeared strongest in structured, rubric-based tasks and more variable for communication, non-technical skills, and context-dependent judgments. Human-reference quality, input equivalence, model choice, and validation design also influenced interpretability across studies.
