title: Residual governance for responsible embodied AI: authority, contestability, and cognitive sovereignty
abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) ethics increasingly concerns systems that do not merely recommend but intervene: clinical decision support, human–machine teaming, robotics and automated handover protocols can shift timing, attention and authority under uncertainty. This article argues that responsible embodied AI requires residual governance: an explicit account of which approximation errors remain, which are safe to tolerate and who may act on them. The paper develops two linked concepts. A residual ledger records action-relevant remainders across physical, causal, human-state, latency, transfer and energy dimensions. An authority ledger records who converts residual evidence into intervention, on what basis, with what uncertainty and with what opportunity for contestation. This framework extends familiar themes in bounded rationality, active inference and safe reinforcement learning by treating authority, contestability and oversight cost as first-class ethical variables rather than external governance add-ons. It uses physical AI, physiological computing and human-AI handover as pressure cases, and proposes evaluation through action calibration, dual-task interference and auditable authority transitions. The central claim is that cognitive sovereignty is preserved not by eliminating all algorithmic influence, but by making influence accountable, contestable and reversible when AI systems act under approximation.
authors: Chia‐Wei Sun

title: Resistance to technological innovation: the case of teleconsultation before and during COVID-19
abstract: Purpose This study analyzes resistance to technological innovation in the healthcare field, focusing on the formal, long-term adoption of teleconsultation in medical practice, which became established during the COVID-19 pandemic. Different institutional studies on resistance to change were analyzed to evaluate their capacity to explain the phenomenon. Design/methodology/approach Qualitative interpretive research was conducted involving documentary research and interviews with professionals from public and private domains, including health regulation organizations and individual practitioners, to capture their understandings of the issue. Findings The results showed that the primary hindering factors were the need for physical examination, the risk of deteriorating remuneration conditions for doctors, and insufficient undergraduate training in telemedicine. Research limitations/implications Thus, the study infers that institutional logics of the same order can coexist, accommodating contradictions between them. Medical autonomy, a principle of democratic logic upheld by part of the professional community and the imperative of public health emergencies, characteristic of professional logic, provoked a rapid response, constituting the driving pressures for the adoption of teleconsultation. Originality/value Technological innovation tends to face resistance during implementation, but under favorable conditions, it becomes consolidated alongside the previous practice. Traditional professional logic resisted the introduction of the new logic represented by teleconsultation until confronted by the pandemic, when it was compelled to adapt to the circumstances.
authors: Hosana Rodrigues; Arnaldo Luiz Ryngelblum; Ernesto Michelângelo Giglio

title: Robotic Splenectomy for Refractory Immune Thrombocytopenic Purpura
abstract: Splenectomy is a well-established surgical option for selected patients with immune thrombocytopenic purpura and persistent thrombocytopenia despite medical therapy. Although laparoscopic splenectomy remains the standard minimally invasive approach, robotic platforms may offer advantages in technically challenging cases. We present a 40-year-old woman with a 4-year history of immune thrombocytopenic purpura, obesity, Hashimoto thyroiditis, and prior sleeve gastrectomy presented with severe thrombocytopenia and abnormal uterine bleeding. After failure of medical therapy, she underwent robotic splenectomy with the da Vinci Xi robotic platform using an anterior approach. Operative time was 240 minutes, and estimated blood loss was 200 mL. The postoperative course was uneventful, and the patient was discharged on postoperative day 3. Pathologic examination findings were compatible with immune thrombocytopenic purpura. Robotic splenectomy is safe and feasible in this selected challenging case and may be considered an alternative minimally invasive approach when enhanced visualization and precise hilar dissection are desirable.

title: Role of microthrombosis in coronary microvascular dysfunction
abstract: Coronary microvascular dysfunction is a common and prognostically important event of ischemic heart disease, yet effective therapeutic strategies remain limited. Microthrombosis is a pivotal driver of microvascular obstruction and no-reflow. This review focuses on the self-amplifying loop between inflammation and platelet activation that sustains microvascular occlusion. Within this loop, myocardial inflammatory signaling suppresses protective autophagy, predominantly in cardiomyocytes, and promotes endothelial dysfunction. The resulting prothrombotic endothelial surface supports activated platelet adhesion, inflammatory mediator release, and platelet-leukocyte aggregation. Neutrophil-derived web-like structures, known as neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs), further enhance platelet aggregation and fibrin deposition. These thromboinflammatory processes lead to microinfarcts, contractile dysfunction, and elevated cardiac troponin, and extend to multiple organs, particularly in patients with common cardiometabolic risk factors such as hypertension, diabetes, dyslipidemia, and hyperhomocysteinemia. Platelet-derived microparticles, platelet-monocyte aggregates, and soluble activation markers show promise as diagnostic biomarkers, but further clinical validation is required. Current antiplatelet, anti-inflammatory strategies, or ischemic conditioning are limited by bleeding risk, narrow therapeutic windows, or inconsistent efficacy. We outline future directions, including developing validated biomarker panels, multi-target therapies that block key inflammatory pathways or NET formation, and human-relevant microphysiological models. Understanding the positive feedback cycle between inflammation and platelets is essential for developing novel diagnostic and therapeutic approaches to mitigate microvascular damage in coronary artery disease as well as other thromboinflammatory disorders.

title: Second‐line MRI after expert transvaginal ultrasound in selected patients with suspected complex deep endometriosis: A prospective cohort study
abstract: INTRODUCTION: The objective of this study was to evaluate the added diagnostic yield of second-line magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) after expert transvaginal ultrasound (TVS) for preoperative mapping of deep endometriosis (DE). MATERIAL AND METHODS: In this prospective observational cohort study, women with suspected DE scheduled for surgery after expert ultrasound were included. TVS was performed according to the International Deep Endometriosis Analysis (IDEA) protocol. MRI was selectively performed as a second-line investigation in patients with suspected advanced disease, inconclusive TVS, or advanced symptoms despite negative TVS findings. Surgical visualization served as the primary reference standard, with histopathology used as a secondary reference standard when available. Diagnostic performance (sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, likelihood ratios, and Cohen's κ) was assessed for TVS, MRI, and their combination, and stratified by prior surgical status. For the combined approach, a positive result was defined as a positive finding on either modality (TVS or MRI), representing a rule-out strategy. RESULTS: Among 221 women with suspected deep endometriosis, 189 underwent surgery, of whom 112 had both TVS and MRI; 55 had previous abdominal surgery. Combined imaging improved sensitivity for rectosigmoid DE (+10.3%; +6 true positives (TP), +3 false positives (FP)) and uterosacral ligament involvement (+29.2%; +14 TP, +12 FP) but reduced specificity for endometriomas (-19.0%; true negatives (TN) 18 to 14), obliteration of the pouch of Douglas (-13.3%; TN 14 to 8), and uterosacral ligaments (-20.3%; TN 35 to 23). Most lesions missed by TVS were in the mid or upper rectum. Accuracy for the urinary bladder and ureters decreased with the addition of MRI (82.2% to 75.7%). Sensitivity for rectosigmoid lesions was higher with the combined method (TVS + MRI) in women with prior surgery. CONCLUSIONS: Among selected complex patients undergoing second-line MRI after expert TVS, combined imaging increased detection of rectosigmoid and uterosacral ligament lesions, but at the cost of reduced specificity. The sensitivity for rectosigmoid disease was greatest among patients with prior abdominal surgery, although this subgroup finding should be considered exploratory. These findings are consistent with a selective rather than routine role for MRI after expert TVS.
authors: Mira Rehal; Malin Brunes; Takayuki Suzuki; E. Epstein

title: Seeing the patient: professional vision in clinical ward rounds (and beyond)
abstract: Clinical ward rounds are complex, high‑stakes encounters in which physicians must integrate clinical reasoning, team coordination, and patient‑centred communication. While ward rounds are routinely described as occasions on which physicians "see" their patients, ironically, the visual dimension of ward round communication has rarely been examined conceptually. In this paper, we argue that communication during ward rounds and other complex clinical encounters crucially relies on physicians' professional vision: learned, task-specific ways of noticing, interpreting, and using visual information in socially and institutionally structured contexts. Drawing on research from medical education, cognitive psychology, and interaction research, we conceptualize professional vision enacted during ward rounds as encompassing two interrelated aspects: a cognitive aspect (noticing and knowledge‑based reasoning) and an embodied and interactional aspect (the coordination of gaze, body, and talk). We show how these aspects unfold across different phases of ward rounds and enable physicians to align information retrieval, decision‑making, teamwork, and patient engagement. By explicating professional vision as a central yet previously under-theorized resource in clinical practice, exemplified here through ward-round communication, this paper offers a conceptual foundation for future empirical research and suggests new directions for simulation‑based and professional vision‑focused instructional approaches in medical education.
authors: Martin Gartmeier; N. McIntyre; Jana Fritsche; G. Kahraman; Christian Kosel; Ann-Kathrin Schindler; Ralf Schmidmaier; K. Vogt; P. O. Berberat; Tina Seidel

title: Seminal bradykinin, fetuin-a, pentraxin-3, and adipolin levels in infertile men with varicocele and varicocelectomy: a cross-sectional case–control study
abstract: Abstract Varicocele is characterized by abnormal dilatation of the pampiniform plexus accompanied by venous reflux and is one of the leading correctable causes of male infertility. Although several mechanisms have been proposed, the molecular pathways underlying varicocele-induced testicular dysfunction remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to investigate seminal bradykinin, fetuin-A, pentraxin-3, and adipolin levels in infertile men with varicocele and to compare these biomarkers among patients with varicocele, patients who had undergone varicocelectomy, and controls. This cross-sectional case-control study included 90 participants: 30 infertile men with clinical varicocele, 30 patients who had undergone varicocelectomy and 30 healthy controls. Seminal bradykinin, fetuin-A, pentraxin-3, and adipolin concentrations were determined using ELISA. Sperm concentration, rapid progressive, non-progressive, and immotile sperm percentages, together with bradykinin, fetuin-A, and pentraxin-3 levels, differed significantly among the study groups. Fetuin-A and pentraxin-3 levels were significantly elevated in the varicocele group compared with healthy controls. Patients assessed approximately 3 months after varicocelectomy exhibited significantly higher bradykinin, fetuin-A, and pentraxin-3 levels than controls. No significant differences were observed among the groups regarding age, height, body weight, body mass index, abstinence duration, semen volume, slow progressive sperm percentage, or Adipolin levels. Our findings indicate that patients with varicocele and patients assessed after varicocelectomy exhibit differences in inflammatory and cellular stress-related biomarkers compared with healthy controls. The higher levels of bradykinin, fetuin-A, and pentraxin-3 observed in patients assessed after varicocelectomy may reflect differences in inflammatory and cellular stress-related profiles between the study groups; however, the cross-sectional design does not allow these findings to be interpreted as postoperative persistence or treatment-related changes. These biomarkers may provide complementary information regarding inflammatory and cellular stress-related profiles in varicocele; however, their clinical significance and utility for monitoring postoperative changes require confirmation in larger prospective longitudinal studies.
authors: Mesut Oc; Ahmet DÜNDAR; Songül Çetik Yıldız; Halit Irmak

title: Six in One: 6S‐NP Supramolecular Nanoparticles for Super‐Lubrication, Inflammation Suppression, and Senescence Reversal in Mechanically Aggravated Joint Disorders
abstract: Mechanical overload and oxidative inflammation jointly drive the progression of friction-induced, age-related joint degeneration. Current clinically employed viscosupplementation strategies, such as hyaluronic acid, only offer transient lubrication, and under high-shear conditions, it undergoes rapid viscoelasticity deterioration, greatly limiting lubrication property. Here, we reported a multifunctional nanoplatform system (6S-NP), which integrated stimuli-responsive, self-renewable, supramolecular-synergistic, super-lubricating, sustained-retaining, and senescence-reversible features for achieving adaptive treatment in mechanically aggravated age-related joint disorders. Under shear, the host-guest bonds partially dissociated, which released and redistributed hydrated zwitterionic chains to rebuild a highly lubricated layer and minimize friction. When shear was removed, the bonds spontaneously reformed, the nanocrown assembled back, and the lubricating components were retained for the next cycle. This mechanically programmed dissociation-reassembly cycle maintained ultralow friction over repeated loading, achieving a >90% lower coefficient of friction than commercial hyaluronic acid. The reactive oxygen species-cleavable linkers enabled targeted drug release in inflammatory joints, effectively reducing IL-6/IL-1β, protecting extracellular matrix integrity, and reversing chondrocyte senescence. In load-driven knee osteoarthritis and frequency-driven temporomandibular joint osteoarthritis model, 6S-NP preserved cartilage, suppressed inflammation, and improved joint morphology. The adaptable design principles of 6S-NP could also be extended to other mechanically and oxidatively stressed degenerative conditions, providing a broadly applicable therapeutic strategy.
authors: Yinuo Yang; Gengtian Sun; Jinna Ren; Yuguang Wang; Hongyu Zhang

title: Skene’s Gland Malignancy from Imaging Diagnosis to Management: A Narrative Review
abstract: Background/Objectives: Skene’s gland malignancies are extremely rare tumors of the female paraurethral region, known almost exclusively from case reports and small case series. Their diagnosis is often delayed because symptoms are nonspecific and may mimic benign periurethral disorders, urethral diverticula, primary urethral carcinoma or anterior vaginal wall tumors. This narrative review focuses on the role of imaging, particularly pelvic magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), in the diagnosis, differential diagnosis, staging and treatment planning of Skene’s gland malignancies, distinguishing evidence from confirmed Skene’s gland cases from evidence extrapolated from female urethral carcinoma. Methods: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus and Web of Science were searched on 27 September 2026 (publication years 2015–2026) and supplemented by reference-list screening; an explicit case definition was applied. Results: Of 191 records (93 after de-duplication), 17 reports of Skene’s gland malignancy were included (15 case reports or series and 2 systematic reviews); fewer than thirty cases have been published overall. Patients were mostly postmenopausal (median age about 70 years, range 45–91), presenting with an asymptomatic periurethral nodule, hematuria or vaginal bleeding, or lower urinary tract symptoms; no uniform staging system has been applied. Most tumors were prostatic-type adenocarcinomas treated by local excision alone; radiotherapy, chemotherapy or androgen deprivation were used mainly for nodal, metastatic or recurrent disease. After examination, ultrasonography can detect and characterize a paraurethral mass, whereas MRI best defines tumor epicenter, urethral, periurethral and anterior vaginal wall involvement and regional spread, and should precede cystourethroscopy and biopsy; CT and PET/CT are complementary for systemic staging. No single immunohistochemical marker establishes Skene’s gland origin. Conclusions: MRI is central to localizing and staging suspected Skene’s gland malignancy and thus to guiding biopsy and the choice between local excision and radical surgery, but most imaging recommendations are extrapolated from female urethral carcinoma and require validation in pooled multicenter data.
authors: Roxana-Denisa Capraș; Teodora Telecan; Lucas Tellier; Miana Gabriela Pop; Adriana Ioana Gaia‐Oltean

title: Smart hip implants: listening to the joint: evaluating biochemical sensors for early detection of peri-prosthetic infection and inflammation
abstract: Total hip implants are being placed in more patients than ever before, with numbers increasing yearly. As implants are increasingly given to younger, more active patients with longer life expectancy, the risk of failure increases. Infection and aseptic loosening are the main causes of hip implant failure and are difficult to detect at an early stage. Current diagnostic methods are often initiated after symptoms appear, delaying treatment and often complicating revision surgery. This thesis explores smart hip implants, implants equipped with integrated sensors, to facilitate earlier detection of hip implant failure. A review of 49 biomedical sensors and a stakeholder analysis identified several types of sensors capable of continuously measuring indicators of failure. Among these, acidity (pH) and reactive oxygen species (ROS) sensors emerged as promising and underdeveloped options. To evaluate their potential, the two types of sensors were tested in controlled laboratory environments designed to represent conditions surrounding a hip implant. Both demonstrated potential for detecting biochemical changes associated with infection and the underlying cause of aseptic loosening: inflammation. The tests also revealed challenges related to sensor performance in the complex hip environment. Together, the findings support the potential of integrating biochemical sensors into the hip implant. While technical, biological, and data safety related challenges remain, this work demonstrates that biochemical sensing in hip implants is both feasible and clinically meaningful. It outlines a pathway toward smart hip implants capable of continuously monitoring, enabling earlier failure detection and targeted clinical intervention, transforming long term patient outcomes.
authors: Helene Noordhuis

title: Smooth total variation regularization for interference detection and elimination (STRIDE) for MRI
abstract: Abstract Objective. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is increasingly required to operate near electronic devices that emit dynamic electromagnetic interference (EMI). Existing reference-channel EMI removal methods estimate a transfer function between EMI sensors and imaging coils from the measured data alone, and do not use prior knowledge about the structure of MR images. We develop and validate an EMI removal method that uses the inherent spatial smoothness of MR images as an additional prior, demonstrated on a head-only 0.5 T scanner. Approach. Smooth total variation regularization for interference detection and elimination (STRIDE) operates in the image domain. For each image column, EMI sensor data are combined and subtracted from the imaging coil data such that the L 2 norm of the total variation (TV) along the readout direction is minimized. This exploits the smoothness of MR images, a property well-known in compressed sensing but not previously used in EMI removal. STRIDE was evaluated on phantom and in-vivo brain datasets under EMI scenarios replicating sources encountered at our affiliated hospitals, and compared against two implementations of External Dynamic Interference Estimation and Removal (EDITER). Main results. STRIDE produced visually better EMI removal and generally higher temporal signal-to-noise ratio than both EDITER implementations, with comparable EMI removal percentage. STRIDE also resulted in lower or equal root-mean-square error than both EDITER implementations in all 8 phantom EMI conditions tested. These results held across both phantom and in-vivo datasets. Significance. STRIDE shows that incorporating known properties of MR images into the EMI removal problem provides meaningful improvements over methods that rely on measured data alone. The approach is deterministic, training-free, sequence-independent, and compatible with existing EMI sensor hardware. STRIDE therefore extends reference-channel EMI removal to scenarios where existing methods fail, particularly point-of-care and interventional MRI outside fully shielded environments, providing a deterministic, training-free alternative to machine-learning approaches.
authors: Alexander Mertens; Diego F. Martinez; Amgad Louka; Ying Yang; Chad Harris; Ian R. O. Connell

title: Spatially Configurable Conformal Sensor Integration on an Ultra‐Fine Metallic Needle for Minimally Invasive Deep‐Tissue Oxygen Monitoring
abstract: ABSTRACT Precise, real‐time biochemical measurement within deep biological tissue remains limited by the challenge of integrating mechanically robust sensing architectures into minimally invasive needle platforms. Here, we report a multi‐point oxygen‐sensing ultra‐fine clinical needle (MO‐UFN, 30‐gauge, approximately 0.3 mm in diameter), fabricated by conformally integrating a microscale flexible thin‐film electrochemical oxygen sensor array onto a clinical needle. The device provides lithographically defined sensing and insulating regions along the needle surface while preserving the ultra‐small needle diameter. Five‐site oxygen sensing was demonstrated through electrochemical characterization in solution and time‐resolved measurement in a hypoxia‐mimicking hydrogel phantom. Ex vivo insertion testing and short‐term in vitro cytocompatibility assessment further supported the mechanical and biological feasibility of the platform under the tested conditions. This work establishes a spatially configurable needle‐based sensing architecture for minimally invasive biochemical monitoring in heterogeneous deep‐tissue environments.
authors: Bokyung Seo; Jaeho Park; Yongrok Jeong; Ji‐Hwan Ha; Junseong Ahn; Jimin Gu; Su A Park; Ilwoo Jun; Kichul Lee; Inkyu Park

title: Staphylococcus epidermidis-associated brain abscess following endovascular treatment of a ruptured intracranial aneurysm: potential immune-inflammatory mechanisms—a case report and literature review
abstract: Background Endovascular treatment(EVT) is a key therapeutic approach for ruptured intracranial Aneurysms; however, postoperative brain abscesses are extremely rare, and their pathogenesis and optimal treatment strategies remain unclear. This article reports a case of a Staphylococcus epidermidis -associated brain abscess that developed following stent-assisted coil embolization for subarachnoid hemorrhage caused by a ruptured anterior communicating artery aneurysm and discusses the underlying immune and inflammatory mechanisms as well as treatment strategies. Case presentation A 49-year-old man underwent stent-assisted coil embolization for subarachnoid Hemorrhage(SAH) from a ruptured anterior communicating artery aneurysm. Recovered well from operation and discharged. He, however, presented on the 34th postoperative day with a high-grade fever, headache, nausea, and vomiting. Brain imaging showed a brain abscess in the left frontal lobe, approximately 42 mm × 27 mm. However, there were no clear signs of severe neurological deterioration or a critical phase of cerebral herniation. Laboratory tests revealed high white blood cell and neutrophil counts, low lymphocyte counts, and variable reductions in CD3+, CD4+, and CD8+ T cells, CD19+ and CD20+ B cells, and Natural Killer cells(NK cells). Meanwhile, IL-1β, IL-6, TNF- α, and IL-10 levels increased, indicating deep immunological and inflammatory changes during infection. Inflammatory and immune markers improved slightly after antimicrobial therapy, but clinical symptoms persisted, and robot-assisted stereotactic abscess drainage was performed. A culture of pus grew methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus epidermidis (MRSE). Whole-genome sequencing confirmed the species and ST2 subtype and genetic features associated with β-lactam resistance. Initially, based on the consultation findings, meropenem and metronidazole were empirically administered as broad-spectrum antibiotics; after MRSE was confirmed, treatment was switched to vancomycin, and the patient’s clinical symptoms and laboratory parameters gradually improved. Postoperative imaging showed no recurrence of abscess, and the patient was in satisfactory general condition and no aftereffects whatsoever at six months’ follow-up. Conclusion We present a case report of an isolated brain abscess due to Staphylococcus epidermidis that developed after EVT of a ruptured intracranial aneurysm, which is a novel and clinically rare case. It also provides new clinical evidence for understanding this type of rare complication and optimizing treatment strategies.
authors: Xufeng Sun; Qile Sun; Shenao Li; Jiahao Zhang; Xiaolin Xu; Yueyang Peng; 温志峰

title: Strangulated Obturator Hernia with Intestinal Perforation in a Nonagenarian: A Case Report and Management Challenge
abstract: Introduction: Obturator hernia is a rare type of pelvic hernia, representing less than 1% of all abdominal hernias. It predominantly affects frail, elderly, multiparous women, leading to high morbidity and mortality rates due to diagnostic delays and the frequency of strangulation. Case Presentation: We report the case of a 95-year-old woman. She presented with a four-day history of obstructive syndrome Associated with pain on the inner thigh. Vital signs were normal except for a heart rate of 95 beats per minute. Clinical examination revealed a distended, tympanic abdomen and free hernia orifices and a positive Howship-Romberg sign. Laboratory tests showed leukocytosis (14,000/mm³) and elevated C-reactive protein (100 mg/L) in front of this clinical presentation an obturator hernia was suspected and an abdominal computed tomography (CT) scan confirmed a small bowel obstruction caused by a left obturator hernia, with no signs of bowel compromise. Management and Outcome: The patient was emergently transferred to the operating room. A sub-umbilical midline laparotomy was performed. Exploration revealed a dilated small bowel proximal to an incarceration in the left obturator foramen. The incarcerated loop was carefully isolated with a tissue tape to protect the surgical field. Upon gentle extraction using a dissector, an 8-cm segment of non-viable small bowel with a 1-cm perforation was identified. A manual small bowel anastomosis was performed after small bowel resection. The hernia defect was repaired by closing the peritoneum with a single buried suture and reinforcing the area with a plasty using the adjacent round ligament. The postoperative period was good with transit resumption at day 4, we however noticed a fixed evisceration successfully treated with Vaseline gauze dressings and cutaneous approximation sutures. title: Supraventricular Tachycardia Associated with Cardiac Hemangioma on the Anterior Mitral Valve Leaflet: A Case Report
abstract: Background: Cardiac hemangiomas are exceedingly rare benign vascular tumors, representing <2% of primary cardiac tumors. Case Presentation: A 65-year-old female patient with a history of palpitations, hypothyroidism, and hypoparathyroidism presented with an acute onset of palpitations and dyspnea. On physical examination, the patient had regular tachycardia with clear and equal bilateral air entry. Initial laboratory tests and chest X-ray showed no acute abnormalities. An electrocardiogram (ECG) showed narrow-complex supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) with a heart rate of 170 bpm and a QRS duration of 80 ms, consistent with atrioventricular nodal reentrant tachycardia (AVNRT), which was unresponsive to vagal maneuvers but was successfully converted with 6 mg of intravenous adenosine. Multimodality imaging, including transthoracic echocardiography (TTE), transesophageal echocardiography (TEE), and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR), was performed. TTE showed a fixed, normoechoic mass (1-1.2 cm) at the aortomitral junction involving the A2 segment of the anterior mitral leaflet; TEE described a nonobstructive heterogeneous echodensity (17 × 6 mm) at the leaflet base near the intervalvular fibrosa; CMR showed a 13 × 11 mm arched structure on the anterior mitral leaflet, beneath the aortic valve, with cavity-like perfusion, T2 hyperintensity, and late gadolinium enhancement. Surgical resection was performed 3 weeks after the diagnosis, and histopathology showed a remodeled remnant hemangioma. Postoperatively, continuous telemetry and long-term clinical and serial ECG follow-up confirmed complete resolution of the arrhythmia without tumor recurrence. Conclusion: We report a cardiac hemangioma on the left atrial side of the anterior mitral leaflet, extending slightly into the left atrial cavity without obstructing blood flow, in a patient with episodes of supraventricular tachycardia. She recovered well after tumor resection, with no clinical signs of arrhythmia recurrence.
authors: Tia Khadra; Rita Balech; Anthony Saadeh; Maribelle Khoury; Tony Bechara; Elie Bitar; Naji Abi Rached
venue: Asploro Journal of Biomedical and Clinical Case Reports

title: SurgGraph: Quantitative Laparoscopic Video Understanding via Geometry-Grounded Scene Graphs
abstract: Surgical videos are a primary resource for teaching trainees anatomy, tool usage, and procedural skills. Yet learning from them at scale requires systems that understand surgical scenes. Existing approaches fall short: vision-language models lack fine-grained domain reasoning, task-specific models do not generalize, and prior scene graphs omit clinically meaningful detail. We present SurgGraph, a training-free pipeline that generates quantitative scene graphs from surgical videos. Operating on segmentation masks and depth maps, SurgGraph encodes each clinically meaningful relation (attachment, occlusion, separation, tool actions) as a tuple whose numeric value quantifies the relation's extent over time. Technical evaluations show more precise scene understanding than state-of-the-art surgical VLM baselines. We then build SurgGraphQA, a proof-of-concept learning application that retrieves meaningful and boundary-case exemplars and generates visual explanations and feedback. A study with 17 medical students and 2 resident surgeons shows significant learning gains, demonstrating its educational value.
authors: Jingying Wang; Rosiana Natalie; Marquise D. Singleterry; Filippos Bellos; Brian George; Gurjit Sandhu; Jason J. Corso; Anhong Guo; Vitaliy Popov; Xu Wang

title: Surgical Approaches and Prognostic Factors in Superior Sulcus Tumors
abstract: Objective: To evaluate surgical approaches, clinical characteristics, and prognostic factors in patients with superior sulcus tumors (SSTs) and to assess survival outcomes according to resection type.Materials and Methods: This study included 20 patients with histopathologically confirmed SSTs who underwent surgical treatment between 1997 and 2004. Eight patients were evaluated retrospectively and twelve prospectively. Demographic, clinical, radiological, histopathological, and treatment-related data were analyzed. Survival outcomes were assessed using the Kaplan–Meier method, and comparisons between groups were performed using the log-rank test.Results: All patients were male, with a mean age of 53 years. Pain was the most common presenting symptom (100%). Tumors were predominantly located in the right hemithorax (75%). Lobectomy was performed in 85% of patients, while 15% underwent wedge resection due to limited pulmonary reserve. Postoperative complications occurred in 45% of patients, with atelectasis being the most frequent. Squamous cell carcinoma was the most common histopathological subtype. Median survival was longer in the lobectomy group compared with the wedge resection group (38 vs. 14 months), although the difference did not reach statistical significance (p=0.075). Patients with nodal involvement and vertebral invasion had poorer survival.Conclusion: Extent of resection, nodal status, and local invasion remain key determinants of prognosis in SST. Lobectomy was associated with more favorable survival outcomes than limited resection, although these findings should be interpreted cautiously. Despite advances in multimodality treatment, prognostic factors continue to guide clinical decision-making in this complex disease.
authors: Hüseyin Eren; Tamer Altınok; Abdullah İrfan Taştepe

title: Synergistic Li + -functionalized Mo 2 CT X MXene and polyaniline composite for rapid and stable moisture sensing in wearable wound monitoring application
abstract: Abstract Managing optimal moisture balance is essential for chronic wound healing, yet current clinical assessments are often subjective and intermittent. This study reports the development of a high-performance, flexible resistive moisture sensor designed for real-time, quantitative wound monitoring. The active sensing layer consists of a lithium-ion (Li + ) functionalized Mo 2 CT X MXene and polyaniline (PANI) composite. Li + intercalation was utilized to expand the MXene interlayer spacing, enhancing water adsorption and ion transport. Simultaneously, in situ polymerized PANI was introduced to provide stable proton-conductive pathways. Current–voltage characterization verified that the Li + –Mo 2 CT X /PANI composite forms robust Ohmic contacts with the electrodes, exhibiting over a 40-fold enhancement in baseline electrical conductance compared to pristine Mo 2 CT X . The composite was integrated onto screen-printed circular interdigitated electrodes on a flexible PET substrate and encapsulated with poly(diallyldimethylammonium chloride) (PDAC). This protective PDAC layer acts as a semi-permeable moisture-diffusion barrier that regulates water molecule transport, prevents surface fouling and uncontrolled hydration saturation, and ensures environmental stability without compromising response speed. The sensor demonstrates a linear response across a wide relative humidity (RH) range of 20%–80%, featuring sensitivity of approximately 2.0 Δ R /%ΔRH, with a rapid response time of ∼1 s and a recovery time of ∼11 s. The device demonstrates high mechanical flexibility, and stable operation over a 15 d period. Real-time assessments using finger-touch tests and PVA-hydrogel wound models successfully distinguished between dry, normal, and wet clinical states. The superior performance is attributed to the synergistic effects of Li + -assisted interlayer hydration, Grotthuss-type proton hopping, and moisture-induced PANI protonation. These findings position the Li + –Mo 2 CT X /PANI composite as a promising candidate for next-generation smart dressings in digital wound management.
authors: Syahirah Umairah Mahadi; Siti Nabila Aidit; Norazriena Yusoff; Sharifah Fatmadiana Wan Muhamad Hatta; Yasmin Abdul Wahab; Fazliyatul Azwa Md Rezali

title: TVT MESH BLADDER EXTRUSION: REPAIR BY COMBINED LAPAROSCOPIC-ENDOSCOPIC APPROACH
abstract: Objective: To present a combined laparoscopic-endoscopic surgical approach for the treatment of a TVT bladder extrusion.Description: A 79-year-old woman with a history of TVT mesh placement for stress urinary incontinence.Five years later, she returned to the clinic with urgency urinary incontinence and pain.Ultrasound and cystoscopy revealed a mesh extrusion at the bladder dome of approximately 1 cm.Given the location of the extrusion, a combined laparoscopic-endoscopic approach was used.Clinically, after one year of follow-up, the pain has subsided, with mild residual urge and stress incontinence.This is an effective and reproducible approach for the management of TVT mesh bladder extrusions with difficult transvaginal access.

title: Tail-Risk-Aware Information Guidance for Angles-Only Spacecraft Rendezvous Under Markovian Measurement Outages
abstract: Angles-only spacecraft rendezvous couples guidance and navigation because trajectory geometry changes both observability and measurement availability. This paper develops tail-risk-aware guidance for geometry-dependent, burst-correlated optical outages. A planar benchmark uses explicit Markov measurement-arrival scenarios and conditional value at risk to shape terminal navigation uncertainty, followed by independent 10,000-run validation. Relative to expected availability guidance, the selected trajectory reduces 95% conditional value at risk by 39.2% and 99% conditional value at risk by 15.7%, at 35.8% higher maneuver expenditure. A separate 200-run nonlinear three-dimensional holdout uses two-body-plus-oblateness truth dynamics, azimuth/elevation sensing, maneuver errors, unscented Kalman filtering, and covariance-weighted terminal feedback. The risk-aware trajectory increases realized measurement availability from 20.7% to 56.1%, reduces mean longest outage from 14.39 to 6.80 epochs, and reduces median and 95th-percentile terminal estimation error from 49.64m to 0.89m and 223.24m to 21.93m, respectively, while mission success remains statistically comparable. This demonstrates that the operational payoff is navigation robustness rather than consistent superior terminal accuracy. Because approach-corridor constraints are monitored but not enforced, the study does not establish safety-compliant proximity operations.
authors: Archit Das

title: Tapering to Enhance the Performance of Nanowire-Based Fluorescent Biosensors
abstract: High-refractive-index nanowires are of interest for signal enhancement in fluorescence-based biosensing. Here, through electromagnetic modelling, we demonstrate substantial fluorescence signal enhancement by incorporating a tapered section into a cylindrical nanowire and investigate two complementary tapering configurations to address practical implementation challenges. Under near-normal excitation, the excitation enhancement increases approximately linearly with taper length, reaching more than three times that of the corresponding non-tapered nanowire at a taper length of 8000 nm. In a non-imaging signal detection scheme using a low numerical aperture (NA), the proposed tapered nanowire achieves more than three orders of magnitude enhancement in fluorescence signal compared with a planar biosensor. Thus, the tapered nanowire should enable efficient fluorescence detection using compact, low-NA optical configuration. In imaging mode, similarly as for non-tapered nanowires, imaging sharpness beyond conventional microscopy limitations is obtained when imaging from the non-tapered nanowire end, while strongly increased excitation enhancement is simultaneously obtained when exciting from the opposite, tapered end.
authors: Farhana Akter Mou; Nicklas Anttu

title: Technical Feasibility of a Multimodal Electro-Optical and Infrared Imaging Pipeline for Postoperative Wound Assessment After Total Knee Arthroplasty: Formative Evaluation Study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Early detection and monitoring of wound-related complications after total knee arthroplasty (TKA) are critical to optimize outcomes and preserve implants. Conventional postoperative monitoring relies on in-person assessment and patient-reported symptoms, which may delay recognition. Noncontact imaging acquired in the clinic or at home offers a potential route to earlier and more consistent assessment. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the technical feasibility and performance of a multimodal AI system integrating electro-optical (EO) and infrared imaging for postoperative wound assessment following TKA and to explore clinical factors associated with early complications. METHODS: We conducted a single-center prospective cohort study of 749 patients undergoing primary TKA. Patients underwent standardized multimodal data collection at scheduled postoperative visits. EO-based models localized surgical landmarks and segmented complication-oriented tissue states; a fine-tuned vision-language model provided protocol verification and contextual visual reasoning. EO landmarks mapped to thermal space via deterministic alignment, followed by infrared region-of-interest segmentation and thermal classification. Each module was evaluated on a defined held-out set. The thermal classifier was assessed out-of-fold under 5-fold cross-validation with folds grouped by patient, in knees imaged on postoperative day 14 or later. Discrimination for clinician-adjudicated infection-related complications served as the primary outcome. Comorbidities and baseline laboratory values were explored for associations with complications. RESULTS: Among 749 patients, 26 (3.5%) had a clinician-adjudicated infection-related complication. On held-out evaluation, the EO landmark detector reached a sensitivity of 0.967 (95% CI 0.954-0.979) and positive predictive value of 0.955 (95% CI 0.940-0.970), and the wound-tissue segmentation model reached a sensitivity of 0.845 (95% CI 0.833-0.857) and positive predictive value of 0.759 (95% CI 0.744-0.772). Infrared region-of-interest extraction isolated the surgical field with a mean intersection-over-union of 0.985 (SD 0.008; 95% CI 0.984-0.986) across 178 held-out patients. The trained thermal classifier discriminated infected scans with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.978 (95% CI 0.959-0.992) in out-of-fold, patient-grouped cross-validation. At a representative operating point, sensitivity was 0.808 (95% CI 0.65-0.92), specificity 0.974 (95% CI 0.96-0.99), positive predictive value 0.618 (95% CI 0.49-0.78), and negative predictive value 0.990 (95% CI 0.98-1.00). Exploratory analyses showed nominal associations of chronic kidney disease and diabetes mellitus with postoperative complications that did not remain significant after multiplicity correction. CONCLUSIONS: In this formative study, a multimodal EO and infrared imaging pipeline demonstrated technical feasibility for postoperative wound assessment following TKA, providing noncontact discrimination of infection-related complications that compared favorably with established adjuncts. This work provides proof-of-concept for multimodal imaging-based assessment and defines the technical requirements for the prospective, multicenter external validation needed to establish clinical utility.
authors: Tej Sanibh Ranade; Emily Hu; Kadambari Beelwar; Sandeep Boddeda; Praharsha Mulpur; Adarsh Annapareddy; A V Gurava Reddy

title: Temporal signatures of prediction error reveal external forces on an embodied robot
abstract: Embodied robots must distinguish self-generated sensory consequences from externally caused perturbations. In predictive processing, such deviation is accounted for as prediction error, but it is commonly treated primarily as a signal to be minimised. Here, we test whether the temporal profile of load-related prediction error provides diagnostic information about the type of physical interaction a robot experiences. We trained and evaluated windowed multilayer perceptrons to predict servo current, used as a proxy for joint load, from proprioceptive, inertial, and servo current history. The training data were recorded during random movements of tilt and pan servo motors of a robotic head. The best model was deployed in the robot in real time and evaluated across free movements and external perturbations, including brief pushes, sustained forces, and obstacle interactions. Prediction error and raw current time series were summarised using features capturing magnitude statistics, temporal structure, and signal shape. A random forest classifier was then used to classify the conditions based on the features. Different interaction conditions produced distinct profiles that supported robust perturbation classification with high cross-validated accuracy. Classification performance for prediction error was equal to the classification of raw current. The results suggest that load-related prediction error is not only a residual of imperfect prediction. Its temporal structure can act as an embodied self-monitoring signal for classifying physical interactions.
authors: Pierre Klintefors; Birger Johansson; Christian Balkenius

title: Testicular Necrosis Following Inguinal Herniorrhaphy: A Case Report
abstract: Testicular necrosis is a rare complication associated with inguinal herniorrhaphy.The main blood supply to the testicles comes from the testicular artery (internal spermatic artery), which branches off from the abdominal aorta; the external spermatic artery, which branches off from the inferior epigastric artery; and the arteries supplying the vas deferens.The testicles are extremely resistant to necrosis.Although early surgical intervention may reverse testicular ischemia, delayed diagnosis can necessitate orchiectomy.We report a case of testicular necrosis shortly after radical inguinal herniorrhaphy requiring orchiectomy following emergency exploration.A 73-year-old man presented to our hospital 18 months after undergoing robot-assisted radical prostatectomy.He developed a left inguinal hernia following radical prostatectomy and subsequently underwent inguinal herniorrhaphy.On the fifth postoperative day, the patient presented to the hospital complaining of pain and swelling in the left testicle.Physical examination revealed swelling of the left scrotum, and scrotal ultrasonography showed no blood flow in the left testicle.Emergency scrotal exploration for suspected testicular necrosis revealed scrotal skin thickening and black discoloration of the testis and epididymis without evidence of strangulation.Owing to absent testicular blood flow on intraoperative ultrasonography, left orchiectomy was performed.Histopathological examination revealed hemorrhage and ischemic necrosis.When scrotal pain, erythema, or swelling develops after inguinal surgery, prompt evaluation with scrotal ultrasonography is warranted, and the potential need for emergency surgical exploration should be considered.
authors: Takuya Yashima; Yoshihiro Nakagami; Kazuhiko Oshinomi; Masakazu Nagata; Takashi Fukagai

title: The Lived Experience of Chinese Patients With Somatic Symptom Disorder: An Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis
abstract: Aim To deeply explore the subjective illness experience of patients with Somatic Symptom Disorder (SSD) throughout the entire course from the initial onset of symptoms and repeated medical consultations to receiving psychological interventions. Methods Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis (IPA) was adopted. Purposive sampling was used to recruit 8 patients meeting the diagnostic criteria for somatic symptom disorder in DSM-5 from the clinical psychology department of a tertiary general hospital between June 2025 and December 2025. Semi-structured in-depth interviews were conducted with these patients. After verbatim transcription of interview recordings, data analysis was carried out in accordance with the six-step coding procedure of IPA. Results Four main superordinate themes emerged from data analysis: (a) Embodied processing of distress and enduring somatic imprinting; (b) An unsafe living world co-existing with Symptoms; (c) Tracing symptom origins and the journey of help‑seeking; (d) Self‑growth within the lived experience of symptom co‑existence Conclusion The underlying driving force for patients with SSD is fear of death. These individuals frequently endure intense feelings of helplessness and insecurity, yet they consistently attribute their symptoms to physical pathology. Healthcare providers may obtain medical histories from patients with SSD to assess their emotional difficulties, family-related factors, personality traits, and illness-related beliefs. Furthermore, clinicians ought to provide feedback on physical-examination findings, refrain from redundant investigations, and validate patients’ distress through empathic responding. It is essential to reframe the meaning of symptoms: draw connections between symptoms and stress- or lifestyle-related triggers; illustrate the anxiety-to-illness transition pathway, alongside the vicious cycle that sustains somatic symptom responses.
authors: Xue Y, Chen F.

title: The Role of Laparoscopic Surgery in Abdominal Trauma: A Case Report and Review
abstract: Background: Abdominal trauma accounts for approximately 15 % of trauma admissions and remains a leading cause of preventable mortality.Traditionally managed by exploratory laparotomy of which up to 40 % are non-therapeutic the paradigm has shifted toward minimally invasive approaches.Laparoscopy now demonstrates diagnostic accuracy rates of 96-98 % and enables therapeutic repair in hemodynamically stable patients, resulting in reduced morbidity, infection rates, and length of stay.Case Presentation: A 23-year-old male sustained blunt abdominal trauma following a motorbike accident.He was hemodynamically stable with a positive FAST scan and CT evidence of hemoperitoneum and mesenteric contusion without solid-organ injury.Diagnostic laparoscopy revealed 6.3 L of hemoperitoneum and a through-and-through mesenteric tear 20 cm proximal to the ileocecal junction.Hemostasis was achieved using V-Loc 2.0 sutures with peritoneal lavage and drain placement.One unit of PRBC was transfused.Postoperatively, hemoglobin rose from 7.6 to 12.0 g/dL and CRP fell from 64 to 21 mg/L.The patient tolerated oral intake within 24 h and was discharged on day 4 without complications.Discussion/Review: Nontherapeutic laparotomies decreased by 58%, postoperative complication rates decreased by four times, and hospital stays decreased from 10.8 to 3.9 days, according to a targeted literature review (2020-2025; 24 studies).Conclusion: Laparoscopy should be a mainstay of contemporary trauma therapy since it provides therapeutic benefit and diagnostic accuracy in stable trauma patients, lowering hospitalization and morbidity.
venue: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology

title: The effects of the arts and arts therapies on mental health outcomes of children and young people: a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Background There is growing evidence on the positive effects of the arts and arts therapies for mental health (MH) outcomes. This review aims to fill a research gap by establishing the evidence on the effects of arts-based interventions on selected MH outcomes for children and young people (CYP). Methods Our systematic review and meta-analysis included randomised controlled trials with CYP aged 5–24 years receiving any type of arts-based intervention. Five databases (CINAHL, Embase.com, MEDLINE, PsycINFO, and Web of Science) were searched for studies published between 1/1/2005 and 18/5/2025. Two reviewers independently screened all records and assessed risk-of-bias using Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB2) and certainty using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE). Data were initially extracted using the AI-assisted review tool Elicit and independently verified by two reviewers. All data were pooled using random-effects meta-analysis, and effect estimates for MH outcomes are summarised as Standardised Mean Differences (SMD) with 95% confidence intervals (CI). Heterogeneity was assessed using the I 2 statistic, with pre-specified subgroup and sensitivity analyses conducted to explore possible sources of inconsistency. This study is registered with PROSPERO (CRD420251015352). Findings One hundred trials across 29 countries involving CYP aged 5–24 years with a range of health conditions, alongside healthy populations, were included in this review. Based on studies with some concerns or high risk-of-bias, arts-based interventions were found to reduce individuals' depression (1.06 SMD lower [95% CI 0.45–1.67, n=1655, I 2 = 97%]), anxiety (0.75 SMD lower [95% CI 0.57–0.94, n=3898, I 2 = 87%]), and increase individuals' wellbeing (0.53 SMD higher [95% CI 0.26–0.80, n=538, I 2 = 49%]) and quality of life (0.54 SMD higher [95% CI 0.25–0.83, n=441, I 2 = 53%]) on average post-intervention. Certainty of results relating to wellbeing and quality of life was low due to imprecision and concerns about risk of bias, and very low for depression and anxiety due to additional inconsistency associated with high heterogeneity. Findings relating to anxiety were further supported by biomarker data (blood pressure and heart rate) with moderate certainty. Interpretation This systematic review provides a comprehensive synthesis of evidence from randomised controlled trials assessing the effects of a wide variety arts-based interventions on the mental health of CYP. Although the strength of any conclusions is limited by heterogeneity, imprecision and bias of the studies assessed, average effects were similar to those typically reported for established non-arts-based psychosocial interventions, including talking therapies. These findings advance our understanding of arts-based therapeutic strategies for CYP's MH. Further high-quality trials, with larger sample sizes and standardised outcome measures and timepoints, are needed to improve the certainty of evidence in this area. Funding UKRI.
authors: Pui Sze Cheung; Sarah Rhodes; Elisabeth Bahr; Wilfried Lakena; Nisha L. Sajnani; Nils Fietje; Vicky Karkou

title: The intersection of Pediatric dentistry and Obstructive sleep apnea – An overview
abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) in children also referred as “Pediatric obstructive sleep apnea” (POSA) is the most commonly observable clinical condition, characterized by adeno-tonsillar hypertrophy and found frequently associated with obesity and craniofacial malformations. It is constituted by different pathophysiological mechanisms, clinical features, and treatment modalities. If not treated, POSA leads to significant morbidity, including neurocognitive complications, cardiovascular problems and growth impairment. Epigenetics is a novel concept and can be defined as heritable alterations in gene expression patterns that are not directly encoded by modifications in the nucleotide genome sequence but by post-translational modifications in DNA and histone proteins and by the regulation of non-coding RNA. Although the domain epigenetics is considered as an exciting arena in realm of biology, its relation with POSA is still in budding stage. Therefore, aim of the present article is to enlighten the literature pertaining to current evidence regarding the prevalence, pathophysiology, diagnostic methods, multidisciplinary management and brief note the role of epigenetics in POSA.
authors: Tuhin A Gupta; Nagaveni NB; Sumedha Kundu Chaudhary; Kanishka Gautam; Isha Goel

title: The relationship between alienation appraisals and trauma
abstract: Systematic Review Research suggests that alienation appraisals, defined as feeling disconnected from the self and others, mediate the relationship between traumatic events and subsequent PTSD symptoms. A systematic search of 6 databases found 463 studies, 9 met full inclusion criteria. Studies were quality assessed using the QATSDD. A random effects meta-analysis for the relationship between alienation appraisals and PTSD symptoms showed a total effect size of r = .57, with 95% confidence intervals between .46 and .66 (Z = 8.41, p < .001). The effect size was large, suggesting that as alienation appraisals increase, PTSD symptoms increase. Although a strong, positive relationship was found between alienation and PTSD symptoms, the mechanism of this relationship remains unclear. Limitations included significant heterogeneity and correlational data. Large-scale Cognitive models highlight the importance of negative trauma appraisals in maintaining symptoms of PTSD. The current study explored the role of alienation appraisals across student and clinical samples, assessing if alienation appraisals significantly mediated the relationship between cumulative trauma and trauma-related distress. Secondly, this study explored if alexithymia, social support and loneliness could also mediate the relationship between cumulative trauma and distress, clarifying the role of alienation. Mediation and hierarchical regression models were tested with questionnaire data from student (N = 100) and clinical samples (N = 93). In the student sample, alienation (B = 1.27) fully mediated the relationship between cumulative trauma and posttraumatic stress, but not depression. When alexithymia, social support and loneliness were entered as parallel mediators, only alienation appraisals (B = 1.03) were significant. For the clinical sample, alienation appraisals (β = .53) were the only significant predictor of posttraumatic stress symptoms whilst alienation appraisals (β = .75), and to a lesser extent, social support (β = .19) and loneliness (β = .30), significantly predicted depression. Clinical implications and limitations are discussed.
authors: Rachel McIlveen

title: Total-field atomic magnetometry using an elliptically-polarized frequency-modulated light beam for geomagnetic-field applications
abstract: We investigate an all-optical scheme for high-sensitivity measurements of the Earth's scale magnetic field ($B$). The scheme is based on the Bell-Bloom technique with frequency-modulated light. A single elliptically polarized light beam is used both for pumping the alkali-metal atoms and probing Larmor precession of their spins under the external magnetic field. In contrast to many other high-sensitivity magnetometry schemes based on nonlinear polarization rotation of the light, the proposed approach enables the observation of magnetic resonance via changes in the light-beam ellipticity parameter. The approach has been validated in experiments with a vertical-cavity surface-emitting laser, irradiating a $0.125$ cm$^3$ cesium vapor cell filled with a buffer gas. In the current experimental conditions, the achieved sensitivity is estimated at $220$ fT/$\surd$Hz under $B$$\,\approx\,$$50$ $μ$T, while the shot-noise floor corresponds to $\approx\,$$20$ fT/$\surd$Hz. The bandwidth is estimated at $\approx\,$$1$ kHz. The proposed simple and robust single-beam scheme is well suited for miniaturization and is therefore particularly promising for the development of compact, highly sensitive, low-power-consumption atomic magnetometers for a wide range of applications in the geomagnetic field.
authors: Denis V. Brazhnikov; A. O. Makarov; K. S. Kozlova; M. A. Rusina; A. M. Mikhailov; V. A. Vasiliev; E. V. Tanakov; Andrei Goncharov; M. A. Bobrov; Ya.N. Kovach; A. A. Blokhin; N. A. Maleev; S. A. Blokhin

title: Towards clinical communication training with LLM-based conversational virtual patients and automatic evaluation systems
abstract: Clinical communication is a fundamental skill that impacts patient satisfaction, treatment adherence, and clinical outcomes. Traditional training methods, such as standardized patients (SPs) or virtual standardized patients (VSPs), face barriers including high costs, logistical complexity, and lack of spontaneous interaction. This study addresses these challenges by developing a scalable alternative based on Large Language Models (LLMs) to train medical students in the anamnesis phase. We developed an interactive Conversational Virtual Patient (CVP) system, understood here as a text- and voice-based simulated patient without graphical embodiment. The conversational logic is orchestrated as an explicit state machine over the interview, implemented with LangGraph, a graph-based framework in which each node performs one processing stage and a shared state persists across turns. Clinical consistency across the interview is maintained by a semantic memory layer implemented with LangMem, a library that stores clinical facts as vector embeddings and retrieves them by similarity. Performance is measured by an automatic evaluation module assessing 24 communication criteria derived from validated instruments such as the Communication Assessment Tool (CAT) and the Communication Skills Scale (CSS). The platform was validated with 21 participants, comprising 9 eighth-semester medical students, 11 practising physicians, and 1 expert in healthcare technology. All sessions were conducted in Spanish. Considering the student cohort, which addresses the educational utility of the tool, the system obtained a Chatbot Usability Questionnaire (CUQ) score of 82.3/100 and an average acceptance of the automated feedback of 4.50/5. The physician and expert cohort, which provides expert clinical validation, obtained 96.5/100 and 4.21/5 respectively, yielding a pooled usability score of 90.4/100 and a pooled feedback acceptance of 4.33/5. In an exploratory comparison against eleven physician ratings of the same interviews, rank agreement was highest for “Interest” ( $$\rho = 0.64$$ ) and lowest for “Completeness” ( $$\rho = 0.09$$ ), and the automated scores fell below the physician scores in every dimension. No dimension attained significance after correction for six comparisons, and the confidence intervals were wide, so these coefficients describe the observed sample rather than the agreement attainable in general. The results support the feasibility of the system as a complement to traditional medical training, providing immediate and standardized feedback. Given the sample size and the single-institution design, these findings should be read as an initial validation of feasibility and acceptability rather than as evidence of pedagogical efficacy.
authors: Andrea Bayona; Rubén Manrique; Christian Grévisse

title: Training the Next Generation of Future Surgical Residents: A Scoping Review and Proposal for an Undergraduate Curriculum From the Italian Polispecialistic Society of Young Surgeons
abstract: AIM: The transition from medical school to surgical residency is marked by a persistent gap between theoretical instruction and clinical readiness. In Italy, variability in training programs across centers creates persistent gaps in residents' medical education. Scientific societies are asked to identify current training gaps and define the core competencies required for effective surgical training. We propose an undergraduate curriculum to support last-year medical students in Italy. METHODS: A scoping review of the literature focusing on structured surgical curricula for undergraduate medical students was conducted. A suggested "curriculum" was introduced at the 2025 Congress of the Italian Polispecialistic Society of Young Surgeons (SPIGC) in Bari, Italy. RESULTS: The SPIGC curriculum includes seven domains: (1) soft skills: communication, informed consent, and interdisciplinary collaboration; (2) clinical and diagnostic skills: outpatient clinic management and perioperative care; (3) hygiene, prevention, healthcare systems; (4) technical skills; (5) emergency and trauma surgery; (6) perioperative management, integrating Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) protocols, nutritional assessment, and infections; (7) evidence-based medicine and recommendations. The SPIGC curriculum highlights the importance of simulation labs, hands-on workshops, and online learning, while providing clear pathways for fellowships or masters. It also introduces artificial intelligence (AI) systems as a modern learning tool, while highlighting the importance of their safe and responsible use. CONCLUSIONS: The SPIGC curriculum may provide a structured plan to improve surgical education for medical students in Italy and to align it with international standards. Its acceptability and impact on training quality and patient outcomes remain to be evaluated through future consensus and prospective studies.
authors: Gianmario Edoardo Poto; Marianna Peruffo; Manfredi Giuseppe Anzaldi; Andrea Castaldi; Gianmarco Elia; Giulia Misasi; Giulia Rovero; Martina Lenzi; Elisa Bassan; Francesca Gigola; Domenico Soriero; Giosuè Giordano Incognito; Gennaro Melone; Roberto Cirillo; Marco Angrisani; Maria Rosaria Mastrangeli; Alessandro Coppola; Michele Maruccia; Gaetano Gallo; Arcangelo Picciariello; Alessandro Pasculli; Ludovico Carbone

title: Twelve tips on engaging effectively with emotion in Health Professions Education
abstract: Emotion is a ubiquitous component of the clinical environment that profoundly influences cognition, academic achievement, and professional identity. This Twelve Tips article highlights the importance of dismantling outdated models of emotions in health professions education and recognizing affect as a fundamental driver of clinical performance and learning. The article provides a practical guide to establishing relational trust, normalizing affective responses, cultivating emotional granularity, and developing adaptive emotion regulation skills for both learners and faculty, with consideration of the essential boundaries of the educator role and the value of shared meaning-making.
authors: Lynnea M. Mills; Jerusalem Merkebu

title: Type I Choledochal Cyst in a Three-Year-Old with Recurrent Vomiting and Pancreatitis: A Case Report
abstract: Introduction: Choledochal cysts are rare congenital dilatations of the biliary tree that may present with nonspecific gastrointestinal symptoms in children, posing diagnostic challenges. Case Report: We report a 3-year-old girl who presented with recurrent vomiting and abdominal pain. Initial laboratory testing revealed a mildly elevated lipase. An abdominal ultrasound demonstrated a pancreatic cyst; the patient was discharged with outpatient follow-up. She returned with worsening symptoms and a markedly elevated lipase of 2,247 U/L (reference range, < 160 U/L). Computed tomography subsequently revealed a type I choledochal cyst. She underwent operative resection with an uncomplicated postoperative course. Conclusion: Persistent gastrointestinal symptoms with uptrending lipase in children should prompt consideration of hepatobiliary etiologies. Choledochal cysts may be missed on initial presentation as the classic triad of jaundice, palpable abdominal mass, and right upper quadrant pain is present in a minority of cases.
authors: Dominic Diprinzio; Rance Del Mar
venue: Clinical Practice and Cases in Emergency Medicine

title: Understanding cognitive function in post-COVID-19 condition with fatigue: an interdisciplinary multimodal investigation
abstract: Abstract Lingering cognitive symptoms of post-COVID-19 condition (PCC) continue to challenge our understanding, highlighting the need for interdisciplinary research. We investigated whether individuals with PCC and fatigue differ from matched controls across neurocognitive, neuroimaging, and immunological measures, integrating these findings with qualitative phenomenological analyses through multimodal cross-analysis. Individuals with PCC and clinically significant fatigue (n=34), and age-, sex-, and education- matched controls recovered from COVID-19 without PCC (n=37) were included. Assessments encompassed physician evaluation, neuropsychological and functional tests, structural and functional MRI, immunological tests, and qualitative phenomenological analysis of interviews. Data were analyzed using established methods and an interdisciplinary cross-analysis to examine persistent cognitive symptoms in PCC. Group comparisons revealed subtle differences between individuals with PCC and controls, while neurocognitive performance and immunological markers remained within normative ranges. Modest differences in white-matter, myelin-related, and global brain measures were observed, alongside differences in associations between network connectivity and neurocognitive performance across groups, suggesting reduced network resilience rather than domain specific deficits. This pattern resonated with qualitative phenomenological findings: altered experiences of concentrating and difficulties to execute decisions and actions, despite preserved performance on standard neurocognitive tests. These findings suggest that cognitive symptoms in post-COVID-19 fatigue are associated with subtle neurobiological alterations not captured by standard cognitive assessments. In this highly fatigued sample, converging neuroimaging, neurocognitive and immunological findings point toward reduced network efficiency rather than overt cognitive impairment. Qualitative phenomenological analysis further highlighted altered modes of being in the world characterized by increased cognitive effort and difficulties executing decisions and actions.

title: Unraveling uterine carcinosarcoma:From population data to precision oncology in the pursuit of improving prognosis
abstract: Accordingly, the primary aim of this thesis is to analyze dedicated, largescale studies focusing exclusively on UCS, with specific attention to its incidence, treatment patterns, and prognosis. Secondary aims involve evaluating diagnostic accuracy, identifying prognostic determinants, assessing QoL outcomes, and exploring molecular targets. Collectively, such research is needed to thoroughly characterize the clinical and molecular profile of UCS, determine the benefits of available treatments, and understand the impact of therapeutic interventions on patients’ quality of life To address these aims, the outline of this thesis is as follows: Chapter 2 analyzes a nationwide cohort of patients diagnosed with UCS in the Netherlands between 2001 and 2021 by using data from the Dutch Cancer Registry (IKNL) and Dutch Pathology Registry (PALGA). The study aims to describe survival across two decades and to identify clinical and histopathological factors associated with these outcomes. The long-term, population‑based dataset also enables comparison between earlier and later cohorts and assesses the impact of the transition from FIGO 2009 to FIGO 2023 staging and evolving treatment strategies on prognosis. Chapter 3 aims to analyze the diagnostic accuracy of preoperative sampling methods in diagnosing UCS. The chapter evaluates the performance of aspiration biopsy, hysteroscopic biopsy, and dilation and curettage in identifying UCS, and examines cases with discrepant preoperative and postoperative diagnoses using the nationwide data from PALGA. Chapters 4 and 5 report findings from the prospective Carcinosarcoma of the Uterus Study (CUS), a registry initiated in 2016 at Erasmus MC, a tertiary referral center in the South-West Netherlands. The study collects detailed clinical, surgical, and histopathological data, and includes longitudinal QoL assessments at baseline, posttreatment, and one, two, and five years after therapy. In Chapter 4 the effect of the UCS and treatment on QoL is assessed patients treated at Erasmus MC. It evaluates QoL with standardized questionnaires focusing on (endometrial) cancer patients. The follow up is up to five years after end of treatment. 17 Introduction Chapter 5 explores the molecular landscape of UCS, with particular attention to its biphasic architecture. Genomic analyses with Next Generation Sequencing (NGS) were performed on both the carcinoma and sarcoma components when available. Beyond confirming the heterogeneity within the TP53mutant subgroup, the study aims to identify additional molecular patterns with prognostic or therapeutic relevance. Analyses include recurrent gene alterations, tumor mutational burden, microsatellite instability (MMRD), homologous recombination deficiency, and dysregulated oncogenic pathways, with the goal of highlighting potential targets for existing or future therapies. By addressing these key points, this thesis critically evaluates current treatment strategies in terms of both survival outcomes and QoL, providing insight into their actual benefit for patients with UCS. Moreover, it highlights the significant gaps in existing research and understanding of UCS, thereby identifying priorities for future studies aimed at improving prognosis.

title: VibraGlot: Contactless Vocal Disorder Screening via mmWave Neck-Surface Vibration Sensing
abstract: Vocal disorders often begin as subtle mechanical irregularities in vocal-fold vibration before speech quality noticeably degrades. Early identification of such abnormalities is valuable because timely intervention may prevent progression to more advanced stages. However, detecting these weak early cues outside clinical settings remains challenging: microphone-based analysis observes an acoustically shaped signal that may only weakly express source-level irregularity, while contact-based vibration sensors suffer from low user compliance. We present VibraGlot, a contactless screening system that leverages millimeter-wave radar to sense neck-surface micro-vibrations during a short, non-linguistic sustained phonation (3-5 s). Rather than adopting generic end-to-end learning, VibraGlot uses a kinematics-first design. It first isolates the laryngeal region through observability-aware locking to suppress static clutter, then performs cycle-synchronous reconstruction in a canonical phase domain. Crucially, this pipeline explicitly preserves template-violating motion as structured residuals, transforming irregular mechanical behavior into diagnostic features rather than smoothing it away as noise. We evaluate VibraGlot on a clinical cohort of 74 subjects spanning five common vocal pathologies and healthy controls, collected in both hospital and home environments. Under a strict minimal-input protocol, the system achieves a macro-F1 score exceeding 0.91. These results demonstrate that radar-based neck-surface kinematics provide a robust, interpretable, and contactless pathway for scalable early vocal disorder screening, particularly when pathology is still expressed as subtle mechanical irregularity.
