title: AI-driven strategies for sustainable cultural tourism marketing: a case study approach to visitor engagement and environmental impact
abstract: Introduction While artificial intelligence (AI) has revolutionized real-time personalization in destination marketing, its strategic deployment to mitigate the negative externalities of cultural overtourism remains undertheorized. Methods Grounded in the Tourism 4.0 paradigm, this paper addresses this gap by introducing the AI–Sustainability–Engagement Nexus (ASEN) framework; a novel conceptual model integrating the Stimulus-Organism-Response (S-O-R) paradigm with the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM). To evaluate the model's structural propositions, we conduct an institutional multi-case desk study of secondary data from eight globally significant cultural heritage sites (e.g., The Louvre, The Palace Museum, Dunhuang Mogao Grottoes, and Machu Picchu). Results The findings suggest that AI-driven smart demarketing and spatial-temporal flow optimization is associated with alleviating localized overcrowding and carbon footprints in the cases where such effects are directly evidenced. Discussion Crucially, the analysis indicates that sustainability returns are not incidental byproducts of marketing efficiencies; rather, they require explicit environmental design parameters and robust institutional governance architectures. The paper concludes with an actionable, agenda-setting framework for destination management organizations (DMOs) to balance economic demands with heritage preservation.
authors: Muhammad Daood; Hongyun Tian; Dan Tshiswaka Dan; Reagan Kapilya; Saba Batool Wadhar

title: AI-powered cardiometabolic assessment from a single facial video
abstract: Abstract Introduction Hypertension and diabetes are leading modifiable risk factors for cardiovascular disease, yet a substantial proportion of affected individuals remain undiagnosed. Current screening relies on dedicated clinical encounters or wearable devices, both of which limit population-level coverage. A passive, contactless monitoring system that can be embedded in everyday environments could overcome these barriers and enable early detection at scale. Purpose We aimed to develop and evaluate a machine-learning algorithm that detects hypertension and diabetes and estimates blood pressure from short-duration facial video captured by a spectroscopic camera, without any physical contact or blood sampling. Methods & Results In this single-center prospective cohort study, 285 consenting participants (patients and healthy volunteers) underwent high-speed spectroscopic video recording of the face and hands. Concurrent cuff-based blood pressure measurements served as the reference standard for hypertension (systolic ≥130 mmHg or diastolic ≥80 mmHg, per AHA 2017 criteria), while HbA1c values and physician-diagnosed diabetes (≥6.5% or clinical diagnosis) were used as the reference for diabetes. The algorithm extracted three categories of features from the video data: pulse wave dynamics, skin blood-flow patterns, and spectral characteristics. For hypertension detection, the pulse wave-based analysis achieved 95.0% accuracy using a 30-second recording in an ensemble model (normal blood pressure sensitivity 100.0 ± 0.00%, hypertension sensitivity 89.2 ± 2.30%), and 90.3% accuracy using 5 seconds of data (normal blood pressure sensitivity 98.3 ± 6.22%, hypertension sensitivity 84.5 ± 7.2). For diabetes detection, a model using 30-second videos based on blood flow patterns achieved 88.2% accuracy (Fine Gaussian SVM, ROC-AUC 0.97), and a model using 5-second videos achieved 81.2% accuracy (SVM kernel, ROC-AUC 0.98). Five-fold cross-validation was used for these binary classifications. In addition, for blood pressure estimation using 30-second videos of the face only, a model using three parallel models—Random Forest, XGBoost, and LightGBM—achieved a Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) of 9.7% and a model correlation coefficient of 0.968. Conclusion A machine-learning algorithm applied to spectroscopic facial video can detect hypertension and diabetes with high accuracy from recordings as short as 5 seconds, and can estimate blood pressure without a cuff. These findings suggest that contactless biometric sensing may serve as a scalable screening tool for cardiovascular risk factors, warranting further validation in larger, multi-center cohorts.ESC2026

title: AI‐Driven Personalized Recommendations and Real‐Time Monitoring for the Prevention and Management of Obesity: Clinical Trial Protocol for the Multicentre BETTER4All Personalized Intervention
abstract: BACKGROUND: Obesity arises from complex interactions among genetic, biological, behavioral, and environmental factors. Traditional "one-size-fits-all" interventions often yield modest, short-term outcomes, failing to account inter-individual variability. Advances in artificial intelligence (AI), polygenic risk scores (PRS), and digital health technologies now enable personalized and adaptive lifestyle interventions. OBJECTIVE: This paper presents the design and evaluation framework of the BETTER4All personalized intervention, a multicentre randomized controlled trial within the EU-funded BETTER4U project. The trial aims to integrate biological and behavioral data into tailored obesity prevention and management strategies. METHODS: . Participants will be randomized to an intervention group receiving AI and PRS-based lifestyle recommendations via a smartphone application, wearable device, and structured counseling, or to a control group receiving standard hypocaloric diet and lifestyle advice. The primary outcome is change in BMI at 6 months. Secondary outcomes include weight-loss maintenance at 1 year, metabolomic and gut microbiota biomarkers, lifestyle behaviors, and psychosocial parameters. Process evaluation incorporates measures of fidelity, acceptability, feasibility, and appropriateness, alongside adherence metrics from the digital tools. CONCLUSION: The BETTER4All trial will provide evidence on the effectiveness and scalability of AI-driven, biologically informed personalization in obesity care, offering a methodological framework for integrating multimodal digital data, from omics and biomarkers to behavior and lifestyle, contributing to the advancement of precision public health strategies. title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI)–ENABLED WEARABLES FOR CARDIAC RHYTHM MONITORING: DIAGNOSTIC PERFORMANCE, REGULATORY TRENDS, AND CLINICAL INTEGRATION.
abstract: Wearable technologies extend cardiac-rhythm monitoring beyond conventional clinical settings. Smartwatches, handheld single-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) devices, adhesive ECG patches, chest straps, rings, and remote-monitoring platforms increasingly use artificial intelligence (AI) and machine-learning methods to detect atrial fibrillation (AF), classify rhythm abnormalities, assess signal quality, prioritize ambulatory recordings, and estimate arrhythmia burden. This review examined the technological, regulatory, diagnostic, and clinical-integration considerations relevant to AI-enabled wearable cardiac monitoring. This review evaluates evidence concerning wearable ECG and photoplethysmography (PPG)-based rhythm-monitoring technologies, with attention to diagnostic performance, regulatory authorization, algorithmic limitations, and requirements for safe clinical implementation. Wearable ECG devices can identify AF with high sensitivity and specificity in selected and supervised populations. However, diagnostic performance varies according to device modality, recording quality, patient characteristics, AF prevalence, reference standard, software version, and the handling of inconclusive or unclassifiable recordings. PPG-based irregular-rhythm notifications can provide useful screening signals but do not independently establish an AF diagnosis because they detect pulse irregularity rather than cardiac electrical activity. In contrast, interpretable wearable ECG recordings may provide rhythm documentation when incorporated into an appropriate clinical evaluation pathway. Regulatory authorization defines a device’s permitted intended use but does not establish universal diagnostic accuracy, generalizability, clinical-outcome benefit, or suitability for autonomous clinical decision-making. Effective implementation requires external validation; transparent reporting of unclassifiable recordings; clinician-overread and confirmatory ECG pathways; governance of algorithm updates; privacy and cybersecurity protections; and ongoing post-market performance monitoring. AI-enabled wearable rhythm monitoring is most likely to improve care when used to support, rather than replace clinical judgment.

title: ATRIAL FIBRILLATION, WEARABLE TECHNOLOGIES AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE: CURRENT EVIDENCE, CLINICAL UTILITY AND LIMITATIONS
abstract: Background: Atrial fibrillation is the most common sustained cardiac arrhythmia in adults and represents an important clinical and public health problem because of its association with stroke, mortality, disability, and healthcare burden. Its paroxysmal and frequently asymptomatic course limits the effectiveness of conventional diagnostic strategies based on occasional electrocardiographic recordings. Aim: This narrative review aims to summarise current evidence regarding the use of wearable technologies and artificial intelligence for the detection of atrial fibrillation, with particular emphasis on diagnostic accuracy, clinical utility, and principal limitations. Methods: A structured literature search was performed using PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar. Studies published between 2021 and 2026 were primarily considered. Search terms included “atrial fibrillation,” “wearable technologies,” “smartwatch,” “electrocardiography,” “photoplethysmography,” “artificial intelligence,” “machine learning,” and “diagnostics.” Priority was given to original studies, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and clinically relevant review articles concerning wearable devices, artificial intelligence, and atrial fibrillation detection. Earlier landmark studies were included when they were necessary to explain key evidence discussed in recent reviews and meta-analyses. Results: Wearable devices such as smartwatches, fitness bands, and portable ECG systems allow longer heart rhythm monitoring in daily life and may help detect paroxysmal and clinically silent atrial fibrillation. ECG-based devices are more consistent with current diagnostic standards, whereas photoplethysmography-based systems are more accessible and can provide passive rhythm monitoring. Artificial intelligence, especially machine learning and deep learning, can support signal interpretation, arrhythmia recognition, and risk prediction. However, diagnostic performance reported in controlled studies may not always translate directly into real-world clinical practice. Conclusions: Wearable technologies and artificial intelligence offer a promising way to support atrial fibrillation screening and monitoring. They may improve early detection, especially in asymptomatic individuals, but should not replace standard diagnostic methods. Photoplethysmography-based alerts should be regarded as screening signals, while a final diagnosis of atrial fibrillation should still be confirmed by ECG in an appropriate clinical context. More large-scale studies are needed before these tools can be widely implemented in routine practice.

title: Adaptive radar–thermal fusion for robust human motion recognition in dynamic environment
abstract: Abstract This paper proposes a motion-enhanced adaptive radar-thermal fusion framework for robust contactless human motion recognition in dynamic environments. The main contribution of this work is to exploit the complementary characteristics of millimeter wave radar and thermal infrared sensing, and to improve recognition robustness when one sensing modality is degraded by environmental interference. To validate the proposed framework, a dual-modal action acquisition system is developed using an IWR6843ISK millimeter wave radar and a 24 × 32 thermal infrared array. Single-participant experimental recordings are collected for five human motions under three indoor conditions, including a clean environment, thermal-hot-object interference, and radar-moving-reflector interference. Based on the collected experimental samples, six recognition models are systematically evaluated, including radar-only, thermalonly, concatenation fusion, gated fusion, motion-only, and motion-gated models. Experimental results from ten randomized trials show that the proposed motion-gated model achieves classification accuracies of 98.67% ± 2.81%, 97.20% ± 2.70%, and 90.00% ± 3.40% under the clean, thermal-hot-object, and radar-moving-reflector conditions, respectively. In comparison, concatenation fusion obtains only 33.60% ± 10.70% under thermal interference, while the radar-only model achieves only 17.60% ± 6.59% under dynamic-reflector interference. These results demonstrate that motion feature enhancement and adaptive gated fusion can effectively improve the robustness of human motion recognition under the investigated dynamic interference conditions.
authors: Qinwei Li; BangXuan Rao; Cheng Fang; Hang Wu; Qinwei Li

title: Adeno‐associated virus ‐mediated restoration of Na V 1.1 in targeted brain regions ameliorates epilepsy in symptomatic Dravet syndrome mice
abstract: Abstract Objective Dravet syndrome (DS) is a developmental and epileptic encephalopathy primarily caused by haploinsufficiency of the SCN1A gene, which encodes the alpha subunit of Na V 1.1 voltage‐gated sodium channel. The disease manifests with febrile and spontaneous seizures, developmental delay, cognitive impairment, and increased risk of sudden unexpected death in epilepsy. Most preclinical therapeutic strategies aim to enhance endogenous Scn1a gene expression or deliver a functional copy via perinatal interventions. Although promising, these approaches face challenges in achieving efficient brain‐wide delivery, targeting all interested brain areas. Methods In this study, we used a conditional DS reversible mouse model ( Scn1a Stop/+ ) to assess the therapeutic potential of postsymptomatic restoration (postnatal day 30) of Na V 1.1 physiological levels in all neuronal populations but restricted to minimal brain regions. Results We found that hippocampal correction alone reduces seizure susceptibility, whereas simultaneous restoration in the hippocampus, thalamus, and overlying somatosensory and visual cortex was associated with a trend toward further reduction in seizure burden and improved survival. Significance These findings indicate that hippocampal restoration accounts for a substantial component of the therapeutic benefit, and broader network correction may confer additional advantages.
authors: Martina Mainardi; Simone Brusco; Serena Gea Giannelli; Vania Broccoli; Gaia Colasante

title: Advances in Deep Learning and Image Processing for Brain Tumor Detection and Classification: A Comprehensive Review
abstract: Brain tumor identification and classification by the application of deep learning and sophisticated image-processing techniques have been receiving a lot of attention in the medical field. Accurate diagnosis, treatment planning, and patient outcome rely on the accurate identification and differentiation of brain tumors, such as gliomas, meningiomas, and metastases. The most recent developments in deep learning-based techniques for brain tumor identification and categorization by applying medical imaging data, including Computed Tomography (CT). This study looks at CT and Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI). The main topic of this study is the general theory and developments in deep learning methods for the identification and classification of brain tumors. It investigates how the precision and efficacy of tumor detection can be increased through a variety of models, including Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). The paper emphasizes the Significance of applying novel deep-learning techniques for facilitating precise and automated brain tumor identification for individualized treatment, with an emphasis on important achievements, challenges, and opportunities in the area.

title: Advances in Mobile Health Strategies for Atrial Fibrillation Detection and Patient Care
abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF), a prevalent cardiac arrhythmia, poses significant risks for stroke and other severe complications.Traditional approaches frequently lack accessibility, accuracy, and patient engagement despite advancements in detection and management.The revolutionary effects of mobile health (mHealth) technologies on the treatment of AF are reviewed in this paper.These innovations, which make use of wearable technology, smartphone apps, and sophisticated algorithms, improve patient adherence, increase early detection, and lower healthcare costs.Better results are produced when realtime monitoring and patient-centered tools are incorporated into daily life because they empower people and allow for prompt interventions.However, issues like device restrictions, possible user anxiety, and fair access still exist.This study recognizes areas for additional research and development while highlighting the potential of mHealth to transform the management of AF.

title: Advancing Occupational Safety with AI-Powered Monitoring Systems: A Conceptual Framework for Hazard Detection and Exposure Control
abstract: Occupational safety remains a critical concern across industries, necessitating innovative solutions to mitigate hazards and control worker exposure to harmful environments. This paper presents a conceptual framework for leveraging Artificial Intelligence (AI)-powered monitoring systems to enhance occupational safety. The framework integrates advanced data analytics, machine learning algorithms, and Internet of Things (IoT) devices to enable realtime hazard detection and exposure control. By utilizing AI's predictive capabilities, the system identifies potential risks and triggers preemptive measures to prevent accidents and long-term health impacts. Key components of the framework include wearable IoT sensors for monitoring workers' vital signs and environmental parameters, AI-driven analysis to process large datasets, and adaptive feedback mechanisms to inform decision-making. The system also incorporates computer vision for identifying physical hazards and proximity detection for alerting workers in high-risk zones. These technologies collectively facilitate a proactive approach to workplace safety, shifting the paradigm from reactive to preventive measures. The framework emphasizes scalability and flexibility, making it adaptable to various industrial sectors, including construction, manufacturing, and healthcare. The integration of AI-powered systems aligns with Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) regulations and supports compliance with safety standards. Furthermore, the proposed framework addresses challenges such as false positives, data privacy concerns, and user adoption through robust algorithm design, secure data management practices, and user-centric interfaces. Preliminary simulations demonstrate the system's potential to significantly reduce workplace injuries and improve hazard response times. Case studies from the construction and oil and gas industries underscore the value of real-time hazard monitoring in high-risk environments. The paper concludes by highlighting future research directions, including advancements in AI algorithms, enhanced sensor technologies, and cross-industry implementation strategies. This conceptual framework positions AI-powered monitoring systems as a transformative solution for advancing occupational safety, offering a pathway to safer, more resilient workplaces through data-driven innovation.

title: Aerial Magnetic Anomaly Target Detection Method Based on Multi-Scale Orthonormal Basis Function Convolution and Convolution-Augmented Gated Attention
abstract: Magnetic anomaly detection from aerial platforms enables passive, non-contact detection of underwater ferromagnetic targets. To address the issues of traditional Orthonormal Basis Function (OBF) detection relying on prior knowledge of the closest contact distance and susceptibility to mismatch with single-scale templates, this paper proposes an aerial magnetic anomaly target detection method that integrates multi-scale OBF with a convolution-augmented gated attention unit (CGAU). Six sets of fixed OBF convolution kernels each output three matching responses, which are concatenated with the original sequence to form 19-channel features. Four layers of one-dimensional (1-D) convolution and two stages of CGAU extract local waveform features and capture long-range dependencies. The precision (PC), detection rate (DR), and F1-score of the proposed network on the simulated test set are 94.70%, 95.11%, and 94.90%, respectively (best-performing seed = 42). On the measured dataset, it detected 11 of 12 overpass events, achieving an event detection rate of 91.67%. The proposed network has approximately 0.43 M trainable parameters and achieves a higher mean F1 across three random seeds than the seven selected baselines, demonstrating its potential for aerial magnetic anomaly target detection.
authors: Haozhe Chen; Ke Zhang; Wanhua Zhu

title: Air-Coupled Acoustic Emission Detection Using a Multifrequency MEMS Sensor
abstract: Acoustic emission (AE) monitoring is widely used for structural health monitoring (SHM) and nondestructive evaluation (NDE), yet most conventional sensors require direct mechanical contact with the monitored structure. Air-coupled sensing offers a non-contact alternative, but only a small fraction of elastic wave energy radiates from solids into air due to severe acoustic impedance mismatch, producing extremely weak airborne signals. This work presents an experimental demonstration of air-coupled acoustic emission detection using a compact multifrequency microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) sensor. The sensor consists of an array of sixteen diaphragm-type resonators with resonance frequencies distributed between 100 kHz and 700 kHz and microfabricated using the PiezoMUMPs process. Airborne acoustic signals generated by pencil lead break excitation on an aluminum plate were recorded with the MEMS sensor positioned in air without mechanical contact. The sensor successfully detected leaky acoustic emission signals, exhibiting clear transient responses and distinct spectral peaks aligned with its designed resonance frequencies while also capturing low-frequency components. The results demonstrate that multifrequency MEMS sensors provide sufficient sensitivity and frequency-selective response for detecting weak airborne AE signals, highlighting their potential for compact and scalable non-contact acoustic emission monitoring in structural health monitoring applications.
authors: Talha Masood Khan; Didem Ozevin

title: AlertSafeNet a multichannel deep learning framework for real time anomaly detection using wearable device data
abstract: This research investigates the integration of wearable device data analysis to enable proactive safety monitoring within intelligent systems. The objective is to develop a deep learning framework capable of automatically detecting anomalous gait patterns from the wearable device data and generating alerts in real-time. Smartwatches and fitness trackers, through their built-in sensors, continuously record physiological and contextual signals including heart rate, SpO₂, ECG, location, and more. Analyzing this multichannel time-series data lets the proposed framework flag abnormal behavioral patterns that could signal a safety risk. The proposed framework enables the identification of abnormal behavioral patterns that may reflect potential safety risk scenarios. In high-risk scenarios, such systems can activate real-time alerts to trusted contacts or concerned authorities. In this work, we propose AlertSafeNet, a multichannel 1D convolutional neural network with residual connections, designed to learn temporal dependencies and detect anomalies from wearable sensor data. The dataset is created using smart watch-derived physiological signals combined with contextual information from smartphones. Once trained, the model runs in a cloud-based environment, supporting real-time inference and continuous monitoring. The results demonstrate promising performance: the model reaches 97.9% classification accuracy, with strong precision, recall, and F1-score — a good indicator of its usefulness for real-time anomaly detection in safety-critical settings.
authors: Bharati Ainapure; Reshma Nitin Pise; Nishu Gupta; Mohammad Omar Derawi

title: Ambient intelligence platforms and new frontiers in surgical safety.
abstract: The operating room is a high-risk, high-entropy environment, prone to human error and preventable adverse events. Drawing on lessons from high-reliability organizations such as the aviation industry, Aimbient (formerly Operating Room Black Box by Surgical Safety Technologies, New York, NY) collects continuous, multimodal audiovisual and physiologic data capture to deepen our understanding of surgical safety. This platform has demonstrated improvements in patient safety domains across several metrics, including ground-truth benchmarking of checklist adherence, video-based multidisciplinary review conferences, and automated physiologic event tagging. Recent integration of key postoperative morbidity and mortality metrics into the data streams collected by Aimbient monitoring platforms allows for us to achieve a holistic understanding of the perioperative record. As artificial intelligence capabilities rapidly expand and begin to integrate into our health care systems, ambient data capture is uniquely poised to generate real-time insights and open new frontiers in surgical patient safety.
authors: Chloe K Nobuhara; Mary T Hawn; Teodor P Grantcharov

title: Ambient intelligence-based framework for quantitative evaluation of cell culture operations to support standardization and training
abstract: Introduction: The widespread implementation of cell therapy has increased the demand for stable and reproducible cell manufacturing methods. However, many cell manufacturing processes rely heavily on manual cell culture operations, and operator training remains largely dependent on subjective assessment and tacit knowledge. This limits the establishment of training targets and hinders operational standardization. Recent advances in ambient intelligence have created new opportunities for digitizing human work processes and supporting their quantitative evaluation. In this study, we developed an ambient intelligence-based framework for digitizing, visualizing, and quantitatively comparing manual cell culture operations. Methods: A defined mock seeding operation was performed by one expert with 10 years of cell culture experience and three trainees with approximately two years of experience. Videos of the operation were recorded inside a biosafety cabinet, and the dominant-hand motion was extracted using an artificial intelligence (AI)-based skeleton estimation. The resulting time-series data were converted into quantitative speed-based temporal profiles for each operation, termed Operation Profiles. To compare operations with different execution times, the similarity between each Operation Profile and the target Operation Profile derived from the expert was evaluated using fast derivative dynamic time warping (fastDDTW). Distance and gap index were used as complementary metrics to assess the waveform deviation and temporal misalignment, respectively. Results: Skeleton estimation AI, combined with visual quality control, interpolation, and manual correction, extracted the dominant-hand motion from the operation videos and enabled the construction of interpretable Operation Profiles that reflect the internal temporal structure of the defined cell culture operation. Although all operators performed the same operation, their Operation Profiles differed, indicating operator-dependent variations in the operation patterns. Iterative feedback based on phase-specific differences from the target expert operation was associated with progressive improvement in the trainees' similarity to the target Operation Profile. Conclusions: This study established a framework for recording, digitizing, and quantitatively evaluating cell culture operations using ambient intelligence. These findings demonstrate that the alignment of cell culture operations toward a target expert operation can be quantitatively evaluated through an Operation Profile analysis. By enabling objective comparison of operator behavior and quantitative evaluation of alignment toward a facility-defined target operation, this approach may provide a basis for operational standardization and training support in cell manufacturing.
authors: Kengo Momose; Takeru Shiina; Yuto Takemoto; Mai Okada; Kakeru Koide; Tomohiro Yokoi; Ayako Sugimoto; Kei Kanie; Kenjiro Tanaka; Ryuji Kato

title: An Enhancing Lung Disease Detection with Scalable UNet-Mamba Segmentation
abstract: Lung diseases are conditions that damage the lung tissues, airways or blood vessels of the lungs, causing breathing difficulties and decreased oxygen supply to the body. Computed Tomography (CT) plays a crucial role in lung disease prediction because it provides detailed cross-sectional images for detecting tumors at initial stages. However, CT scans have drawbacks such as radiation exposure, high cost, large data size, and the possibility of false positives. Recently, many Deep Learning (DL) techniques have been used to automatically analyze CT images for early and accurate detection of lung diseases, improving diagnostic efficiency. However, existing models may struggle to capture fine spatial details, leading to inaccurate boundary delineation and poor segmentation of small or low-contrast regions. Some models are also sensitive to imaging artifacts, which can reduce performance in real-world conditions. In this paper, a lung disease prediction model is developed using ResNet and Mamba Network (LRMNet) to solve the aforementioned issues for lung disease prediction. The first step is improving the model's ability to conduct pre-processing and enrich the data using a Deep Convolutional Generative Adversarial Network (DCGAN). Then, the Scalable Vision UNet-Mamba (SVU-M) model is developed to efficiently capture fine spatial details along with long-range contextual information. SVU-M leverages Scalable Vision State Space (SVSS) blocks to efficiently model the global dependencies while maintaining linear computational complexity. The integration of SVSS within a U-shaped framework enhances the boundary delineation and improves segmentation of small or low-contrast regions, which increases the efficiency against imaging artifacts for more reliable performance. The decoder feature maps of SVU-M are further processed using Global Average Pooling (GAP) to determine image-level feature representations for classification. Simultaneously, the input image is directly fed into ResNet-50 for capturing the whole image's semantic features. A Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) classifier is trained with the extracted features to forecast lung diseases. A total accuracy of 94.15% on the customized dataset and 93.29% on the SARS-CoV-2 CT dataset was achieved by the suggested model, according to the experimental results, exceeding the performance of other models.
authors: Sivasakthi S; Radha V
venue: International Journal of Engineering Trends and Technology

title: An Explainable Software-Based Framework for Pre-Symptomatic Grape Disease Risk Assessment Using MobileNetV2, Grad-CAM, and Weather Data
abstract: Viticulture faces severe yield losses from major fungal diseases such as Downy Mildew, Powdery Mildew, and Black Rot. Existing deep learning classification models predominantly rely on visible symptomatic lesions on leaves or fruit clusters. However, waiting for visual symptoms to manifest often delays chemical mitigation beyond the optimal therapeutic window, resulting in irreversible crop degradation. This paper proposes a software-based, explainable framework for pre-symptomatic grape disease risk assessment. The architecture combines finegrained leaf image feature extraction using MobileNetV2 with micro-climate weather telemetry (temperature, relative humidity, leaf wetness duration, and rainfall forecast). To ensure clinical transparency for agronomists and farmers, Explainable AI (XAI) is integrated via Gradientweighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM), generating visual saliency heatmaps that highlight sub-visual cellular stress indicators and necrotic margins. A dynamic Epidemiological Micro-Climate Risk Index (EMRI) fuses deep learning probabilities with real-time weather analytics. Evaluated on multi-source datasets including PlantVillage and field-captured vineyard imagery, MobileNetV2 achieves a classification accuracy of 97.84%. Based on a comprehensive literature review, a critical research gap is identified: current agricultural systems treat image classification and micro-climate forecasting as disjoint workflows without explainable decision support. The proposed framework fills this gap through an integrated web and mobile platform featuring automated risk alerts and actionable advisory generation
authors: Chaskar Prajwal Doke Atharva, Balsaraf Sahil, Prof. S S Bhor

title: An Indoor Object Detection and Navigation System
abstract: “Indoor Object Detection for Blind” is a dedicated assistive technology project designed to enhance indoor navigation for visually impaired individuals. Utilizing advanced computer vision techniques, the system detects and identifies objects in real-time using wearable devices like smart glasses or smartphones. It integrates YOLO-based deep learning models, fine-tuned with a custom indoor dataset, to ensure high accuracy in recognizing objects such as furniture, doors, and appliances. Additionally, natural language processing (NLP) enables context-aware descriptions, providing adaptive feedback. The project is designed to be flexible and seamlessly integrate with wearable technology, ensuring a smooth and efficient user experience. The system evaluates various aspects of objects, including their spatial positioning and contextual information, to assist users in real-time. By concentrating solely on object detection within indoor environments, this system significantly improves spatial awareness and navigation for visually impaired individuals. Extensive testing demonstrates the system's performance in detecting and identifying objects while minimizing false positives.

title: An Integrated Visual–Textual Approach for Accurate Phishing Detection on Social Media Platforms
abstract: The rapid rise of phishing attacks on social media platforms highlights an urgent and growing cybersecurity challenge in today’s digitally connected world. As millions of users rely on these platforms for communication, business, and information sharing, cybercriminals increasingly exploit them to distribute deceptive links, fake advertisements, and fraudulent messages designed to steal sensitive data such as login credentials, financial information, and personal identities. The sophistication of these attacks—often leveraging social engineering techniques, impersonation of trusted entities, and AI-generated content—makes them difficult for users to recognize and avoid. Consequently, there is a critical need for robust and intelligent detection systems capable of reliably identifying malicious content in real time. Such systems should incorporate advanced machine learning models, behavioral analysis, and continuous adaptation to emerging attack patterns in order to effectively mitigate risks, protect users, and maintain trust in social media ecosystems. This paper proposes a multimodal phishing detection framework that integrates visual indicators (e.g., logos and page imagery) with textual signals (e.g., URL structure and phishing-related keywords). Our contributions are threefold: (i) a feature fusion strategy that combines visual and textual cues, (ii) the construction of a comprehensive dataset using feature extraction and natural language processing (NLP), and (iii) a comparative evaluation of multiple machine learning models. We extract 27 discriminative URL features and evaluate Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, and Naı̈ve Bayes. Random Forest achieves the best performance, reaching 98.6% accuracy with a false positive rate of 0.01, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed multimodal approach for phishing detection on social media.
authors: Ala’ S Mughaid; Andaleep Shdeifat; Abedalmuhdi Almomany; Mohammad Kharabsheh; Shadi Mahmoud Faleh AlZu’bi

title: Antecedents of Adoption Intention for AI-Driven Wearable Technology in Malaysian Healthcare
abstract: This study reports the pilot phase of a larger doctoral investigation into the adoption of AI-driven wearable technology in Malaysian healthcare. Guided by an integration of Diffusion of Innovations theory and the Technology Acceptance Model, the pilot tested seven direct effect hypotheses linking compatibility, relative advantage, trialability, complexity, observability, perceived ease of use, and perceived usefulness to adoption intention. Data were collected from healthcare sector respondents at a professional conference in Kuala Lumpur in August 2026 (N = 93, after removing two duplicates from 95 raw responses). Partial least squares structural equation modeling was used for its suitability to prediction oriented research. The structural model explained 60.0 percent of the variance in adoption intention. Perceived usefulness (beta = 0.261), perceived ease of use (beta = 0.201), observability (beta = 0.174), compatibility (beta = 0.162), and complexity (beta = -0.152) significantly predicted adoption intention (all p < .05); relative advantage and trialability did not. Composite reliability exceeded 0.78 for all nine constructs, and heterotrait monotrait ratios for all 36 construct pairs fell below the conservative 0.85 threshold as point estimates, but bootstrap confidence intervals crossed 0.85 for six of the eight adoption intention pairs, so discriminant validity for that construct remains provisional. Perceived regulatory support was retained for reliability assessment but not tested as a moderator here, a test reserved for the full study. Findings offer preliminary support for the framework and considerations for the full scale study.
authors: Syeda Hafsa Rizwan; Anusuyah Subbarao; Shereen Khan
