title: Effects of eyelash extensions on the ocular surface: a systematic review of clinical outcomes and adverse events
abstract: Topic To synthesise evidence on ocular surface outcomes, symptoms and adverse events associated with semi-permanent eyelash extensions. Clinical relevance Eyelash extensions are applied beside the ocular surface; their clinical effects and associated complications warrant assessment. Methods PubMed, Ovid, CINAHL and Scopus were searched to 3 September 2026 without date or language restrictions for primary human studies reporting extension-specific ocular or periocular outcomes. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data and appraised studies using adapted Newcastle-Ottawa and Joanna Briggs Institute tools. Findings were synthesised narratively owing to heterogeneity. The review followed PRISMA 2020 and a prospectively registered protocol (PROSPERO CRD420261383757). Results Nineteen studies were included: two prospective studies, five cross-sectional studies, four case series and eight case reports. In one prospective study, corneal staining peaked at one hour and tear-film stability was lowest at one week after application. A matched comparator study found between-group differences in tear break-up time and clinical signs. One removal study showed improvement in symptomatic users. Four self-report studies included 845 users; symptom prevalence ranged from 26.8% to 97.5%, reflecting different samples and methods. Reported adverse events included keratoconjunctivitis, contact dermatitis, bacterial keratitis and eyelid leukoderma. Conclusion Eyelash extensions are associated with ocular surface disturbance and diverse adverse events, involving exposures beyond the adhesive. Small uncontrolled studies, self-reported surveys and case-level evidence limit certainty and prevent population-risk estimation. The findings support clinical enquiry about extension use in patients with unexplained ocular surface or perioperative symptoms.
authors: Minnan Al-Khafaji; Hussain Al-Hilali; Stephen Ong

title: Electret materials for tele-perception
abstract: Tele-perception is an emerging non-contact sensing paradigm that enables long-range perception and establishes a new interface for intelligent human-machine interaction. Unlike conventional tactile sensing, tele-perception relies on material-generated spatial electrostatic fields, placing unprecedented demands on electret materials capable of generating, retaining and dynamically regulating electric fields. However, current electret research lacks a unified materials framework tailored to tele-perception. Here, we establish a materials perspective that classifies tele-perception electrets into electron-trapping and iontronic electret systems. Electron-trapping electrets generate persistent electrostatic fields through electron trapping and dielectric polarization, whereas iontronic electrets enable adaptive field modulation through ionic migration and space-charge redistribution. We further propose a paradigm shift from passive charge-trapping materials to active spatial electric-field engineering, establishing a unified materials design strategy for next-generation tele-perception toward embodied intelligence, autonomous robotics, and intelligent sensing in complex and dynamic environments.
authors: Yan Du; Zhong Lin Wang; Di Wei

title: Electronic Devices and Digital Therapeutics in Neuromuscular Diseases: Narrative Review on Current Applications in Patients' Management and Pharmacovigilance
abstract: Digital health technologies have revolutionized the management of neuromuscular diseases (NMDs), offering novel opportunities for disease monitoring, rehabilitation, telemedicine, pharmacological research, and pharmacovigilance. This narrative review aims to provide an integrated overview of the current applications of digital health technologies in NMDs, highlighting their role in diagnosis, disease monitoring, rehabilitation, telemedicine, pharmacological research, and pharmacovigilance. Relevant articles were identified by interrogating PubMed using combinations of keywords including "neuromuscular diseases," "digital health," "digital therapeutics," "telemedicine," "wearable devices," "remote monitoring," "telerehabilitation," and "pharmacovigilance." This review describes how wearable devices, digital biomarkers, telemedicine platforms, and digital therapeutics can facilitate continuous and real-time monitoring of clinically relevant parameters, including muscle strength, mobility, physical activity, and disease progression. In addition, digital technologies support remote patient management, rehabilitation programs, early detection of clinical changes, and the development of personalized therapeutic interventions. Emerging evidence also suggests that digital health tools may improve the design and conduct of clinical trials, enhance the collection and analysis of real-world data and patient-reported outcomes, and contribute to more effective pharmacovigilance strategies. Despite challenges on data privacy, digital literacy, integration into healthcare system and the need for large-scale or long-term clinical trials, the integration of digital therapeutics, digital biomarkers, and pharmacovigilance frameworks represents a promising and still underexplored area of research that may substantially contribute to the development of precision medicine approaches in NMDs.
authors: Ilaria Saltarella; Concetta Altamura; Paola Laghetti; Giuseppina Settanni; Nicola Savino; Angelo Galiano; Bodvael Fraysse; Angelo Vacca; Jean‐François Desaphy

title: Enhancing Maternal and Child Health in Rural Areas Through AI and Mobile Health Solutions
abstract: Enhancing maternal and child health in rural areas presents significant challenges due to geographic isolation, limited healthcare infrastructure, and a shortage of medical professionals. This abstract explores the transformative potential of artificial intelligence (AI) and mobile health (mHealth) solutions in addressing these challenges and improving health outcomes for mothers and children in underserved regions. AI technologies offer robust tools for predictive analytics, decision support, and personalized care. In rural healthcare settings, AI can enhance maternal and child health by providing real-time insights into patient data, predicting potential complications, and supporting personalized treatment plans. For instance, AI algorithms can analyze data from electronic health records to identify high-risk pregnancies, enable early intervention, and optimize resource allocation. Furthermore, AI-driven chatbots and virtual health assistants can offer remote consultations and health education, reducing the need for travel and making healthcare more accessible. Mobile health solutions, including smartphones and wearable devices, play a critical role in bridging gaps in rural healthcare. mHealth applications facilitate remote monitoring of maternal and child health metrics, such as blood pressure, glucose levels, and fetal heart rates. These applications can alert healthcare providers to potential issues, enabling timely interventions. Mobile platforms also support health education, offering resources on prenatal care, nutrition, and childhood vaccinations, thus empowering individuals with knowledge and tools to manage their health proactively. By integrating AI and mHealth technologies, rural healthcare systems can achieve significant improvements in maternal and child health outcomes. These technologies provide essential support in areas with limited medical resources, enhance access to quality care, and enable more effective management of health conditions. However, successful implementation requires addressing barriers such as technology adoption, data privacy concerns, and infrastructure limitations. In conclusion, leveraging AI and mHealth solutions holds promise for transforming maternal and child health care in rural areas, offering innovative approaches to overcoming existing challenges and enhancing overall health outcomes
authors: Ashiata Yetunde Mustapha
venue: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF MEDICAL EVALUATION AND PHYSICAL REPORT

title: Enhancing breast cancer detection: A CycleGAN-enhanced approach with enhancing sparrow search optimization
abstract: Breast cancer remains one of the leading causes of mortality among women worldwide, necessitating the development of highly accurate and computationally efficient diagnostic methods. Recent advancements in artificial intelligence and deep learning have provide the way for more reliable automated systems to assist in tumor classification. In this study, a novel hybrid classification framework called Cycle-consistent Adversarial Adaptation Network with Enhancing Sparrow Search Optimization (Cy2AN-ESSO) is proposed to improve the diagnostic performance for breast cancer detection using two benchmark datasets: BreakHis and TCGA-BRCA. The proposed approach begins with pre-processing using Robust Double-Weighted Guided Image Filtering (RD-WGIF) to enhance image quality and remove noise, ensuring that relevant features are preserved for subsequent stages. For segmentation, the Memory Efficient Vision Transformer (MEVis-Tr) is employed to accurately identify and isolate tumor regions, providing a reliable foundation for feature extraction. Feature extraction and classification uses the Multimodal Cycle-Triplet Adaptation Attention Network (MCT2AN), which integrates Triplet Attention Network (TAN) for feature extraction and the Cycle-consistent Adversarial Adaptation Network (C-2AN) for robust classification. The process is optimized using Enhancing Sparrow Search Optimization (ESSO) to refine decision boundaries and improve learning accuracy. The experimental results demonstrate that Cy2AN-ESSO demonstrated improved classification performance than current techniques for measuring accuracy and precision as well as recall and sensitivity and specificity and F1-score. Both accuracies and precisions and recalls reach 98.4%, 98.6% and 98.8% respectively for BreakHis data as well as TCGA-BRCA subtypes IDC, ILC, DCIS and LCIS. The proposed framework provided better classification accuracy and computational efficiency over the test datasets. More validation is needed on independent clinical cohorts before clinical use. Using Cy2AN-ESSO enables robust breast cancer classification that shows strong potential for accurate early disease diagnosis.
authors: Megha Sinha; M.SivaramKrishnan; B. Veeramalini; Nivethitha Thangavelsamy; D. Kavitha; M. Siva Ramkumar; Khayala Mammadova; Kasim Sakran Abass; Mekhrbonu Rakhimova; Mohammad Khishe
venue: Medicine in Novel Technology and Devices

title: Epidural Spinal Cord Stimulation Reduces Intrinsic Gait Abnormalities in Spinal Muscular Atrophy
abstract: ABSTRACT Introduction/Aims Epidural spinal cord stimulation (SCS) has recently been explored in ambulatory individuals with spinal muscular atrophy (SMA), where an increase in muscle strength and endurance with concomitant reduced fatigability was observed. However, the underlying kinematic changes associated with these improvements remain poorly understood. This study aimed to examine whether previously documented improvements following SCS were associated with changes in joint kinematics and movement strategies. Methods A secondary kinematic analysis of previously collected 6‐min walk test (6MWT) data using a 3D motion‐capture system and subsequent principal component analysis (PCA) was completed on two ambulatory individuals with SMA. Speed as well as spatio‐temporal gait variables and sagittal‐plane joint kinematics were defined and compared before and after SCS intervention. Results After 4 weeks of SCS, participants walked farther and showed faster, more consistent speeds during the 6MWT. PCA revealed that these improvements were associated with changes in proximal joint velocity (SMA02 mean(L 2 ) = 0.45, SMA03 mean(L 2 ) = 0.54) and proximal joint mobility (SMA 02 mean(L 2 ) = 0.51, SMA03 mean(L 2 ) = 0.40) in both SMA participants. Consistent with these findings, hip range of motion, velocity, and acceleration increased by up to 48%, 44% and 28%, respectively, without evidence of exacerbated compensatory strategies. Discussion SCS may restore access to motor pathways selectively impaired in individuals with SMA. While confirmatory, larger cohort studies are needed, SCS has the potential to reduce intrinsic movement abnormalities and enhance treatment opportunities for SMA.
authors: Serena Donadio; Carly Magun; Cara H. Kanner; Rafael S. Rodriguez-Torres; Genís Prat-Ortega; George Z. Mentis; Marco Capogrosso; Jacqueline Montes

title: Establishment of Standardized Normative Reference Values for Pressure-Based Gait Analysis in the Healthy Korean Population: A Nationwide Multi-Center Registry Study
abstract: Objective: Normative gait data for Asian populations remain scarce, and Western reference values may not apply to Koreans. We aimed to establish nationwide reference values for pressure-based gait analysis in healthy Korean adults. Methods: Healthy community-dwelling adults (N = 612, aged 20 to 80s) were enrolled at 11 randomly selected centers using quota-based recruitment across 18 sex- and age-stratified cohorts. Spatiotemporal gait parameters, classified into five domains, were recorded on a pressure-based electronic walkway. Gait speed cutoffs were defined at -1.0 and -1.5 standard deviations (SD) below age- and sex-specific means. Age-group differences were evaluated using ANOVA and linear mixed-effects models adjusted for height and study site. Results: Gait velocity followed a normal distribution in all strata. In both sexes, older age groups showed lower Pace domain values and higher step length variability, which remained significant after adjustment for height and study site. In contrast, Rhythm domain parameters and asymmetry indices were preserved across age groups. Cutoffs were provided at -1.5 SD for normally distributed parameters and the 7th percentile for non-normally distributed parameters. Conclusions: This is the first nationwide multicenter reference dataset for spatiotemporal gait parameters in healthy Korean adults across the full adult age range. These population-specific values provide a practical baseline for interpreting pressure-based gait analysis and for applying gait-based clinical criteria in Korea.
authors: Jinse Park; Phil Hyu Lee; Seong‐Beom Koh; Jinyoung Youn; Do‐Young Kwon; Kyum‐Yil Kwon; Jeongho Park; Min Seung Kim; Suk Yun Kang; Kyoungwon Baik; Jung Hwan Shin; Min Seok Baek; Sang‐Myung Cheon

title: Evaluating CNN Architectures for Optimal Deployment in Plant Disease Detection Systems
abstract: This paper presents a web-based plant disease detection system presented in this study which classifies plant diseases from uploaded photos using deep learning techniques. Users can upload photos of their plants to the portal, and those photos are evaluated to find diseases. For picture categorization, the system uses Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), more especially the VGG-16 and VGG-19 models. The effectiveness of these two models in detecting plant illnesses was the main subject of a comparison study. VGG-19's superior disease detection accuracy led to its selection as the best model for this application. For farmers and agricultural specialists, the system offers a complete answer by not only identifying the ailment but also suggesting treatments. The potential of AI-based methods to enhance plant health monitoring and support precision agriculture is demonstrated by this study.
authors: V. Nivethitha; S. Rohith; S. K. Miruthula; J. Sanjay

title: Evaluation of the Perimouse Online Suprathreshold Visual Field Test for Glaucoma Screening in a Chinese Population: A Comparison with the Humphrey Field Analyzer
abstract: Purpose: To evaluate the diagnostic performance and spatial agreement of an online suprathreshold perimeter (Perimouse) compared with the Humphrey Field Analyzer (HFA) for detecting glaucomatous visual field defects. Patients and Methods: In this prospective comparative study, 174 participants (283 eyes with open-angle glaucoma or healthy controls) underwent Perimouse suprathreshold program and HFA. Abnormal points (missed stimuli in Perimouse; points with P<0.5% on HFA total deviation map) were compared. Diagnostic performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. Point-wise performance used neural network-derived area under the curve (AUC) and Cohen's κ. Results: = -0.80, P < 0.001). The intraclass correlation coefficient for abnormal-point counts between Perimouse and HFA was 0.93, and Bland-Altman analysis showed a mean bias of 0.73 abnormal points, with 95% limits of agreement ranging from -10.70 to 12.17. A cutoff of five abnormal points achieved 85.9% sensitivity and 97.9% specificity (AUC = 0.97), with performance improving with disease severity. Point-wise κ values ranged from 0.32 to 0.78 (AUC, 0.67-0.96). The test duration for Perimouse was 2.64 ± 1.83 minutes. Conclusion: Perimouse demonstrated reasonable overall diagnostic accuracy for detecting HFA-defined visual field defects. Diagnostic performance was higher for moderate and advanced glaucomatous defects than for early defects, with variable point-wise agreement with HFA. Perimouse may serve as a rapid, adjunctive tool for preliminary functional screening of glaucomatous visual field loss.
authors: Xiaoyuan Shen; Zidong Chen; Kaixin Tan; Yanmei Fan; Pingping Liu; Haorui Wang; Jing Samantha Pan; Yangfan Yang; Minbin Yu

title: Evolution of evidence-based medicine: toward digital evidence ecosystems and artificial intelligence
abstract: Evidence-based medicine (EBM) has transformed clinical decision-making by integrating the best available research evidence with clinical expertise and patients’ values and preferences. Over the past three decades, EBM has evolved from the critical appraisal of individual studies into a broader framework encompassing evidence synthesis, clinical practice guidelines, assessment of evidence certainty, research transparency, and shared decision-making. Despite these advances, contemporary EBM faces important challenges, including the rapidly increasing volume of research, delays in evidence synthesis and implementation, limited applicability of randomized controlled trials to heterogeneous real-world populations, and difficulties in individualizing population-level evidence. Emerging approaches—including real-world evidence, living evidence, learning health systems, precision medicine, and artificial intelligence (AI)—offer opportunities to address these limitations. Together, these approaches may enable a transition from static to continuously updated evidence, from population-average to more personalized evidence, and from a linear evidence pipeline to a learning evidence ecosystem in which clinical practice both uses and generates evidence. AI may further accelerate evidence retrieval, synthesis, updating, and individualized decision support, while introducing challenges related to reliability, bias, transparency, reproducibility, and accountability. Next-generation EBM should therefore be conceptualized not as a replacement for traditional EBM but as its evolution into a digitally connected, continuously learning evidence ecosystem. In the AI era, the foundational principles of EBM—source verification, critical appraisal, uncertainty assessment, integration of patient preferences, and accountable human judgment—will become increasingly important.
authors: Soo Young Kim

title: Exercise snacks in university settings: a mini review of daily physical activity and sedentary behavior among university students
abstract: University students spend much of their daily life in classrooms, online learning, screen use, library study, dormitory routines, and campus commuting, making insufficient physical activity and prolonged sitting important concerns for health promotion in higher education. Exercise snacks, defined here as brief, repeated, low-barrier bouts of physical activity that can be embedded in ordinary routines, have attracted growing attention in exercise health, public health, and sedentary behavior research. Compared with physical education courses or structured exercise, exercise snacks use short gaps in learning and daily life, for example through brisk walking, stair climbing, dynamic stretching, body-weight exercise, or brief moderate-to-vigorous activity, to increase movement opportunities and interrupt prolonged sitting. This mini review adopts an integrative thematic approach to synthesize work on exercise snacks, physical activity snacks, brief intermittent physical activity, active breaks, sedentary behavior interruption, incidental physical activity, Brain Breaks, and physical activity among university students. It discusses conceptual boundaries, potential effects, contextual conditions, and future directions for translating exercise snacks into university settings. The literature suggests that exercise snacks should be viewed as a supplementary strategy alongside physical education and structured exercise. They may help increase daily physical activity, reduce or interrupt prolonged sitting, and improve the distribution of activity across the day. However, the field is marked by inconsistent definitions, a limited body of university-specific research, scarce evidence from real campus contexts, and insufficient objective measurement. Future studies should define exercise snacks operationally for higher education, prioritize safe, feasible low- to moderate-intensity activities, test interventions within real timetables and campus spaces, and combine wearable devices, smartphone step counts, and activity logs to assess physical activity and sedentary behavior. Exercise snacks in university settings should therefore not be framed as a replacement for physical education, but as a low-cost, accessible, context-embedded pathway for promoting daily physical activity.
authors: Xiaotian Wang; JingLin Wu; Liang Heng; HaoRan Li; ZeYu Zou

title: Facilitators and Barriers to Home Use of Wearable Devices Among Older Adults With Ischemic Stroke: An Exploratory Qualitative Study
abstract: Abstract Background Long-term management of modifiable risk factors is essential for secondary stroke prevention, yet home-based health management among older adults with ischemic stroke remains suboptimal. Wearable devices may support continuous monitoring and personalized health feedback; however, little is known about how this population perceives their use at home or the factors shaping their adoption and continued engagement. This study aimed to explore older adults’ perceptions and experiences regarding the use of wearable devices for home-based health management after ischemic stroke and to identify perceived facilitators and barriers to their adoption and continued use. Methods The Health Belief Model and the Technology Acceptance Model were integrated to guide the conceptual framework of this study. Using purposive sampling, 26 older adults with ischemic stroke who had prior knowledge of or experience with wearable devices were recruited from the neurology department of a Grade A tertiary hospital and a community health service center in Xuzhou, China, between November 2025 and January 2026. Data were collected through focus groups and individual semistructured interviews and analyzed using qualitative content analysis that incorporated both deductive and inductive approaches. Results The analysis identified 6 themes: (1) practical challenges in home health management; (2) perceived technological value and health benefits; (3) barriers to technology use and challenges concerning trust; (4) multilevel social support and empowerment through technology; (5) preferences for age-friendly design; and (6) needs for functions specific to stroke and expectations for health care integration. Continuous health monitoring, real-time feedback, behavioral reminders, and support from family members, peers, communities, and healthcare professionals emerged as key facilitators of wearable device adoption. Major barriers included limited digital literacy, complex operation, concerns regarding monitoring data accuracy, privacy and data security, and affordability. Participants also emphasized the need for personalized monitoring, timely risk alerts, and integration with primary healthcare services. Conclusions Wearable devices have potential to support home-based health management among older adults with ischemic stroke, but successful adoption requires attention to patients’ perceptions, technology-related challenges, social support, and stroke-specific needs. Future interventions should incorporate user-centered and age-friendly design principles, strengthen support from families, communities, and healthcare professionals, and integrate wearable technologies into stroke self-management and preventive care pathways. These findings highlight the importance of developing patient-centered approaches to support sustainable use of wearable technologies in post-stroke home health management.
authors: Nana Chen; Ranran Song; Guoxin Shi; Yulong Wang; Tingting Huang; Ying Peng; 汤先萍; Muwei Zhu

title: Factors influencing the intention to use smart wristbands among patients with COPD: an extended UTAUT model
abstract: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) imposes a substantial global health burden. Despite the considerable potential of wearable devices for early detection and disease management, suboptimal engagement limits their clinical utility. This study aims to identify factors associated with the intention to use smart wristbands among patients with COPD. The study extends the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) by incorporating health risk perception and interface presentation. A sequential mixed-methods design was employed, commencing with semi-structured interviews ( n = 28), followed by a questionnaire survey ( n = 233). Structural equation modeling was used to validate the measurement model and examine the hypothesized relationships. All six constructs demonstrated statistically significant positive associations with intention to use ( P < 0.05). Health risk perception (β = 0.272, P < 0.001) and social influence (β = 0.271, P < 0.001) were the primary correlates of intention to use. This study extends UTAUT by identifying factors correlated with COPD patients’ intention to use smart wristbands. The findings offer practical insights for user-oriented device design and intervention strategies, thereby supporting the promotion of digital health monitoring among COPD patients.
authors: Jingyi Ye; Jianhua Chen; Mi Yao; Guanning Jing; Wenping Li; Yujing Su; Hongjing Pei; Jiapei Xu; Chunhua Chi

title: Faradaically Resilient Triphase Wedge‐Shaped Nanowire Arrays for Robust Bioanalysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Gas‐containing triphase interfaces are attractive for oxygen‐mediated electrochemical systems, yet faradaic stress‐induced electrowetting remains unresolved in triphase biointerfaces. This work presents faradaically resilient wedge‐shaped copper nanowire arrays (W‐CuNWAs) that stabilize oxygen‐enriched triphase interfaces during sustained and repeated electrochemical operations. In contrast with conventional passive liquid‐repellent nanostructures, W‐CuNWAs employ co‐programmed structural–wettability anisotropy to reconcile wettable charge‐transfer regions with gas‐retaining regions within a single nanoarchitecture. Compared to cylindrical CuNWAs, W‐CuNWAs introduce shape‐encoded wetting barriers that increase capillary breakthrough pressure by 2.85‐fold and pin the contact line at the upper edge. Across 3 h of continuous bias, 500 potential cycles, repeated impedance perturbations, and cathodic electrodeposition of a high‐surface‐energy co‐catalyst, W‐CuNWAs retain stable wettability and electrochemical responses with only 0.88 kΩ mass‐transport‐resistance drift, whereas cylindrical counterparts undergo electrolyte infiltration and structural failure. The retained atmosphere‐connected gas phase enables Pt/W‐CuNWAs to achieve 1.65‐fold higher oxygen‐reduction current, 8.96‐fold lower oxygen mass‐transfer resistance, and 2.96‐fold faster current stabilization than cylindrical counterparts. Integration with an FeOOH/BiVO 4 photoanode enables near‐drift‐free, unbiased photoelectrochemical operation over 8.42 h of repeated cathodic cycling, and reliable detection of Alzheimer's neurofilament light chain in clinical plasma. This work establishes shape‐encoded faradaic electrowetting resistance as a design principle for operationally stable, oxygen‐mediated triphase nanoarchitectures in bioanalysis.
authors: Hayeon Kim; Hyeok Lim; Sung Hyun Park; Jaejin Kim; Joonseok Lee; Kayoung Kim

title: Fault identification for intelligent real-time monitoring via mobile accessible networks: a critical review of MEMS microphone-based sensing for bearing diagnostics
abstract: The main objective of Condition Monitoring (CM) is to prevent unexpected downtime by monitoring machine conditions and reducing maintenance costs. To prevent failure, particularly in rotating machinery, CM is performed utilizing sensing devices, which have been the focus of extensive research in recent decades. This paper presents a critical review and provides comprehensive coverage of recent advances in CM for rotating machinery that utilize MEMS microphone-based sensing, with particular emphasis on bearing fault diagnosis relevant to the Fault Identification for Intelligent Real-time Monitoring via Mobile Accessible Network research programme. It synthesises recent journal articles focusing on MEMS (Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems) microphone technologies, signal processing and machine learning techniques, methodological study design and experimental framework, and reported comparative analysis, advantages, limitations, and future research directions. Furthermore, the study reveals a dominant trend toward the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) techniques, resulting in significant advances in CM and an emerging on non-contact-based sensing via mobile accessible system and self-powered sensing. Key gaps identified include the under-representation of MEMS microphone-based sensing, noise robustness and high sensitivity sensors, insufficient edge-deployment validation, the barriers of large datasets processing to achieve effectiveness, and the absence of multi-domain adaptive diagnostic frameworks. As a final point, options for scalable, low-cost, acoustic-based sensing and edge-intelligent computing are proposed, to deliver real-time monitoring across multiple domains.
authors: Firmansyah; Muhammad Khan; Isidro Durazo Cardenas

title: Feasibility of Using a Wearable Device to Identify Loneliness Among Older Adults Living Alone: Mixed Methods Study
abstract: Background: Addressing loneliness is a public health priority, with increasing interest in technological solutions for older adults. However, evidence on real-world feasibility and acceptability of such technologies remains limited. Objective: This study evaluated the feasibility and acceptability of the Conversation as Therapy (CaT) Pin, a wearable device designed to capture time spent in conversation among older adults living alone, following prototype refinement. Specifically, the study assessed whether a sufficient amount of synchronized, device-derived conversation data and self-reported loneliness data could be generated to explore the relationship between conversation time and loneliness. Methods: A 2-phase, mixed methods feasibility study was conducted. In phase 1, a Consumer Advisory Group (CAG) participated in a 1-hour discussion to inform study processes and device design, followed by a 1-week prototype test with older adults (n=3). Prototype usability, device design, and study procedures were explored through interviews and informed iterative refinement. In phase 2, community-dwelling adults aged 65 years or older living alone trialed the device for 2 weeks. Participants completed activity logs capturing loneliness, activity engagement, device wear, and conversations at 6-hour intervals. Device-captured conversation time was compared with self-reported data where available. Qualitative interviews were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis to understand participant experiences of device acceptability and feasibility. Results: In phase 1, 6 CAG participants, including 3 prototype testers, identified usability and design issues that led to modifications before phase 2. Phase 2 involved 23 participants (15 women; mean age 79.4 y, SD 6.7 y), with 7 classified as lonely using the UCLA-3 scale. However, only 8 (34.8%) participants generated sufficient concurrent device and activity log data, preventing meaningful assessment of the relationship between conversation time and loneliness. Feasibility challenges were driven by device acceptability, namely usability, comfort, aesthetics, and integration into daily life, which limited sustained wear and data synchronization. Qualitative findings indicated that participants prioritized quality rather than quantity of social interaction, and many did not perceive personal benefit from device use, citing lack of perceived need or concerns related to functionality and design. Together, methodological and conceptual challenges were identified in using conversation time as a potential indicator of loneliness. Conclusions: This study demonstrated that, in its current form, using a wearable device to capture time spent in conversation and align these data with self-reported loneliness was not feasible among older adults living alone. Feasibility was constrained by device acceptability related to usability, participant adherence, and data synchronization challenges. Findings also suggest that conversation time alone may be insufficient as an indicator of loneliness, given participants' emphasis on the quality and personal meaning of social interaction. These results provide practical lessons for future digital health research with older adults, including the need for early co-design, monitorable data-capture systems, and more nuanced approaches to measuring loneliness.
authors: Rajna Ogrin; Georgina Johnstone; Bradley Crammond; Judy A. Lowthian

title: Fine-Grained Human Activity Recognition in Domestic Settings Using Ultra-Wideband Radar: A Comparative Study of Deep Learning Models
abstract: Human activity recognition with ultra-wideband (UWB) radar offers contactless, privacy-preserving monitoring of daily living, but distinguishing fine-grained activities performed in the same posture remains difficult. We recorded nine daily activities from 30 participants with a single PulsON 410 radar (3.1–5.3 GHz); seven are performed seated in the same chair and differ only by subtle hand and arm motions. Each 15 s recording is a 120×1440 channel–impulse–response matrix, preprocessed by background subtraction, two-dimensional wavelet denoising and standardization. Six deep learning models (Transformer, CNN-LSTM, 1D-CNN, LSTM, GRU and MLP) and a soft-voting ensemble were compared with participant-independent splits (22 training, 3 validation and 5 test participants) and five-fold cross-validation. The Transformer reached the highest cross-validation accuracy (97.74±0.30%). On the held-out participants, the Transformer (97.16%), 1D-CNN (96.93%) and GRU (96.45%) performed similarly, ahead of the CNN-LSTM, LSTM and MLP (87.47%), and a three-model ensemble reached 98.35%. Two additional participant splits and a retrained re-run confirmed that the MLP is clearly the weakest model, but the order of the other models changed by several points between runs; in the re-run, an ensemble of all six models did not exceed the Transformer (97.74%), and a range–Doppler baseline reached only 50.63%. Eating versus drinking tea and mobile phone use versus reading or sitting idle were the most confused pairs. Given the small test cohort and the controlled setting, the results are indicative rather than definitive.
authors: Muhammad Amjad Raza; Nasir Mehmood; Hafeez Ur Rehman Siddiqui; Adil Ali Saleem; Lázaro Javier Hernández Rodríguez; Pablo Herrero García; Isabel de la Torre Díez

title: From Measurement Failure to Privacy Infrastructure: Reframing Contact Tracing Governance for the Next Pandemic
abstract: No measurement, no understanding; no understanding, no control: this foundational scientific principle was exposed as a public health dysfunction by the COVID-19 pandemic. Transmission chains spread invisibly, and the contact histories, mobility patterns, and biosignals necessary for control were never systematically collected. Although sensors and digital technologies existed, the fundamental reason measurement failed was the absence of privacy infrastructure that would have enabled people to provide data with confidence. This failure had structural reasons. The object of measurement in infectious disease control is not a physical phenomenon but human beings, and measurement therefore enters the core of privacy: contact histories, social relationships, and bodily states. Because greater precision also deepens privacy intrusion, contact-tracing apps faced 2 failures: privacy-centered designs lost epidemiological utility, while utility-centered designs were rejected through public distrust. Neither achieved sufficient measurement. This Viewpoint reframes the problem. Privacy protection is not a constraint that impedes infectious disease control but the enabling condition upon which effective measurement depends. Existing regulations and technical methods have not been designed from this premise and have therefore failed to break the cycle of structural distrust. As an institutional approach to filling this gap, we present VRAIO (verifiable record of AI output), which integrates democratic rule-setting, metadata declaration, third-party verification, tamper-proof ledgers, and violation-deterrence incentives. Once privacy infrastructure is established, this foundational principle can operate freely in infectious disease control for the first time. It will enable high-resolution epidemiology and precision intervention, opening a new path for public health that reconciles infection control with individual autonomy and social freedom without relying on blanket social shutdowns.
authors: Yusaku Fujii

title: From Prediction to Prevention: A Systematic Review of AI-Driven Predictive Analytics In Healthcare
abstract: Purpose: This study examined how Artificial Intelligence (AI)-enabled predictive analytics moves from technical prediction towards actionable preventive healthcare and identified the conditions that enable or constrain this translation. Design/methodology/approach: A systematic literature review of 12 peer-reviewed studies published between 2021 and 2026 was conducted using Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA)-guided screening, Critical Appraisal Skills Programme (CASP) quality assessment, and open, axial, and selective coding with frequency analysis. Findings: Three themes emerged: predictive performance does not equal preventive value, timeliness and actionability shape preventive utility, and implementation conditions shape translation into practice. The findings show that preventive value depends on the alignment of predictive validity, timely action, workflow integration, decision ownership, and governance. Originality/value: The study introduces the prediction-to-prevention translation gap and develops a decision-oriented framework for evaluating AI beyond model performance.
authors: Soon Eu Hui; Marcus Teunissen; Yash Bafna; Nishu Ayedee
venue: Asia Pacific Journal of Health Management

title: From Speed and Sensitivity to Robust Reliability: Addressing the Detection Bias of Loop-Mediated Isothermal Amplification (LAMP) in Food Authentication
abstract: Food adulteration poses severe threats to the integrity and safety of global food supply chains. Innovations in analytical techniques, especially the rapid development of LAMP-based detection methods, are indispensable for addressing these risks. However, the dominant research paradigm, which has long prioritized accelerated amplification kinetics and ultralow detection limits, largely obscures a critical limitation: insufficient detection reliability when deployed in complex field environments. This review consolidates state-of-the-art advances targeting reliability optimization and delineates key technical strategies to construct robust, improved-reliability LAMP platforms for real-food testing. Specifically, we summarize critical factors at the reaction and readout levels that compromise the reliability of LAMP under realistic scenarios, such as inexperienced operators, degraded samples, matrices containing inhibitory substances, and uncontrolled environments. We further elaborate on effective solutions to bridge the reliability gap between laboratory validation and on-site deployment, which requires coordinated technical improvements throughout the full LAMP testing pipeline. Ultimately, we propose a forward-looking developmental principle for next-generation LAMP assays: analytical reliability and operational robustness should be elevated to equal priority alongside the traditionally pursued ultra-rapid amplification and high sensitivity. This balanced technical framework may help pave the way toward large-scale standardization of LAMP-enabled food authentication, although its presumptive results must be confirmed by an independent validated method before they can support regulatory enforcement or other formal decisions.
authors: Xiong Xiong; Yahui Zhang; Mengxuan Liu; Yan Guo; Ying Yang

title: From affect to rules: A conceptual model of compensation in prodromal behavioral frontotemporal degeneration
abstract: Behavioral-variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD) is typically described in terms of progressive loss of social and behavioral control. However, the earliest stages of the disease may also involve active, developed forms of compensation that remain largely invisible to standard assessment. These strategies are rarely characterized, yet they may offer a unique entry point into the mechanisms by which social functioning is temporarily preserved despite emerging degeneration. Here, I report a longitudinal single-case study of a young C9orf72 repeat-expansion carrier followed from the prodromal stage to established moderate bvFTD. Based on more than a dozen hours of semi-structured interviews initiated at symptom emergence, thematic analysis identified five compensatory subthemes. Together, these strategies suggested a coherent shift in the architecture of behavioral control that remain largely invisible to standard medical or neuropsychological assessment. As implicit, flexible, and internally sustained regulation became less reliable, functioning appeared to rely on control processes that were more explicit, environmentally distributed, routine-based, and effortful. These observations can be organized around three broader principles: explicitation, externalization, and stabilization. The case suggests that early preservation in bvFTD may reflect not only residual capacities, but also an active and fragile reorganization of social and behavioral control. By foregrounding the patient’s own compensatory work, this study provides a hypothesis-generating conceptual framework for understanding how everyday functioning may be maintained during the prodromal-to-dementia transition, and highlights qualitative longitudinal single-case designs and participatory research as a powerful tool for identifying hidden forms of adaptation in neurodegenerative disease and refine theoretical models of social behavior.
authors: Maxime Bertoux

title: From digital phenotype to closed-loop therapy: artificial intelligence–enabled wearable and connected technology for allergic diseases
abstract: Background The prevalence of allergic diseases continues to rise, yet episodic outpatient care remains constrained by delayed symptom recognition, the "black box" of medication adherence, and fragmented management. Wearables, the Internet of Things (IoT), and artificial intelligence (AI) now converge in "digital phenotyping." From a pharmaceutical perspective, this review appraises these AI-enabled technologies for allergic diseases along the thread of "from digital phenotype to closed-loop therapy." Methods A narrative review synthesizing recent literature on the technical framework, real-time monitoring, risk early warning, long-term management, therapeutic wearables, psychological digital phenotypes, and equity and safety. Results These technologies span the "sensing–warning–management–treatment" chain. Adaptive baseline learning, time-aware modeling, and multimodal fusion enable individualized early warning from noisy physiological and environmental signals. The strongest evidence concerns long-term management: digital inhalers and smartwatches, validated in randomized controlled trials and meta-analyses, improve adherence and asthma control and reduce exacerbations, with economic value in averting biologic escalation; devices are extending from passive sensing to active interventions—nasal acoustic therapy, "feedback as therapy," and conceptual closed-loop epinephrine injection. However, most applications remain at small-sample, single-center validation; portable quantitative pollen detection is an empty niche; and drug confounding of digital phenotypes (β 2 -agonist contamination of heart rate variability) and closed-loop amplification of skin-tone–related bias challenge clinical translation. Conclusions AI-enabled wearables are shifting allergy care from intermittent, subjective consultation toward continuous, closed-loop management, with evidence most mature for digital inhalers. Future work should develop multimodal digital phenotypes and allergy-specific foundation models and strengthen medication-covariate modeling, hard-endpoint validation, and whole-lifecycle equity governance.
authors: Yuxiang Pei; Yongxia Wu; Ruoyu Hou; Kun Wan

title: From shōnen to seinen to Studio Ghibli: attraction to anime and manga, and their relation to mental health and social outcomes
abstract: Abstract Aim Interest in anime and manga can be very diverse (from action-packed stories to romantic tales to works by the famous Studio Ghibli). Our aim was to examine the association of interest in manga and anime (and specifically certain genres) with mental health, social disconnectedness, and subjective well-being outcomes. Subject and methods We used data from a sample of the general adult population in Germany ( N = 2591, mean age 47 years, 50.6% female). Outcomes were quantified using psychometrically sound tools (e.g., Patient Health Questionnaire-9 [PHQ-9] or Satisfaction with Life Scale [SWLS]). General interest in manga and anime and also interest in certain genres (among those who were interested) served as key independent variables. Results A general interest in manga and anime was consistently associated with poor mental health and social disconnectedness (compared with the absence of such interest), whereas it was generally not associated with subjective well-being outcomes. Among those who were interested, while most interest in specific manga genres was only partly or not significantly associated with the outcomes, interest in manga from Studio Ghibli was associated with better mental health and less social withdrawal. Moreover, an interest in anime from Studio Ghibli was associated with several favorable outcomes (better mental health, social connectedness, and higher ikigai levels). Conclusion While a general interest in anime and manga was consistently associated with poorer mental health and social disconnectedness, certain genres were associated with favorable outcomes among those who were interested in them. Further differentiated research is needed to better understand the psychosocial outcomes of anime and manga passion.
authors: André Hajek; Hans‐Helmut König

title: Fuzzy Fault Detection and Band-Conditioned Data Quality Assessment for Sensor Streams: A Continuous Glucose Monitoring Case Study
abstract: Sensor faults can propagate beyond raw measurements and distort the aggregates used to interpret a monitored phenomenon. We propose a domain-agnostic, five-layer fuzzy pipeline that characterizes the reliability of a sensor stream jointly over time and value bands and carries it through to every derived aggregate: (L1) fault tagging of each sample against five fuzzy failure primitives; (L2) fuzzy windowing; (L3) band reliability; (L4) routed repair with propagated reconstruction uncertainty; and (L5) veracity aggregation with linguistic protoforms. An end-to-end acquisition architecture is also specified. The pipeline was instantiated for continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) with clinical knowledge of glucose dynamics and applied to a 14-month recording of an adult with type 1 diabetes (FreeStyle Libre 3, 5-min cadence), of which 294 days contained at least 120 readings. Clean reference days remained essentially unchanged (mean sample quality 0.98-0.99). On the most corrupted day, the estimated time below range fell from 16% to 3%, with a veracity of only 0.14. Over the recording, 38% of the days were too unreliable to phenotype and 5% changed phenotype. Joint time- and band-conditioned reliability assessment thus prevents corrupted sensor data from producing falsely precise clinical conclusions.
authors: Juan Guerrero; Carmen Martínez-Cruz; Macarena Espinilla; José Luis López Ruiz

title: GAP BETWEEN SPONTANEOUS AWARENESS, SELF-REPORTED USE OF PHYSICAL ACTIVITY AS A PREVENTIVE MEASURE, AND QUESTIONNAIRE-ASSESSED MOVEMENT BEHAVIOUR AFTER MYOCARDIAL INFARCTION: A CROSS-SECTIONAL ANALYSIS OF A STRATIFIED RANDOM SAMPLE
abstract: Objective. To determine the discrepancy and degree of agreement between spontaneous awareness, self-reported adherence, and questionnaire-assessed physical activity in patients during long-term follow-up after myocardial infarction, and to identify independent informational, sociodemographic, and clinical factors associated with engagement in approximately 30 minutes of continuous physical activity. Materials and Methods. A secondary cross-sectional analysis was conducted on a stratified proportional random sample of 333 patients following myocardial infarction. Spontaneous awareness was assessed using an open-ended question; self-reported behavioural adherence was evaluated based on spontaneously reported preventive measures that patients were actually implementing. Daily walking, approximately 30 minutes of continuous purposeful physical activity, barriers, and the doctor's recommendation regarding exercise were assessed separately. The primary outcome was engagement in approximately 30 minutes of continuous purposeful physical activity. Independent associations were assessed using modified Poisson regression. Results. Data regarding approximately 30 minutes of continuous purposeful physical activity were available for 315 patients; 98 of these were active – 31.1% (95% CI 26.3–36.4%). At the same time, 240 out of 333 participants (72.1%) reported walking for at least 30 minutes a day. The largest behavioural group consisted of patients who walked for ≥30 minutes but did not engage in 30 minutes of purposeful physical activity – 48.6%. Overall, 14.3% of participants spontaneously identified physical activity as a means of secondary prevention, whilst 11.2% spontaneously reported actually using it as a preventive measure. The agreement between these indicators was low: κ = 0.237; positive agreement was 33.3%, and negative agreement was 90.2%. Spontaneous awareness was associated with a higher prevalence of purposeful physical activity: adjusted prevalence ratio 1.46 (95% CI 1.01–2.13; p = 0.047). Receiving a doctor's recommendation showed a stronger association: 1.97 (1.27–3.05; p = 0.002). Diabetes mellitus was associated with lower activity levels: 0.46 (0.23–0.96; p = 0.037). The main barriers were health status – 45.6%, lack of willpower – 32.1%, lack of time – 13.5%, and underestimating the benefits of exercise – 10.2%.. Conclusions. In the long-term period following myocardial infarction, a discrepancy was found between everyday walking, spontaneous awareness of the preventive role of physical activity, self-reported use of physical activity as a preventive measure, and engagement in approximately 30 minutes of continuous purposeful activity. A doctor's recommendation was associated with a higher prevalence of such activity; however, the cross-sectional design does not allow for the establishment of causality.
authors: І. V. Savchuk; А.М. Sitovskyi
venue: Реабілітаційні та фізкультурно-рекреаційні аспекти розвитку людини (Rehabilitation & recreation)

title: Gaze in the Machine: How Mechanical and AI-Based Eye Contact Correction Shape Communication Experience and Gaze Behaviour in Video Calls
abstract: Abstract Video calls prevent mutual eye contact because the camera and the partner’s image on screen are spatially separated. Teleprompters and AI-based gaze correction promise to restore it, but their effect on users is largely unknown. In a within-subjects study (N = 32), participants played a conversational guessing game with a partner in four conditions: face-to-face, a standard video call, a video call in which the partner used a teleprompter, and a video call with AI-based gaze correction of the partner’s video. We measured social presence , gaze-specific experience and camera awareness by questionnaire, and gaze behaviour by mobile eye tracking. All video conditions showed a large and robust loss of co-presence compared with face-to-face conversation (Cohen’s d z ≈ −1.5 to −1.8), together with heightened camera awareness. Neither intervention narrowed this gap; equivalence tests confirmed comparable co-presence and camera awareness across video conditions. AI-based correction made eye contact feel less natural than the standard video call (d z = −0.54), yet participants’ gaze behaviour remained equivalent. Gaze differences in the teleprompter condition 1 coincided with a smaller on-screen face and are attributable to framing. Restoring the appearance of eye contact thus does not restore what video calls lack. We discuss implications for evaluating and designing gaze technologies.
authors: Leonie Wichers; Leon Schreiber; Sebastian Möller; Robert P. Spang

title: Geography-Aware Energy-Adaptive IoT-WSN Monitoring for Sustainable Smart Irrigation in Precision Agriculture.
abstract: IoT-based wireless sensor networks are increasingly used in smart irrigation, allowing continuous monitoring of soil, weather and crop-water conditions. However, the deployment of sensors knowing only the geographical location cannot ensure sustainable monitoring as the operational constraints such as communication distance, residual energy, packet delivery, dynamic irrigation risk, and node lifetime are still critical. This paper presents a sustainable smart irrigation monitoring framework using a geography-aware energy-adaptive IoT-WSN. The framework encompasses optimized sensor deployment, radio-energy modeling, sink placement analysis, event-driven and adaptive communication, solar energy harvesting, and machine learning-based next-round irrigation risk prediction. Simulations were performed with an irrigation monitoring dataset consisting of multiple measurements of soil moisture, soil nutrient status, temperature, humidity, precipitation, solar radiation, evapotranspiration, spatial coordinates, and critical-event labels. Results show that direct transmission provides complete packet delivery but short lifetime, and event-driven communication reduces transmissions over 94% but weakens the monitoring continuity. ML-assisted adaptive monitoring reduces the transmissions between 56.57%–61.94% while adaptive harvesting achieves the strongest composite sustainability ranking of 0.8317 packet delivery ratio and 1000-round lifetime. This work provides an integrated framework for the joint assessment of energy efficiency, reliability, prediction and sustainability under field constraints for precision agriculture.
authors: Mr. Giriraja C. V; Dr. T. K. Ramesh

title: Glow Up: a single-centre observational study protocol to develop digital biomarkers for prediabetes screening and digital phenotyping
abstract: Introduction Prediabetes, a key precursor to type 2 diabetes, is highly prevalent and underdiagnosed, particularly among adults aged ≥45 years with elevated body mass index (BMI). Early detection is critical because lifestyle interventions can delay or prevent progression to type 2 diabetes. The Glucose Observation and Wearable Use for Prevention (Glow Up) study aims to (1) test the feasibility of a digital biomarker for pre-diabetes screening using wearable- and smartphone-derived lifestyle factors (eg, sleep, physical activity and nutrition patterns) in daily life and to (2) characterise individual- and metabolic subgroup-level variability in lifestyle factors and glycaemic control. Specifically, we aim to examine how lifestyle factors relate to glycaemic status and identify personalised predictors of early metabolic dysregulation. Methods and analysis Glow Up is a prospective, single-centre, observational case-control study conducted in Switzerland. Adults (n=200) aged ≥45 years with body mass index (BMI) ≥25 kg/m² will be recruited, including n=100 individuals with pre-diabetes and n=100 age- and sex-matched normoglycaemic controls. Participants will undergo 4 weeks of continuous monitoring using a blinded continuous glucose monitor (CGM) and commercial- and medical-grade wearables; for example, capturing physical activity, sleep and physiological markers (heart rate variability, heart rate and skin temperature), in addition to completing daily image-based meal logs using smartphones. Glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c), fasting plasma glucose (FPG) and body anthropometrics will be collected at the enrolment visit (T0) and repeated at follow-up (T3), approximately 5 weeks apart. The primary outcome is glycaemic status at T3, classified from HbA1c and FPG using prespecified thresholds. Secondary outcomes include CGM metrics, lifestyle profiling (sleep, physical activity, stress and nutrition) and adherence to image-based meal logging. Ethics and dissemination The study received ethics approval from the Ethics Committee of Eastern Switzerland on 15 May 2025 (BASEC ID: 2025–00972). Written informed consent is obtained from all participants before any study procedures are performed. Findings will be disseminated as articles in international peer-reviewed journals and as posters and oral presentations at national and international conferences. Summaries will be provided to funders and collaborators, and personalised reports to participants. Trial registration number NCT07373418.
authors: Victoria Brügger; Magdalena Fuchs; Qiuhan Jin; Benjamin Wirth; Stefan Bilz; Michael Brändle; Tobias Kowatsch; Mia Jovanova

title: Grouped cross-validation and inter-sensor agreement analysis of expert labels in an open milling anomaly dataset
abstract: Abstract Open datasets let detectors of machining anomalies be compared on the same labels. We analysed the expert path labels of the multi-sensor and MTConnect (MSM) milling dataset on its laboratory machine with accelerometers: 1,498 labelled cutting paths from 34 runs, 325 of them abnormal. Of three predictions specified before any of their statistics was computed, one held and two failed. For logistic models on the root-mean-square (RMS) amplitudes of the accelerometer and sound channels, the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) fell by 0.002 (95 percent interval \textminus{}0.001 to 0.007) from unseen runs to unseen tool families, with their materials and spindle speeds; for models on the spindle signals streamed through MTConnect it fell by 0.033 (0.015 to 0.060). Both falls stayed below the specified threshold of 0.05; a post hoc jackknife over refitted models leaves the size of the MTConnect fall unresolved. Among abnormal paths, the spindle accelerometer and a stethoscope sensor on the base column showed a dominant spectral line off the spindle harmonics on the same paths (Cohen's kappa 0.71, against 0.004 under independence within spindle-speed classes; threshold 0.41), and no robustness variant contradicted this result. Seen before the predictions were specified, every abnormal path and 38 percent of normal paths had more than 1 percent of one microphone's samples at full scale; in exploratory analyses that share alone ranked the labels with an AUC of 0.985 on unseen runs. Detector comparisons on this dataset should split by run and report a clipping baseline.
authors: Adam Park; Luke Yin; Cooper Lee; Andrew Wong; Yoo Choi

title: HeadRoom: Lightweight, Edge-deployable Pipeline for Adaptive Notification Routing
abstract: Emerging wearables, such as smart glasses, can deliver notifications through multiple sensory channels, but there is still a limited understanding of how to choose the right channel at the right moment. We propose HeadRoom, a lightweight, edge-deployable pipeline that estimates the availability of visual and auditory channels in real time from egocentric video and audio. Our controlled user study (N = 25) shows that, under high perceptual load, routing notifications to the more available channel reduces response time relative to routing them to the less available channel. This work opens up a new possibility for adaptive routing of notifications in wearable and immersive systems.
authors: Dinithi Dissanayake; Prasanth Sasikumar; Suranga Chandima Nanayakkara
venue: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology (UIST)

title: Healing cascades and infections in wounds monitored using a wearable sensor of gaseous flux
abstract: Abstract Capabilities for quantitative monitoring of chronic wounds remain an unmet clinical need, as existing diagnostic approaches rely on semiquantitative evaluation of symptoms that lack sensitivity especially during early stages of infection. Here we present a scheme for tracking wound physiology that leverages a miniature, wireless skin-interfaced device for non-contact, transient measurements of the flux of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) and water vapor from the wound microenvironment. Unlike emerging smart bandage platforms that rely on physical contact with the fragile wound bed to interrogate liquid-phase biomarkers, this strategy uses an engineered microclimate and suspended suite of sensors to measure the diffusive transport of wound-derived gases across the wound surface but separated from it. The result enables quantitative evaluation of metabolic activity and healing progression without perturbing the healing tissues. In biofilm growth models of Staphylococcus aureus , measurements demonstrate that trends in VOC flux correlate strongly with bacterial growth kinetics and precede any visible biofilm formation. Longitudinal monitoring in infected murine wound healing models shows that concurrent measurements of water vapor and VOC flux provide complementary physiological insights, capturing both the trajectory of barrier restoration and the dynamics of bacterial burden. The findings establish this non-contact sensing scheme as a distinct and clinically translatable paradigm for wound monitoring, with broad implications for non-invasive surveillance of disease states in which tissue metabolic activity and skin barrier integrity serve as actionable physiological readouts. Significance Statement Limited capabilities in continuous, quantitative assessment of a wound make early diagnosis and effective management challenging, particularly in cases of infection that rapidly progress before symptoms appear. Non-contact approaches for wound monitoring that preserve fragile tissue can transform wound care. In this context, gaseous flux from the wound bed provides an integrative measure of microbial activity and barrier restoration. This study establishes a wearable sensing platform that quantifies these fluxes in real time, enabling early infection detection and temporal tracking of wound healing. These results highlight a path toward personalized treatment strategies and reduced reliance on episodic clinical evaluation.
authors: Chong-Min Kyung; Ansen Tan; Zixi Chen; Kyung Rok Pyun; Shupeng Li; Fujie Yin; Aiwa Zhang; Neena Feldman; Evan J. Neuhart; Amara D. Moreno; Joyce Eunsung Yoon; Jaeho Shin; Joseph Woojin Song; Jacob T. Trueb; Yonggang Y. Huang; Guillermo Antonio Ameer; John A. Rogers
