title: Higher explanation-necessity scores are associated with longer written explanations of autonomous driving scenes
abstract: Explanations of automated-vehicle behavior may help occupants understand what prompted a maneuver, but how much an explanation should say remains an open design question. Retrospective annotation of recorded driving scenes can supply candidate content. We analyzed 1,103 training and test records from the release, matching the source-described corpus size; each paired human-written text with an aggregate perceived explanation-necessity score. Explanations contained 9,541 whitespace-delimited tokens (mean 8.65; range 2–20) before lexical preprocessing. Higher scores were associated with longer explanations (Pearson’s \(r=0.374\) ; template-cluster bootstrap 95% interval [0.266, 0.448]), including after score-1.0 observations were excluded. We call this corpus-level length association progressive elaboration . Bounded-model comparisons did not identify a unique latent-category count. For groupwise summaries, we used four descriptive partitions: three below-ceiling regions and 59 records scored 1.0. Record-weighted and unique-template analyses showed higher within-partition lexical distinctiveness in upper than in lower partitions. In template-grouped cross-validation of these exploratory partitions, the unweighted text model exceeded token-count and stratified-dummy baselines in balanced accuracy (0.382 versus 0.327 and 0.247). The 1,280-record rerun preserved the score—length, lexical, and predictive findings and left the latent-category count unresolved. These results motivate prospective studies of how annotation-derived content should be selected, compressed, and delivered in real time.
authors: Gwangbin Kim; Dohyeon Yeo; Yumin Kang; Minwoo Oh; SeungJun Kim

title: Hip Mobility Is Associated with Isokinetic Hip Adduction Torque in Recreationally Active Females: An Exploratory Study
abstract: This exploratory study examined whether trunk and hip mobility are associated with isokinetic hip torque in recreationally active females. Twenty-two women completed standing isokinetic hip testing at 60°·s⁻¹, yielding peak torque (PT; normalised to body mass), time to peak torque, and joint angle at peak torque for hip flexion–extension and abduction–adduction. Segmental (lumbar, thoracic, hip) and global mobility indices, composites of active range of motion, were quantified with inertial measurement units. Ninety-six Spearman correlations were computed with Benjamini–Hochberg false-discovery-rate (FDR) control; regression models were fitted post hoc. Two associations survived FDR correction: dominant hip adduction PT was related to hip mobility (r = .70, 95% CI .36 to .87) and to global mobility (r = .66, 95% CI .34 to .84). A segmental model accounted for 49% of the variance (adjusted R² = .485), with hip mobility the only stable predictor (β = 0.57, 95% CI 0.13 to 1.00). Sensitivity analyses indicated that this finding was robust to the construction of the indices and was carried mainly by hip flexion range of motion, which is unrelated to the fixed testing excursion. A side-matched analysis weakened the dominant-side association (r = .57). Associations of global mobility with the timing and angle of non-dominant adduction torque did not survive correction. The global index contains the hip index (r = .85), so the two are not independent constructs. Hip mobility is associated with hip adduction torque magnitude; the findings are hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in larger, preferably longitudinal studies.
authors: Şeyma Tuba Acar; Büşra Yücelsoy; Enda Francis Whyte; Cengiz Ölmez
venue: Research in Sport Education and Sciences

title: Host–Virus Immune Interactions in Andes Virus Infection: Implications for Human-to-Human Transmission, Pathogenesis, and Public Health
abstract: , andesense) is unique among hantaviruses in that it may transfer from person to person and cause severe vascular damage. The evidence on host-virus immunological interactions and their importance in disease progression, transmission, and public health is compiled in this narrative review. ANDV mostly affects pulmonary endothelial cells and does not result in widespread cell loss. Rather, the loss of vascular barrier integrity is caused by vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) signaling, Ras homolog family member A (RhoA) activation, breakdown of vascular endothelial (VE)-cadherin, hypoxia-related pathways, and mediators produced from infected pericytes. Additionally, the virus interferes with early antiviral defenses involving protein kinase R (PKR), TANK-binding kinase 1 (TBK1)-interferon regulatory factor 3 (IRF3), mitochondrial antiviral-signaling protein (MAVS), and retinoic acid-inducible gene I (RIG-I)/melanoma differentiation-associated protein 5 (MDA5). The intensity or outcome of the disease has been associated with increased interleukin-6 (IL-6), altered complement activity, thrombocytopenia, neutralizing-antibody reactions, and specific host genetic variations; nevertheless, significant T-cell activation does not necessarily correspond with viral clearance. Blood and a number of mucosal and secretory samples have been found to contain ANDV ribonucleic acid (RNA), albeit RNA discovery by itself does not prove the presence of an infectious virus. Epidemiological evidence indicates that Secondary transmission is rare and mostly linked to extended close or intimate contact. Genomic sequencing, when paired with epidemiological evidence, can shed light on transmission chains. Recent outbreaks linked to travel further emphasize the significance of worldwide surveillance and coordinated contact tracing. Prospective studies integrating genomic analysis, serial virological sampling, and standardized exposure evaluation are required to more effectively define the infectious phase and transmission patterns.
authors: Awadh Alanazi; Mohamed Nabil Fathy Ibrahim; MaramAwied Alenezi; Rahaf Ziyad I. Alabdullah

title: Human Digital Twins: A Paradigm Shift in Personalized Healthcare and Predictive Medicine
abstract: Human Digital Twins (HDTs) are rapidly emerging as a transformative innovation in personalized healthcare and predictive medicine. Through the integration of real-time, high-resolution data from multiple sources like genomics, wearable devices, electronic health records, and behavioral inputs, HDTs create virtual replicas of individuals that can simulate, predict, and optimize health outcomes. This article explores the conceptual framework that underpins HDTs, their current and potential applications in personalized healthcare, as well as their role in advancing predictive medicine and population health. It also addresses the technological and ethical challenges associated with HDT development, including data privacy, interoperability, algorithmic bias, and regulatory gaps. Furthermore, the article outlines future directions, and emphasizes the importance of multi-omics integration, cognitive modeling, edge computing, and interdisciplinary collaboration. Through a comprehensive analysis, this study highlights HDTs as a paradigm shift with the potential to revolutionize healthcare delivery, improve patient outcomes, and enable a more proactive, data-driven model of care.
authors: Somkenechi Chinwe Okpala
venue: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF MEDICAL EVALUATION AND PHYSICAL REPORT

title: Human-Computer Co-Regulation: A Review of Biofeedback for Meditative Practice
abstract: Biofeedback has been proposed to support meditation and mindfulness practices through wearables, mobile applications, VR/AR systems for decades, and other interactive devices. However, evidence of its effectiveness remains mixed and fragmented across existing research in psychophysiology and Human-Computer Interaction (HCI). This work analyzes 39 studies published between 2015 and 2025 on real-time, user-facing biofeedback for contemplative practice. We first outline a taxonomy of biofeedback interfaces based on sensing modality, feedback channel, interaction context and temporal feedback characteristics, then we synthesize the existing study results on modality-practice fit, showing that the performance of each biofeedback sensing modality in meditative practice is closely related to the meditation practice type: Respiration and heart rate variability (HRV) are the most suitable modalities for paced breathing and stress recovery, and EEG is more appropriate for attention-oriented and experiential targets. Electrodermal activity (EDA) mainly reflects arousal awareness rather than directly measuring meditation quality. In addition, a review-informed co-regulation framework consisting of within-session physiological regulation, experiential mediation, and transfer support is proposed in this work. Finally, we summarize the main gaps in the existing literature and propose design principles for future systems.
authors: Mengxi Liu; Danyang Peng; Sizhen Bian; Lala Shakti Swarup Ray; Yajun Cheng; Bo Zhou; Siyu Yuan; Kanyu Chen; Kai S. Kunze; Kouta Minamizawa; Paul Lukowicz
venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Interactive Mobile Wearable and Ubiquitous Technologies

title: Hybrid intelligent modeling for enhanced surface integrity, process dynamics, and sustainable performance in finish ultra-precision hard turning of AISI D2 under dry conditions
abstract: Abstract This study presents a hybrid intelligent modeling framework for improving surface quality, process dynamics, and sustainable performance in ultra-precision hard turning of AISI D2 steel of 62 HRC under dry conditions. To address gaps in material-specific modeling and the omission of dynamic process variables in sustainable machining, tool vibration ( V rms ) was integrated with cutting speed, feed, and depth of cut using a full factorial experimental design. ANOVA and Sobol sensitivity analyses identified feed as the most influential factor affecting surface roughness ( R a ) and resultant cutting force ( F R ), while tool vibration exhibited significant interaction effects. Three machine-learning models, Bayesian regularization neural network (BRNN), GA-BRNN, and PSO-BRNN, were developed and compared. BRNN demonstrated the best overall performance based on predictive accuracy and computational efficiency. External validation showed highly accurate prediction of F R with an R 2 of 80.35% and a MAPE of 9.30%. For R a , BRNN achieved an R 2 of 70.43% and a MAPE of 38.41%, corresponding to satisfactory predictive performance according to the adopted MAPE criteria. The comparatively lower R a accuracy reflects the greater complexity and variability of surface generation compared with cutting force formation. The BRNN model was analytically formulated and integrated with a multi-objective particle swarm optimization algorithm to determine Pareto-optimal machining parameters. The optimal conditions ( v c = 75 m/min, f = 0.025 mm/rev, a p = 0.06 mm) yielded predicted F R and R a values of 119.87 N and 0.58 µm, respectively. Confirmation experiments produced an average minimum error of 6%, supporting the framework''s applicability for sustainable machining optimization and intelligent decision support in smart manufacturing.
authors: Ugonna Loveday Adizue; Vahid Pourmostaghimi
venue: The International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology

title: Hydrogel Microneedles for Perioperative Applications: Drug Delivery, Biosensing, and Theranostic Translation
abstract: Hydrogel microneedles provide access across the skin barrier for drug delivery and interstitial-fluid sampling. Their perioperative use depends on whether that access remains reliable during skin preparation, surgical positioning, and changes in tissue perfusion. This narrative review examines how material design affects delivered dose, measurement accuracy, and clinical feasibility. Human sampling studies establish feasibility for selected measurements; most therapeutic and integrated sensing applications remain at the preclinical stage or have been investigated in other clinical settings. The review distinguishes these findings from evidence in surgical patients. Particular attention is given to insertion and adhesion on disinfected or compromised skin, the relationship between interstitial and plasma measurements, and drug exposure after delivery is interrupted. Short-duration superficial procedures and observational drug or wound-adjacent monitoring offer focused questions for initial studies with standard care maintained. Progress toward treatment requires validation of the complete product, including sterilization, batch consistency, shelf life, and safeguards against uncontrolled release. Clinical studies should report failed applications and adverse events alongside patient outcomes. Autonomous anesthetic administration remains a development goal whose safety cannot be inferred from separate demonstrations of sensing and drug release.
authors: Yue Qi; Cong Wang; Jinyue Chen; Dalong Wu

title: INTELLIGENT INTRUSION DETECTION USING MACHINE LEARNING FOR SECURE DIGITAL INFRASTRUCTURE
abstract: The growing interconnectivity of digital infrastructure has increased exposure to cyber threats and strengthened the need for effective intrusion detection. Machine-learning techniques offer promising capabilities for recognizing malicious network behavior from structured traffic observations. However, differences in the representation of benign and attack traffic can affect the development and interpretation of intelligent detection systems. This study characterized the dataset and examined the distribution of legitimate and malicious network traffic, with particular attention to major intrusion groups and less frequently represented attack categories. A secondary descriptive analysis of the original CIC-IDS2017 network-flow dataset was conducted. Dataset structure, traffic attributes, class labels, and traffic-category distributions were systematically examined. Network observations were organized into benign traffic and broader intrusion groups to describe their relative representation. The analysis identified substantial variation across traffic categories. Legitimate network communication represented the largest component, whereas malicious observations comprised multiple attack types with different levels of occurrence. Denial-of-service-related activities represented a major portion of intrusion traffic, while port scanning, brute-force, web-based, botnet, infiltration, and other attack categories contributed additional security-relevant observations. Several specialized attack classes were sparsely represented, demonstrating notable class imbalance. These findings indicate that CIC-IDS2017 provides a diverse foundation for machine-learning-oriented intrusion-detection research. The observed traffic diversity supports analysis of multiple malicious behaviors, while class imbalance highlights the importance of appropriate evaluation strategies and careful interpretation of future predictive models. The study provides a structured basis for subsequent intelligent cybersecurity research and model development.
authors: Mohammad Majharul Islam Jabed; Bhanu Pratap Singh

title: IOT- BASED WOMEN SECURITY SYSTEM
abstract: The safety of women in public places, workplaces, and while travelling remains a serious social concern. Incidents of harassment, stalking, and assault often take place in situations where the victim cannot reach a phone, unlock it, and dial for help in time. Even when a call is made, the person receiving it may not know the exact location of the victim. This paper presents an IoT-based women security system in the form of a small wearable device that can raise an emergency alert with a single action and share the live location of the wearer with trusted contacts and the nearest police control room. The device is built around an ESP32 microcontroller connected to a GPS receiver, a GSM module, a pulse sensor, a three-axis accelerometer, a small microphone, and a concealed push button. When the button is pressed, or when the device detects a combination of an abnormally high heart rate and sudden violent movement, it enters the emergency mode. In this mode it obtains the current coordinates from the GPS receiver and sends SMS messages containing a map link to preconfigured contacts. At the same time it places an automatic voice call to the first contact so that someone is alerted even if messages are not read immediately. Where Wi-Fi or mobile data is available, the device also publishes its location and sensor readings to a cloud platform using the MQTT protocol. A companion mobile application and a web dashboard display the live track of the wearer, the time of the alert, and the recorded audio clip captured by the microphone during the first seconds of the emergency. The location is updated every few seconds until the alert is cancelled by the wearer with a secret button sequence or closed by a responder, so that contacts can follow the movement of the victim if she is being taken away. The system also includes deterrent features. A loud buzzer can be activated to attract the attention of people nearby, and an optional shock circuit provides a means of selfdefence. A fake call feature on the mobile application allows the user to leave an uncomfortable situation without confrontation. All alerts are logged in the cloud with time, place, and sensor data, which can later assist police investigation and help authorities identify locations where incidents occur repeatedly.

title: Institutional Strengthening for Internet of Things-Based Water Quality Monitoring in Aquaculture Ponds of Lontar Village
abstract: Purpose: This project implemented an IoT-based water quality monitoring system at a pilot milkfish pond in Lontar Village, integrated with knowledge transfer and institutional strengthening for sustainable system management.Methodology: Conducted from July 8 to August 8, 2026, the intervention combined four phases: (1) installation of the IoT-based monitoring system, (2) participatory education and hands-on operator training, (3) competency evaluation using 15 observational indicators, and (4) institutionalization through SOP handover and official operator appointment by the Lontar Village Government.Results: The system acquired 458,646 valid records (82.96% completeness), detecting a critical drop in dissolved oxygen to 3.4 mg/L. Two local operators achieved competency scores of 73.3% and 80.0%. Autonomy gaps in technical troubleshooting were mitigated via SOP standardization and administrative legitimization through Village Letters of Assignment.Conclusions: Integrating precision monitoring, community capacity, and village-level legitimacy is essential for adaptive and sustainable coastal technology governance.Limitations: Implementation was limited to one pilot pond for one month, excluded the Total Dissolved Solids (TDS) parameter owing to a sensor malfunction, and did not use a pretest/post-test design or post-harvest economic analysis.Contributions: This study offers a replicable framework for technology governance and capacity building in aquaculture, which is applicable to village governments, academics, and IoT developers.

title: Integrated Taguchi and Grey Relational Optimization of Drilling Process Parameters
abstract: The appropriate selection of machining parameters plays a vital role in enhancing productivity, improving surface finish, and reducing machining costs in drilling operations. The present study focuses on optimizing spindle speed, feed rate, depth of cut, and drill diameter to improve Material Removal Rate (MRR) and minimize surface roughness. Experimental investigations were conducted on EN 36 steel using a CNC drilling machine equipped with carbide-coated HSS twist drills, following an L16 orthogonal array based on the Taguchi design. Signal-to-Noise (S/N) ratio analysis was employed to identify the optimal parameter settings for the individual performance characteristics. Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) was subsequently performed to assess the statistical significance and relative contributions of the selected machining parameters. To achieve simultaneous optimization of MRR and surface roughness, Grey Relational Analysis (GRA) was implemented to convert the multiple-response problem into a single Grey Relational Grade (GRG). Based on the GRG analysis, the optimal machining conditions were determined as a spindle speed of 2500 rpm, a feed rate of 100 mm/min, a depth of cut of 15 mm, and a drill diameter of 18 mm. The ANOVA findings indicated that depth of cut was the most significant factor influencing the overall drilling performance, followed by drill diameter, spindle speed, and feed rate. The results demonstrate the applicability of integrating Taguchi methodology, ANOVA, and GRA for optimizing multiple performance characteristics in the drilling of EN 36 steel.
authors: Naveen Gandhi M; P Rajeswari

title: Interactive Industrial Metaverse Platform based on Digital Twin and Extended Reality for Real-time Process Monitoring
abstract: The transition toward Industry 4.0 and the emerging Industry 5.0 paradigm highlights the need for real-time integration of heterogeneous machines, human-machine collaboration, and interoperable data flows. Modern factories frequently combine advanced machines with legacy systems, leading to inconsistent data structures and limited process visibility. To address these challenges, a DT-XR-based industrial metaverse framework was developed to enable standardized data acquisition, cloud-centered information management, and immersive visualization across diverse manufacturing environments. The framework provides a multilayer architecture that consolidates heterogeneous controller and sensor data into a unified structure, processes them on edge devices, stores them as cloud-based time-series records, and delivers them to digital twin and XR interfaces for real-time monitoring. This approach supports the cyber-physical integration emphasized in Industry 4.0 and the human-centered decision-making prioritized in Industry 5.0. The framework was validated through two case studies. In a hybrid additive-subtractive testbed, heterogeneous controller data and sensor signals were synchronized within a digital twin with an end-to-end latency of approximately 33.00ms. In an industry-scale blow molding system operating with PLC-based legacy machine, standardized data management and AR-based visualization of heater temperatures, mold timing, environmental conditions, and inline states were achieved, with an average round-trip latency of approximately 1040.92ms. These results demonstrate that the proposed DT-XR framework enhances interoperability, process transparency, and operator-centered decision-making, and shows strong potential for scaling to larger production systems and future Industry 5.0 applications. © 2026 The Authors. title: InteractiveWorld: A Verifiable Human-Centric Environment for Building Better Interactive MLLM Assistants
abstract: People have long dreamed of an assistant that is always there to guide them and remind what they forget, from new dishes to lost keys. Powered by multimodal large language models (MLLMs), egocentric AI assistants on wearable devices are bringing this dream within reach: they see what the user sees and give instructions for user's physical work when necessary. However, testing such assistance is challenging and usually requires real people. The expensive and rare real interaction data leaves a key question unanswered: Can today's MLLMs truly help people in physical world? To answer this question, we propose InteractiveWorld, the first verifiable environment for closed-loop interaction between human and AI assistant. Unlike existing robot-centric simulators, InteractiveWorld lets the assistant guide a human agent who observes the scene, understands instructions, and acts independently. It thus realistically simulates how AI assistant collaborates with human: the assistant instructs, the human acts, and the environment executes actions and updates what they see next. Building on it, we introduce InteractiveBench, the first dynamic benchmark for egocentric AI assistants, with 120 multi-turn tasks across six categories. In each task, the assistant guides the human in real time, and every instruction shapes the outcome, which is scored by verifiable, state-based rewards. Experiments with 12 frontier MLLMs show they are still far from reliable assistants. Even the strongest model, Claude Fable 5.1, achieves at most 20% and 25% on long-horizon Guidance and Planning tasks, respectively. Overall, our work offers a verifiable platform and a rigorous evaluation set, laying a solid foundation for research on interactive MLLM assistants that truly help people in the physical world.

title: Invasive species detection from high resolution aerial photographs
abstract: This project focuses on the automatic detection of invasive plant species along railway tracks. Initially, the project targets two highly invasive species: Asian Knotweed (Fallopia japonica) and Giant Hogweed (Heracleum mantegazzianum). ProRail, the Dutch railway infrastructure manager, collects yearly high-resolution helicopter imagery covering all railway tracks in the Netherlands. A deep learning-based classifier is applied to this imagery to detect the aforementioned invasive species. This work was presented as a poster at the 25th anniversary event of the Ambient Intelligence research group.

title: Investigating effects of day-to-day variations in environmental exposure on the human brain: study protocol for the Day2Day Environment project
abstract: BACKGROUND: Understanding how daily environmental exposures influence the human brain and mental health is increasingly important in the context of global urbanization and climate change. Previous studies have focused primarily on long-term environmental factors or isolated features like green space and air quality, neglecting the interaction between multiple exposures encountered in everyday life. This protocol paper describes the study design and dataset of the Day2Day Environment project, an ongoing study investigating how real-world, day-to-day environmental variability affects brain structure, function, and well-being. METHODS: This dense longitudinal study collects multimodal data from 30 participants over 25 testing sessions, including neuroimaging and tracking of physiological, behavioral, and environmental variables. Using wearable devices, geographic ecological momentary assessments, and GPS-based geospatial tracking, we collect data on air quality, noise, light exposure, physical activity, stress, cognition, and affect. Neuroimaging measures include T1- and T2*-weighted images during rest and tasks, quantitative multi-parameter mapping, high-resolution proton density imaging of the hippocampus, and diffusion tensor imaging sequences. CONCLUSION: The Day2Day Environment dataset offers a unique opportunity to study short-term neuroplasticity in response to the dynamic interplay between multiple environmental exposures. Furthermore, the diversity of measurements in this dataset may be valuable for addressing research questions beyond environmental neuroscience.
authors: Kim Falkenstein; Claire Pauley; Simone Kühn

title: IoT Based Smart Safety Wristband Using BLE Zone Sensing and LoRa Long-Range Alerting for High-Density Public Gatherings
abstract: Large religious and public gatherings, such as the Kumbh Mela, bring together millions of people in a small area for a short period. In these conditions mobile networks become congested, and an individual in distress often cannot be identified or reached in time. This paper presents the design of an IoT Based Smart Safety Wristband that combines two complementary low-power radio technologies. Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) is used for short-range zone sensing and active geofencing: fixed beacons advertise their zone identity, and the wristband classifies the zone it is in. LoRa is used for long-range, infrastructure-independent delivery of compact alert packets to a gateway, from where a web dashboard shows the zone and status of every wristband. The wristband is built around an ESP32 microcontroller with an SOS button, an OLED display, a vibration motor, a buzzer and status LEDs, and is powered by a rechargeable Li-ion cell. We review thirteen published studies on LoRa range and reliability, BLE zone detection and crowd safety, and use their findings to justify key design choices: a very short payload, a sliding-window RSSI filter with hysteresis, and local alerting that works even when the backhaul is unavailable. The paper reports the system design, the alert protocol, an analytical time-on-air estimate and a structured evaluation plan. Field measurements are deliberately not reported, because the prototype tests are still in progress; the evaluation tables are provided so that measured values can be entered once available

title: IoT-Based Sleep Apnea Prevention, Detection, and Emergency Alert System
abstract: Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA) is a common sleep disorder that often goes undiagnosed. It causes breathing to stop and restart repeatedly during sleep, which can increase long-term risks for heart and metabolic health. Polysomnography is the standard method for diagnosing OSA. However, it relies on lab equipment, overnight supervision, and trained technicians, making it expensive and mostly impractical for use at home. This work proposes an IoT-based system for preventing, detecting, and alerting about sleep apnea. The goal is to allow affordable, continuous monitoring a t home. The design uses a n ESP32 microcontroller connected to a MAX30102 pulse oximetry sensor, an INMP441 digital MEMS microphone, and an MPU6050 motion sensor. Together, these devices capture data on SpO₂ levels, heart rate, snoring, body posture, breathing movement, and respiratory rate. The system filters and normalizes these signals, converting them into Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC) and Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT) features. This data goes to a hybrid CNN-BiLSTM-XGBoost model, which evaluates sleep quality and the severity of apnea, categorizing it as Normal, Mild, Moderate, or Severe. If a Severe episode is detected, the system uploads the information to Firebase Cloud, retrieves the patient's location from a NEO-6M GPS module, and sends a n emergency SMS to registered caregivers via a SIM800L GSM module. It also gently wakes the patient using a micro speaker that plays a softly rising tone and activates a relaycontrolled mini air pump for additional support. A thematic review of related IoT, wearable technology, deep learning, contactless systems, a n d cloud-based monitoring supports the proposed design and explains the integrated sensing- to-response process. Since this paper discusses a proposed system instead of one that has been built and tested, it emphasizes design intent and expected functionality, rather than actual results

title: Irish giants: from myth to medicine
abstract: The archetype of the 'Irish giant' in folklore appears to be rooted in historical individuals afflicted by pituitary gigantism. This review compiles and critically assesses the veracity of historical accounts, primarily from the late 17th to the early 20th century, for a group of individuals with gigantism that had Irish origins. Clinical and, in some cases, osteological data (e.g., Charles Byrne, Cornelius Magrath, and Patrick Cotter) confirm a diagnosis of pituitary gigantism, a rare disease that is caused by excess growth hormone secretion from a pituitary adenoma. In the pre-scientific era, the effects of the unopposed hormone excess resulted in extreme tall stature, debilitating morbidity, and usually premature death. This aligns with our modern understanding of the potential severity of hormonal excess and tumour growth in pituitary gigantism. The high concentration of cases in Ulster is explained by a founder germline pathogenic variant (c.910 C > T, p.(R304*)) in the AIP gene, that was identified in multiple contemporary families, later in the skeleton of Charles Byrne and most recently, among the Irish diaspora. Estimated to have arisen around 2500 years ago, this variant established a direct medical explanation for a regional phenomenon. In this review we provide a detailed compilation of historical Irish giants and discuss the evidence linking myth and folklore to the modern medical reality of pituitary gigantism as a rare, severe genetic disease.
authors: Wouter W. de Herder; Paul Benjamin Loughrey; Márta Korbonits; Adrian Daly

title: LLMs as Narrators of Lived Experience: A Study of Generative Hermeneutical Epistemic Injustice in ADHD Sense-Making
abstract: Large language models (LLMs), as non-human actors, do not have access to first-hand experiences. Yet they are increasingly consulted in processes of making sense of them, from mental health chatbots to reflexive journals. As a result, complex lived realities risk being distorted or flattened through second-order representations. In this paper, we expand on conceptual work to empirically examine narrative mechanisms through which LLMs as narrators give rise to hermeneutical epistemic injustice. We foreground narration as a key interpretive process through which experience is made intelligible. Focusing on ADHD as a motivating case, we compare first-person narratives from online ADHD communities with narratives generated by LLMs. Using an interpretive, reflexive analysis, we examine how these forms of narration construct lived experience. We find that generated narratives organise ADHD experience through recurring modes that individualise, standardise, and stabilise interpretation, reducing messiness, complexity and ambiguity present in community narration. More situated and unresolved accounts remained possible when foregrounded through prompting. We argue that the epistemic concern lies not only in what models can represent, but in which interpretations they make readily available and which require prior conceptual and prompting work.
authors: Anne Arzberger; Dongying Zhang

title: LOng COvid Multidisciplinary consortium: Optimising Treatments and servIces acrOss the NHS (LOCOMOTION) - COV-LT2-0016
abstract: Plain English Summary Long COVID affects over two million people in the UK, it has various symptoms and impacts daily life. Although there are over 90 long COVID clinics in England, most people have not had access to them, and waiting times to be seen are long. Our research aimed to produce a ‘gold standard’ for care by analysing existing practices, creating new systems of care and establishing best practices nationally. This research has been developed with patients with lived experience and a wide range of NHS professionals in ten long COVID clinics across the UK and led by academics (universities) with links to other long COVID funded studies. Key priorities were understanding and improving: clinical assessment; advice and treatment; NHS pathways and costs; and returning to work and other roles. Comparing findings across our partnership of ten clinics, we learnt more about treatment, provided real-time education to other healthcare staff and patients, and established best practice guidance that was shared with clinics outside our study group. We identified the disadvantages experienced by those from ethnic minority and faith backgrounds and explored ways these could be reduced. We understood the barriers at the workplace and produced guidance to improve returning to previously held roles. An ideal way of engaging patients in supporting each other by sharing experiences (peer support) was put forward. Variations in symptoms on a daily and weekly basis were understood using wearable technology. We showed the value of using an objective 10-min Lean test in clinics for detecting dysautonomia. We tested a questionnaire instrument that we had developed to measure change in long COVID and approved its use for future studies. The impact of the condition on caregivers and the country's economy was estimated. In summary, we established how the condition of long COVID needs to be recognised and how the condition should be ideally managed, and we helped improve the NHS pathways for the condition. Executive Summary Background: Long COVID, a novel condition of persistent symptoms beyond 4 weeks after COVID-19 infection, affects more than 2 million people in the UK. The NHS in England invested in starting specialist clinics for the condition. Many patients did not have access to these specialist clinics, there were long waits to be seen, and there was considerable variation in practice and pathways. There was a need for more recognition of the condition, peer support and informing national policy for the condition. Aims and objectives: We sought to optimise and standardise long-term COVID care both within and outside NHS specialist clinics, including improving access, reducing inequalities, helping patients manage their symptoms effectively at home, and providing guidance and decision support for primary care. We aimed to systematically analyse variation in symptom presentation and current practices, iteratively improve pathways and systems of care, standardise outcome measurement, and disseminate better practices. Methods and analysis: This mixed-method, multi-site study was informed by the principles of applied health services research, quality improvement, co-design, outcome measurement and learning health systems. It was developed in close partnership with patients (whose stated priorities were prompt clinical assessment; evidence-based advice and treatment; and help with returning to work and other roles) and with front-line clinicians. Workstreams and tasks to optimise assessment, treatment and monitoring were based in three contrasting settings: [1] specialist management in 10 long COVID clinics across the UK, via a quality improvement collaborative (QIC), experience-based co-design and targeted efforts to reduce inequalities of access, analyse vocational problems and develop a vocational rehabilitation programme, recommend a framework for peer support groups; [2] patients self-management at home, with wearable sensors and technology-supported symptom monitoring, and regular completion of outcome measures including the C19-YRS (COVID-19 Yorkshire Rehabilitation Scale) on our digital outcome measures platform; and [3] harnessing electronic record data from primary and secondary care to study referral pathways, analyse primary care coding and referrals at the primary-secondary care interface, along with analysis of productivity loss and healthcare burden. Study governance included a 9- member active patient advisory group (PAG) and patient advisory network (PAN). The PAG co-designed and co-produced all steps of the study from concept to dissemination. An external advisory group (EAG) provided strategic oversight and access to stakeholders independent of the study. We also undertook additional service evaluation studies from NHS England and Public Health Scotland analysing outcomes of long COVID clinics in their respective nations. Results and key findings: Some of the key findings were: The goal of accessible, holistic, multidisciplinary assessment and management was met by different services using different service models and staff mix. Most topics prioritised for quality improvement had a weak or contested evidence base, but even in the absence of high-quality research evidence, much learning and improvement occurred. The dual burden of having to fight to be heard in a context of structural inequalities takes its toll and could be part of the reason why so few people from ethnically minoritised communities attend long COVID clinics. A roadmap resource has been developed to address many people’s experience of multiple poorly planned return-to-work attempts and inadequate adjustments. Peer support in long COVID in the form of online networks has benefited many long COVID patients already but does not suit everyone in its current format. Clinical severity types (mild/moderate/ severe) have been identified, which fluctuate longitudinally. Understanding the triggers help patients make adjustments to physical/cognitive/emotional exertion and minimise the fluctuations in daily life. C19-YRSm was shown to be a valid, reliable, responsive, and easy-to-administrate measure for the condition. The Minimal Important Difference (MID) (2 points) and Minimal Clinically Important Difference (MCID) (4 points) values for C19-YRSm have been determined to be used in clinical and research settings to reliably capture the condition trajectory and the effect of interventions and also help inform clinical policy. Primary care coding for the condition was found to be inadequate. The average aggregate value of productivity loss since incident infection nationally was £5.7 billion per year and the corresponding value for informal caregiving was £4.8 billion annually. The 10-min Lean Test (active stand test) must be undertaken as a regular objective test on all patients to detect and manage orthostatic intolerance (dysautonomia). The NHS England and NHS Scotland service evaluation studies showed specialist clinics led to some improvement in condition severity, but many patients continued to have symptoms and disability similar to a long-term condition. Conclusions and recommendations for future research: The care of long COVID in the UK has been improved and optimised. We need further research on longer term outcomes in the condition, continued investment in clinical services and further development of integrated services to manage long COVID and related post-infection conditions. An integrated pathway at the interface of primary and secondary care enabled management by a multidisciplinary team. A whole systems approach is needed that can take into account the interaction of multiple elements that ultimately impact the experiences of minoritised groups living with long COVID. This may enable better recognition, treatment and support for people from minoritised groups living with the symptoms of this condition. title: Let there be music: Prompt, command, and cultural capital in the AI music generator Suno
abstract: This paper examines the role of language in prompt-based music production through the case of the AI music generator Suno and questions the widespread claim that such systems democratize music production. Building on Agamben’s (2022) concept of command, the paper conceptualizes the prompt as a command that initiates production. Drawing on Bourdieu’s (1986) concept of cultural capital, the paper considers how linguistic competence may shape prompt construction. The paper adopts an interpretive case study approach. For Suno, the paper tested one minimal and one elaborated text-based prompt in the platform’s freely accessible v4.5 Simple mode and compared the first musical output presented for each prompt. The minimal prompt consisted of a brief, general description, whereas the elaborated prompt included linguistic detail and musical terminology specific to the selected genre. The analysis focused on rock music because its well-established terminology – such as riff, distortion, power chord, pre-chorus, and guitar solo – enabled a clearer comparison of how linguistic and musical specifications were reflected in the musical outputs. The findings indicate that, in these two examples, the minimal prompt is accompanied by a more detailed style description displayed by the platform, whereas the description associated with the elaborated prompt selectively retains, renames, and restructures elements of the original prompt. Thus, algorithmic interpretation is defined as a theoretical account of how the platform maps the user’s command to the resulting musical decisions. The paper concludes that the musical output can be understood as the asymmetrical co-production of the user’s command, shaped by cultural capital, and the platform’s algorithmic interpretation, with the latter occupying a structurally dominant position in this relationship. These findings suggest that the widespread discourse presenting AI music generators as democratizing music production may overlook the distinction between access to production and control over the production process.
authors: Selim Tan

title: Lifefulness - feasibility and acceptability of a self-guided digital intervention promoting mental health among older adults in Sweden
abstract: Background: The number and proportion of older adults (≥65 years) is increasing worldwide, already exceeding 20% in Sweden. The growing number of older adults with concurrent physical and mental health issues, pose a major challenge for healthcare, rendering a critical need for low-cost, easily accessible behavioural interventions. Methods: This single-group feasibility trial evaluated a transdiagnostic digital self-help intervention, "Lifefulness", specifically adapted for older adults and designed to promote behaviour change and mental health. Content was based on cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) and healthy ageing principles. Older adults were recruited from the community (age range 65-85) and were assigned to the six week intervention, which included three brief phone interviews focusing on program adherence. Outcomes included program use and acceptability as well as preliminary effects on quality of life and mental health outcomes. Results: A total of 73 individuals were included. Program utility was high on average, with 72% of participants engaging with the intervention daily or several times a week. The average time spent on the three interviews was 33 min per participant. The program was associated with favourable changes in various mental health symptoms and higher ratings of quality of life and the participants reported high satisfaction and credibility. Conclusions: These findings support the feasibility and resource-efficiency of a digital self-help intervention for older adults. The intervention warrants further testing in a randomized trial with long-term follow-up assessments of both outcomes and healthcare consumption.
authors: Martin Kraepelien; Karin Romberg; Neda Agahi; Nitya Jayaram‐Lindström; Amit Chakrabarti; Arun Kandasamy; Indranil Saha; Christopher Sundström

title: LukeNet: A lightweight CNN integrated with an XAI model for Smart acute lymphoblastic leukemia detection and management
abstract: Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL) patients require early, accurate detection to enable timely treatment and effective patient management. A Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is well-suited for creating an end-to-end enabling environment for ALL detection and classification. However, most CNN-based ALL detection systems are theoretical and unsuitable for deployment on edge devices due to high computational demands. The Internet of Medical Things (IoMT)-enabled devices offer an opportunity to monitor ALL patients in real time. Wearables that track temperature, heart rate, oxygen saturation, and activity can deliver critical data to support timely clinical intervention and improve patient outcomes. In smart IoMT environments, a lightweight CNN is essential because connected devices often operate under limited computational power, memory, and latency constraints. To address this need, this study proposes LukeNet, a lightweight CNN integrated with explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) for an IoMT-based SMART Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia Detection and Management System. Trained on three (3) ALL datasets and five-fold cross-validation, LukeNet achieved an impressive 99% model accuracy as well as 99% unseen test accuracy, which is higher than six state-of-the-art (SOTA) CNNs, such as DenseNet121, MobileNet, ResNet50, InceptionV3, Xception, and VGG16, as well as transfer learning models. Furthermore, LukeNet was compared with two ensemble models. In addition, explainable AI methods are integrated to highlight relevant regions in microscopic images. The novelty of this study lies in the architecture of LukeNet, which balances model depth and computational efficiency by using depthwise separable convolutions, mitigates the risk of gradient loss in deeper layers, and provides strong global and local feature extraction capabilities.
authors: Md Taimur Ahad

title: Lung Disease Detection and Classification Based on AI, Deep Learning and Machine Learning: A Comprehensive Survey
abstract: Background: Lung diseases significantly contribute to substantial global morbidity and mortality, which pose considerable diagnostic challenges. Manual analysis of medical images like chest X-rays and CT scans is often subject to human error, requires specialized expertise, and is time-consuming. To build fully automated systems that analyze the information contained in medical images, robust and efficient algorithms are required. In response, artificial intelligence (AI), especially deep learning (DL), has become an innovative approach that shows excellent results for the automation of lung disease detection and classification. Objective: Following a strict systematic literature review methodology, this study aims to provide an extensive survey of artificial intelligence, machine learning, and deep learning approaches for the detection and classification of lung diseases. Methods: The survey discusses over 30 reported approaches in the field. These approaches have been categorized and evaluated based on the methodology and reported results. We also discuss relevant datasets and benchmarking that have been used in state-of-the-art models and have undergone peer review. Results: The survey reveals a strong trend towards powerful ensemble and hybrid architectures like ResNet, VGG, RVCNet, Vision Transformers (ViTs), etc., and their variations. These models have achieved high accuracy for detecting and classifying various diseases. Conclusions: This work highlights the advancement and recent progress in using AI and deep learning to detect and classify lung diseases while addressing identified gaps and the limitations related to dataset availability, standardization, and imbalance, in addition to model transparency and the computational cost, providing a prospective roadmap for further research or implementation.
authors: Harith S. Hassan; Sinan A. Naji; Abdullah Ghanim Jaber

title: METHODS FOR REAL-TIME PROCESSING AND MONITORING OF VENTILATION PARAMETERS BASED ON SENSOR NETWORKS
abstract: This study presents an IoT-based sensor network for continuous real-time monitoring of key ventilation parameters. The system integrates ESP32 microcontrollers with temperature, relative humidity, CO2, air pressure, and air velocity sensors. Data are collected and transmitted via MQTT to a centralized platform for real-time visualization and analysis. A web-based dashboard provides monitoring of sensor data, communication status, and alarm notifications. Laboratory tests confirmed stable wireless communication, reliable data acquisition, and continuous data transmission. Variations in CO2 concentration reflected changes in ventilation effectiveness, demonstrating the system’s ability to detect dynamic indoor air quality conditions. The modular architecture enables integration with cloud platforms and future intelligent ventilation control systems, providing a scalable solution for smart ventilation management in various buildings.
authors: Tukhtamishova M
venue: Journal of Advances in Engineering Technology

title: MSAFE: A Monitoring, Modeling and Prediction Framework for Smart Manufacturing Systems
abstract: Capturing a consistent global state is a significant challenge when it comes to cyber-physical systems (CPS) and, in particular, smart manufacturing systems. Three critical challenges stand in the way of obtaining such a global view: (i) multiple controllers in one system, (ii) modeling of programmable logic controllers (PLCs), especially multiple ones and (iii) multiple products being manufactured at the same time, say on different parts of the plant. In this paper, we introduce the Manufacturing State Auto-Transformation Framework (MSAFE) to not just overcome the above issues but also predict the future states of a manufacturing system. MSAFE uses a combination of the code from PLCs, system topology models and pilot runtime data to generate a “State Progress Table” (SPT) that is then used to: (i) reconstruct the existing state of the system and (ii) extrapolate future behavior. By associating runtime (sensor, actuator) data from real plants with static information (code, topology models), our framework can reconstruct current and future states for the plant (as well as individual components). The states predicted by MSAFE can be used to compute additional information, e.g., throughput, end-to-end latencies, number of live widgets, etc. Using two realistic testbeds and thirteen third-party PLC code samples, we demonstrate the effectiveness of MSAFE at (a) recreating current states of manufacturing systems and (b) predicting future states of — both for entire plants and individual components

title: Machine Learning Algorithms for Predicting Psychostimulant Intoxication in Emergency Department Patients: A Multicenter Study
abstract: Introduction: Psychostimulant detection rates among emergency department (ED) patients presenting with suspected substance intoxication are low and are influenced by limited access to confirmatory testing, insufficient clinical information, and variability in physician experience. These challenges often result in high false-positive rates and unnecessary resource use. We hypothesized that machine learning (ML) algorithms could maintain reliable diagnostic performance across a temporal validation cohort and perform comparably to physicians with varying experience levels. Methods: This multicenter study prospectively enrolled ED patients with suspected substance intoxication between March 2019 and January 2020. We chronologically partitioned data into a training set (March–October 2019) and a temporal validation cohort (November 2019–January 2020) to assess model generalizability. After determining psychostimulant intoxication via liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry from urine samples, we trained the ML algorithms using the confirmed positive cases. The primary outcome was the diagnostic discrimination of the models, measured by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) in the temporal validation cohort. Secondary outcomes included model accuracy, the Youden index, and a comparative assessment of sensitivity and specificity relative to five physicians of varying experience levels. Results: Among 1,382 patients (mean age 43.8 [standard deviation 19.2] years; 55.3% male), 302 patients (21.9%) had confirmed psychostimulant intoxication, primarily involving (meth)amphetamines (134 [44.4%]), cathinones (107 [35.4%]), and ketamine (97 [32.1%]). In the temporal validation cohort (n = 382), the ML models demonstrated consistent performance, with AUCs ranging from 0.786 to 0.836. The primary outcome was met by the top-performing extreme gradient boosting (XGB) model (AUC, 0.836, 95% CI, 0.785-0.882; accuracy, 0.866 (95% CI, 0.838-0.895); and Youden index, 0.590 (95% CI, 0.480-0.694). To evaluate secondary outcomes, the XGB model’s predictive accuracy was evaluated against 5 emergency physicians. The model surpassed the junior emergency physicians in both specificity (0.910 vs 0.633-0.867) and sensitivity (0.681 vs 0.500-0.633); its specificity was comparable to that of the senior emergency physicians (0.900-0.933). Conclusion: Machine learning models provide reliable diagnostic utility for identifying psychostimulant intoxication, achieving performance comparable to senior emergency physicians. While moderate sensitivity (0.389–0.708) limits their role as standalone rule-out tools, their high specificity provides a standardized tool to assist clinical decision-making and reduce diagnostic uncertainty in the fast-paced ED setting.

title: Machine Learning Augmented Detection of Trace Explosives on Surfaces Using Active Longwave Infrared Imaging
abstract: There is a need for rapid non-contact detection of trace explosives on arbitrary surfaces for applications such as checkpoint screening and post-blast forensics. In this work, active longwave infrared imaging, using a tunable quantum cascade laser light source, is shown to be able to detect three common explosives on typical luggage material substrates at surface concentrations as low as 230 ng/cm 2 . Use of a random forest machine learning algorithm, trained using synthetically produced spectra, allows performance beyond predicted limitations of speckle noise. The random forest algorithm further allows discrimination against ambient dust without specific training. Use of high collection angles reduces the dynamic range requirement of the system without impairing performance. Potential system improvements are discussed to meet the area coverage rate needs of several applications.
authors: William M. Barney; Mitesh Amin; William D. Herzog; Jason M. Jong; Max Kenngott; Keegan Quigley; Patrick Wen; Roderick Russell Kunz

title: Machine Learning and Deep Learning for Early Disease Detection Across Modalities: A Comprehensive Review of Methods, Applications, and Clinical Translation.
abstract: Early disease detection is not a single classification problem. It includes population screening, presymptomatic risk estimation, identification of early pathological change, and detection of disease before conventional clinical recognition. Machine learning and deep learning systems approach these targets through medical images, physiological signals, longitudinal health records, molecular measurements, wearable sensors, and multimodal combinations. This survey organizes the evidence around the complete decision pathway linking the clinical target, data generation process, preprocessing, representation, model, validation design, reported performance, methodological limitation, and level of clinical translation. The analysis distinguishes early detection from ordinary diagnosis, prognosis, and progression prediction, as merging these tasks can make apparently strong results clinically misleading. Across modalities, deep learning is most useful when spatial, temporal, or cross-modal representations must be learned from sufficiently large and representative data. Traditional machine learning remains competitive when cohorts are modest, clinically meaningful variables are available, or transparent feature-level reasoning is required. The evidence also shows that performance is strongly influenced by patient-level separation, cohort construction, prevalence, label definition, missingness, external validation, calibration, and the handling of uncertain cases; therefore, high discrimination on an internal split cannot establish clinical utility. The survey further examines the gap between retrospective model development and deployment, emphasizing temporal and external validation, prospective workflow evaluation, decision thresholds, false negative consequences, demographic robustness, interpretability, and post-deployment monitoring. The resulting synthesis provides a modality-aware and clinically grounded framework for deciding not only which algorithms perform well but also what their results mean and what evidence remains necessary before they can support early clinical action.
authors: Ahlem Aziz; Seydi Kacmaz; Azam Isam Abdulkareem Aladwani

title: Mapping Conventional and Emerging Sensors for Neonatal Physiological Monitoring: A Scoping Review of the Technological Transition and Validation Gaps
abstract: Continuous physiological monitoring is a cornerstone of neonatal intensive care. Yet, current NICU sensing technologies- adhesive electrodes, contact pulse oximeters, and wired thermistors- carry well-documented clinical limitations, including adhesive-related skin injury, restricted mobility, and interference with family-centered developmental care protocols. Although the past decade has witnessed a proliferation of alternative sensing proposals spanning flexible electronics, wireless wearable platforms, and fully contactless approaches, this body of research remains fragmented across distinct technical communities, and no comprehensive mapping of the conventional and emerging sensor ecosystem has been published to date. To address this gap, this scoping review followed the PRISMA-ScR guidelines and was structured around a Population, Concept, and Context (PCC) framework: Population, neonates admitted to the NICU; Concept, sensors used in physiological monitoring equipment; Context, the hospital neonatal intensive care setting. Searches in PubMed, Scopus, and IEEE Xplore retrieved 197 records, reduced to 166 unique records after deduplication; 40 studies published between 2016 and 2026 were included following a two-stage screening process. The synthesized evidence reveals that emerging technologies predominate (26 of 40, 65%), with optical transduction as the leading physical principle (15 of 40) and flexible or wearable form factors already outnumbering rigid designs (23 of 40 versus 9 of 40). Research activity concentrates heavily on respiratory rate (20 of 40) and heart rate (18 of 40), while electroencephalography and transcutaneous bilirubin each appear in only 1 of 40 studies and blood pressure exclusively as a secondary channel in multiparameter platforms (3 of 40), gaps independently corroborated by contemporaneous systematic reviews of the same domain. Regulatory transparency is markedly absent, with 85% of included studies making no mention of regulatory status, reflecting the field's predominantly proof-of-concept readiness. These findings delineate the current technological frontier of neonatal sensing, identify priority targets for future complementary searches, and underscore the urgent need for standardized validation frameworks to enable direct cross-technology comparisons in subsequent reviews.
authors: Gabriela Cianciarullo; Salvador Pinillos Gimenes; Carlos Eduardo Thomaz

title: Mechanically Robust and Self‐Healing Sustainable Solid‐State Ion‐Conductive Elastomer for Near‐Infrared‐Driven Noncontact Sensing
abstract: ABSTRACT Stretchable solid‐state ionic conductive elastomers (SICEs), serving as essential materials for ionotronic devices, exhibit great promise in emerging applications in electronic skin, soft robotics, especially in wearable sensors. Nevertheless, the development of such materials with high strength, self‐healing, and ionic conductivity remains highly desirable yet challenging, as simultaneously integrating these properties is often hindered by intrinsic trade‐offs among molecular chain dynamics and desired functions. Herein, we develop a SICE featuring a natural rubber‐based segregated network, in which latex particles are encapsulated by carboxylated cellulose nanofibers, polydopamine, and lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide. The formation of integrated dense interfacial hydrogen and lithium bonds among the components leads to a robust interface and superior integral architecture, delivering an unprecedented combination of properties: a tensile strength of 6.23 MPa, a room‐temperature self‐healing efficiency of 98%, and an ionic conductivity of 4.15 × 10 − 3 S·m −1 . Such performance substantially outperforms the most state‐of‐the‐art bio‐based counterparts, noting that all main components are derived from bio‐based resources. Furthermore, the polydopamine imparts photothermal conversion capability, enabling not only remote‐triggered rapid self‐healing but also non‐contact sensing via near‐infrared light‐mediated thermal stimulation. This study advances a sustainable and remotely controllable platform based on bio‐based SICEs, opening new avenues for next‐generation intelligent flexible electronics.
authors: Mingliang Wu; Quanyong Cheng; Yi‐Dong Li; Caili Huang; Jian‐Bing Zeng

title: Mechatronic Platform Driven by Thoracic Impedance Signals for the Experimental Evaluation of a Radar-Based Respiratory Monitoring System
abstract: Short-range FMCW radar has emerged as a promising contactless technology for respiratory monitoring. However, the experimental evaluation of radar-based respiratory monitoring systems using human subjects is often affected by inter-subject variability, involuntary body movements, and the limited repeatability of respiratory patterns. This work presents a mechatronic platform that reproduces respiratory motion using thoracic impedance signals from the publicly available BIDMC dataset to enable controlled evaluation of the Acconeer XM132 radar. The respiratory signals were resampled, normalized, and converted into motion commands for MG90S servo motors, reproducing physiological breathing patterns through a movable PLA and acrylic structure. A total of 12 recordings, each lasting 240 s, were analyzed. The filtered radar signal was used as the primary source for respiratory rate (RR) estimation, while an MPU6050 inertial sensor provided an auxiliary measurement of the platform motion. Different analysis window lengths and RR estimation methods were investigated. FFT-based estimation using 60 s windows achieved a mean error of 1.94 breathing per minute (bpm) and a median error of 0.09 bpm, whereas analysis of the complete 240 s recordings yielded a median error of 0.03 bpm. The proposed platform contributes to the development of biomedical instrumentation for radar-based respiratory monitoring by providing a controlled and repeatable environment for evaluating radar acquisition parameters, signal filtering techniques, and RR estimation algorithms, representing an intermediate step between laboratory characterization and clinical validation.
authors: Júlio Cardoso Scorpion; João Lucas Pereira dos Santos de Paula; Feres A. Salem; Elço João dos Santos; Flávio Gabriel Oliveira Barbosa; Paulo Alberto Macedo Vieira Violada
