abstract: Optimal growth of structures governed by spatially stochastic dynamics arises in many scientific settings, for example in processes such as solution-based crystallization and the formation of microbial biofilms on patterned substrates or microfluidic networks. In this work, we investigate lattice growth using a two-dimensional, zero-temperature stochastic model ofshort-range spin interactions. Our goal is to determine how external perturbations can be optimized to steer the system efficiently toward the uniformly positive state, starting from two initial clusters of positive sites. To achieve this, we cast the problem as a Markov decision process adapted for a two-dimensional Ising model with zero-temperature dynamics. Within this framework, we compare alternative growth geometries and identify the structure of optimal strategies across three representative regimes.
authors: Maike C. de Jongh; Cristian Spitoni; Emilio N. M. Cirillo

title: Optoelectronically Enabled Simultaneous and Decoupled Navigation and Selective Pairing of Electrically Driven Janus Particles for Multi-Agent Microrobotics
abstract: Self-propelled Janus particles are promising active agents for microscale manipulation and microrobotic applications. However, when powered by a global external energy source, such as an electric, magnetic, or optical field, all particles respond simultaneously, preventing their independent and concurrent control. Achieving parallel, decoupled control without continuous particle-specific feedback, while preserving intrinsic self-propulsion, remains a significant challenge. Here, we present an optoelectronic (OE) strategy for simultaneously and independently controlling electrically driven, self-propelled metallo-dielectric Janus particles (JPs) using spatially programmable virtual electrodes. These electrodes are generated by projecting a single predefined illumination pattern from a digital micromirror device onto a photoconductive surface. The resulting confinement landscape enables multiple JPs to follow distinct trajectories without continuous monitoring, feedback, or pattern reconfiguration. We demonstrate controlled pairing of JPs with passive polystyrene particles and biological cells. For automated multi-agent operation, an image-based assignment framework identifies optimal agent-target pairs, excludes intersecting trajectories, and generates a single composite pattern for simultaneous, selective pair formation without real-time updating. Finally, we demonstrate independent manipulation of multiple magnetically rolling JPs under a globally applied magnetic field. Overall, this programmable open-loop strategy provides a versatile framework for multi-agent microrobotic manipulation, with potential applications in in-vitro micromanipulation and microfluidic systems.
authors: Srikanta Debata; Ido Rachbuch; Gilad Yossifon

title: POSTOPER ATIVE COMPLICATIONS AFTER COLORECTAL CANCER SURGERY: RISK FACTORS, IMPACT ON SURVIVAL, AND CONTEMPORARY PREVENTION STRATEGIES (A LITERATURE REVIEW)
abstract: Relevance: Postoperative complications remain major determinants of unfavorable outcomes following colorectal cancer surgery, contributing to increased mortality, reoperation rates, disease recurrence, and reduced long-term survival.The study aimed to analyze current evidence on postoperative complications after colorectal cancer surgery, identify major risk factors, evaluate their impact on long-term survival, and summarize contemporary preventive strategies.Materials and Methods: This structured literature review covered 39 publications from January 1, 2021, through July 31, 2026, including 34 original studies and 4 systematic reviews or meta-analyses; the GLOBOCAN 2022 fact sheet was used only for epidemiological context and was not counted among the included studies.Results: Reported overall postoperative morbidity ranged from 8.1% to 33.3%, while colorectal anastomotic leakage occurred in 4.7% to 15.1% of patients. Wen et al. reported postoperative infectious complications in 95/593 patients (16.0%), including wound infection, anastomotic leakage, intra-abdominal infection, pneumonia, and other infectious events. Severe complications (Clavien-Dindo grades III-V) occurred in 9.7-29.7% of patients. Significant adjusted associations included sarcopenia and postoperative complications (OR = 2.53; 95% CI: 1.45-4.42), three or more linear stapler firings and anastomotic leakage (OR = 2.71; 95% CI: 1.17-6.26), and male sex in a CT-based leakage model (OR = 3.75). In one colon cancer cohort, postoperative complications were associated with a higher adjusted risk of death (HR = 1.70; 95% CI: 1.19-2.45). Multimodal prehabilitation reduced major complications from 29.7% to 17.1%, while diverting ileostomy was associated with fewer leakage-related reoperations.Conclusion: Postoperative complications are consistently associated with adverse short- and long-term outcomes following colorectal cancer surgery. Adjusted analyses identify nutritional, metabolic, patient-related, and technical factors that may support risk stratification. Multimodal prehabilitation, nutritional optimization, structured perioperative pathways, meticulous anastomotic technique, and selective diversion may reduce postoperative morbidity; however, the predominantly observational and heterogeneous evidence does not establish causality.
authors: Ye.M. Zheldibaev; Aman Berkinbay; A. Aitakyn; Dauren A. Nurmakov; A. Raimkhanov; Dauren T. Zhumatayev
venue: Eurasian Journal of Oncology and Radiology

title: PV-WTConv: a parallel network for abnormal white blood cell classification based on wavelet transform convolution
abstract: In the field of cell detection research, the detection of abnormal white blood cells is not only central to the early diagnosis of malignant haematological diseases such as leukaemia and myelodysplastic syndromes, but also serves as a key indicator for assessing infectious diseases, immunodeficiencies and the efficacy of chemotherapy. The use of computer-aided techniques to accurately classify white blood cells in microscopic images can assist clinicians in diagnosing and detecting various blood-related diseases more promptly and accurately. However, the accurate identification and classification of white blood cells remains challenging due to the blurred boundaries between abnormal white blood cells and normal white blood cells—or even those exhibiting physiological variations—the lack of uniform and fixed morphological criteria for different types of abnormal cells (such as leukaemic cells and hyperplastic cells), and interference from factors such as the complexity of cell imaging and staining techniques. Therefore, this paper proposes a parallel classification network for abnormal white blood cells based on wavelet transform convolution, designed to enhance the accuracy of recognising and classifying different categories of abnormal white blood cells. This study utilised the AWBC-LZWH dataset of abnormal white blood cell images, provided by the Department of Clinical Laboratory Medicine at Liuzhou Workers’ Hospital, for the main training, validation and testing phases, and conducted supplementary experiments using the PBC_dataset of peripheral blood cell images, which was collected and publicly released by the Hospital Clínic de Barcelona. PV-WTConv achieved an accuracy of 94.4% on AWBC-LZWH, compared with 56.9% for the convolutional baseline and 91.4% for ResNet50, corresponding to absolute differences of 37.5 and 3.0 percentage points, respectively. The results of this study indicate that PV-WTConv demonstrates good classification performance on the evaluated white blood cell image datasets; however, its clinical diagnostic value still requires further validation through prospective, multicentre studies.
authors: Xiangsuo Fan; Xipeng Song; Borui Sun; Zhenxing Yao; Jie Meng

title: Passive Cell-Flux Partitioning Enables Single-Cell-Constrained Impedance Sensing From High-Density Microbial Cultures
abstract: Fermentation is a process through which microorganisms are used to transform basic molecules into high value substances in various applications such as biopharma, food production, and biofuel generation. In such processes, monitoring the health of microbial cells is essential, as it is a key factor in the final product yield. Traditional methods of assessing the health of fermenter populations have involved manually extracting samples from the fermenter for benchtop testing, which lacked the accuracy and efficacy of real-time continuous measurements. This has opened the door for inline sensors to be integrated into fermenters for continuous measurement; including microfluidic based Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy (EIS). EIS utilizes a range of frequencies to gain insight into the characteristics of microbial populations, such as cell size and membrane capacitance. EIS cytometry, in particular, has emerged as a relevant tool, as it enables single-cell level detection in real-time. However, current EIS cytometry devices cannot be deployed directly within fermenters due to the high cell density conditions. This has limited EIS analysis in fermenters to bulk measurements averaged across a population. Here, we present a microfluidic chip that uses passive cell-flux-partitioning geometry to direct cells from high-density culture through a single-cell-constrained flow path containing integrated impedance-sensing electrodes. The proposed chip combines geometric channel design and embedded electrodes to enable continuous impedance measurements from cell-containing flow while operating at input cell densities on the scale of 10 9 CFU/mL. This work demonstrates a first step toward integrating single-cell-constrained microfluidic handling with impedance sensing for inline monitoring in industrial biomanufacturing.
authors: Woud Alsadoun; Luca Pungan; Yash H. Patel; Juan José Robayo Yepes; Yueying Yang; Rabia Tugce Yazicigil; Miguel Jiménez

title: Pendant drop microtraps for signal enhancement of microbead-based bioassays
abstract: Reliable fluorescence-based biosensing often requires efficient preconcentration of analytes, but existing preconcentration methods are highly prone to clogging and biofouling. Active methods, on the other hand, demand complex tools and operational steps. In this study, we present a pendant drop microtrap that uses a wall-free and pump-free configuration to preconcentrate microbeads before fluorescence readout. Droplets (0.5–4 μL) containing microbeads were dispensed onto hydrophobic polystyrene substrates and inverted to form stable hemispherical pendant drops. Target non-magnetic microbeads accumulated at the drop apex under gravity alone, whereas magnetic beads were concentrated by gravity and magnetic force. We studied the effects of droplet volume on bead distribution and fluorescence signal intensity. The platform was evaluated with fluorescently labeled magnetic Dynabeads and non-magnetic polystyrene beads, and demonstrated up to a 5.7-fold signal enhancement with 4 μL droplets. The pendant drop microtraps concentrated Dynabeads and non-magnetic polystyrene beads functionalized with various labels and antibodies, specifically streptavidin-Cy5, an anti-TNF-α antibody, and a FITC-conjugated rabbit anti-goat IgG (H + L) antibody. The pendant drop microtrap therefore offers a simple, wall-free, pump-free, and cheap preconcentration platform that can be readily integrated into existing fluorescence-based bioassay workflows.
authors: Amin Ghaffarzadeh Bakhshayesh; Isabella Walker; Huiyan Li

title: Persistent Lipotoxicity Overwhelms Adaptive Capacity in Human Hepatic Cell Line.
abstract: Chronic fatty acid (FA) elevation drives metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease. Hepatocytes buffer transient lipid overload via coordinated adaptive mechanisms, but the temporal limits of this capacity remain undefined. We characterized early, intermediate, and prolonged hepatocellular responses to sustained lipid excess. HuH7 hepatocytes were exposed to an equimolar palmitic/oleic acid (PA/OA) mixture for 1, 14, or 28 d. Viability, lipid accumulation, stress-response pathways, insulin signaling, metabolic regulators, mitochondrial markers, [14C]-PA uptake, and exometabolomic profiles were assessed (n ≥ 3/group). Data (mean ± standard error of the mean) were analyzed by 2-way analysis of variance with Bonferroni post hoc testing; cumulative cell death was analyzed by linear regression. P < 0.05 was considered significant. FA treatment increased lipid droplet accumulation 1.4- to 1.7-fold compared with time-matched bovine serum albumin controls at all time points (P < 0.001) and increased the rate of cumulative cell death ∼4.3-fold (1.556% ± 0.083% compared with 0.365 ± 0.054%/d, P < 0.001). Exometabolomic principal component analysis explained 88.5% of variance (Q2 = 0.758), with peak lactate release at day 14 and progressively rising acetate through day 28. [14C]-PA accumulation at day 28 was ∼30% lower than day 1 (∼800 compared with ∼500 cpm/mg protein), with a declining rather than plateauing profile between 20 and 60 s. By day 28, FA-treated cells showed lower FA synthase (P < 0.001), CD36 (P < 0.05), FABP1 (P < 0.001), SIRT1 (P < 0.005), and CLOCK (P < 0.01) protein levels, and higher carnitine palmitoyl transferase 1A (P < 0.001), phosphorylated AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK)/AMPK (P < 0.01), p53 (P < 0.001), Bax/Bcl2 (P < 0.005), and respiratory complex I-V abundance (P < 0.05-P < 0.001) compared with controls. Sustained PA/OA exposure induces a staged hepatocellular response, early lipid-buffering adaptation, intermediate metabolic compensation, and late decompensation, indicating that chronic lipotoxicity reflects progressive loss of regulatory coordination despite persistent metabolic adaptation.
authors: Ilaria Serra; Elisa Bisconti; Francesco Vari; Eleonora Stanca; Federica De Castro; Federica Angilè; Daniele Vergara; Francesco Paolo Fanizzi; Anna M Giudetti

title: Phage phenotyping by measuring plaque expansion dynamics
abstract: Abstract Bacteriophages exhibit staggering genomic diversity, yet phenotypic characterization remains bottlenecked by assays that generally yield simple binary infection outcomes. Quantitative traits can be extracted from standard liquid cultures, but many phages fail to produce a measurable effect in these settings, necessitating an improved quantitative approach on semi-solid media. While end-point plaque size is commonly used for quantitative phenotyping, it only provides a static snapshot that fails to disentangle phage performance across changing bacterial growth phases. Here, we report a cost-effective, scalable method to quantify the bacterial killing rates of diverse phages by continuously tracking plaque development using a consumer-grade flatbed scanner and custom open-source computer vision software. By fitting a minimal, phenomenological model to the diverse BASEL collection of Escherichia coli phages, we accurately captured plaque expansion dynamics across all bacterial growth phases. We discovered that plaque expansion parameters vary significantly across individual phages and taxonomic families, with the initial expansion rate demonstrating an inverse correlation with viral genome size. Notably, these plaque expansion dynamics did not correlate with bacterial collapse times in liquid culture, indicating that they represent distinct physiological and kinetic processes. Finally, we demonstrated that phage taxonomic family can be predicted with 72.1% accuracy solely from dynamic plaque parameters using a random forest classifier, whereas conventional endpoint plaque sizes held no predictive power. This time-lapse phenotyping approach yields robust kinetic data superior to end-point measurements, establishing a scalable platform to accelerate phage discovery and genotype-phenotype mapping.
authors: Jonathan Costa; Baltus A. van der Steen; Yuval Mulla

title: Physicochemical rule-embedded generative modeling for constrained peptide therapeutics
abstract: Constrained peptides couple covalent topology, stereochemistry, three-dimensional structure, conformational dynamics and developability. We review physicochemical rule embedding across chemical-language, target-conditioned structural, geometric, atom-bond, ensemble and property-guided generative models, distinguishing generated molecular objects from downstream inference and predictions from prospective evidence. We identify limitations in chemical coverage, applicability, uncertainty and pipeline attribution, and routes towards identity-preserving, environment-aware and experimentally calibrated design.
authors: Yuzhou Wang; Dongsheng Cao; Xiangzheng Fu; Xiangxiang Zeng; Xiaojun Yao

title: Plasmonic metasurface microfluidic accelerates redox reactions for rapid phenotypic antibiotic susceptibility testing
abstract: Electron-accepting chain reactions play crucial roles in diagnostics for bacterial infections, from nucleic acid amplification for bacterial identification to metabolic assays for phenotypic antibiotic susceptibility testing. When coupled with redox mediators, these reactions can be interrogated using an electroanalytical method. We demonstrate kinetic acceleration of loop-mediated isothermal amplification-based identification and resazurin-based phenotypic antibiotic susceptibility profiling through enhanced electromagnetic fields and modulated hot electron injection at the multilayered plasmonic metasurface-fluidic interface. We systematically investigate rounded versus sharp-apex plasmonic architectures, quantifying near-field magnitude and decay to identify geometries that maximize kinetic amplification under electrochemical readout. This approach is further combined with machine learning-assisted Gaussian fitting to improve data quantification and interpretation. Across diverse bacterial species, we achieved rapid identification with no cross-reactivity and phenotypic antibiotic susceptibility testing without overnight culture. In a prospective pilot clinical study of urine specimens directly from patients with suspected urinary tract infections, we observe high accuracy and strong essential and categorical agreement with standard clinical microbiology assays for bacterial identification and antibiotic susceptibility testing.
authors: Roozbeh Siavash Moakhar; Mahsa Jalali; Tamer AbdElFatah; Sripadh Guptha Yedire; Max Petkun; Carolina del Real Mata; Ziwei He; Hamed Shieh; Geoffrey A. McKay; Rachel Corsini; Grace Reszetnik; Seyed Vahid Hamidi; Sahar Sadat Mahshid; Cédric P. Yansouni; Dao M. Nguyen; Sara Mahshid

title: Polymer Informatics in the Era of Foundation Models: From Representation to Autonomous Design
abstract: Foundation models, pretrained on broad datasets and adapted to multiple tasks, offer a way to reuse chemical knowledge across polymer property prediction and inverse design. Realizing this opportunity requires connecting learned representations to materials whose properties also depend on molecular populations, formulation, processing, and measurement conditions. Here, we review advances in polymer foundation models and the data, representations, and experimental workflows that support their use in materials design. We organize these developments around the polymer material state, a description linking chemical identity to molecular distributions, architecture, morphology, and preparation history relevant to a target property. This organization connects data resources and pretraining strategies to questions about what models learn, how that knowledge transfers, and which experimental choices it can support. We compare learning objectives and adaptation methods, examine representations of polymer chemistry and state, and follow inverse design from candidate generation through synthesis and processing to validation. Pretrained models now support prediction across multiple properties and generation for specified targets, with selected polymer candidates reaching synthesis and thermal characterization. Broader polymer design campaigns show how precursor accessibility, polymerization outcomes, and specimen preparation influence whether a predicted advantage becomes a measured material response. Building on this evidence, we discuss opportunities to combine chemical pretraining with richer sample information and to assess transfer across polymer families, preparation conditions, and experimental campaigns. The resulting synthesis connects model development to a practical objective for polymer informatics: reducing the new experimentation needed to obtain materials with reproducible, targeted performance.
authors: Jianxin He; Ying Li

title: Polymer-Based Microfluidic Devices for Point-of-Care Diagnostics: A Comprehensive Review
abstract: Background/objectives: Polymer-based microfluidic platforms have emerged as a critical area for the development of point-of-care (POC) diagnostics, driven by the need for rapid, low-cost, and portable testing solutions. This review examines how these systems utilize polymeric substrates to integrate complex laboratory processes into compact, user-friendly devices for healthcare and environmental applications. Methods: This review examines various polymeric substrates, including polydimethylsiloxane, thermoplastics, paper, and hydrogels. It also discusses diverse fabrication approaches ranging from soft lithography, hot embossing, and laser ablation to three-dimensional printing and paper-based patterning besides detection strategies spanning optical and electrochemical sensing, surface plasmon resonance, and smartphone-based readouts. Results: The unique properties of polymers, including optical transparency, biocompatibility, tunable surface chemistry, and cost-effectiveness, support the development of diagnostic assays for infectious diseases, cancer biomarkers, and environmental monitoring. Advances in fabrication and detection strategies have improved device sensitivity, portability, and scalability. However, there remain challenges related to material selection, standardization, reproducibility, and regulatory translation. Conclusions: Despite these challenges, continued advances in novel polymers, sustainable materials, and integrated “sample-to-answer” systems are expected to accelerate the development of polymer microfluidic devices for POC diagnostics. Nevertheless, overcoming regulatory, manufacturing standardization and clinical validation challenges is essential for their widespread clinical adoption. Ultimately, polymer microfluidic devices have the potential to support decentralized diagnostics and personalized medicine while improving healthcare accessibility.
authors: Jibrin Muhammad Yelwa; Haruna Musa; Magaji Ladan; Dini Sabo; Hussaina G. Anchau; Hauwa Kinjir; Markus Gaya Jocthan; Checkwube Martin Obiano; Alhagie Drammeh

title: Precision Fermentation for Sustainable Food Production: Technological Advances, Food Applications, Sustainability, Challenges and Future Perspectives
abstract: Precision fermentation (PF) has developed into an important food-biotechnology platform that employs engineered microorganisms to produce specific food ingredients, such as proteins, enzymes, flavour compounds, sweet proteins, and bioactive molecules, under controlled fermentation conditions. This review critically examines developments in PF, with emphasis on technological progress, microbial cell factories, fermentation productivity, scale-up, food functionality, circular feedstocks, and the increasing application of artificial intelligence. Environmental performance, techno-economic feasibility, safety, regulatory considerations, and consumer acceptance are also considered. The evidence reviewed indicates that PF can support the controlled production of selected food ingredients and has the potential to complement plant-based proteins, biomass fermentation, and cellular-agriculture approaches. However, PF should not be considered inherently sustainable or automatically better than conventional production methods. Its environmental performance is strongly influenced by electricity sources, feedstock selection, titre, rate and yield (TRY), aeration intensity, fermentation duration, and downstream processing. Likewise, commercial success depends on achieving high productivity, efficient product recovery, affordable feedstocks, and suitable scale-up strategies. Safety evaluation should remain product-specific, particularly for allergenic proteins and novel ingredients, while regulatory differences across regions and consumer perceptions will continue to influence the adoption of precision fermentation. A central argument we advance is that PF should be evaluated as an integrated food-system technology, requiring simultaneous consideration of biological engineering, process engineering, food science, life-cycle assessment, techno-economic analysis, and social governance. Looking forward, we see pressing needs for pilot-scale validation, standardized TRY reporting, renewable-energy integration, circular feedstock development, AI-assisted experimental design, food-matrix functionality studies, and harmonized safety and regulatory approaches.
authors: Nura Salihu; Hashimu Imam Tanko; Abdulhakim Zubairu

title: Precision Injection‐Compression Molding and Functional Integration of Hollow Microneedle Microfluidic Chips for Minimally Invasive Continuous Health Monitoring
abstract: Real-time biomarker monitoring through interstitial fluid (ISF) sampling using hollow microneedle (HMN) arrays is crucial for personalized precision medicine and chronic disease management. However, clinical translation faces a critical bottleneck: the absence of stable, cost-effective, scalable high-precision manufacturing technologies. This work systematically establishes a comprehensive end-to-end solution encompassing precise molding and functional integration. We employed injection-compression molding with multi-objective optimization algorithms to elucidate relationships between critical process parameters and HMN array molding quality. The results demonstrate that positioning the HMN array at the far-gate locations enhances filling quality and reduces core-pin impact force by 15%, revealing the underlying physical mechanisms governed by shear heating effects and pressure transmission dynamics, which enriches conventional micro-injection molding theory. The optimized process achieves >6.8% filling ratio improvement and 10% injection pressure reduction. Furthermore, we established a complete design and fabrication workflow for ISF extraction chips, developed patterned microelectrode bonding technology for complex microchannel sealing, and validated in situ detection platform advantages. In vitro testing validated safe and efficient ISF extraction with a 95% success rate while maintaining exceptional portability for wearable health monitoring applications. This work provides theoretical and practical guidance for scalable HMN manufacturing, establishing a foundation for commercializing next-generation continuous health monitoring systems.
authors: Baishun Zhao; Dimitrios Kontziampasis; Mingyong Zhou; Wangqing Wu; Zhiyu Yang; Bingyan Jiang; Dou Zhang

title: Precision weeding and spraying robot vehicle integrating spatial perception and closed-loop control
abstract: To address the problems of unstable target positioning, accumulated end-effector errorsand insufficient dynamic operation response in traditional pesticide application equipment in complex field environments, this study proposes a target-oriented weeding robot vehicle with dynamic spatial compensation for precision spraying, achieving autonomous perception, spatial correctionand precise intervention against weeds. The system addresses the spatial uncertainties of agricultural robots during continuous movement by constructing a multi-source information fusion architecture integrating high-precision satellite positioning, inertial attitude perception, structural error compensationand edge intelligent control. The real-time nozzle spatial pose calculation model is established to uniformly describe the robot's motion state, suspension mechanism changesand nozzle installation geometry, enabling continuous estimation of the spraying end position under dynamic conditions. Simultaneously, a nonlinear structural compensation mechanism based on Gaussian process regression is introduced to jointly model and correct suspension mechanism motion errors, mechanical connection deviations, structural deformationand random disturbances, improving the stability and environmental adaptability of nozzle spatial positioning. Furthermore, the dynamic deposition prediction model integrating robot motion state, droplet motion patternsand target spatial distribution information is constructed. By predicting the spatiotemporal relationship between the spray landing point and the target area, the nozzle response strategy is adjusted in advance to achieve precise triggering and targeted coverage of the target area. This research breaks through the limitations of traditional agricultural spraying systems that rely on fixed geometric relationships, static compensation parametersand preset triggering rules. It deeply integrates spatial perception, error compensation, motion predictionand spraying control, providing a new technical path for the development of agricultural robots from mechanized operations to intelligent precision operation systems with environmental understanding and autonomous decision-making capabilities.
authors: Ruipeng Tang

title: Predicting droplet landing in angle-controlled surface acoustic wave jetting
abstract: Abstract Nozzle-free droplet generation eliminates the need for a dispensing orifice, but useful printing also requires control over where droplets are deposited. Here we demonstrate predictable droplet deposition using a nozzle-free, angle-controlled surface acoustic wave jetting platform. Opposing focused interdigital transducers steer droplets from a pendant parent drop toward a collection substrate, with the ejection angle set by the time-integrated acoustic acceleration imbalance. The overall acceleration ratio identifies the operating window for single-droplet ejection and separates it from no-ejection, satellite-droplet, and multiple-droplet regimes. We then connect ejection angle to landing position through a geometric deposition model referenced to a balanced shot in each experiment. At a 5.2 mm parent-drop-to-substrate spacing, 80 steered shots across twenty experiments show strongly anisotropic relative placement scatter: 0.59 mm in the steering direction and 0.06 mm transverse to it. In tests conducted independently over several days, a model calibrated on six earlier collection dates predicted landing positions on two later dates with a root-mean-square error of 0.71 mm; boot-strap resampling placed the 95% confidence range for this error between 0.41 and 1.01 mm. The results establish a practical framework for predicting relative droplet landing in angle-controlled surface acoustic wave jetting and identify the limits imposed by steering angle, separation distance, and actuation regime from an orifice-free, clog-free droplet ejection method.
authors: Md Aminul Islam; Sara Adibi; James Friend

title: Predictive Design of Greener Ultrafast Chromatography for Accelerated Discovery and Development Chemistry
abstract: Liquid chromatography (LC) is the analytical workhorse of pharmaceutical research and, at the same time, one of its largest sources of organic solvent waste and energy consumption. High-throughput experimentation amplifies this burden by generating thousands of samples per campaign, each conventionally analyzed by methods that consume milliliters to liters of solvent per system and keep instruments running for hours. Because solvent consumption and instrument energy demand scale directly with run time, accelerating these analyses is both a throughput and a sustainability priority. Routine implementation of ultrafast LC, however, has been limited by two related barriers: the experimental effort required to identify high-speed conditions that retain decision-critical selectivity, and the solvent-intensive nature of method development itself. Herein, we introduce a predictive in silico framework that transforms ultrafast LC assay development from empirical screening into a model-driven design workflow. Experimental retention data are used to model chromatographic selectivity across temperature, gradient slope, flow rate, and column geometry, enabling rapid identification of the fastest separation conditions that preserve the information required for decision-making. Retention modeling is further combined with fit-for-purpose resolution criteria and in silico peak clustering to selectively resolve critical components while intentionally grouping noncritical analytes to maximize throughput. The approach is demonstrated across closely related isomers, chiral analyses, and high-throughput reaction screening, where model-predicted separations translated directly into reliable experiments, substantially shortened analysis cycle times, and required minimal manual intervention. The resulting methods give lower analytical method greenness scores, in some cases by more than 10-fold. Together, this framework establishes a general strategy for systematically deploying greener ultrafast chromatographic assays while reducing method-development burden, solvent consumption, and energy demand, with broad applicability to biocatalysis, natural products, metabolomics, high-throughput experimentation, and modern synthesis.
authors: Devin M. Makey; Rodell C. Barrientos; Andrew McGrath; Dan Lehnherr; Andrew N. Singh; Eli J. Larson; Emmanuel Appiah‐Amponsah; Erik L. Regalado

title: Programmable Axial–Radial Multichannel Nickel Microtubes Fabricated by Core-Filament Jet Electrodeposition
abstract: Programmable hollow metallic microdevices with lateral outlets are attractive for distributed fluid handling, but integrating an axial lumen, side channels, and a sealed distal tip remains fabrication-intensive. Here, a core-filament jet electrodeposition (CF-JED) strategy combines segmented electrolyte-jet operation with sacrificial nylon-fiber templating to fabricate multichannel nickel microtubes. An 80 μm nylon core defines the axial lumen, whereas 50 μm transverse and helical fibers prescribe lateral channels. Interrupting the jet creates the in situ assembly interval for template placement; resumed localized electrodeposition encapsulates the fibers and can close the distal tip, and physical pull-out releases the channels without chemical dissolution or drilling. Stable growth was obtained at 2.5 mA with an axial growth rate of approximately 15 μm·min−1. Micro-computed tomography revealed a 50 ± 5 μm radial channel and a 76 ± 6 μm axial lumen interconnected within the sealed-tip structure. SEM/EDS confirmed open lateral apertures and nickel-rich walls, while water-immersion gas testing provided qualitative evidence of channel interconnectivity. CF-JED therefore provides a template-defined route to programmable multichannel hollow-metal microstructures; direct liquid-flow, mechanical, and biological validation remain necessary for application-specific use.
authors: Wei Wang; Hongtao Qian; Pengju Liu; Zhonghe Li; Yulong Li; Xiaohong Yang

title: Programmable Porosity in Polymers via Microfluidic Templating and 3D Printing
abstract: Polymeric functionally graded porous materials (pFGPMs) enable spatial control over transport and mechanical response in a continuous solid in which porosity is strategically placed rather than uniformly distributed. Early research on the production of pFGPMs has demonstrated that graded architectures can be induced as indirect outcomes of time-evolving temperature, pressure, or concentration fields. Because these gradients emerge from process-driven kinetics, reproducibility and spatiotemporal control remain limited. Fluid templating offers a more direct route: the transient structure of polymerizable/crosslinkable foams or high internal phase emulsions (HIPEs) can be transferred into a solid matrix while controlling compartment size, packing, and film stability during solidification. Microfluidics enhance fluid management by confining interfacial breakup to produce monodisperse bubbles or droplets whose size, volume fraction, and interconnectivity can be tuned independently, transforming liquid templates into programmable solid architectures. This review follows the evolution of microfluidic templating toward its integration with additive manufacturing, with an emphasis on platforms that embed in-line bubble or droplet generation at the printhead. We conclude with an outlook on the opportunity to expand the palette of available materials and discuss the emerging role of data-driven approaches in managing the coupled dynamics of formulation, breakup, and solidification, enabling truly programmable polymeric FGPMs.
authors: Federico Serpe; Roberta Angelini; Andrea Barbetta; Vanessa Rosciardi

title: Programmable synthetic engineering of adaptive microbial cell factories: from amide transforming enzymes to advanced biocatalytic systems
abstract: Microbial cell factories integrate metabolic engineering, synthetic regulation, protein engineering, and computational design to improve catalytic performance and process robustness. Within this landscape, amide transforming enzymes provide diverse functions ranging from nitrogen metabolism and hydrolysis to covalent protein remodeling. This review examines amidases, asparaginases, glutaminases, nitrilases, nitrile hydratases, acylases, and carbamylases, with particular emphasis on microbial transglutaminase (MTGase). MTGase is distinguished by its ability to catalyze covalent ε-(γ-glutamyl) lysine crosslinking through acyl transfer reactions, enabling protein stabilization, molecular assembly, immobilization, and spatial organization of catalytic systems. This review critically examines the transition from classical amide transforming enzymes toward engineered biocatalytic systems and evaluates how MTGase could be leveraged as a protein level control component in microbial cell factories. Experimental developments in MTGase production, structural and protein engineering, synthetic genetic circuits, CRISPR based regulation, metabolic control, nanobiomaterials, and spatial biocatalysis are evaluated alongside computational approaches including AlphaFold assisted structure prediction, molecular docking, molecular dynamics, machine learning guided mutagenesis, and metabolic modeling. Emphasis is placed on experimentally validated outcomes and current limitations. Key unresolved barriers include intracellular off target crosslinking, proteostatic burden, variable crosslink stoichiometry, limited temporal control of MTGase activity, chassis dependence, and industrial scale up. Where direct evidence is lacking, prospective applications are distinguished from established capabilities and corresponding engineering strategies are proposed. Collectively, this review envisions MTGase as a controllable protein level platform for synthetic biology, while defining the evidence, limitations, and experimental requirements needed for its broader application in microbial biotechnology.
authors: Syeda Warisul Fatima; Shahenvaz Alam

title: Protein Language Models: Learning From Evolution, Designing Beyond It
abstract: Abstract Protein language models (PLMs) have transformed our ability to learn from evolutionary sequence space, but protein engineering ultimately asks a different question: not what evolution selected, but what we should build next. Zero-shot likelihoods therefore provide useful, but not universal, measures of fitness and can misalign with engineering objectives. Experimental supervision redirects these priors towards properties of interest, enabling target-specific prediction and closed-loop optimization. PLMs thereby complement structure-based design: structural methods provide geometric control, while PLMs integrate experimental feedback to optimize functional and developability properties. Realizing this potential requires evaluation beyond retrospective predictive accuracy, towards extrapolation, multi-objective optimization, and prospective experimental success. We argue for recurring competitions combining scalable predictive benchmarks with prospective experimental challenges. Ultimately, progress should be measured not by predicting existing experiments, but by enabling successful new ones.
authors: Maurice Brenner; Julius Schlensok; Alexander P.; Robert Schmirler; Michael Heinzinger

title: Protruding Geometry Provides Potential Homing Sites of Circulating Tumor Cells
abstract: Abstract Circulating tumor cells (CTCs) must adhere to the vascular endothelium to initiate metastasis, yet the role of vessel wall topography remains unclear. We present an integrated microfluidic platform combining defined protruding geometries, live-cell imaging, and controlled perfusion to study CTC homing. Using a multiscale device that reproduces hierarchical vascular branching, we show that CTCs accumulate preferentially at locations with protruded geometry, including bifurcations, sharp corners and positively curved segments. At these hotspots, a viscoelastic, polymer-like network assembles, capturing CTCs and accompanying progressive multicellular aggregation. This network undergoes stretching and elastic recoil even under laminar flow. Mechanistically, knockdown of DSG2 and ITGB3 reduces retention, suggesting a potential anti-metastasis strategy targeting molecular–mechanical coupling. Computational fluid dynamics simulations indicate that hotspots coincide with pronounced velocity and pressure perturbations. Our experiments identify local geometry as a critical determinant of CTC arrest and provide a platform for studying the physical mechanisms of metastatic homing.
authors: Yeqing Leng; Bo Li

title: Quantum-Inspired Graph Neural Digital Twins for the sub-microsecond topological co-design and temporal degradation modeling of cellulose, hemicellulose, and lignin smart gels.
abstract: The clinical translation of lignocellulosic smart gels is constrained by empirical formulation screening, complex structure-property relationships, and uncertainty in degradation and therapeutic-release behavior. This study aims to determine whether a unified computational digital-twin framework can (i) optimize the crosslinking topology of cellulose-, hemicellulose-, and lignin-based matrices, (ii) predict their mechanical and temporal degradation behavior, and (iii) translate optimized formulations into real-time control parameters for microfluidic synthesis. To address these objectives, we develop a Quantum-Inspired Graph Neural Digital Twin (Q-GNDT) that represents molecular interactions as dynamic non-Euclidean graphs and formulates topological optimization as a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) problem. A temporal graph-decay model couples pH-dependent hydrolysis, enzymatic cleavage, percolation loss, and drug diffusion to predict time-resolved degradation and release. The computational architecture is integrated with an edge-AI control model designed for sub-microsecond microfluidic actuation. Retrospective cross-validation against published experimental datasets from three independent studies yielded mean absolute errors of 2.1% for pore size, 2.9% for storage modulus, and 1.5% for drug-release kinetics, with an overall RMSE of 0.74%. An in-silico targeted-delivery case study further produced 4.1% initial burst release, 98.0% cumulative delivery, and near-linear release kinetics (R<sup>2</sup> = 0.991). These results indicate that Q-GNDT can serve as a computational design and screening framework for narrowing the experimental search space of programmable lignocellulosic biomaterials. Prospective synthesis, biological testing, and in vivo validation remain necessary before clinical translation.
authors: Bajpai K.

title: Quo vadis ultrasound: toward a terminologia sonographica
abstract: The increasing use of artificial intelligence, automated image analysis, and robotic systems in ultrasound diagnostics necessitates a consistent, physically grounded, and cross-device comparable terminology. However, contemporary ultrasonographic findings are frequently described using historically evolved, metaphorical, and ambiguously defined terms. This semantic variability limits reproducibility, data harmonization, and the learning and reporting capacity of AI-based models. Ultrasound images do not represent direct anatomical depictions, but rather algorithmic reconstructions of acoustic interactions based on model-dependent assumptions. Artifacts and echo patterns, therefore, reflect the discrepancy between physical reality and mathematical approximation within signal processing. Inconsistent nomenclature widens the gap between measured variables, reconstruction models, and clinical interpretation. This paper analyses this structural problem and outlines a development framework for an internationally compatible Terminologia Sonographica. It proposes the systematic collection of existing descriptors, their translation into operationalizable categories, and consensus-based validation involving ultrasound societies. The aim is to establish an ontologically precise, interoperable semantic infrastructure for quality assurance, digital documentation, and future AI-supported decision-making.
authors: Jan Nawratil; Kathleen Möller; Claudia Lucius; Ole Graumann; Christoph F Dietrich

title: RPA-primed droplet-partitioned CRISPR/Cas12a assay for low-copy detection of Candida albicans in vaginal specimens
abstract: Candida albicans is a major cause of vulvovaginal candidiasis, and sensitive detection of low-abundance fungal DNA remains challenging in clinical specimens. In this study, we developed a two-stage assay combining rapid recombinase polymerase amplification (RPA) with droplet-partitioned CRISPR/Cas12a fluorescence detection. Target DNA was first amplified by RPA for 10 min and subsequently analyzed in vortex-generated polydisperse droplets without microfluidic chip fabrication. Using predefined NTC-based analytical criteria, the operational LoDs were 10 copies/μL for the bulk RPA-Cas12a assay and 1 copy/μL for the droplet-partitioned format under the tested conditions. No cross-reactivity was observed with the tested non-target organisms, including additional clinically relevant non- albicans Candida species. In a preliminary evaluation of 28 residual vaginal swab specimens, the assay showed complete concordance with a routine composite clinical reference using an exploratory cohort-derived droplet-count cutoff. Because the comparator was not species-specific for C. albicans , these findings represent preliminary concordance rather than definitive diagnostic accuracy. The complete workflow was performed within approximately 1 h using basic laboratory equipment. These findings demonstrate that droplet partitioning can improve the low-copy analytical readout of RPA-Cas12a detection and provide a practical approach for qualitative identification of C. albicans DNA in vaginal specimens.
authors: Ju Long; Juan Xie; Fang Liu; Jie Peng; Wenfei Xu; Xu-Hui Li
venue: Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology

title: Rapid Antibiotic Susceptibility Testing by Reflectometric Interference Fourier Transform Spectroscopy on pH-responsive Hydrogel Infiltrated Porous Silicon Integrated into Microchips
abstract: Abstract Rapid antimicrobial susceptibility testing is essential for timely therapeutic decision-making and limiting the global spread of antimicrobial resistance. However, conventional methods are labor-intensive and require prolonged incubation, delaying antibiotic selection. Here, we present a microfluidic–interferometric platform for rapid label-free antimicrobial susceptibility testing based on antibiotic-dependent bacterial metabolic acidification. A 3D-printed concentration gradient generator microchip was interconnected with a five-channel microfluidic chip containing gelatin-infiltrated porous silicon Fabry–Pérot nanosensors. Scanning electron microscopy, energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy, and transfer matrix method simulations confirmed partial gelatin infiltration into the porous silicon layer. The simulations further revealed pH-dependent swelling of the infiltrated hydrogel within the pores, providing the basis for optical pH sensing. Acidification of the culture medium during Escherichia coli metabolism increased the effective optical thickness, which was continuously monitored by reflectometric interference Fourier transform spectroscopy. A pH calibration established using buffer solutions agreed well with bacteria-induced optical responses, confirming that the measured optical changes originated from metabolic acidification. The platform was then used to evaluate the susceptibility of Escherichia coli to ciprofloxacin, gentamicin, and ceftazidime. Results obtained after only 1.5 h showed strong agreement with those from 8 h of conventional incubation, yielding Pearson correlation coefficients of 0.92 for ciprofloxacin and gentamicin and 0.96 for ceftazidime. This platform accelerates antimicrobial susceptibility testing by combining rapid microfluidic analysis with on-chip generation and simultaneous incubation of multiple antibiotic concentrations. Together with label-free optical sensing and low sample consumption, these features make the proposed platform a promising approach for rapid antimicrobial susceptibility testing.
authors: Fereshteh Rahimi; Shima Abarghoe; Nizami Duran; Ali Abouei Mehrizi; Mahsa Sedighi; Mahya Mosayebzadeh; Elif Yaprak Çolak; Selin Sabancı

title: Rare Earth Elements Recovery with Membranes, Additive Manufacturing, and AI/ML Workflows
abstract: Rare earth element (REE) extraction and separation from secondary sources are entering a critical stage as the demand for REE-enabled materials accelerates while conventional supply chains face technical, economic, and environmental pressure. Although significant progress has been made in REE separations from primary resources, inherent variability of secondary sources introduces substantial chemical and processing challenges, rendering REEs an ever-moving target for extraction and production. In this review, we discuss conventional and novel methods in separations, additive manufacturing–enabled separations, role of AI in separations, data driven approaches, AI/ML implementation, self-driving labs, and AI/ML workflows.
authors: Pasindu Samaraweera; Ilia N. Ivanov; Mariappan Parans Paranthaman; Rigoberto C. Advíncula

title: Real-time estimation of high-resolution flow fields and reduced-order coordinates from event-based imaging velocimetry
abstract: A data-driven framework is proposed to estimate high-resolution (HR) velocity fields and reduced-order flow coordinates from coarse real-time event-based imaging velocimetry (rt-EBIV) measurements. Low-resolution (LR) data are retrieved through fast event analysis on a coarse grid. During offline training, the LR/HR mapping and a linear dynamical model in a proper orthogonal decomposition (POD)-based reduced-order space are identified. Online, each incoming LR snapshot is projected onto the LR basis, and the corresponding HR reduced-order coordinates are estimated and temporally regularized. Three estimators are proposed and compared: a direct Kalman filter (KF), a linear stochastic estimation (LSE) combined with Kalman filtering, and a variance-rescaled implementation (LSE+VR). The full HR velocity field is then reconstructed from the estimated reduced-order coordinates using the retained POD basis. The framework is assessed on two turbulent flows acquired by pulsed event-based imaging velocimetry (EBIV): a submerged water jet and a channel flow over a square rib. All three estimators outperform direct cubic interpolation of the LR fields, recovering physically consistent HR flow states with improved estimation of turbulent kinetic energy, spectral content, reduced-order dynamics, and temporal coherence. The linear stochastic estimator yields the lowest overall reconstruction error, while its variance-rescaled implementation provides nearly identical values and improves the recovery of fluctuation energy and higher-order content. The direct KF formulation remains highly efficient in terms of computational cost and provides the closest agreement with the HR reference in the temporal and spatial spectral analyses. The bulk of the computational cost lies in the full-field HR reconstruction, whereas the reduced-order coordinate estimation alone is negligible compared with the cost of the LR processing itself. The framework enables deliberately coarse real-time EBIV processing to be combined with reduced-order refinement, extending the effective real-time operating range towards higher update frequencies while still providing richer and dynamically more consistent HR flow representations. This makes the approach attractive for high-quality real-time flow diagnostics and as a first step towards future observer-based and closed-loop flow-control applications.
authors: Luca Franceschelli; Enrico Amico; C. Willert; Marco Raiola; Gioacchino Cafiero; Stefano Discetti

title: Recent Advances in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in Pharma Drug Discovery, Physiotherapy Practice, and Personalized Medicine: A Comprehensive Review
abstract: The convergence of artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), and deep learning (DL) architectures has established a paradigm shift across the continuum of modern bio-medicine.Historically, biomedical innovation operated within isolated silos: pharmaceutical research grappled with exorbitant attrition rates and extended development timelines; physical rehabilitation relied on subjective observational assessments; and clinical medicine administered standardized therapeutic regimens to heterogeneous patient cohorts.Today, generative deep learning, geometric graph neural networks (GNNs), computer vision algorithms, and multi-omics integrative frameworks bridge these domains into a unified ecosystem.In drug discovery, modern AI models execute high-throughput virtual screening, predict three-dimensional macromolecular target structures, and design optimized lead compounds with precise pharmacokinetic properties.In physical therapy and rehabilitation, vision-based motion tracking, wearable sensor fusion, and smart robotics enable continuous, quantitative bio-feedback and dynamic intervention tailoring.Concurrently, in personalized medicine, transformer-based genomic language models and multi-modal clinical decision support systems (CDSS) aggregate multi-omics data, longitudinal electronic health records (EHRs), and real-world evidence (RWE) to optimize treatment strategies for individual patients.This comprehensive review synthesizes the cross-disciplinary advances, underlying mathematical architectures, clinical validation pipelines, regulatory challenges, and future trajectories of AI and ML across pharmaceutical discovery, physical rehabilitation, and precision therapeutics.
venue: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology

title: Recent Advances in Automated Single-Cell Manipulation Platforms: Optical Tweezers, Microfluidics, Microrobots, and Micropipette/Microneedle Systems
abstract: Automated micromanipulation enables precise, repeatable interaction with single cells and subcellular structures. This review examines four platform archetypes defined by their dominant interaction mechanism: field-mediated optical tweezers, flow-mediated automated microfluidics, mobile microrobots, and fixed-probe micropipette/microneedle systems. Rather than treating them as equivalent robot classes, the review compares their working principles, sensing and control architectures, application fit, quantitative performance evidence, and biological trade-offs. Recent advances in closed-loop operation, intelligent perception, multimodal sensing, and hybrid workflows are analyzed, and a standardized set of reporting metrics is proposed to support objective comparison and translation.
authors: Adnan Shakoor

title: Recent Advances in Closed-Loop Control Techniques for Additive Manufacturing: A Review
abstract: Additive manufacturing (AM) has transformed modern manufacturing by enabling the layer-by-layer fabrication of complex components directly from digital models. However, variations in process parameters, material behavior, thermal conditions, and machine dynamics can significantly affect product quality, dimensional accuracy, and process stability. This review examines advanced closed-loop control techniques for additive manufacturing, emphasizing real-time monitoring, feedback control, and intelligent process regulation. The AM process, major printing technologies, and conventional closed-loop control concepts are first discussed to establish the fundamental framework. In-situ monitoring techniques, including imaging and acoustic sensing, are examined for real-time defect detection and process validation. Advanced control strategies such as Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) control, Adaptive Control, Gain Scheduling, Model Reference Adaptive Systems (MRAS), and fuzzy logic-based control are then reviewed. These approaches enable dynamic adjustment of printing parameters in response to process deviations, thereby improving manufacturing consistency and reducing defects. The review also highlights an integration of AI with closed-loop systems to support predictive and autonomous control. Finally, current challenges and research opportunities are identified, emphasizing intelligent sensing, adaptive algorithms, and data-driven control for reliable and autonomous additive manufacturing.
authors: Mr. Mohit Sahu
venue: International journal of computer science & information system.

title: Recent Advances in Sample Preparation for Cholesterol and Oxysterol Analysis in Complex Biological Matrices
abstract: Cholesterol and oxysterols are key molecules that regulate physiological processes and participate in the occurrence and progression of various major diseases. Accurate and efficient analytical detection of these substances in complex biological matrices is critical for disease mechanism research and biomarker discovery. However, challenges including complex biological matrices, large differences in analyte abundance, susceptibility to auto‑oxidation, low ionization efficiency, and difficulty in isomer separation pose severe obstacles to reliable analysis, making sample preparation the core step for accurate quantification and valid identification. Continuous innovations have been achieved in sample preparation techniques, such as liquid-liquid extraction, solid‑phase extraction, deep eutectic solvent extraction, molecularly imprinted extraction, derivatization, as well as integrated and automated workflows. These advances improve extraction efficiency, selectivity, antioxidant protection, and throughput, while effectively reducing matrix interference and artificial oxidation. This paper systematically reviews the research progress in sample preparation for cholesterol and oxysterol analysis in complex biological matrices from 2015 to 2026, highlights the technical advantages, application scenarios, and current limitations of various pretreatment strategies, and prospects the development trends toward greening, intelligence, and high throughput.
authors: Haizhen Zhang; Longchan Liu; Haoyue Zhang; Linnan Li; Zhengtao Wang; Li Yang

title: Recent advances in nanofabrication strategies for biosensors: from precision nanopatterning to scalable, flexible, and AI-assisted manufacturing
abstract: Nanofabrication has become central to the development of high-performance biosensors by enabling precise control over sensing interfaces, enhanced signal transduction, and integration across optical, electrochemical, microfluidic, and wearable platforms. This review examines the evolution of biosensor nanofabrication from deterministic top-down patterning toward scalable and integrated manufacturing strategies. Top-down approaches, including electron-beam lithography, focused ion beam milling, nanoimprint lithography, reactive ion etching, and laser-based fabrication, are discussed alongside replication and transfer processes, soft lithography, lithography-free plasmonic structuring, and additive three-dimensional fabrication. Bottom-up strategies based on nanoparticle assembly, DNA nanotechnology, block-copolymer and nanoporous templating, and stimuli-responsive materials are further considered as routes to programmable nanoscale organization and functional biointerfaces. Particular attention is given to flexible and wearable biosensors, where substrate mechanics, conductive-interface fabrication, textile integration, epidermal microfluidics, packaging, power management, and wireless communication introduce manufacturing requirements beyond conventional rigid devices. Across these approaches, the review emphasizes that analytical sensitivity alone is insufficient for translation; nanoscale precision must be accompanied by reproducibility, scalable processing, stable biofunctionalization, antifouling performance, packaging, storage stability, and device-level quality control. Emerging AI-assisted fabrication and process optimization strategies are also discussed as tools for linking manufacturing parameters with structural and analytical performance. Overall, the review provides a manufacturing-oriented perspective on how hybrid nanofabrication strategies can bridge high-performance laboratory biosensors with reproducible, scalable, and application-ready sensing systems.
authors: Meryem Beyza Avci; Furkan Kocer; Seda Nur Topkaya; Konstantinos Papatryfonos; Arif E. Çetin

title: Recent progress and future opportunities in rheology: a review by the British Society of Rheology
abstract: Abstract Rheology plays a critical role across science and engineering, affecting sectors from healthcare to energy. In the UK, rheological research supports innovation in both academia and industry. This review, coordinated by the British Society of Rheology (BSR), provides an updated overview of current research directions across the UK and beyond.

title: Reconfigurable acoustic tweezers based on a programmable droplet array
abstract: Conventional acoustic manipulation relies on either direct acoustic radiation force acting on particles or indirect methods using acoustic streaming generated by acoustic pressure fields to manipulate particles. While acoustic devices generating standing waves can create patterned arrangements of particles and cells, these methods are typically limited to producing regular arrays in static configurations. This study introduces a dynamic acoustic field modulation method to overcome these limitations, significantly enhancing manipulation flexibility. Crucially, the propagation of acoustic energy varies substantially at liquid-solid interfaces or gas-solid interfaces due to differences in acoustic impedance matching. To exploit this, we use a digital microfluidic chip (DMF) to manipulate droplets and generate a programmable droplet array via the electrowetting-on-dielectric effect. By utilizing the programmable droplet array, we dynamically alter the spatial distribution of the acoustic field from a bulk acoustic wave (BAW) device in real time and demonstrate this technique's capability for capturing and manipulating particles on demand. We believe this is a unique method to create acoustic tweezers with great flexibility and reconfigurability, which holds promising potential for advanced applications in micromanipulation, micro-assembly, and beyond.
authors: Zhen Wang; Menglei Zhao; Kangfu Chen; Yao Lu; Haopu Wang; Zongliang Guo; Zonghao Li; Meiyi Zhou; Huiliang Cao; Kaiqiang Cao; Xiaoyi Wang; Rongxin Fu; Hang Li; Zhichao Ma; Jiafang Li; Huikai Xie; Xicheng Zhang

title: Reframing decentralized diagnostics with a programmable multi-dimensional microfluidic system
abstract: Decentralized diagnostics are vital for infectious disease control, yet current point-of-care tools remain largely one-dimensional, failing to capture the multidimensional profiles required for precision management. Here, we show SID-WAVES (Smartphone-Integrated Diagnostics with Wax-encoded Amplified and Versatile Evaluation System), an intelligent, multimodal microfluidic platform. Integrating low-melting-point phase-change and dual-siphon valves with RPA–CRISPR/Cas12a nucleic acid detection and protein immunoassays, the platform enables automated, one-step, sample-to-answer operation via an AI-assisted smartphone readout that reduces operator-dependent variability. Spatial-temporal-signal encoding supports multiplexed, multi-sample, and multimodal analysis, achieving attomolar-level sensitivity (10−18 M) and >95% diagnostic accuracy across 225 clinical and self-collected molecular assays, demonstrating robust usability. For proteins, a triple-amplification strategy and hierarchical capture enhance sensitivity 125-fold, improving accuracy from 87.6% to 100% in 54 simulated samples. Functioning as a reconfigurable analytical framework where panels are changed by swapping targets and probes, this work helps mitigate the Sensitivity–Multiplexing–Accessibility trade-off, reframing decentralized diagnostics from single-target screening to multi-dimensional health profiling. Decentralized diagnostics has the potential to improve health equity as well as support a more rapid response to disease outbreaks. Here authors present SID-WAVES, a multimodal microfluidic platform which allows ‘sample-in, results-out’ detection of both nucleic acid and protein biomarkers.
authors: Tao Xu; Ying Zhang; Xin Tang; Hongguo Wei; Lingyan Kang; Qize Zhou; Shunji Li; Xudong Zhao; Jiashuo Li; Zimeng Zhang; Chao Wan; Yufei Zhang; Dongjuan Chen; Ye Tian; Bi-Feng Liu; Peng Chen

title: Regular exercise augments gut-brain communication and visceral feedback control of appetite
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Regular exercise is widely accepted to support long-term body weight management; however, the neurobiological adaptations that contribute to the beneficial effects of habitual physical activity beyond increases in energy expenditure per se remain unclear. Here, we investigated whether regular exercise alters gut-brain communication and visceral feedback control of feeding. METHODS: Mice were subjected to regular voluntary wheel running. Energy expenditure and feeding were assessed under basal conditions and following an overnight fast. Nutrients were delivered directly into the stomach by intragastric infusion. Brain-wide responses to intragastric nutrient delivery were assessed using positron emission tomography (PET). Single-cell sequencing and histological analyses were used to determine nutrient-responsive neuronal populations in the caudal brainstem. Genetic associations with body weight were evaluated using GWAS data. RESULTS: Intragastric nutrient delivery suppressed feeding more strongly in exercising mice. Brain-wide PET revealed enhanced responses to intragastric nutrients in various brain regions. Single-cell sequencing identified several nutrient-responsive caudal brainstem populations, including a previously unrecognized population marked by expression of fibrinogen C domain containing 1 (FIBCD1). Regular exercise selectively enhanced the nutrient-evoked activation of FIBCD1 neurons. Histological analyses demonstrate that FIBCD1 neurons are also present in the human brainstem, and GWAS data suggest a potential relevance of this neuron population to body-weight regulation. CONCLUSIONS: Regular exercise enhances behavioral and brain responses to intragastric nutrient delivery and sensitizes FIBCD1 neurons in the brainstem of mice. These findings reveal an exercise-associated adaptation of gut-brain communication that may contribute to improved matching of caloric intake to energy expenditure.

title: Remote‐Controlled Genetic Circuits: Light, Ultrasound, and Magnetic Fields for Programmable Gene Regulation
abstract: Remote-controlled genetic circuits use externally applied physical signals to regulate gene expression and cellular functions with spatial and temporal precision. Light, ultrasound, and magnetic fields provide complementary advantages in controllability, tissue accessibility, and biological compatibility, but their performance depends on both physical-field propagation and efficient conversion of external energy into intracellular signals and predictable gene-regulatory outputs. This review presents a unified framework of physical transduction, biological sensors, signal processors, and genetic effectors for comparing prokaryotic and eukaryotic systems. Core genetic circuits are distinguished from delivery and auxiliary platforms that support cargo release, cellular uptake, or energy conversion without directly regulating genes. Representative systems are compared by circuit architecture, transduction mechanism, stimulus parameters, dynamic range, basal leakage, response kinetics, reversibility, in vivo actuation, delivery requirements, and safety. The evolution from inducible switches toward multi-input logic, tunable regulation, genetic memory, and feedback control is discussed. An end-to-end codesign workflow and modality-specific reporting framework are proposed to integrate physical inputs, transducers, genetic circuits, delivery strategies, and stimulation devices. Quantitative benchmarking and standardized safety evaluation are essential for advancing these systems toward predictable and clinically translatable therapeutic platforms.

title: Research progress on the application of multi-scale computational methods in the research and development of anti-tuberculosis infection drugs
abstract: Tuberculosis (TB), driven by Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), remains a leading cause of mortality from infectious disease worldwide.​ The global dissemination of multidrug-resistant (MDR) and extensively drug-resistant (XDR) strains—coupled with protracted treatment regimens and the persistence of latent infection—has not only compromised first-line chemotherapies but also underscored the stagnation of conventional drug development pipelines. In this review, we systematically synthesize how multi-scale computational strategies are reshaping anti-TB drug discovery and explicitly delineate their hierarchical integration—a cohesive framework that, to our knowledge, has yet to be comprehensively mapped in the existing literature.​ We survey four interconnected computational layers: (i) systems and network pharmacology for macroscopic target and pathway prioritization; (ii) machine learning (ML) for mesoscopic virtual screening, resistance classification, and ADMET prediction; (iii) molecular docking for microscopic elucidation of ligand–target binding modes; and (iv) molecular dynamics (MD) simulations for atomic-level validation of binding poses and assessment of complex stability. Representative studies demonstrate that this workflow has pinpointed pivotal TB vulnerabilities (e.g., MmpL3, InhA, DprE1, ATP synthase, and FtsZ), enabled ML models to predict drug resistance from genomic data with high fidelity, and identified promising candidates such as vazabitide A (predicted binding affinity of −85.8 kcal/mol against Pks13) alongside repurposed agents (e.g., aldoxorubicin, quarfloxin). Critically, these computational predictions are reinforced by orthogonal experimental validation spanning in vitro enzymatic and phenotypic assays, in vivo infection models, clinical pharmacokinetic profiling, and multi-omics corroboration. We conclude that the top-down pipeline-spanning network pharmacology to ML, docking, and MD-integrated with bottom-up feedback constitutes a closed-loop paradigm that accelerates lead identification while addressing emergent drug resistance.​ Nevertheless, inherent limitations in predictive reliability and cross-layer error propagation necessitate rigorous downstream experimental validation. Looking forward, generative artificial intelligence, self-driving laboratories, and standardized cross-method benchmarking are poised to consolidate this multi-scale pipeline into a robust engine for next-generation anti-TB therapeutics.

title: Reshaping the scissors: From directed evolution to AI-driven design for enhanced Cas performance
abstract: CRISPR/Cas gene editing holds great promise for applications in agricultural breeding and gene therapy; however, native Cas proteins face bottlenecks such as off-target effects, PAM limitations, and delivery challenges. This review explores a three-tiered, progressive, and synergistic analytical framework comprising directed evolution, rational structural design, and integrated protein engineering. Following the logic of "random exploration-precision modification-system integration," it systematically clarifies the principles, advantages, disadvantages, and complementary interactions among these three optimization techniques. By comprehensively mapping the entire technical pathway for Cas protein improvement, this study fills a gap in systematic analysis within the field and provides a theoretical framework for tiered, synergistic modification to support the development of high-performance editors. The paper further analyzes a novel research and development paradigm in which AI and protein language models profoundly empower Cas modification. It summarizes intelligent toolchains such as structure prediction, virtual mutation, and de novo design of artificial Cas proteins, and highlights the unique advantages of AI in overcoming the performance trade-offs inherent in traditional protein engineering. At the same time, it identifies existing challenges, such as data scarcity and insufficient model interpretability, and looks ahead to how multimodal gene-editing large language models and automated closed-loop experimental systems will drive the iterative development of miniaturized, broad-spectrum, and highly precise editing tools, thereby facilitating the clinical and industrial implementation of gene-editing technologies.

title: Review of AI-driven discovery of cathode anode and electrolyte materials for advancing sodium-ion batteries
abstract: Abstract Sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) are emerging as a sustainable, cost-effective alternative to lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) for grid storage, electric vehicles, and electronics. However, commercialization depends on overcoming the performance bottlenecks in energy density, kinetic rates, and safety. Artificial Intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) are accelerating this shift by enabling a transition from empirical “trial-and-error” approach to data-driven, predictive “closed-loop autonomous” material discovery. This review covers AI-driven discovery advancements in SIB materials, including layered oxides/polyanionic/Prussian blue analogues cathodes, hard carbon/alloy-type/anode-free anodes, and advanced electrolyte formulations. The key AI techniques are discussed, including graph neural networks (GNNs), generative AI (GenAI) models, and deep neural networks (DNNs) coupled with multi-objective optimization to identify Pareto-optimal materials by linking atomic-scale design to macroscale performance. Some promising materials for enhancing electrode performance are discussed. AI-driven workflows are explored spanning inverse design, high-throughput screening, property prediction, and autonomous discovery, targeting high-performance materials for next-generation applications. The current challenges and knowledge gaps are discussed, including data scarcity, interfacial modeling complexities, and model interpretability, while outlining future perspectives for fully autonomous, closed-loop material discovery platform.
