title: THE DESCRIPTIVE AND METHODOLOGICAL ANALYSIS OF GRADUATE THESES CONDUCTED IN THE FIELD OF ROBOTIC REHABILITATION IN TURKIYE
abstract: Objective: Robotic rehabilitation has become an increasingly important research area in neurorehabilitation due to its potential to provide intensive, repetitive, and task-oriented interventions. This study aimed to examine graduate theses completed in the field of robotic rehabilitation in Türkiye in terms of bibliometric, thematic, and methodological characteristics. Methods: This retrospective and descriptive bibliometric analysis was conducted using data obtained from the National Thesis Center database of the Council of Higher Education (YÖK). The database was systematically searched on April 23, 2026, using keywords related to robotic rehabilitation. After removing duplicate records and applying the inclusion and exclusion criteria, 44 theses were included in the analysis. The theses were evaluated according to publication year, university, department, thesis type, advisor title, and patient group. Descriptive statistics were calculated as frequencies and percentages. Results: A total of 398 thesis records were initially identified, and 106 unique theses remained after duplicate removal. Of these, 44 theses met the eligibility criteria. The highest number of theses was completed in 2023 and 2025. Most theses were conducted at the University of Health Sciences and Istanbul Medipol University. The majority were carried out in Physiotherapy and Rehabilitation and Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation departments. Master’s theses constituted the largest proportion. Stroke was the most frequently examined patient group. Conclusion: Robotic rehabilitation is a developing and increasingly studied field in Türkiye. However, doctoral-level studies and research involving diverse patient groups remain limited. Future studies should adopt methodologically rigorous designs and focus on broader patient-centered outcomes.
authors: Sumeyye Akcay; Duygu Aktar Reyhanıoglu

title: THE IMPACT OF ERP SYSTEMS ON BUSINESS PROCESSES AND THEIR VALUE FOR SHAREHOLDERS AND TOP MANAGEMENT: EVIDENCE SYNTHESIS AND A CONCEPTUAL MODEL FOR UZBEKISTAN
abstract: This paper investigates how enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems transform core business processes and through which mechanisms these changes create value for shareholders and top management in the context of Uzbekistan. A structured qualitative review of 17 empirical studies (2001–2026) and national regulatory documents was conducted within the frameworks of agency theory, the resource-based view, the IS success model, and the TOE framework. ERP creates value indirectly: it standardises, integrates, and automates processes, thereby improving information quality and internal control, which in turn deliver value for top management (decision support, agility) and shareholders (performance, lower agency costs). Each link depends on process redesign, top management support, and training. The paper links ERP process effects to corporate governance outcomes and adapts the model to Uzbekistan with five testable hypotheses.
authors: Fakhriddinov Anvarkhon; Anvarov Ahrorjon

title: TM-APR: Thermal Temporal-Memory Localization via Analytic Online Adaptation
abstract: Thermal Visual Place Recognition (Thermal VPR) maps camera observations to metric poses within a mapped environment, serving as a prerequisite for autonomous navigation. However, thermal VPR suffers from severe environmental dependence, heavy online retraining overheads, and an inability to model dynamic non-linear shifts, causing existing frameworks to fail during online deployment. To achieve robust domain-invariant place recognition, we bridge Analytic Class-Incremental Learning (ACIL) with domain-invariant VPR for the first time, revealing that its gradient-free matrix updates construct a surprisingly strong baseline that outperforms conventional fine-tuning. Nevertheless, standard ACIL exhibits a critical vulnerability to extreme non-linear thermal fluctuations due to its structural linear assumptions. To overcome this limitation, we exploit a novel algebraic equivalence between ACIL and modern control theory, proposing a framework which embeds Unscented propagation (U-ACIL), Gaussian Mixture partitioning (GMM-ACIL), and minimax $H_\infty$ optimization ($H_\infty$-ACIL) directly into the update loop. Our formulation guarantees exact closed-form matrix updates within $\mathcal{O}(1)$ computational complexity, bypassing backpropagation to ensure that the online update latency ($Δt_{\mathrm{learn}}$) remains strictly bounded below the sensor acquisition interval ($Δt_{\mathrm{acquire}}$), thereby eliminating trajectory jumps in real-time SLAM pipelines.
authors: Yanshuo Bai; Kanji Tanaka

title: TMS timed to interictal epileptiform discharges
abstract: Abstract Interictal epileptiform discharges (IEDs) are pathological hypersynchronous bursts of electrical brain activity that occur between seizures in patients with epilepsy. IEDs are caused by transient brain states that are difficult to predict, making them a challenging neurophysiological and technological case for brain-state-dependent stimulation. Administering stimulation at IED onset may provide insight into the epileptic network and optimize neurostimulation therapies. Here, we assessed the feasibility of IED-triggered transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) in two children with self-limited epilepsy with centrotemporal spikes (SeLECTS), a common pediatric epilepsy in which IEDs emerge from the motor cortex. A convolutional neural network (CNN) was trained on the participants’ pre-recorded electroencephalography (EEG) data with IEDs annotated by an epileptologist. The CNN was integrated into an EEG-processing pipeline that classified EEG segments as “IED” or “non-IED” in real time. With this pipeline, TMS pulses were administered during IED or non-IED periods in an interleaved, randomized design. We stimulated both the motor cortex generating the IEDs and the contralateral motor cortex and tested the impact of IEDs on TMS-evoked potentials (TEPs). Our study demonstrated that TMS can be timed to IEDs and that there is a site-specific increase in TEP amplitude when stimulating during IEDs. Out of the TMS pulses aimed at an IED, 19% and 39% were successfully delivered during an IED for the two participants, respectively. For future research, we propose ways to address the methodological challenges of IED-timed TMS, enabling brain-state-dependent TMS for epilepsy research and treatment.
authors: Matilda Makkonen; Olli‐Pekka Kahilakoski; Miguel Menchaca; Ivan Zubarev; Oula Siljamo; Umair Hassan; Xiwei Shé; Wendy Qi; Tuomas P. Mutanen; Risto Juhani Ilmoniemi; Pantelis Lioumis; Fiona Mitchell Baumer

title: TMS-EEG Investigation of Cortical Activity Induced by Individualized rTMS in Patients with Prolonged Disorders of Consciousness
abstract: Abstract Objective To establish an individualized repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) target selection protocol based on resting-state electroencephalography (EEG) directed functional connectivity for patients with prolonged disorders of consciousness (pDoC), and to explore the underlying electrophysiological mechanisms using transcranial magnetic stimulation combined with EEG (TMS-EEG). Methods We enrolled 42 pDoC patients and randomly assigned to an individualized rTMS group, a conventional rTMS group, and a sham stimulation group. The individualized rTMS group selected the target with stronger directed functional connectivity between F3 and Pz as the stimulation site based on Granger causality analysis. The conventional rTMS group received random stimulation at either F3 or Pz. Both active groups received 10 sessions of high-frequency rTMS over 10 consecutive days, while the sham group underwent sham stimulation. Behavioral improvement and cortical connectivity were assessed before and after treatment using the Coma Recovery Scale-Revised (CRS-R) and TMS-EEG, respectively. Results CRS-R scores significantly increased in both the individualized and conventional rTMS groups ( p < 0.05), whereas no significant improvement was observed in the sham group ( p > 0.05). TMS-EEG analysis demonstrated that the amplitudes of N100 and P180 components significantly increased post-treatment in both active groups ( p < 0.05), with no statistically significant changes in the sham group ( p > 0.05). Global mean field amplitude (GMFA) significantly increased post-treatment in both active groups ( p < 0.05). Specifically, significant increases were found in the 1-100 ms and 101–200 ms time windows post-treatment in both active groups ( p < 0.05). Additionally, the individualized rTMS group showed a significant increase in the 201–300 ms window ( p < 0.05), which was not observed in the conventional group ( p > 0.05). No significant differences were found in the sham group across any time windows (1-100 ms, 101–200 ms, 201–300 ms, 301–400 ms, 401–500 ms; p > 0.05). Correlation analyses indicated that the change in CRS-R score positively correlated with the change in N100 amplitude in both the individualized ( r = 0.82, p < 0.001) and conventional ( r = 0.79, p = 0.001) treatment groups. Similarly, the change in CRS-R score positively correlated with the change in P180 amplitude in the individualized ( r = 0.77, p = 0.0002) and conventional ( r = 0.62, p = 0.025) groups. Conclusion Individualized rTMS based on resting-state EEG directed functional connectivity is more effective in promoting consciousness recovery in pDoC patients. Compared to conventional rTMS, this approach may better facilitate the sustained propagation of post-stimulation cortical activity along residual consciousness networks and promote integration during middle-to-late stages. This study provides preliminary evidence supporting the transition of neuromodulation therapy for pDoC from fixed-target interventions to individualized precision regulation. Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05682248. Ethics approval : Ethics Committee of Xuanwu Hospital, 2022[022].
authors: Ye Zhang; Xiao Yan; Zilong Zhu; 杜巨豹; Lei Cao; weiqun Song; Yong Wang

title: The Evolution of Brain-Computer Interfaces Towards Collaborative Intelligence
abstract: Abstract Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) are evolving from unidirectional control toward deeper integration of biological and machine intelligence. This transition is constrained by two complementary bottlenecks: Intent Mismatch, or Brain-to-Machine Underreach, in which user intentions cannot be sufficiently decoded, represented, or executed by the machine; and State Mismatch, or Machine-to-Brain Overload, in which system demands exceed the user’s current cognitive, affective, or neural resources. This review uses these two mismatches as an organizing framework for examining the evolution of BCIs toward brain-machine collaborative intelligence, while distinguishing non-invasive and invasive modalities according to their signal characteristics and translational constraints. We review neural decoding, generative artificial intelligence, and shared control as approaches for reducing Intent Mismatch, and passive BCIs, adaptive interaction, neurofeedback, and neuromodulation as approaches for reducing State Mismatch. By integrating these solution paths, this review outlines a pathway toward adaptive, bidirectional, and human-centered BCI systems.
authors: Yang Yu; Yingxin Liu; Zhipeng Fan; Zongtan Zhou; Ling‐Li Zeng; Dewen Hu

title: The GenAI Who Knew Too Little: Revisiting Transactive Memory Systems in Human GenAI Collaboration
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is rapidly transforming knowledge work, creating new collaborative dynamics that challenge tradi-tional human-human interaction patterns. This study investigates how Transactive Memory Systems (TMS) manifest in human-GenAI collabora-tion. Through qualitative interpretive interviews with 14 knowledge work-ers and thematic analysis, we identified distinct TMS manifestations across its three main dimensions: (1) regarding specialization, expertise recogni-tion exhibited asymmetry. Humans developed awareness of GenAI capabili-ties while GenAI demonstrated only temporary recognition of human exper-tise; (2) in terms of credibility, humans formed ambivalent trust relation-ships with GenAI, simultaneously attributing expertise to the latter while implementing additional verification processes; and (3) concerning coor-dination, where humans primarily directed more passive GenAI systems lacking initiative, resulting in hierarchical interaction patterns and unidi-rectional information flow. Our findings reveal that TMS manifests differ-ently in human-GenAI compared to human-human collaboration, necessitat-ing theoretical adaptations including trust markers, acknowledging GenAI's absent metamemory, and identifying its temporary memory.
authors: Christian Meske; Tobias Hermanns; Florian Brachten

title: The Reality Gap in Automated Driving Systems Testing: Landscape, Challenges, and Research Directions
abstract: Simulation is essential for testing automated driving systems (ADS), but discrepancies between simulation and reality can undermine testing conclusions. It remains unclear which discrepancies the literature addresses and what evidence supports correspondence claims. We present a systematic mapping of 235 primary studies that measure or mitigate the reality gap in ADS testing, selected from 4,195 publications. We characterise objectives, targets, approaches, experimental setups, and evaluation evidence. Our classification distinguishes simulated and real-world execution across six ADS test components, separately for each approach and its evaluation reference. This distinguishes real-world information used to construct an approach from evidence used to evaluate its claims. Of the included studies, 76% address mitigation, primarily targeting scenario and actor realism and perception, while 94% report validation or measurement procedures. Only 61 studies report metrics from multiple families covering sensor/perception correspondence, ADS behaviour, vehicle dynamics, or safety outcomes; this coverage does not establish causal links between discrepancies and test verdicts. The synthesis highlights that real-world content and physical execution must be interpreted against the claim evaluated. The findings motivate claim-specific evaluation and component-level reporting to establish which discrepancies affect testing conclusions and when simulation evidence supports conclusions about real-world ADS behaviour.
authors: Stefano Carlo Lambertenghi; Oliver Weißl; Johannes Betz; Andrea Stocco

title: The Relationship Between Self-Regulation and Time Management Among College Students
abstract: Being a college student represents the highest status an individual can attain in the learning process. During their college years, students are not only expected to adapt well to both academic and non-academic demands but also to manage themselves effectively, including efficient time management and self-regulation to maintain a balance in their behavior that enables them to move toward their desired goals. This study aims to determine the relationship between Self-Regulation and Time Management among college students using a quantitative correlational research design. The plan of sample size for this study was calculated using G*Power with an effect size of 0.3, alpha of 0.05, and power of 0.80, resulting in a minimum total sample size of 84. An additional 20% was added to account for invalid data, resulting in a final sample size of 101 participants. The Self-Regulation variable was measured using the Short Version of the Self-Regulation Questionnaire (TSSRQ), which was modified by Puspawardani (2019), and the Time Management scale was measured using the Time Management Scale (TMS), which had been tested on Indonesian college students by Khoirunnisa et al. (2026).
authors: Aurelia Azzahra Haridiani; Rizky Putra Santosa

title: The Role of Physicians and Caregivers in the Implementation of a Surgical Treatment Strategy for Hip Subluxation and Dislocation in Children with Cerebral Palsy
abstract: Introduction . Hip joint pathology is one of the most common and serious orthopedic complications in cerebral palsy. We conducted a study to identify the reasons for delays in surgical treatment of spastic hip instability from the perspective of parents’ roles and attitudes toward this issue. Aim : to determine the reasons for delays in surgical treatment for spastic hip instability in children with cerebral palsy and to examine parents’ perceptions of information provided by healthcare professionals. Materials and methods. An anonymous survey was conducted among parents of children who had undergone hip surgery. The study group included parents of 50 children with hip dislocation. The control group consisted of parents of 50 children who had undergone surgery for hip subluxation. Results . The average age of children at the time of surgery was 7.2±3.1 years (study group) and 5.8±2.9 years (control group); the differences were not statistically significant (p=0.12). Among parents of children with hip dislocation, 86% believed that the surgery was performed too late (compared to 55% in the subluxation group). Sixty-four percent of respondents attributed the primary responsibility for the delay to healthcare professionals. In the dislocation group, 60% of parents indicated that they completely rely on healthcare professionals regarding their child’s health, compared to only 29% of parents in the control group (p=0.003). In the dislocation group, 78% of parents reported being informed of the presence of hip pathology at least 3 years prior to surgery, but 82% believed that doctors did not provide them with complete and understandable information. In the control group, the corresponding figures were 52% and 36%, respectively (p <0.01). The study revealed a significant gap between the objective information provided by healthcare professionals and parents’ subjective perceptions of it. Parents tend to shift responsibility to healthcare professionals, which, in the absence of clear guidelines, leads to uncertainty and reliance on the doctor’s decision, which, however, is not always clear. Conclusion . Improving communication between the doctor and the family is an important condition for implementing a general rehabilitation program for children with cerebral palsy, who are at high risk of progression of musculoskeletal pathology, and should be considered an integral part of the prevention of orthopedic complications.
authors: Vladimir Markovich Kenis; T. I. Kiseleva; I. Yu. Klychkova; Andrey V. Sapogovskiy; Evgenii V. Melchenko; Stanislav V. Ivanov; Федосеева Александра Сергеевна

title: The Superior Fascicle of the Anterior Talofibular Ligament Functions as a Restraint Against Internal Rotation: A Cadaveric Biomechanical Study.
abstract: Lateral ankle sprains frequently result in anterior talofibular ligament (ATFL) dysfunction, leading to chronic lateral ankle instability. The ATFL consists of superior and inferior fascicles; however, the stabilizing role of the superior fascicle remains unclear. We biomechanically evaluated its function using cadaveric models. Nine frozen cadaveric ankles were tested using a robotic system (FRS2015). The superior fascicle was sequentially transected arthroscopically to simulate cumulative 3 injury types: type 1, partial detachment at the medial margin of the fibular attachment; type 2, proximal detachment; and type 3, complete detachment. Anterior talar translation, internal rotation, and inversion angles relative to the tibia were measured as displacements under the anterior drawer, internal rotation, and inversion loads, respectively, at 15° dorsiflexion and 15° and 30° plantarflexion. In situ forces and ankle kinematics were also measured. Internal rotation displacement at 30° plantarflexion was significantly greater in type 3 than in the intact (mean difference, 2.9°; 95% CI, 0.6°-5.0°; P = .01), type 1 (mean difference, 2.6°; 95% CI, 0.5°-4.8°; P = .02), and type 2 (cumulative with type 1; mean difference, 2.5°; 95% CI, 0.4°-4.5°; P = .02). With the numbers available, no significant differences were found among intact, type 1, and type 2, nor in anterior or inversion displacement across any conditions. The in situ force was greater in type 3 than in type 1 during anterior drawer and internal rotation loading, and ankle kinematics did not differ. Partial injury to the superior fascicle of the ATFL was not associated with a statistically significant difference in ankle instability under the tested conditions, whereas complete injury was associated with significantly greater internal rotational displacement. Injury to the superior fascicle of the ATFL is associated with increased internal rotational laxity, supporting the use of internal rotation testing, such as the anterolateral drawer test, when evaluating suspected ATFL injury.
authors: Tomoki Koyama; Atsushi Teramoto; Yuta Mori; Yasutaka Murahashi; Katsunori Takahashi; Nanami Ueda; Kota Watanabe; Toshimi Aizawa

title: The one-millimetre varus knee: titrating femoral rotation to the medial flexion gap in functional-alignment robotic total knee arthroplasty
abstract: Abstract Purpose. The varus knee is medially tight and has classically been balanced by stepwise soft-tissue release, which risks over-release. We tested whether, in functional-alignment (FA) robotic total knee arthroplasty (TKA), femoral rotation titrated to the medial gap balances the varus knee to within one millimetre with only a mild release, and derived a bedside rule. Methods. Observational analysis of 65 consecutive varus primary FA robotic TKAs by a single surgeon using an image-based platform. Femoral rotation, medial–lateral (M–L) gap asymmetry across preoperative, planned and final states, the graded release and balance were analysed; regression related rotation to medial flexion tightness; Wilson 95% confidence intervals; no imputation. Results. Femoral external rotation was titrated to the medial flexion gap — approximately 1.9° plus 0.34° per millimetre of tightness (ρ = −0.57; R² = 0.26; p < 0.001) — giving a simple bedside rule. With this, the medial release stayed mild in 64/65 knees (no escalation). M–L asymmetry fell from 3.8/4.5 mm (extension/flexion) to 0.4/0.3 mm — below one millimetre in 83%/93% of knees — mostly by planning. Functional balance reached 98% and strict-mechanical balance 91%; WOMAC improved from 74.6 to 2.5 and FJS-12 reached 95.2 at one year. Conclusion. In the varus knee, rotating the femur to the medial gap — rather than releasing more soft tissue — balances the knee to within one millimetre with only a mild release. A simple titration chart and playbook translate this into daily practice.
authors: Eduardo Frois Temponi; MATEUS BRAGA JACQUES GONÇALVES; Luiz Fernando Machado Soares; LUCIO HONORIO DE CARVALHO JUNIOR; PEDRO HENRIQUE Henrique Oliveira Gomes

title: The role of emotional intelligence and empathy as personal resources in enhancing employee performance in the IT industry: a job demands-resources perspective
abstract: This study investigates the relationships among Organisational Ethics (ETH), Interpersonal Relationships (IR), Job Autonomy (AUT), Support from Top Management (STM), Job Demands, Job Resources, Emotional Intelligence (EI) and Empathy (EMP) and Employee Performance (EP) within the IT (Information Technology) Industry through the JD-R (Job Demands-Resources) theory. This study examines how organisational and job-related factors are associated with Job demands and Job resources which are subsequently associated with Emotional Intelligence, Empathy and Employee Performance. Given the limitations from the previous empirical studies on EI and EMP as personal resources in IT industry context, this research aims to fill this gap by investigating the association of these personal resources with EP with a special focus on the IT industry. A quantitative research design was adopted using a structured questionnaire administered through a survey among IT employees working in different management and technical positions in Bengaluru, India. Around 318 valid responses were collected and analysed using SPSS and Jamovi. Structural Equation Modelling (SEM) was used to analyse the relationships among the constructs. The findings indicate that Emotional Intelligence and Empathy are significantly positively associated with Employee Performance in the IT industry. Further, the significant association of Job demands and Job resources with EI and EMP indicates the significance of workplace conditions in shaping employees’ emotional capabilities. This study applies the JD-R framework to examine EI and EMP as personal resources connecting job characteristics with employee performance outcomes in the IT industry. These research findings contribute to the literature of EP by providing practical insights for the IT industry seeking to enhance employee performance by developing emotional competencies and creating a supportive work culture.
authors: V. Lakshmi Voleti; Meenakshi Verma

title: Tibial spine fracture in children - a retrospective cohort study with clinical results and sports participation
abstract: Abstract Background In Norway, no previous studies have investigated the incidence or mechanism of injury of tibial spine fractures in children. The aim of this study was to describe the treatment outcomes of patients treated for a tibial spine fracture at Akershus University Hospital between 2010 and 2020. Methods This was a retrospective cohort study with cross-sectional follow-up including children (boys ≤ 16 years and girls ≤ 14 years old at time of injury) treated for tibial spine fractures at Akershus University Hospital between 2010 and 2020. The included patients were invited to a clinical follow-up visit with clinical examination of knee laxity testing (Lachman test and portable Rolimeter arthrometer measurements) and assessment of patient reported outcome measures (PROMs), including Pediatric International Knee Documentation Committee Subjective Knee Evaluation Form (pedi-IKDC) and Hospital for Special Surgery Pediatric Functional Activity Brief Scale (HSS Pedi-FABS). The primary outcome of this study was to describe outcomes after a tibial spine fracture while secondary observations included injury mechanisms, additional injuries, treatment, reinjuries and clinical examination of knee laxity. Results Twenty-four patients were included in this study. 17 (70.8%) were male and median age was 12 years old (range 6 to 16 years). Alpine skiing was the injury mechanism in 33.3% of cases. 14 of the patients were treated surgically. 6 patients (25%) had additional intraarticular injury at baseline, 3 patients later developed an anterior cruciate ligament injury, and 2 patients sustained a contralateral tibial spine fracture. The median pedi-IKDC score was 92,9, and the median HSS pedi-FABS score was 14,5. Most of the patients had differences in Rolimeter measurements between the injured and uninjured knee, with the largest side-to-side difference being 5 mm and a median difference of 1 mm. Conclusion We found increased laxity measurements with Rolimeter, but the clinical significance of this finding is uncertain. In our patient cohort, PROMs were acceptable compared with normative values. Due to the rarity of this type of injury, there is a need for a multicenter prospective study on tibial spine fractures in children. Level of evidence Level 4.
authors: Maren Gundersen; Asbjørn Årøen; Jan Harald Røtterud; Guri Ranum Ekås

title: Toward Engineering Application: A Comprehensive Review on Fracture and R-Curve of Ceramics and Ceramic Composites
abstract: Ceramics are increasingly being recognized as emerging candidates for high-performance structural applications. However, their unpredictable fracture behavior challenges reliable service-performance under complex operating conditions. Hence, screening candidates based on fracture and R-curve behavior has become indispensable to promote the applications with high reliability. Therefore, this review critically examines the relationships among composite design, sintering parameters, testing methodologies, microstructural features, extrinsic toughening mechanisms, and crack-growth resistance. The analysis reveals that crack-growth resistance is governed by the synergistic interaction of microstructural architecture, processing conditions, and toughening mechanisms, while inconsistencies in current experimental methodologies remain a major obstacle to obtaining reliable and reproducible R-curve data. The review further highlights that combining advanced numerical modeling with experimental characterization provides a more robust framework for predicting fracture behavior and optimizing ceramic performance. Emerging data-driven and artificial intelligence-based approaches are identified as promising tools for accelerating materials design, performance prediction, and optimization, although their effectiveness depends on the availability of high-quality experimental and computational datasets. By integrating current experimental evidence, numerical modeling, and emerging computational techniques, this review establishes a comprehensive understanding of fracture and R-curve behavior, identifies critical research gaps, and proposes future directions for developing reliable, high-performance, damage-tolerant ceramics for advanced engineering applications.
authors: Mostafizur Rahman; M M Tariqul Islam Mesbah; Wazed Al Islam; Mehedi Hassan Maruf; Md Rahat Al Hassan; Shingo OZAKI

title: Transcranial magnetic stimulation in autism spectrum disorder: a narrative review of neurobiological mechanisms, clinical efficacy, and future directions
abstract: Abstract Background Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a complicated neuropsychological disorder associated with social communicational problems, stereotypical interests, and behavior patterns. Though ASD has many causes, there are no treatment modalities today that have an overall impact on the condition itself, leaving room for improvement in existing approaches. Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (TMS) is one of the innovative approaches to treat such disorders by means of a noninvasive method of neuron activation using a strong magnetic field. Body The TMS could have an influence on the interconnection of the brain networks, synaptic plasticity, and the brain cortex excitability, which are associated with the alleviation of the symptoms of ASD. Although some randomized and open-label studies have reported improvement, the evidence is weakened by small samples, inconsistent protocols, and the large proportion of uncontrolled studies. This would mean that the process of selecting patients as well as administering TMS would need careful attention. There are no documented long-term impacts of TMS. For future studies, there should be incorporation of the principles from neuroimaging and electrophysiology. TMS is performed using different techniques depending on its objectives, which include single-pulse TMS that assesses brain topography; paired-pulse TMS in evaluating the inhibitory or facilitating nature of the brain cortex; repetitive TMS (rTMS). Conclusion It can be concluded from all the information presented above that TMS might have immense potential as an add-on treatment for ASDs based on the data we have accumulated. However, more studies are needed to assess the efficacy of this treatment method in addressing ASDs.To summarize, TMS is a relatively novel neuromodulation therapy that can benefit individuals with ASDs based on the neurobiological aspects of their disorders.
authors: Abdur Rehman; Md. Tosaddeque Hossain Siddiqui; Maryam Asghar Jamal; Awais Ahmad; Syeda Hamna; Zain Ul Abedeen; Zahoor Ullah; Anousheh Malak; Maliha Said; Asma Gulshan; Waheed Khan
venue: The Egyptian Journal of Neurosurgery : the official publication of the Egyptian Society of Neurological Surgeons/Egyptian journal of neurosurgery

title: Transcranial temporal interference stimulation combined with soft robotic glove training improves upper-limb motor function after subacute stroke: a randomized controlled pilot trial
abstract: Background Upper-limb dysfunction, particularly impaired distal hand function, remains one of the most disabling sequelae following a stroke. Soft robotic glove (SRG) training can provide repetitive and task-specific hand practice; however, its therapeutic effects may be limited by insufficient modulation of the damaged motor network. Transcranial temporal interference stimulation (tTIS), a novel non-invasive neuromodulation approach capable of targeting deeper neural circuits, may enhance post-stroke motor recovery by engaging cerebellar-related motor pathways and promoting network-level plasticity. Objective This study investigated whether cerebellar tTIS combined with SRG training improves upper-limb motor function in patients with subacute stroke and explored the associated changes in cortical activation and resting-state functional connectivity (FC) using functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS). Method In this prospective, single-center, randomized, sham-controlled pilot trial, 46 patients with first-ever subacute stroke were randomized 1:1 to the tTIS-SRG group ( n = 22) or the SRG group ( n = 22). Both groups received conventional rehabilitation and SRG training. The tTIS-SRG group additionally received active cerebellar tTIS, whereas the SRG group received sham stimulation, delivered once daily, 5 days per week, for 2 weeks. The primary outcome was the upper-limb motor function assessed by the Action Research Arm Test (ARAT), and the secondary outcome was activities of daily living (ADL) assessed by the modified Barthel Index (MBI). fNIRS was used to evaluate task-related cortical activation and resting-state functional connectivity before and after the intervention. This trial has been registered with the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2500107031). Results Of the 46 randomized participants, 44 completed the trial and were included in the final analysis (22 per group). One participant in the tTIS-SRG group withdrew from the study due to hospital discharge, and one participant in the SRG group declined the final assessment for personal reasons. Participants in both groups showed improvements in ARAT and MBI scores following treatment. The tTIS-SRG group demonstrated a significantly greater improvement in ARAT scores than the SRG group ( Z = −2.955, p = 0.003), whereas the between-group difference in MBI change was not significant ( Z = −1.706, p = 0.088). fNIRS analysis revealed that false discovery rate (FDR)-corrected channel-level analysis identified greater oxyhemoglobin (HbO) changes in the tTIS-SRG group than in the SRG group in two channels located in the ipsilateral frontal pole area (FPA) and ipsilateral somatosensory cortex (SSC). No region of interest (ROI)-level comparison remained statistically significant after FDR correction. Although several channel-level comparisons reached nominal significance before correction, only two channels remained statistically significant after FDR correction. Conclusion In this pilot trial, cerebellar tTIS combined with SRG training provided a more significant improvement in upper-limb motor recovery compared with SRG training alone in patients with subacute stroke. The observed clinical improvement was accompanied by enhanced task-related cortical activation and changes in motor-related functional connectivity. Larger multicenter trials with longer follow-up are needed to confirm the efficacy, durability, and underlying mechanisms of this combined intervention. Clinical trial registration https://www.chictr.org.cn/searchprojEN.html , identifier ChiCTR2500107031.
authors: Ailipinai Yasen; Xiaoyu Liao; Conghui Wei; Xinyu Zhang; Jun Lu; Xumiao Peng; 苗渝梓; Dan Zhen; Zhaodan Gan; Guangxu Xu

title: Transformational leadership and service innovation performance: the role of knowledge sharing and innovation culture in the hospitality sector employees
abstract: Abstract This research examines how Indian hotels can systematically create “wow” moments for guests by translating transformational leadership (TL) into frontline employees’ service innovation performance (SIP) rather than treating innovation as ad hoc or leader‑driven in a vacuum. Drawing on social exchange theory, organizational learning theory, and the job demands–resources (JD–R) model, we develop and test a conditional process model in which TL shapes SIP through two distinct yet complementary mechanisms: knowledge sharing (KS) as a proximal learning behaviour and innovation culture (IC) as a deeper normative infrastructure, while psychological safety (PS) functions as a contextual resource that regulates how strongly these pathways operate. Survey data from 492 frontline employees in Indian hotels and resorts were analyzed using covariance‑based structural equation modeling (AMOS 29) and bootstrapped conditional process analysis (SPSS 29). The results indicated that TL is linked to SIP through its relationship with KS and IC, and KS emerged as the stronger conduit. Moreover, PS strengthens the direct TL–SIP link once a minimum safety threshold is reached and simultaneously attenuates the TL → KS → SIP and TL → IC → SIP pathways, potentially reducing employees’ dependence on leader-driven KS mechanisms while enabling the translation of leader-driven cultural norms into SIP. These findings extend existing leadership–innovation theory in hospitality by distinguishing behavioural and cultural routes from TL to SIP, which are most consequential for SIP when PS acts as a booster vs a contextual ceiling, offering actionable guidance on how hospitality practitioners can align leadership development, knowledge systems, and PS‑building practices to achieve sustained, perceptible innovation outcomes.
authors: Sekhar Pal; MK Rao

title: Transient and Immediate Motor Effects of Endurance Training in People With Multiple Sclerosis: The Exploratory TIME Study
abstract: Background: People with multiple sclerosis (MS) occasionally report deterioration of motor function after endurance training. Endurance training is recommended to help manage MS symptoms, but its immediate impact on functional mobility and spasticity is not well understood. Therefore, the aim of this exploratory pre/post analysis was to investigate the immediate effects of a single bout of endurance training on a bicycle ergometer on functional mobility and lower extremity spasticity in people with MS. Methods: Forty people with MS (21 men and 19 women; Expanded Disability Status Scale score ≤ 6.0) were randomly assigned to perform either a single bout of high-intensity interval training (HIIT) or moderate continuous training (MCT) on a bicycle ergometer. Functional mobility and spasticity were assessed using the Timed Up and Go (TUG), Numeric Rating Scale for Spasticity (NRS-S), and Modified Ashworth Scale (MAS) at 5 timepoints: before exercise, up to 5 minutes after exercise, at 60 minutes, 180 minutes, and 300 minutes after exercise. Results: = .01), were observed immediately after exercise in both groups. However, within 1 hour, TUG reverted to baseline, whereas NRS-S and MAS improved beyond baseline at 180 minutes post exercise. Conclusions: The findings of this study can be used to reassure patients that acute, exercise-related symptom worsening is short-lived and to inform them about the time course to performance and symptom recovery to baseline, or even beyond.

title: Treinamento de marcha assistido por robô em pacientes com encefalopatia crônica não progressiva da infância: revisão integrativa.
abstract: Introduction: Cerebral Palsy (CP), also referred to as Non-Progressive Chronic Encephalopathy of Childhood (ECNPI), presents different levels of motor and functional impairment, which may affect gait and gross motor function. Robot-assisted gait training (RAGT) uses devices that assist lower-limb movements, providing repetitive and controlled stimuli during gait. Objective: The objective of this study was to evaluate the effects of the use of robot-assisted gait training on the motor function of patients with CP. Materials and methods: This is an integrative review, guided by the PICO strategy, considering patients with CP, RAGT as the intervention, other therapeutic interventions as the comparison, and gross motor function and gait-related aspects as outcomes. The search was conducted in the PubMed, PEDro, Virtual Health Library (VHL), and CAPES Journals databases, using descriptors and keywords related to cerebral palsy, gait training, and robotics. Articles published within the last 5 years, in English, Portuguese, and Spanish, were considered. Initially, 1,068 articles were identified, of which 1,050 were excluded after screening according to the established criteria. At the end, 20 articles were included in the review, distributed among PubMed (n = 14), PEDro (n = 1), VHL (n = 3), and CAPES (n = 2). Results: The results allowed the analysis of the effects of RAGT on gross motor function, gait capacity, and gait parameters in patients with CP. Conclusion: The studies demonstrated that RAGT has beneficial effects on some aspects of gross motor function in children with CP. Robotic gait training represents a therapeutic alternative with the potential to complement conventional physical therapy; however, more consistent evidence is still needed to determine its effects in this population.

title: Unveiling the Antecedents of Technology‐Organization‐Environment on Low Carbon Performance: A Comparative Analysis of Emission‐Controlled and Non‐Emission‐Controlled Firms
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines firm low‐carbon performance (FLCP) by integrating the Technology–Organization–Environment (TOE) framework with the Natural Resource‐Based View, Dynamic Capabilities Theory, and Institutional Theory. Using survey data from 318 managers in Chinese firms and partial least squares structural equation modeling, it examines direct and indirect associations between TOE drivers and FLCP, plus supplementary multi‐group analysis (MGA) based on regulatory exposure and managerial awareness. Results reveal positive associations of technological competence, top management support (TMS), government support, and regulatory factors with FLCP. Financial benefits relate to FLCP indirectly through TMS, whereas government support relates directly and indirectly through TMS. The MGA results indicate that regulatory factors are stronger for firms aware of their emission‐control status, government support is stronger for unaware firms, and corporate social responsibility relates more strongly to FLCP among emission‐controlled firms. The study clarifies capability‐based TOE mechanisms and the institutional context of emerging‐economy carbon trading.

title: Unveiling the potential of needle knife therapy for post-stroke spastic hemiparesis: a comprehensive systematic review and meta-analysis protocol
abstract: Introduction Post-stroke spastic hemiparesis is a common and disabling complication after stroke. It is associated with impaired motor function and activity limitation, and it places a substantial long-term burden on patients, families and health services. Needle knife, also known as acupotomy, is a minimally invasive technique that uses a blade-tipped needle and is widely used in China; it is intended to release soft-tissue adhesions and reduce abnormal muscle tone, with the aim of improving limb function. However, the effectiveness and safety of needle knife for post-stroke spastic hemiparesis have not been systematically evaluated. This protocol describes the methods for a systematic review and meta-analysis that will assess the efficacy and safety of needle knife treatment for post-stroke spastic hemiparesis. Methods and analysis The following electronic databases will be searched from inception to 1 August 2026: CINAHL, MEDLINE, Embase, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, the Allied and Complementary Medicine Database, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, Chinese Biomedical Literature Database, VIP Database and Wanfang Database. Randomised controlled trials evaluating needle knife alone or needle knife combined with routine rehabilitation for post-stroke spastic hemiparesis will be included. The primary outcomes will be spasticity measured by the Modified Ashworth Scale and the Clinical Spasticity Index. Secondary outcomes will include motor function measured by the Fugl-Meyer Assessment, muscle strength measured by Manual Muscle Testing, activities of daily living, quality of life and adverse events. Two reviewers will independently screen records, extract data and assess risk of bias using the Cochrane risk-of-bias tool. Review Manager V.5.4 or later will be used for data synthesis. Risk ratios with 95% CIs will be calculated for dichotomous outcomes. Mean differences or standardised mean differences with 95% CIs will be calculated for continuous outcomes. Heterogeneity will be assessed using the χ2 test and I2 statistic. When meta-analysis is not appropriate, a structured narrative synthesis will be performed. The certainty of evidence will be evaluated using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation approach. Trial registration number CRD42023464211.

title: Upper-Limb Robotic Exoskeletons for Neuromuscular Rehabilitation: A Systematic Review on Lightweight Architectures and Bio-Cooperative Control
abstract: Stroke and neuromuscular trauma constitute a leading global cause of severe long-term upper-limb motor disability. Although rehabilitation robotics has proven effective in inducing activity-dependent cortical neuroplasticity through high-intensity training, a significant translational gap persists between complex laboratory prototypes and commercially accessible home-based systems. To address this, a systematic review was conducted following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, analyzing 45 studies from high-impact databases (2016–2026) focused on mechatronic design and clinical validations. The findings reveal a critical transition from rigid-link anthropomorphic exoskeletons toward cable-driven and soft robotic architectures, successfully reducing arm-coupled inertia to under 1.5 kg and mitigating kinematic misalignment risks at the human-robot interface. However, a severe validation gap persists, with less than 10% of studies evaluating prototypes on actual post-stroke cohorts. Additionally, the high computational cost and noise susceptibility of advanced sEMG-driven Assist-as-Needed (AAN) controllers currently limit their viability for autonomous home use. The review concludes that democratizing robotic telerehabilitation requires prioritizing intrinsic mechanical compliance, affordability, and IoT telemetry over redundant structural complexity, alongside an urgent shift toward multicenter Randomized Controlled Trials (RCTs). Aunque la robótica de rehabilitación ha demostrado ser eficaz para inducir neuroplasticidad cortical dependiente de la actividad mediante entrenamiento de alta intensidad, persiste una importante brecha traslacional entre los complejos prototipos de laboratorio y los sistemas de uso domiciliario comercialmente accesibles. Para abordar esta problemática, se realizó una revisión sistemática siguiendo las directrices PRISMA 2020, en la que se analizaron 45 estudios procedentes de bases de datos de alto impacto (2016–2026), centrados en el diseño mecatrónico y las validaciones clínicas. Los hallazgos revelan una transición significativa desde los exoesqueletos antropomórficos de eslabones rígidos hacia arquitecturas robóticas accionadas por cables y estructuras blandas, que han logrado reducir la inercia acoplada al brazo a menos de 1,5 kg y mitigar los riesgos de desalineación cinemática en la interfaz humano-robot. Sin embargo, persiste una importante brecha de validación, ya que menos del 10 % de los estudios evaluaron los prototipos en cohortes reales de pacientes que habían sufrido un accidente cerebrovascular. Además, el elevado coste computacional y la susceptibilidad al ruido de los controladores avanzados de asistencia según necesidad (Assist-as-Needed, AAN) basados en sEMG limitan actualmente su viabilidad para un uso domiciliario autónomo. La revisión concluye que la democratización de la telerehabilitación robótica requiere priorizar la conformidad mecánica intrínseca, la asequibilidad y la telemetría mediante Internet de las Cosas (IoT) frente a una complejidad estructural redundante, junto con una transición urgente hacia ensayos controlados aleatorizados (RCT) multicéntricos. title: Validez y fiabilidad de la Escala del Escritor Frustrado en la educación superior
abstract: La frustración en la escritura académica se identifica como una experiencia en estudiantes de educación superior, asociada a exigencias institucionales, dificultades lingüísticas y procesos formativos. El objetivo del estudio fue diseñar y obtener evidencias de validez y fiabilidad de la Escala del Escritor Frustrado en estudiantes universitarios. Se realizó una investigación instrumental con una muestra no probabilística de 243 estudiantes de educación superior con una media general de edad de 20.87 años, 83.13% fueron mujeres, 15.24% hombres, 0.82% no binario y 0.82% prefirió no decirlo. La versión inicial del instrumento fue sometida a una evaluación de evidencias de validez de contenido mediante juicio de expertos y, posteriormente, a un análisis de componentes principales (ACP) con rotación oblicua Robust Promin. Asimismo, se evaluó la adecuación muestral mediante el índice Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin (KMO) y la prueba de esfericidad de Bartlett, y se estimó la consistencia interna mediante el coeficiente omega de McDonald. La estructura final quedó integrada por 22 ítems agrupados en tres componentes determinados mediante análisis paralelo. La adecuación muestral fue satisfactoria (KMO = .888; prueba de esfericidad de Bartlett = 2098.1, p < .001). Los componentes explicaron el 48.3% de la varianza acumulada. La escala presentó un coeficiente omega de McDonald de .901, mientras que los tres componentes mostraron valores entre .807 y .826. Se concluyó que la Escala del Escritor Frustrado presentó evidencias preliminares de validez de contenido y estructura interna, así como de fiabilidad para evaluar experiencias de frustración asociadas con la escritura académica en educación superior, con utilidad potencial para el estudio de la dimensión emocional de la escritura académica.

title: Varying Lateral Extra-articular Tenodesis Femoral Fixation Points and Fixation Flexion Angles Do Not Affect ACL Graft Force and Tibiofemoral Motion After ACL Reconstruction.
abstract:
Background

The addition of lateral extra-articular tenodesis (LET) to anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) reconstruction (ACLR) has been shown to reduce rotational laxity and improve graft survivorship. Despite the increased utilization of LET with ACLR, there remains a lack of consensus on the ideal location of the femoral attachment site of LET.

Purpose

To compare ACL graft force and tibiofemoral motion in cadaveric specimens undergoing ACLR with the addition of LET at varying fixation angles and fixation points.

Study design

Controlled laboratory study.

Methods

A total of 10 fresh-frozen cadaveric knees were tested in 6 conditions, including LET fixation at 2 anatomic locations. Location 1 was defined as 8 mm proximal and 4 to 5 mm posterior to the lateral femoral epicondyle, at the insertion of the anterolateral ligament. Location 2 was defined as 31 mm proximal to the lateral femoral epicondyle, at the insertion of the distal Kaplan fibers. The testing conditions were as follows: (1) native; (2) ACLR; (3) ACLR + LET at location 1, fixed at 30°; (4) ACLR + LET at location 2, fixed at 30°; (5) ACLR + LET at location 1, fixed at 60°; and (6) ACLR + LET at location 2, fixed at 60°. Specimens were mounted on a 6 degrees of freedom robotic system to assess tibial internal rotation and anterior tibial translation at 0°, 30°, 60°, and 90° of knee flexion. A load cell was utilized to assess ACL graft force.

Results

There were no differences between the 4 LET states in any outcome. In internal rotation, the addition of LET demonstrated reductions in ACL graft force in all 4 configurations, ranging from -14.9 N (14%) to -19.5 N (20%) at 0°, -19.7 N (51%) to -21.4 N (55%) at 30°, and -3.9 N (30%) to -4.6 N (35%) at 60° (all P < .05). The addition of LET also demonstrated reductions in internal rotation range of motion in all 4 configurations, ranging from -1.86° (15%) to -2.45° (19%) at 0°, -4.87° (18%) to -5.75° (20%) at 30°, and -4.70° (19%) to -5.92° (23%) at 60° (all P < .05).

Conclusion

Variations in LET fixation location and fixation flexion angle did not alter its effect on ACL graft force reduction or tibiofemoral motion in the cadaveric knee. The addition of LET had a protective effect on the ACL graft in internal rotation while demonstrating overconstraint compared to the native knee.

Clinical relevance

The findings suggest that surgeons may have flexibility in selecting the femoral fixation location and knee flexion angle for LET without substantially altering its biomechanical effect on ACL graft loading or tibiofemoral kinematics. However, because LET reduced internal rotation beyond the native state, care should be taken to avoid excessive constraint when performing the procedure.
authors: Kruckeberg BM, Brady AW, Cinque ME, Sidrak JP, Kanakamedala AC, Hackett TR, Vidal AF, Godin JA.

title: Vibrotactile Stimuli For Functional Rehabilitation In Neurological Individuals
abstract: Background: Neurological disorders such as Spinal Cord Injury (SCI), Cerebral Palsy (CP), and stroke pose significant challenges to sensorimotor function in affected individuals, with traditional therapies often yielding incomplete recovery. This thesis investigates Focal Muscle Vibration (FMV) as a non-invasive intervention to enhance motor and sensory rehabilitation in neurological diseases, addressing gaps in mechanistic understanding, functional performance and clinical efficacy. Objective: The overarching aim of this thesis is to investigate FMV's role in sensorimotor rehabilitation by understanding its neurophysiological impacts following its use as an exercise intervention in people suffering from neurological diseases. Three specific research objectives were pursued: Objective 1 (OB1) — Device Engineering: To engineer a wearable FMV device capable of delivering precise and reproducible vibrations suitable for neuromuscular and sensory rehabilitation. Objective 2 (OB2) — Neurophysiological Effects: To investigate the specific effects of prolonged FMV exposure on motor function, spasticity, and brain activity in individuals with SCI and CP, and how these effects vary with different vibration frequencies. Objective 3 (OB3) — Device Feasibility: To evaluate the feasibility, usability, and short-term clinical effects of a co-designed wearable FMV device on spasticity and upper limb function in stroke survivors. Methods: An FMV device was developed using ERM vibration motor and characterized for frequency output using accelerometers. An electronic circuitry using was designed to operate the device at the desired frequencies (60-120 Hz) after the frequency characterization. This device was then used for the experimental studies. Experimental evaluations included three cohort studies investigating the neurophysiological impacts and usability of the FMV device in CP, SCI and stroke cohorts as detailed below: CP: Effects of 8 weeks of FMV applied to quadriceps at 80 Hz and 100 Hz was assessed via EEG and EMG in a cohort of 65 CP children. Resting-state functional connectivity (FC) and movement related cortical potentials (MRCPs) were used to see the cortical impacts of FMV through the EEG assessments. Muscle activations, fatigue and co-contraction metrics were assessed through EMG assessments. SCI: Three weeks of FMV to the Achilles tendon was delivered to 10 SCI patients, and their EEG FC was investigated. Stroke: An FMV device usability study in stroke (n= 12) was also conducted using a specifically modified commercial FMV device, with a view to establish for its potential for translation from laboratory to home-based use. Patient feedback was collected to update the original device design. After the updated device design, a single 30-minute dose of FMV was delivered to the arms, and clinical assessments of Fugl-Meyer Upper Extremity (FMUE) and modified Ashworth scores (MAS) were conducted. Results: OB1 — Fully Met: A wearable FMV device was designed and developed, delivering vibration frequencies at four levels (60, 80, 100 and 120 Hz) with a mean accuracy of 96.83%. The device was wearable, lightweight (65 g), and low-cost (under £100), meeting all pre-specified engineering requirements. OB2 — Fully Met (CP); Partially Met (SCI): In CP, FMV demonstrated frequency-dependent enhancements in beta-band functional connectivity, reduced movement-related cortical potentials, improved muscle activation, and delayed fatigue, with 100 Hz yielding superior motor outcomes. In SCI, significant alpha- and beta-band EEG connectivity changes in central-parietal regions were observed, suggesting neuroplasticity; however, clinical spasticity reductions were modest and the sample size (n = 10) precluded definitive conclusions, making this objective partially met for the SCI cohort. OB3 — Partially Met: The co-designed device was found to be comfortable and easy to use by stroke patients and clinicians. A single session of FMV produced improvements in FMUE scores but no significant changes in spasticity (MAS). Given the feasibility-study design with a small cohort (n = 12) and a single-session protocol, the clinical effectiveness component of OB3 is considered partially met, warranting further investigation in powered randomised trials. Conclusion: Findings support FMV's role in modulating cortical and neuromuscular pathways, with implications for personalised, accessible rehabilitation. OB1 was fully met through the development of a characterised, wearable, low-cost FMV device. OB2 was fully met for the CP cohort, demonstrating cortical and neuromuscular benefits, while SCI findings remain promising but preliminary, partially meeting OB2 for that population. OB3 was partially met, confirming device usability and short-term upper limb gains in stroke, with further powered trials needed to confirm clinical efficacy. Limitations include small samples and short follow-up periods, warranting larger trials. This work advances wearable FMV therapy toward evidence-based practice, bridging engineering innovation and clinical application for improved neurological outcomes.

title: When Agent Memory Needs to Compute: Evidence Access and Executable Aggregation
abstract: Questions about an agent's history often require aggregating events, which retrieval alone does not resolve. We combine source-preserving evidence access with executable aggregation. Trajectory Memory (TM) retains the original trajectory and constructs a source-addressable reading view at question time. TallyMem augments it with a reusable event ledger, model-generated event specifications and deterministic execution. With a commit-specific adaptation on 776 questions from 99 held-out MINTEval repositories, TallyMem raises Qwen3-32B exact match from 35.2% to 49.0%, a 13.8-point gain over TM; gains span 12.8-13.9 points across three readers. A controlled probe with event sets parsed independently from raw logs shows an 11.0-point gain, from 82.8% to 93.8%, without routing. On full AMA-Bench, the routed system yields a smaller 1.3-point gain, from 69.8% to 71.1%. These results support executable aggregation on tasks that require combining events, with benefits dependent on the task and event specification, the largest residual system-error category in our diagnostic analysis.

title: When humans and agents form a collective: a framework for collective intelligence in persistent organizational human-AI teams
abstract: Artificial systems increasingly participate in organizational work as recurrent contributors to interdependent activity, yet research remains fragmented across system capabilities, individual responses, episodic interactions, and constructs derived from human-only teams. This article develops Organismic Human-Artificial Intelligence (OHAI) as a bounded integrative theoretical framework for studying collective intelligence in persistent organizational human-AI teams. Its focal unit is a bounded collective of distinguishable human and artificial contributors whose interdependent activity extends across successive cycles and whose prior collective activity can affect later artificial participation. The framework distinguishes system configuration, collective functioning, and collective intelligence (CI) as analytical objects, with CI as its primary theoretical target. CI denotes a general group-level capacity manifested across diverse tasks within a specified and empirically qualified task universe. Task performances may provide indicators for estimating CI or serve as external criteria, while the framework separately examines broader employee, team, and organizational consequences, including changes in human working relationships and employee wellbeing. Its central inferential rule is that a property implemented in an artificial component does not by itself establish a corresponding team-level phenomenon. Collective functioning must instead be demonstrated in the enacted organization and use of distributed contributions. Partner modeling, transactive-memory-system-related coordination, and shared-mental-model-related representational alignment provide selective lenses on such functioning. Persistence makes collective history consequential, bringing recursive updating, overlapping timescales, reconfiguration, and collective-intelligence trajectories into view without presuming adaptation or improvement. Human-only teams serve as secondary epistemic references for bounded tests of observable-pattern and functional correspondence, while relational-pattern correspondence remains a limited future methodological possibility. The empirical program distinguishes four nonmandatory stages of research maturity: configuration and measurement qualification, local relations, longitudinal team-level phenomena, and integrated multilevel studies. The framework thereby provides a disciplined basis for cumulative research on how heterogeneous contributions become collectively consequential and change over time.

title: Транскраниальная магнитная стимуляция в сочетании с когнитивной провокацией и интегративной психотерапией улучшает отказ от курения
abstract: Введение. Применение транскраниальной магнитной стимуляции (рТМС) с предварительной когнитивной провокацией в сочетании с интегративной психотерапией формируют надежную стратегию совладания у лиц с синдромом табачной зависимости. Цель. Повысить эффективность лечения лиц с синдромом зависимости от табака путем комплексного воздействия на физический и психологический компоненты патологического влечения. Материалы и методы. В основную группу вошли 60 респондентов с диагнозом по МКБ 10: F 17.2 – синдром зависимости от табака, мужского и женского пола, в возрасте 18–44 года, проходивших курс комплексного лечения с применением высокочастотной рТМС на левую дорсолатеральную префронтальную кору и медиальную префронтальную кору с предварительной когнитивной провокацией в сочетании с интегративной психотерапией. Результаты. Метод лечения лиц с синдромом зависимости от табака, с использованием транскраниальной магнитной стимуляции и интегративной психотерапии прошли 60 человек. Средний возраст составил 32,5±12,3 года. Процедуры транскраниальной магнитной стимуляции проводились с частотой до 2 раз в неделю: от 5 до 9 процедур прошли 78% человек, 10 процедур 16% человек, остальные 2% до 3 процедур и 4% до 15 сеансов. Сеансы интегративной психотерапии в индивидуальном формате проводились с частотой до 2 раз в неделю прошли 60 человек: от 5 до 9 процедур прошли 53% человек, 10 процедур 45% человек, и 3% до 12 сеансов. Полностью прекратили употребление табака 48 (76%) человека, остальные 16 (24%) человек находились в состоянии контролируемого приема и готовности к отказу. Отмечено снижение тревожности после курса лечения: ситуативной тревожности (с 51,5±12,3 до 40,7±10,0 баллов, p<0,001), личностной тревожности (с 50,4±14,2 до 45,9±10,0 баллов, p=0,021), усиление внутреннего локуса контроля в сферах достижений, неудач и профессиональной деятельности, развитие адаптивных копинг-стратегий (принятие ответственности и планирование), уменьшение отрицания проблемы и повышение готовности к активным действиям по отказу от курения. Заключение. Нормализация уровня тревожности после проведения транскраниальной магнитной стимуляции и интегративной психотерапии зависимых от табака лиц подтверждает снижение эмоционального дистресса и ослабление одного из основных триггеров курения – стресс-индуцированной тяги, повышение стрессоустойчивости и способности к саморегуляции в провоцирующих курение ситуациях. Активация схемы зависимости путем когнитивной провокации делает ее более поддающейся модуляции, где рТМС может открыть «окно пластичности», и поведенческое вмешательство интегративной психотерапии может быть более эффективным. Полученные данные демонстрируют высокую клиническую эффективность разработанного метода лечения, основанного на использовании интегративной психотерапии и транскраниальной магнитной стимуляции у зависимых от табака лиц. Introduction. The use of transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) with preliminary cognitive provocation in combination with integrative psychotherapy forms a reliable coping strategy in individuals with tobacco dependence syndrome. Purpose. To improve the effectiveness of treatment for individuals with tobacco dependence syndrome through a comprehensive approach to the physical and psychological components of pathological craving. Materials and methods. The study group included 60 respondents with an ICD-10 diagnosis of F17.2 – tobacco dependence syndrome, male and female, aged 18–44 years, who underwent a course of comprehensive treatment using high-frequency rTMS to the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex and medial prefrontal cortex with preliminary cognitive provocation in combination with integrative psychotherapy. Results. A total of 60 people underwent a treatment method for tobacco dependence syndrome using transcranial magnetic stimulation and integrative psychotherapy. The average age was 32.5±12.3 years. Transcranial magnetic stimulation procedures were performed up to twice a week: 78% of people underwent 5 to 9 procedures, 16% of people underwent 10 procedures, the remaining 2% up to 3 procedures, and 4% up to 15 sessions. 60 people underwent individual integrative psychotherapy sessions up to twice a week: 53% of people underwent 5 to 9 procedures, 45% of people underwent 10 procedures, and 3% up to 12 sessions. 48 (76%) people completely quit smoking, the remaining 16 (24%) people were in a state of controlled use and readiness to quit. A decrease in anxiety was noted after the course of treatment: situational anxiety (from 51.5±12.3 to 40.7±10.0 points, p<0.001), personal anxiety (from 50.4±14.2 to 45.9±10.0 points, p=0.021), strengthening of the internal locus of control in the areas of achievements, failures and professional activity, development of adaptive coping strategies (acceptance of responsibility and planning), reduction of denial of the problem and increased readiness for active steps to quit smoking. Conclusion. The obtained data demonstrate the high clinical efficacy of the developed treatment method based on the use of integrative psychotherapy and transcranial magnetic stimulation in persons with tobacco dependence.

title: A Passive AI System for Verifying Physical State on Automated Liquid Handlers
abstract: Automated liquid handlers execute digital protocols, but operators must assemble the deck and confirm that the physical setup matches the intended experiment. We present the Labware Setup Checker, a passive vision system that verifies deck preparation on an Opentrons Flex without modifying its hardware or firmware. A consumer webcam mounted outside the robot supplies images to a browser application. The checker segments the deck into slots, corrects slot assignments using the known deck geometry, classifies the labware, and compares the observed setup with a reference protocol library to report missing, misplaced, or unexpected labware. It operates independently of the robot controller and does not interrupt or gate a run. During SwabSeq Respiratory Viral Panel (RVP) pre-PCR deck preparation, the checker tracked a slot from empty to a base and then to the completed plate-and-base assembly, identifying the completed assembly in all 29 frames before robot motion. Across these frames, 95.1% of the 348 labware classifications for slots requiring exact matches agreed with the protocol reference. In 480 frames with partially occluded reservoirs, all 6,720 slot assignments were correct. Across three camera positions and two lighting conditions, slot assignment was 100% correct, and 97.73% of labware classifications matched the protocol reference. Median verification time was 2.10 s on a laptop using only its CPU and 4.24 s from frame capture to receipt of results during AWS deployment in the laboratory. These results show that an external camera and independent software can provide verification of deck setup against protocol requirements within seconds, allowing operators to review the physical setup before starting a run.

title: A fully-automated high-throughput DNA extraction protocol for human microbiome samples
abstract: Abstract Microbial DNA extraction is a critical step in metagenomic analyses and a major source of technical bias. With the rapidly increasing demand for large-scale metagenomic studies, there is a growing need for robust and high-throughput DNA extraction workflows. Here, we developed a fully automated microbial DNA extraction pipeline inspired by the International Human Microbiome Standards (IHMS) integrating liquid-handling robots, automated sample management, and a dedicated data-handling suite. This pipeline, named “epsilon”, enables the processing of up to ten times more samples compared to the standard, with a throughput capacity of approximately 30,000 samples per year with two technicians. To assess the impact of automation, we applied this pipeline to 11 fecal samples and compared its performance to the corresponding semi-automated protocol. No significant differences were observed in DNA yield or overall quality. In conclusion, we present a fully automated microbial DNA extraction pipeline that substantially increases throughput and reduces both costs and carbon footprint, while preserving DNA quality and compatibility with international standards. This workflow provides a reliable reference for large-scale microbiome studies and represents a step toward a modern, high-throughput DNA-extraction standard for both academic and industrial settings.

title: A large audit of Cobas CT/NG screening and Xpert CT/NG supplemental testing reveals low confirmatory rates in oropharyngeal samples with evidence of commensal cross-reactivity with an isolate of <i>Neisseria lactamica</i>.
abstract: Sensitive and high-throughput testing for Neisseria gonorrhoeae (NG) is widely underpinned by automated commercial solutions using nucleic acid amplification tests. We outline our experience of using Roche Cobas 8800 CT/NG (Cobas NG) for primary testing of NG at scale. Over 360000 specimens were tested over a three-year period. A disproportionate number of 'indeterminate' oropharyngeal swabs (25%) tested positive by Cobas NG but failed to confirm by Xpert CT/NG, significantly higher than genital samples (4%) (chi-square p-value <0.05). Such samples are highly problematic, as they fail to provide a definitive result for the patient. To investigate this non-specificity, publicly available sequences for Cobas NG DR-9 targets were aligned with Neisseria genome databases. We found a strain of Neisseria lactamica (PubMLST 49718), isolated from a throat swab, which was predicted to cross-react with Cobas NG. We subsequently confirmed a Cobas NG false-positive result with this isolate. BLAST analysis showed the target gene NG DR-9 was rare among available non-NG Neisseria whole genome sequences. This may suggest the existence of an as-yet unknown and difficult to cultivate oral commensal that contains NG DR-9. Our findings further highlight the need for NG confirmatory testing of oropharyngeal samples screened with Cobas NG.
authors: McEwan A, Lucidarme J, Whitfield T, Buttery R, Tilston P, Machin N, Guiver M.

title: A mosaic RBD-nanoparticle pan-sarbecovirus vaccine elicits nanobodies that target highly conserved epitopes
abstract: SARS-CoV-2, the virus that causes COVID-19, continually mutates, producing new variants of concern (VOCs). Substitutions in the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein receptor-binding domain (RBD) have resulted in reduced efficacies of vaccines and therapeutic monoclonal antibodies. Indeed, since the emergence of Omicron and earlier VOCs, most previously approved anti-RBD therapeutic monoclonal antibodies are no longer authorized as therapeutics. To address VOC substitutions effects on therapeutic antibody efficacy, we sought to identify single-domain nanobodies (VHHs) targeting RBD regions (class 4, class 1/4, portions of class 3 and class 5 RBD epitopes) that are more conserved across VOCs, reasoning that the smaller size of camelid nanobodies compared with conventional two-domain antibody combining sites would facilitate access to occluded RBD epitopes. We used a Beacon optofluidic platform to isolate and characterize single memory B cells from a llama immunized with a mosaic RBD-nanoparticle immunogen that elicits broad antibody responses across sarbecoviruses. Using multiplex binding assays, we identified nanobodies that bind to spike RBDs from diverse sarbecovirus strains. Competition ELISAs and crystal structures of VHH-RBD complexes showed that isolated nanobodies recognize broadly conserved epitopes, including those on the RBD that are inaccessible to analogous conventional two-domain antibodies. Promising VHH-Fcs neutralized SARS-CoV-2 variants of concern and zoonotic sarbecoviruses, demonstrating potential therapeutic utility for current and future outbreaks.
