title: Comparative diagnostic performance of robotic, electromagnetic navigation, and fluoroscopy bronchoscopy for lung cancer in peripheral pulmonary lesions: a prospective, multicenter, parallel-controlled trial.
abstract:
Introduction

Peripheral pulmonary lesions (PPLs) are difficult to access bronchoscopically due to their distal location. Although robotic, electromagnetic navigation, and fluoroscopy-guided systems have been developed, inconsistent study designs have limited direct comparison of their diagnostic performance.

Objectives

This study aimed to compare the diagnostic performance and lesion-specific advantages of robotic bronchoscopy system (RBS), electromagnetic navigation bronchoscopy(ENB), and fluoroscopy bronchoscopy(FB) for PPLs.

Methods

In this multicenter, prospective, parallel-controlled trial, consecutive patients with suspected PPLs from 7 centers were assigned to the RBS, ENB or FB groups according to a predefined cyclic sequence for biopsy between 2019 and 2023. Subgroup analyses of diagnostic yield were performed according to lesion characteristics. Machine-learning models and a web-based platform were developed for clinical evaluation.

Results

A total of 270 patients were included, with 90 patients in each group. RBS achieved a higher overall diagnostic yield than ENB and FB (87.8%, 83.3% and 63.3%, respectively; P < 0.001). Strict diagnostic yield was also highest in the RBS group (81.1% vs 61.1% and 47.8%; P < 0.001). In the subgroup analysis, RBS performed better for 15-30 mm lesions and lesions within 15 mm of the pleura (P < 0.005), whereas ENB showed a diagnostic yield comparable to RBS for malignant, larger and solid lesions. Navigation and biopsy success rates in the RBS group were 100%, with more precise trajectories and lower displacement than the other two techniques (P < 0.001). Based on lesion characteristics, internally developed models (all AUC > 0.96) were integrated into a visualization platform to estimate the technique-specific diagnostic success for individualized PPLs.

Conclusion

This multicenter study demonstrates that RBS, ENB and FB have distinct diagnostic advantages across different PPL subgroups. RBS showed better diagnostic performance in selected challenging lesions, whereas ENB achieved comparable performance in malignant, solid, or larger lesions. The image-based prediction platforms may further support individualized selection of transbronchial navigation strategies for PPL or lung cancer diagnosis.
authors: Zhong C, Huang J, Xu L, You Z, Wang F, Sun J, Jiang J, Liu D, Huang J, Zhang H, Li H, Li Z, He W, Lin Z, Zheng X, He L, Liu J, Chen D, Wang G, Li S.

title: Comparison of Procedural Safety and Diagnostic Yield Between Robotic-Assisted Bronchoscopy Platforms.
abstract: Robotic-assisted bronchoscopy platforms are becoming ubiquitous to aid in sampling peripheral pulmonary nodules. A head-to-head performance between the 2 widely available platforms (Ion and Monarch) has not been investigated. To explore differences in diagnostic yield and safety parameters of the Ion and Monarch platforms. A secondary objective was to elucidate radiographic features of nodules that predicted procedural success. A retrospective, 2-site cohort study of adult patients scheduled for robotic-assisted bronchoscopy of pulmonary nodules between August 2020 and August 2023. The procedure was performed with either the Ion or Monarch robotic-assisted bronchoscopy platform, depending on the site, with the assistance of standard 2D fluoroscopy. A series of logistic regression models was constructed to explore the effect of platform type on diagnostic yield, after correction of prespecified confounders. We utilized an inferential lasso regression model to explore the predictive properties of nodule radiographic characteristics on yield. A total of 217 cases were analyzed. The median nodule size was 1.4 cm (IQR=1.1 to 2.1), which was similar across both groups. Our parsimonious model suggested no difference in obtaining a positive diagnosis for the Ion platform [OR: 1.5 (0.9-2.7)]. Both nodule size [OR: 1.42 (1.09-1.86)] and presence of a bronchus sign [OR: 2.14 (1.14-4.01)] correlated with diagnostic yield in our inferential model, both in systems and in aggregate. Both platforms offer promise in sampling small peripheral nodules. Neither platform appears to improve procedural yield, although caution is advised regarding the generalizability of this finding. Both nodule size and the presence of the bronchus sign may be helpful in preprocedural patient selection.
authors: Peter C Nauka; S Mehdi Nouraie; John Tepper; Paul Yacono; Matthew Vercauteren; Matthew Schuchert; Rajeev Dhupar; Daniel G Dunlap; Roy Semaan

title: Cotton‐Swab‐Anchored Suspension Technique for Hands‐Free Lower Extremity Limb Sterilization During Surgical Preparation
abstract: Manual limb suspension during surgical preparation is labor-intensive, requires additional personnel, and may increase the risk of musculoskeletal injuries among surgical staff. We describe a cotton-swab-anchored suspension technique that uses a sterile bandage (Kerlix) looped around the ankle, secured with 2 cotton swabs inserted into the knot, and suspended from a heavy-duty intravenous pole. This method enables hands-free limb elevation, allowing efficient preoperative preparation. After completion of preparation, the limb is released by simply removing the cotton swab. This technique eliminates the need for manual limb holding, reduces occupational strain, provides stable mechanical support, and enables quick, controlled limb release without instruments. It is cost-effective, reproducible, and suitable for various lower extremity procedures.
authors: Chen Zhou; 狐周周; Lather Sagar; Shengwu Yang; Zhenhan Deng

title: DNA metabarcoding samples from nest soil and beaks outperform samples from talons and faeces when identifying diversity of white-tailed eagle diet in South Greenland
abstract: Abstract DNA metabarcoding is an emerging approach to study diets across a broad range of species but requires careful optimisation of the sample collection method and substrate used. The suitability of different sample types to identify the diet of the target species remains under investigated. Here, we address these knowledge gaps by collecting four different sample types - faeces, beak swabs, talon swabs, and soil samples - during nest visits of white-tailed eagles ( Haliaeetus albicilla ) during the 2025 breeding season in South Greenland. We further investigated whether some eagle dietary taxa could act as vectors for microplastic pollution. Our analyses revealed a broad diet, with 25 dietary taxa for white-tailed eagles. Lumpfish ( Cyclopterus lumpus ) was the most frequently detected dietary taxon in the diet, which was composed of 75 % fish, 19 % birds, and 7 % mammals. Our findings indicate that diets varied strongly between nesting sites. Although each sample type was efficient in capturing diet, soil and beak swabs were most promising for eagles and gave comparable results. On the other hand, faeces provided a distinct dietary profile with a reduced detection of fish, while requiring an increased sample size, and talon swabs missed rare food items. Finally, we recovered microplastic contamination in 33 % of our samples, but no dietary taxon was associated with microplastic pollution. Taken together our results underline the overlooked value of soil from nests to provide dietary information and highlight the necessity to deepen our knowledge of Arctic food webs and their microplastic contamination.
authors: Mael Perroud; Kay Lucek; Knud Falk; Nicholas Per Huffeldt

title: Design and Development of a Smart HVAC Duct Cleaning Robot Incorporating Real-Time Vision Monitoring and UVGI-Based Microbial Control
abstract: Indoor air quality within HVAC systems significantly influences occupant health, thermal comfort, and energy efficiency. Over time, air ducts accumulate dust, debris, allergens, and microbial contaminants, leading to reduced airflow performance and increased health risks. This paper presents the design and development of an Autonomous Air Duct Cleaning Robot integrated with high-pressure water jet cleaning and Ultraviolet Germicidal Irradiation (UVGI) technology. The robotic system is equipped with a compact locomotion mechanism, ESP32-CAM for real-time monitoring, and a controlled rotary nozzle operating at high velocity for effective contaminant removal. Fluid dynamic principles validate the cleaning mechanism, achieving dust removal efficiencies exceeding 90% for fine particles. In addition to mechanical cleaning, the UVGI module operating at approximately 254 nm enables microbial inactivation within enclosed duct environments, enhancing biological safety. Experimental evaluation confirms stable navigation, reliable wireless communication, and sufficient battery endurance for sectional duct cleaning tasks. The integrated approach reduces human exposure to hazardous environments while improving HVAC efficiency and indoor air quality. The proposed system offers a cost-effective and scalable solution for modern duct maintenance applications.
authors: A. S. N. Husainy; Anish Vishwakarma; Shreyash Gurav; Sudarshan Jagtap; Samruddhi Gharage

title: Designing a Functional Social Robot for Blood Test Procedures in the Emergency Department: A Human-Centered Approach
abstract: Blood tests are a common initial procedure in the emergency department (ED) and are often experienced as highly stressful, particularly in acute care areas. Robots’ social capabilities may help address patients’ emotional needs, yet their integration into such a complex environment requires clear alignment with existing clinical workflows. We present a human-centered design process for a robotic platform intended to support blood test procedures in the acute care area of the ED. A need study indicated two central guidelines: practical assistance with blood test equipment and emotional support for patients and nurses. The informed iterative design process resulted in a robotic platform that provides a mobile work surface for blood test equipment, with a small robotic arm that performs social gestures intended to provide emotional support. An initial field-validation deployment of the robot across four blood test procedures suggested that patients and nurses perceived the robot as a positive assistant capable of supporting emotional needs. We highlight the potential of integrating social features into functional robots in challenging environments such as the acute care ED.

title: Detection of Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) in Black-Horned Capuchin Monkeys, Brazil
abstract: We carried out a viral surveillance study on 30 black-horned capuchin monkeys (Sapajus nigritus) in Rio Doce State Park, a protected area in the Brazilian Atlantic Forest. Samples were tested for orthopoxviruses, flaviviruses, coronaviruses, influenza viruses, and a wide range of other respiratory viruses using molecular and serological methods. RT-qPCR detected the respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) genome in oral swabs from two asymptomatic juvenile females sampled in an area with high human interaction. This finding indicates a possible exposure of an population to RSV, a contagious human pathogen, and highlights the importance of increased surveillance at the human-wildlife interface.

title: Detection of Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa among Diabetic Foot Ulcer Patients in Wasit Province
abstract: Diabetic foot ulcer infection is a severe clinical complication that is determined by neuropathy, vascular impairment, tissue injury and successful bacterial invasion. Diabetic foot infections are the most common complication affecting people with diabetes, and bacterial pathogens play a key role. In this study, 90 subjects including 35 patients with diabetic foot ulcer (DFU) as well as 35 diabetic patients without ulcers and 20 healthy controls were enrolled. Methods: Wound swabs from ulcer group were processed through conventional culture, selective media, VITEK 2 identification and PCR. Univariate analysis identified isolation of P. aeruginosa (17/35;48.6%) being the most frequent isolate followed by S.aureus (13/35;37.1%) while other bacteria represented only 14.3%. Molecular confirmation using 16S rRNA, nuc and oprL genes showed complete concordance with phenotypic identification. Identification probabilities of both species on the VITEK 2 were greater than 90%. P. aeruginosa and S. aureus are clinically significant in diabetic foot ulcers due to their persistence, biofilm-forming ability and antimicrobial resistance; study results highlight concurrent use of culture, automated identification and PCR for accurate diagnosis/management
authors: Zaman Sami Kareem; Alaa Ali Matrood

title: Detection of the pqsA Gene and Histological Changes Induced by Pseudomonas aeruginosa
abstract: Pseudomonas aeruginosa uses quorum-sensing systems to coordinate activities regulated by specific genes, such as metabolic and environmental responses. The pqsA gene is a key component of the pqs pathway (quinolone signaling in Pseudomonas aeruginosa).This study focused on applying a mouse model to some local isolates of P. aeruginosa and identifying those carrying the pqsA gene. The study included isolating 150 samples for analysis, which resulted in confirmation of the presence of 58 isolates of P.aeruginosa. The specimens including wound swabs, burn samples, urine samples, middle ear swabs, and sputum were collected from different hospitals. The presence of the pqsA gene was confirmed molecularly using polymerase chain reaction (PCR) on 19 selected isolates, all of which showed positive amplification (448 bp). The experimental mouse model consisted of Swiss albino mice, divided into a control group and two treatment groups with low (1×10⁴ CFU) and high (1×10⁸ CFU) concentration of bacteria. We evaluated body weight before and after exposure and also performed histological examinations of the liver and lung tissue. The results showed that increased bacterial concentrations led to increased weight loss and extensive histological changes. In contrast, low concentrations produced only minor tissue changes. Statistical analysis (results are presented as means ± SE calculated using one-way ANOVA) confirmed these findings as statistically significant (p ≤ 0.05). Based on the above information, it can be concluded that the pqsA gene is highly conserved in local isolates of P. aeruginosa and that the presence of this gene leads to significant effects in host tissue in controlled in vivo studies. Therefore, this research contributes to understanding of the bacterial quorum sensing mechanism, the pathogenicity of bacterial species and their ability to interact with host bacteria in in vivo studies
authors: Zahraa Hasan Khaleefah; Enas Abdalhadi Hussain

title: Development, validation and clinical implementation of cellular swab materials for quality assurance of pharmacogenomic point-of-care testing
abstract: Abstract Background Pharmacogenomic point-of-care testing (PGx POCT) enables genotype-informed prescribing at the bedside, but implementation is limited by the lack of suitable reference materials for clinical verification and standardised external quality assessment (EQA). Methods Fixed lymphoblastoid cell lines were formulated as swab-based materials at defined cellular inputs for MT-RNR1 POCT. Materials were evaluated using Genedrive® assays, quantitative PCR, acceptance quality limit batch release, workflow-perturbation testing and stability studies, then deployed for clinical verification and in an international EQA programme. Results Materials were homogeneous, workflow compatible and reproducible, with 100% correct genotype calls at the lowest intended manufacturing cell load. Clinical verification of 11 Genedrive® systems across five neonatal units demonstrated 99% concordance with expected genotype classifications (232/234 results). Seven EQA surveys yielded 253 participant results, with full-mark rates of 87.5–100%, and six test failures. Most failures occurred with low cell-input materials near the assay limit of detection. The materials supported genotype concordance, performance monitoring and identification of workflow and sample-related variability. Conclusions Workflow-compatible cell-based reference materials combined with EQA provide a scalable framework for quality-assured PGx POCT beyond specialist laboratories. Clinical verification of Genedrive® systems within neonatal units using the cell-based swab materials, together with deployment of an International MT-RNR1 PGx POCT EQA programme, demonstrated their suitability for supporting both pre-implementation testing and ongoing quality assurance in decentralised healthcare settings. The framework may provide a model for the implementation, clinical verification and ongoing quality assessment of PGx POCT services. Further evaluation across platforms, analytes, settings and participant groups is required to establish broader applicability.
authors: Henry Thomas; John Henry McDermott; William G. Newman; Shaun Ainsworth; Gino Miele; Simon J. Patton; Rosa Morra

title: Diagnostic Performance and Safety Profile of Shape-Sensing Robotic-Assisted Bronchoscopy in Peripheral Pulmonary Lesions: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract:
Introduction

Shape-sensing robotic-assisted bronchoscopy (ssRAB) has emerged as a promising modality for diagnosing peripheral pulmonary lesions. This meta-analysis evaluated its diagnostic performance and safety profile.

Methods

PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Library were searched from inception to December 2025. Study quality was assessed using the Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies-3. Random-effects model was used to estimate the pooled diagnostic yield, sensitivity for malignancy, and complication, with rates (%) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) when the I2 index exceeded 50%. Cumulative meta-analysis was performed to assess the temporal stability and evidence saturation of the pooled diagnostic yield. Publication bias was evaluated using funnel plots and Egger's test.

Results

A total of 3,678 lesions from 18 studies were included. Notably, diagnostic yield varied significantly by outcome definition, with pooled diagnostic yield of 82.5% (95% CI: 78.3%-86.0%) under strict definition vs. 88.1% (95% CI: 82.8%-92.0%) under the intermediate definition (p = 0.036). The pooled sensitivity for malignancy of 90.0% (95% CI: 86.4%-92.8%). Cumulative meta-analysis showed stabilized diagnostic performance after approximately 1,500 lesions for the strict definition and 500 lesions for intermediate definition. Moreover, the safety profile was favorable, with pooled rates of pneumothorax of 1.8% (95% CI: 1.3%-2.3%), chest tube placement of 1.1% (95% CI: 0.7%-1.5%), and severe bleeding of 0.0% (95% CI: 0.0%-0.3%). Subgroup analyses showed consistent performance across study designs, region, and nodule characteristics. Diagnostic yield was significantly influenced by publication year and lesion size (p < 0.05).

Conclusion

ssRAB was associated with favorable, definition-dependent diagnostic yield (82.5%-88.1%) with exceptional safety, supporting ssRAB as an attractive first-line minimally invasive diagnostic option in appropriately selected patients, especially for small nodules (<2 cm) and patients at elevated procedural risk.
authors: Hu X, Wang L, Shi J, Fernandez-Bussy S, Liu D.

title: Diagnostic Yield and Molecular Testing Adequacy of Transbronchial Cryoprobe Biopsy Versus Needle Aspiration in Robotic Bronchoscopy.
abstract: In the AQuIRE trial, most cases (83.6%) did not involve transbronchial needle aspiration (TBNA), often underutilized due to challenges in accessing peripheral pulmonary lesions (PPLs). Advances in robotic bronchoscopy with shape-sensing technology (ssRAB) have mitigated these challenges, but the optimal number of needle and cryoprobe passes for reliable diagnosis remains undefined. This retrospective study compares the diagnostic yield (DY) of TBNA and transbronchial cryoprobe biopsy (TBCB) and their adequacy for molecular testing in PPLs. We performed a retrospective analysis of 166 patients who underwent ssRAB with both TBNA and TBCB from May to August 2024. Fisher exact tests and McNemar χ2 tests were used to compare prevalence differences in DY and molecular testing adequacy between discordant cases. Odds ratios (OR) and 95% CIs of associations between the number of passes and diagnostic yield and rates of obtaining adequate samples for molecular testing were obtained using generalized linear mixed models (GLMMs) with a logit link. TBCB demonstrated a higher diagnostic rate than TBNA (89% vs. 80%, OR=2.04, 95% CI=1.06-4.03; P=0.032), as well as better rates of obtaining samples adequate for molecular testing (60% vs. 20%, OR=5.94, 95% CI=2.31-16.38, P<0.001). TBCB provided diagnostic yields in 55% (χ2=9.33, P=0.002) of cases where TBNA failed to provide a diagnosis and was able to obtain adequate samples for molecular testing in 42% (χ2=15.06, P<0.001) of cases where TBNA was unable to. TBCB suggests a higher diagnostic yield and higher cellular adequacy for molecular testing compared with TBNA, underscoring its potential value as a reliable and versatile diagnostic tool in PPLs.
authors: Tariq Odeh; Vishwajit Hegde; Maggie Chen; Steven Haworth; Maykol Postigo

title: Diagnostic testing for pulmonary tuberculosis in low and middle-income countries: innovations to achieve universal access—a narrative review
abstract: Though rapid molecular diagnostics for tuberculosis (TB) have substantially improved diagnostic accuracy and turnaround times, implementation and impact has been constrained by cost, infrastructure requirements, and continued reliance on sputum. This review examines advances in diagnostic technologies and sampling strategies that could overcome these barriers and accelerate universal access to TB diagnostics. We conducted a narrative review of studies published between Jan 1, 2020, and April 30, 2026, focusing on near-point-of-care molecular (NPOC) platforms, next-generation lipoarabinomannan (LAM) assays, and non-sputum sampling approaches. Emerging NPOC molecular platforms, demonstrate high sensitivity using both sputum and tongue-swab specimens while substantially reducing equipment and testing costs compared with existing nucleic acid amplification test platforms. Next-generation urine LAM assays offer improved sensitivity and potential for use beyond people living with HIV. In addition, parallel testing approaches with multiple sample types, including sputum, tongue swab, stool for children, and urine testing, can substantially increase diagnostic yield in specific populations. Integrating low-cost technologies with non-sputum sampling strategies could provide a scalable pathway towards universal access to TB diagnostics. Realizing this potential will require streamlined regulatory pathways, sustainable financing, and integration of these tools into primary healthcare systems. Funding: None.

title: Diagnostic yield and predictors of complications in CT-guided percutaneous lung biopsy: an analysis based on ATS/ACCP criteria.
abstract:
Background

CT-guided percutaneous lung biopsy (CT-PLB) remains a cornerstone for the diagnosis of pulmonary nodules (PNs), although several alternative techniques, including robotic-assisted bronchoscopy, are increasingly adopted. This study aimed to evaluate CT-PLB in a real-world cohort, focusing on predictors of diagnostic yield and complications.

Methods

We retrospectively evaluated patients who underwent CT-PLB between 2020 and 2024. The diagnostic yield was defined according to the recently published ATS/ACCP criteria. Clinical, radiological, and periprocedural variables were assessed as predictors of diagnostic outcome and complication [pneumothorax (PNX) and pulmonary hemorrhage].

Results

Six hundred fifty-seven patients were included (mean age 69 ± 11 years; 54% male). The diagnostic yield was 84% with higher yield observed for nodule size (diameter ≥ 10 mm), density (solid), and location (peripheral). Increasing subcutaneous fat thickness was independently associated with a modest but significant reduction in diagnostic yield. PNX was radiologically present in 44.4% of cases; however, only 5.9% required hospitalization, and 4.7% required chest-tube placement. Greater parenchymal depth, trans-fissural needle passages, pleural tags and supine and left-lateral decubitus positions were associated with increased PNX extent, while intraparenchymal lesion and greater chest-wall thickness showed a protective effect. Radiological pulmonary hemorrhage >2 cm occurred in 38% of patients, whereas only 1.5% experienced major bleeding requiring intervention. Greater parenchymal depth and non-solid density were associated with increased hemorrhage severity.

Conclusions

In a contemporary diagnostic landscape, CT-PLNB still demonstrates high diagnostic yield and an acceptable safety profile when strict diagnostic criteria are applied. These findings support its continued role as a primary diagnostic approach for PNs.

title: Differences in microbiota profiles of simple and complicated pediatric appendicitis cases
abstract: This study aimed to identify the differences in microbial composition between simple appendicitis (SA) and complicated appendicitis (CA) in a limited sample size using culture and microbiota analysis. Appendix tissues and rectal swabs for microbiota analysis and conventional cultures were collected from patients. 16S rRNA regions were amplified using a DNA preparation kit with primers designed to target the V3-V4 region. Sixteen (41%) of the patients were classified as CA based on the histopathological analysis, and the rest as SA. The effect size was slightly greater in rectal swab samples than in appendiceal tissue samples. Based on the conventional culture, the most common aerobic bacteria were Escherichia , Klebsiella spp., and Enterococcus spp. A decrease in both Pseudomonadota and Bacteriodota phyla was observed in tissue samples, while a decrease in Bacteriodota and an increase in Pseudomonadota were observed in rectal samples. Differences in the relative abundance of Coprobacter and Hungatella were observed between CAT and SAT samples; however, no genus-level difference remained significant after ANCOM-BC2 multiple-testing correction. The most notable feature of the CAT group was the relatively higher presence of potential pathobionts. Bacteriodes and Roseburia showed higher relative abundance in the SA rectal (SAR) group. The genera Eubacterium and Clostridioides showed a significant increase in both the SAR and CA rectal (CAR) groups. Lower relative abundances of Parvimonas, Prevotella , and Dialister and a higher relative abundance of Tyzzerella were observed in CAR compared with controls, although these differences did not remain significant after multiple-testing correction. In the ANCOM-BC2 pairwise analysis, an unclassified genus within Enterobacteriaceae was significantly enriched in CAR compared with healthy controls (LFC = 3.56, q = 0.003). No statistically significant distinction was shown at the alpha and beta diversity levels between SA and CA cases. Our findings support previous studies on increased density and diversity at the phylum level in the CA group. The main limitations were the limited sample size and the use of pre-operative antibiotics. Microbiota profiling of appendiceal tissue and rectal swab samples may provide complementary information for understanding microbiota-associated patterns in appendicitis; however, the diagnostic or predictive utility of these microbial profiles requires validation in larger, independent cohorts using dedicated predictive modeling and diagnostic performance analyses.

title: Distribution and Age Dynamics of Respiratory Mycoplasmosis in Birds on Farms of the Nakhchivan Autonomous Republic
abstract: Experiments revealed that 1- to 60-day-old chickens are more susceptible to respiratory mycoplasmosis. Those chickens that contracted the disease experienced developmental delays. Serological studies revealed that the serum droplet agglutination test (SDR) in chickens testing positive for mycoplasmosis resulted in high infection rates in 1- and 20-day-old chickens, amounting to 57.5% and 62.5%, respectively. Respiratory mycoplasmosis infection was recorded in 35.5% of 40-day-old chickens and 6.6% of 60-day-old chickens. Thus, during the study, the percentage of infected chickens did not fall below 50.0% in the RSPN, with the infection peaking at 7 and 10 months of age, amounting to 91.6% and 80.0%, respectively. According to the hemagglutination test, 100% antibodies to mycoplasma were detected at all age periods. At the same time, the maximum average titer (5286±932) was also recorded during the period of intensive egg production. With age, a decrease in the average titer to 3171±428 was recorded. Bacteriological examination of throat swabs taken from healthy laying hens revealed M. gallisepticum cultures in 26.6%–53.3% of all age groups. Detection of the causative agent of respiratory mycoplasmosis in embryos and one-day-old chicks indicates that the infection is transmitted transovarially. The highest mycoplasma carriage rate (53.3%) was detected in 10-month-old hens. Among 12-month-old roosters, the mycoplasma carriage rate was 64.0%.

title: Drill with Confidence: Real-Time Automated Drilling Fluid Testing and Dynamic Hydraulic Modeling for Drilling Optimization
abstract: Abstract Manual drilling fluid measurements typically conducted 2–4 times per day, lack the resolution required for precise hydraulic calculations and management in high-performance wells. This paper details the implementation of a closed-loop workflow involving an inline automated fluid testing device and real-time hydraulics simulation and monitoring across two wells in the field. The primary objective was to replace intermittent manual sampling with high-frequency data integrated into a live hydraulic and hole-cleaning simulator to monitor and optimize drilling performance parameters such as Rate of Penetration (ROP), tripping speeds, and circulation times. The technology utilized an inline dual-sampling drilling fluid characterization device to continuously analyze mud properties in the circulating system. The automated system achieved a significant increase in data density, providing 46 rheology tests and 1,920 density readings per day, a massive improvement over the conventional 2–4 rheology tests and 48 density readings. These real-time parameters (Density, PV, YP, and 6-speed readings) and drilling parameters were streamed to a Real-Time Center where a hydraulics modelling software was used for real-time monitoring and optimization. This allowed for the continuous monitoring of the Hole-Cleaning Index (HCI), Cuttings Bed Height (CBH), and Equivalent Circulating Density (ECD) against planned pressure and fracture gradients and identify opportunities for drilling parameter optimization. The integration of real-time data into predictive simulations yielded substantial operational efficiencies as follows: Drilling Performance: The system enabled a maximum ROP of 400 ft/hr while maintaining good hole cleaning. A field-best 24-hour footage of 3,945.68 feet was achieved in the 6-inch section at this time.Circulation Optimization: While the original plan was six bottom-up cycles, predictive simulations suggested optimizing this sequence to just two (a potential saving in circulation time of 67% whilst ensuring a clean wellbore)Tripping Efficiency: Real-time surge/swab monitoring enabled potential tripping speed increases of nearly 100% over previous rig KPIs, offering 15–25% time savings compared to the best-performing rigs in the region.Data Accuracy: Comparative analysis showed a high correlation between simulated ECD and actual annular pressure while drilling (APWD) data, confirming the reliability of automated fluid inputs for pressure management. This work demonstrates that automating the fluid-data-to-simulation loop moves the industry from reactive monitoring to proactive drilling management. It quantifies the specific "time-savings" value of high-frequency rheology data, proving that automated testing is a critical precursor to fully autonomous drilling systems.

title: Dual closed-loop training using an AI-driven exoskeleton hand robot and movement-triggered transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation helps people learn a difficult finger individuation task
abstract: Abstract Background Vagus nerve stimulation paired with successful movement enhances motor recovery after stroke. However, transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) has rarely been synchronized with movement completion or combined with a robotic hand exoskeleton. Therefore, this study aimed to determine whether dual closed-loop training combining an AI-powered, electromyography-controlled hand exoskeleton with movement-triggered taVNS improves independent ring-finger control in healthy adults. Methods In this open-label study, 52 healthy adults were randomized into volitional training (VOL), passive robot training (PAS), AI-robot training (ROBOT), or AI-robot training with taVNS (ROBOT + taVNS; n = 13 each). Training targeted the “Guwashi” pose (ring-finger extension with middle- and little-finger flexion), comprising three sets of 100 repetitions on alternate days. In ROBOT + taVNS, an infrared sensor detected little-finger flexion, triggering a 500-ms, 30-Hz stimulation train to the left tragus. Primary outcomes were changes in proximal interphalangeal joint angle differences between the middle and ring fingers (ΔPIP M–R ) and little and ring fingers (ΔPIP L–R ). Results ΔPIP M–R gain was greater with ROBOT + taVNS (54.6 ± 10.1°) than ROBOT (23.2 ± 9.1°, p = 0.040), PAS (6.3 ± 6.3°, p < 0.001), and VOL (10.9 ± 5.9°, p = 0.002). Non-parametric post hoc analysis revealed that ΔPIP L–R increased more in the ROBOT + taVNS group (vs. PAS, p = 0.011; vs. VOL, p = 0.016) and the ROBOT group (vs. PAS, p = 0.008; vs. VOL, p = 0.011), with no significant difference between the two robot groups (p = 1.000). Conclusions Movement-triggered taVNS may enhance AI-robot training for the challenging middle–ring finger coordination required for the Guwashi pose in healthy adults. These findings support further investigation of this combined approach for improving finger individuation after stroke.
authors: Hikari Kirimoto; Sota Nabekura; Koki Fukuda; Sena Watanabe; Iroha Seo; Kangjing Yang; Tatsuya Mima; Tomohisa Nezu

title: E-Tactile Flow: Exploring A Novel Path of Pain Relief through Interactive Electrotactile Stimulation
abstract: Chronic or recurrent pain significantly impairs quality of life, and conventional pharmacological treatments often produce side effects, motivating the search for non-pharmacological alternatives. This study introduces a novel paradigm — E-Tactile Tactile Flow (E-Tactile Flow)—which integrates electrotactile stimulation with attentional engagement and flow-related task design. Inspired by a bidirectional attention mechanism, the paradigm designed goal-directed task mode and stimulus-driven task mode to examine the role of cognitive engagement in pain modulation. A preliminary study validated the feasibility and safety parameters of an 8×8 electrotactile system. In Experiment 1 (n = 42), both attention modes effectively reduced pain perception, with the goal-directed task mode showing significantly stronger modulation of several physiological measures and a marginal trend toward lower subjective pain ratings than the stimulus-driven task mode. Building on this, Experiment 2 introduced adaptive difficulty modulation to better align task challenge with participant performance. Results showed that dynamic task adjustment significantly enhanced attentional engagement and reduced pain ratings. Overall, this study provides initial empirical support for an electrotactile interaction paradigm for non-pharmacological pain modulation.

title: Early applications of apple vision pro in clinical medicine and medical education: a scoping review
abstract: The Apple Vision Pro (AVP), a next-generation spatial computing device, has demonstrated potential applications in multidisciplinary clinical diagnosis, treatment, and medical education, by leveraging its unique technical architecture and performance advantages. In clinical practice, its fundamental advantages of three-dimensional (3D) visualization, real-time image integration, and immersive interaction have been preliminarily employed in disease diagnosis and treatment, surgical planning, precise operations, and postoperative rehabilitation across multiple disciplines. In medical education, AVP surpasses the limitations of conventional models, offering a novel methodology for anatomy education, clinical skills development, specialized practical training, and collaboration of distance learning, thereby alleviating persistent challenges such as unequal distribution of teaching resources, low efficiency in skills and specialized training, and the high cost of distance education. However, AVP faces some limitations, including limited hardware portability, insufficient system compatibility, a lack of specialized medical applications, high costs, and incomplete medical certification. Currently, most evidence derives from feasibility studies, case reports, and opinion pieces. Only two Stage 2b confirmatory studies were identified. Thus, high-level evidence for clinical benefit remains scarce. Readers should interpret all reported benefits as preliminary technical demonstrations rather than established clinical outcomes. Future advancements necessitate iterative development of lightweight hardware design, development of specialized medical software, cross-system optimization, and establishment of standardization protocols. Moreover, more randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and multicenter studies are urgently needed to fully explore and validate its intrinsic value in precision medicine and the equitable allocation of medical resources.

title: Effect of Early Tourniquet Release on Hemolysis in Emergency Department Phlebotomy: The TOURNI-ED Randomized Trial
abstract: Background and Objectives: Hemolysis is the most common preanalytical error in emergency department samples and can compromise diagnostic reliability. Evidence on tourniquet-release timing under standardized pressure is limited. We assessed whether initiating cuff deflation when blood enters the first tube and completing it as that tube fills reduces hemolysis. Materials and Methods: In a single-center, parallel-group, 1:1 randomized trial (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07617103), 792 adults triaged as Emergency Severity Index (ESI) 3 to 5 underwent venipuncture with stasis applied at 60 mm Hg by sphygmomanometer. Cuff deflation was initiated when blood entered the first tube and completed as that tube filled (n = 396) or after the last tube filled (n = 396). The primary outcome was the proportion of serum separator gel tubes with a hemolysis index of 1+ or greater, assessed by personnel blinded to allocation. The primary complete-case analysis included 790 participants analyzed as randomized. Results: Hemolysis occurred in 68 of 395 patients (17.2%) with early release and 103 of 395 (26.1%) with late release (absolute risk reduction 8.9 percentage points; 95% confidence interval (CI), 3.1–14.5; p = 0.003; number needed to treat (NNT) 11.3). The adjusted odds ratio in the prespecified model was 0.58 (95% CI, 0.41–0.82), and the ordinal distribution also favored early release (p = 0.002). No early-release patient exceeded 60 s of stasis, versus 29.0% with late release. Complication estimates were imprecise (8.1% vs. 5.6%; risk difference +2.5 points; 95% CI, −1.0 to 6.1). Conclusions: In adult emergency department patients presenting with non-critical acuity (ESI 3–5) undergoing direct 21-gauge venipuncture under standardized 60 mm Hg cuff pressure, early cuff release significantly reduced specimen hemolysis (NNT 11.3 for preventing one laboratory-defined hemolyzed sample). These findings cannot be generalized to resuscitated patients (ESI 1–2), intravenous catheter blood draws, winged collection devices, or uncalibrated elastic tourniquets.

title: Effects of Immersive Virtual Reality and Relaxation Video on Symptom Severity, Distress, and Quality of Life in Lung Cancer Patients During Initial Chemotherapy Cycles: A Three-Arm Randomised Controlled Trial
abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: To examine the effects of immersive virtual reality (VR) and a theme-matched relaxation video (RV) on symptom severity, distress, and quality of life in lung cancer patients. METHODS: = 105) group. During the first two chemotherapy cycles, the VR and RV groups were assigned two 20 min sessions of immersive nature-themed VR or theme-matched RV, while the CG received routine care alone. The primary outcome domain was symptom severity, assessed through within-session changes in ten individual Edmonton Symptom Assessment Scale (ESAS) symptom scores; distress and quality of life were secondary outcomes. Data were analysed with linear mixed models, and between-group differences are reported with Bonferroni-adjusted 95% confidence intervals (CI). RESULTS: Compared with the CG, the within-session improvement was greater for eight of the ten ESAS symptoms with VR and for five with RV; the largest differences were for well-being (VR 1.26 points, 95% CI 0.98 to 1.53; RV 0.76, 0.49 to 1.03), with smaller differences for tiredness, depression, and anxiety. Distress also decreased more with VR (1.04, 0.73 to 1.34) and RV (0.73, 0.42 to 1.03) than in the CG. VR improved more than RV for well-being (0.50, 0.22 to 0.77), tiredness (0.47, 0.16 to 0.79), and distress (0.31, 0.002 to 0.62). No intervention-specific effect emerged for nausea, lack of appetite, or quality of life. CONCLUSIONS: Compared with routine care, two sessions of VR or RV improved acute symptoms, mainly well-being, tiredness, depression, and anxiety, and reduced distress, with no intervention-specific effect on quality of life. The additional benefit of VR was small and, for the ESAS symptoms, below the minimal clinically important difference, so RV may be a practical and accessible option. title: Effects of Sample Matrix, RNA Extraction Method, Carrier RNA, and Storage Conditions on RT-qPCR Detection of Foot-and-Mouth Disease Virus
abstract: Reliable molecular detection of foot-and-mouth disease virus (FMDV) depends on RT-qPCR performance and pre-analytical factors, including sample matrix, RNA extraction method, carrier RNA supplementation, and storage conditions. This study compared silica membrane- and magnetic bead-based RNA extraction workflows for detection of FMDV serotypes O, A, and SAT2 in serum, PBS-based swab suspension, and tissue homogenates at three virus dilutions, with and without carrier RNA. FMDV RNA stability in serum stored at room temperature or -20 °C for up to 60 days and following five freeze-thaw cycles was also evaluated using serotype O. Extraction performance was matrix-dependent. In serum, silica-based workflow yielded significantly lower Ct values than magnetic bead-based extraction. In tissue homogenates, magnetic bead extraction yielded significantly lower Ct values with carrier RNA, whereas carrier RNA impaired silica-based extraction. No significant differences were observed for PBS-based swab suspension samples. FMDV RNA detectability remained stable at -20 °C for 60 days, whereas room-temperature storage caused progressive signal loss, which was reduced by carrier RNA. Five freeze-thaw cycles did not progressively affect RNA detectability. These findings demonstrate that the effects of extraction workflow and carrier RNA supplementation on FMDV RT-qPCR detectability differed according to the sample matrix and experimental conditions, highlighting the importance of matrix-specific optimization of pre-analytical procedures.

title: Effects of a low dose of 3-nitrooxypropanol and a combination of direct-fed microbials on methane emission, oral swab bacterial community, and performance in dairy cows
abstract: Abstract Background 3-Nitrooxypropanol (3-NOP) can inhibit ruminal methane production by inactivating the key enzyme during methanogenesis. Combining 3-NOP and direct-fed microbials (DFM) can potentially provide a dual-action approach to reduce ruminal methane production. The objective of this study was to investigate the effects of supplementation of a low dose of 3-NOP and a mixture of DFM, on methane emissions, performance, and rumen microbial community of dairy cows. Results Forty-eight Danish Holstein dairy cows were used in a 14-week randomized complete block design. Due to a mixing error, 3-NOP was included at an unexpected low dose (6.0 mg/kg DM). Cows were fed with one of four experimental diets: (1) control diet, and other treatment diets were control diet supplemented with (2) 3-NOP, or with (3) DFM (12 mg/kg P. acidipropionici strain P169 and 120 mg/kg Bacillus subtilis and B. licheniformis mixture), or with (4) a combination of 3-NOP and DFM. 3-NOP inclusion did not affect DMI, feed efficiency, or milk yield and composition. DFM supplementation reduced partial mixed ration intake and total DMI. 3-NOP supplementation significantly reduced CH 4 production (g/d) (8%) and CH 4 intensity (g/kg ECM) (9%) but did not affect CH 4 yield (g/kg DMI). Furthermore, 3-NOP supplementation increased H 2 production, yield, and intensity. DFM supplementation reduced milk yield from weeks 3 to 8 and ECM yield from weeks 3 to 7, but these effects diminished over time. 3-NOP alone or in combination with DFM resulted in higher abundance of Megasphaera and Prevotella genera in oral swab samples. DFM supplementation had no effect on gas emissions, and it only tended to improve feed efficiency (ECM/DMI, kg/kg) during the later stage of the experiment. DFM supplementation led to higher abundance of certain species within the Lactobacillaceae family particularly at later stages of the experiment. Conclusions An unforeseen reduced dose of 3-NOP supplementation still can effectively mitigate methane emissions (both production and intensity) and increase H 2 emissions without affecting DMI or performance. DFM supplementation reduced DMI and milk yield at the onset of the experiment, but the effects subsided over time, resulting in an increased feed efficiency by the end of the experiment.
authors: Wenji Wang; Sadjad Danesh Mesgaran; Ruth Gómez Expósito; A. Rytz; N. Walker; Elodie Soussan; S. Pruvost; D Yáñez-Ruiz; P. Lund

title: Efficient bronchoscopy image triaging via distilled cascaded deep networks: a lightweight framework for pulmonary pathology classification
abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) and lung cancer are major pulmonary diseases that contribute substantially to morbidity and mortality worldwide. Differentiating these diseases from bronchoscopic images can be challenging because some of their visual features overlap. In this study, we developed a knowledge-distilled cascaded convolutional neural network for classifying bronchoscopic images into three categories: normal, tuberculosis, and lung cancer. The framework uses two sequential binary classifiers. The first classifier separates normal from abnormal bronchoscopic images, and the second classifies abnormal images as either TB or lung cancer. DenseNet-121 was used as the teacher network. Smaller student networks were then developed through knowledge distillation by removing the fourth Dense Block and optimizing the depth of the third Dense Block using the Neural Network Intelligence (NNI) framework. NNI was also used to optimize the training hyperparameters of both the teacher and student networks. The method was evaluated using 515 bronchoscopic images from 81 normal subjects, 76 patients with pulmonary tuberculosis, and 277 patients with lung cancer. Since several patients had more than one image, primary five-fold cross-validation was carried out at the patient level, ensuring that images from the same patient were not included in both the training and test sets. The distilled network achieved an accuracy of 91.5%, compared with 90.5% for the teacher network, with sensitivities of 92.2% for lung cancer, 80.3% for TB, and 98.8% for normal cases. Although the distilled network achieved a higher accuracy in the primary five-fold cross-validation evaluation, the difference between the teacher and student models was not statistically significant in the repeated paired hold-out analysis (Wilcoxon signed-rank test, p = 0.4378). In the 30 repeated hold-out experiments, the teacher and student models achieved mean accuracies of 0.8890 ± 0.0325 and 0.8568 ± 0.0839, respectively, with a 95% confidence interval of [-0.0214, 0.0857] for the paired teacher–student accuracy difference. Compared with the teacher network, the distilled model reduced the number of trainable parameters by 54.1%, the model size by 54.1%, and the FLOPs by 14.6%. The inference time was also reduced from 0.0920 s to 0.0567 s per image. The results indicate that architectural reduction combined with knowledge distillation and automated hyperparameter optimization can substantially reduce model complexity and computational requirements, while no statistically significant difference in classification accuracy was detected between the student and teacher models. The reduced model provides a basis for future evaluation in bronchoscopy computer-aided diagnosis systems.
authors: Rojin Setayeshi; Javad Vahidi; Ehsan Kozegar

title: Electrochemical Detection of PFAS Contaminants Across Environmental and Pharmaceutical Matrices:Sensing Mechanisms, Nanomaterial Platforms, Biological Monitoring, and Regulatory Convergence
abstract: PFAS are a class of over 14,000 synthetic compounds characterized by a stable carbon-fluorine bond that confers resistance to thermal and biological degradation, resulting in common contamination of various aquatic matrices at concentrations ranging from sub-parts per trillion to parts per billion.Demand for directly deployable sensitive quantification methods has been spurred by increasingly stringent regulatory responses such as the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) proposed maximum contaminant levels of 4 ppt for PFOA and PFOS in 2024 under its third Fourth Unregulated Contaminant Monitoring Rule and sub-parametric values recommended by the EU Drinking Water Directive.Conventional liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry provides the required sensitivity but is still limited by centralized infrastructure and slow sample preparation that prevents point-of-care or real-time surveillance.Another critically understudied dimension includes pharmaceutical matrices, where PFAS can act as formulation excipients or derive from the synthesis of fluorinated active pharmaceutical ingredients and pharmacokinetically interfere with albumin binding and hepatic CYP450 activity in exposed populations.The current review summarized the existing electrochemical sensing strategies, including molecularly imprinted polymers, aptasensors, and CRISPR-Cas12a biosensors, and state-of-the-art electrode structures, including metal-organic frameworks, MXenes, and covalent triazine frameworks, for targeting PFAS in environmental and biological matrices.While some of these can be implemented analytically with detection below 1 ppt, critical benchmarking using regulatory thresholds reveals that 10% of sensor studies validate their performance in non-spiked field or clinical matrices.This highlights the need for multi-analyte array development to allow standardized sensor validation frameworks across environmental and pharmaceutical quality monitoring.
venue: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology

title: Enhancing Adolescent HIV Screening: A Quality Improvement Approach Using Point-of-care Testing in an Outpatient Pediatric Setting
abstract: Introduction: Routine HIV testing remains poorly implemented nationwide, despite national recommendations. Half of adolescents who are HIV positive do not know their status. This quality improvement project aimed to increase the rate of routine HIV screening during well-child checks (WCCs) for eligible adolescents 15-18 years of age with no prior lifetime HIV test to greater than 50% within 1 year through implementation of point-of-care (POC) oral swab HIV testing at a pediatric outpatient clinic affiliated with Loma Linda University in Moreno Valley, Calif. Methods: All adolescent patients 15-18 years of age presenting for WCC who had not yet been tested once in their lifetime for HIV were eligible. We conducted 6 plan-do-study-act cycles from August 2023 to September 2025, including initial and subsequent implementation cycles. Key drivers included standardizing the process to facilitate HIV testing in the clinic, improving provider awareness, providing standardized information on patient eligibility, and providing patient and family education on HIV screening. The primary intervention was implementing oral swab POC testing during WCC visits. Other interventions included creating an educational curriculum for physicians on HIV screening guidelines, developing multilingual resources for families on the importance of HIV screening, and using a multidisciplinary team to integrate testing into clinic workflow. The primary outcome measure was the monthly percentage of adolescents 15-18 years of age who were screened for HIV via the POC swab during their WCC. Results: Before implementation, the average percentage of eligible patients screened from January 2023 to July 2023 was 29%. Screening rates increased from 29% to 51% among eligible adolescents over the first eight months. With implementation of the POC oral swab HIV test, screening rates increased from 51% to 56% over an additional 8 months. During the later implementation cycles (December 2024 to September 2025), monthly screening rates generally exceeded the project goal of 50%, averaging 64%. Eligibility was based on age, visit type, and prior lifetime HIV testing status. No reactive or positive HIV test results were identified during the study period. Potential balancing measures included additional time needed during clinical visits, false-positive results, and the potential workflow burden on clinical staff. Conclusions: Improving HIV screening among adolescents is feasible through a multicomponent quality improvement strategy that incorporates POC rapid antibody testing. This type of testing is painless, can be performed quickly during clinic visits, and improves patient confidentiality because results are available at the time of the visit rather than by phone or email. Medicaid covers POC testing for HIV. This makes this form of testing feasible in many clinics.
authors: Graydon Dietrich; Natasha Thomas; Alexandria Grellmann; Gabrielle Pina; Rachel Davidge; Jerard Tambunan; Mona Abutouk

title: Ethanol improves RNase P stability in nasopharyngeal samples stored at room temperature for SARS-CoV-2 RT-qPCR diagnosis.
abstract: Despite the end of the global health emergency, COVID-19 and its etiological agent, SARS-CoV-2, remain topics of high scientific and public health relevance due to the continued circulation of the virus, the emergence of new variants, and the persistent risk of outbreaks. RT-qPCR is the gold standard procedure for SARS-CoV-2 detection, but its reliability depends on preserving viral RNA and the human Ribonuclease P (RNase P; internal control) target during sample storage and transport. This study aimed to evaluate the effect of different preservation conditions on nucleic acid stability for SARS-CoV-2 detection by RT-qPCR: samples maintained in 0.9% saline and samples supplemented with absolute ethanol to reach a final concentration of 70% (v/v), under different storage temperature conditions. Nasopharyngeal swab samples, initially collected and transported in 0.9% saline and previously classified into different viral load categories, were pooled and redistributed into the experimental storage conditions: ethanol or saline under refrigerated conditions (4°C) or at room temperature. RNA was extracted using an automated magnetic bead-based method and analyzed by RT-qPCR targeting the SARS-CoV-2 E gene and the human RNase P internal control, with nucleic acid stability monitored over a 12-day storage period. Viral RNA detection remained stable in both storage media; however, RNase P detection progressively declined in saline, particularly during room temperature storage, while ethanol maintained consistent amplification. These findings indicate that 70% ethanol better maintains the stability of the human internal control (RNase P) than saline during room temperature storage of nasopharyngeal samples for up to 12 days.
authors: Lia Ayumi Umezawa; Fabiana Barcelos Furtado; Gabriela Boni Poli; Leonardo Nazario de Moraes; Maércio José De Oliveira Alho; Flavia Hebeler-Barbosa; Guilherme Targino Valente; Rejane Maria Tommasini Grotto

title: Evaluating robotic-assisted bronchoscopy for bronchus-unconnected peripheral pulmonary nodules: diagnostic efficacy and safety
abstract: Background: Bronchus-unconnected peripheral pulmonary lesions (PPLs) pose diagnostic challenges due to lack of direct airway access and computed tomography (CT)-to-body divergence (CTBD). We evaluated robotic-assisted bronchoscopy (RAB) combined with the intraprocedural CT-guided navigation with ventilatory strategy for atelectasis (ICNVA) strategy.Methods: This prospective, single-arm study enrolled patients (18–75 years) with pulmonary nodules (6–30 mm) lacking a bronchus sign. All underwent RAB with the ICNVA strategy, integrating preoperative mapping, intraprocedural breath-holds to minimize atelectasis, and real-time CT confirmation. The primary endpoint was tool-in-lesion (TIL) rate. Secondary endpoints included diagnostic yield, center strike rate, CTBD, and safety.Results: Thirty patients were enrolled (mean age 55.6±10.7 years). Lesions had a mean diameter of 14.0±4.3 mm and a median distance to the nearest bronchus of 18 mm. The ICNVA strategy resulted in a mean CTBD of 13.4 mm. We achieved a 100% (30/30) navigational success rate (TIL) and a 66.7% (20/30) center strike rate. The overall diagnostic yield was 90% (27/30), with 90.9% (20/22) sensitivity for malignancy. Pneumothorax occurred in 2 patients (6.7%) and mild hemorrhage in 7 (23.3%), with no severe adverse events occurred.Conclusions: RAB combined with the ICNVA strategy demonstrates high diagnostic yield and safety for bronchus-unconnected PPLs. This approach effectively mitigates CTBD, enabling precise localization and sampling of lesions traditionally considered difficult to access.
authors: Shaohua Dai; Wei Zuo; Bentong Yu

title: Evaluation of Gene Xpert Xpress System for Detecting SARS-CoV-2 in Suspected Clinical Samples
abstract: Background: The emergence of SARS-CoV-2 caused a global COVID-19 pandemic, necessitating rapid and accurate diagnostic tools, especially in resource-limited settings. Materials and methods: This cross-sectional study evaluated the diagnostic performance of the fully automated Gene Xpert Xpress SARS-CoV-2 assay compared to conventional real-time RT-PCR (Gold standard) using nasopharyngeal swabs from 105 suspected COVID-19 patients at BITID, Bangladesh from December 20 to December 21. Results: Of the 105 samples, 65 (61.9%) were RT-PCR positive and 40 (38.1%) were negative. The Gene Xpert Xpress detected 62/65 positives (sensitivity 95.4%) and 32/40 negatives (Specificity 80.0%) yielding an overall accuracy of 89.5%. Discordant results were mainly attributed to differences in limit of detection and Ct value interpretation. Conclusion: The Gene Xpert Xpress system demonstrated high sensitivity, rapid results (~45 minutes) minimal training requirements and suitability for decentralized settings, making it a valuable tool for timely SARS-CoV-2 detection and clinical decision-making in emergency situations and low-resource environments. authors: Md Shakeel Ahmed; Md Zakir Hossain; Md Rakibul Bulbul Hassan; Md Zahirul Islam; Md Fazle Rabby; Mahabubul Mowla; Md Shamiul Islam

title: Evaluation of the Hologic Aptima® Vaginitis and Seegene Allplex™ assays for microbiological diagnosis of bacterial vaginosis and Candida vaginitis in women in France, relative to Nugent score and culture
abstract: Introduction. Molecular assays such as the Hologic Aptima ® Vaginitis Panel and Seegene Allplex ™ Vaginitis assay offer improved sensitivity and multiplex detection for the diagnosis of vaginitis compared with the non-molecular standard of care. Gap Statement. Evidence comparing the relative performance of Aptima versus Seegene is limited, as is knowledge of Aptima’s compatibility with non-proprietary swabs. Aim. This prospective study assessed the diagnostic performance of the Aptima BV (bacterial vaginosis) and Aptima CV/TV assays ( Candida vaginitis/ Trichomonas vaginitis) alongside the Seegene Allplex assay in symptomatic women (≥18 years) presenting for vaginitis testing in primary care in France. Methodology. Two vaginal swabs were taken per patient: one Aptima Multitest Swab and one non-proprietary Σ-TRANSWAB liquid Amies collection swab. Aptima swab data were used solely to confirm performance of the Aptima assays under current test conditions, while all primary assay comparisons were performed using Σ-TRANSWAB samples. These comparisons were performed for each assay relative to Nugent score (for BV) or culture (for CV), as well as Aptima relative to Seegene. Results. In total, 500 women underwent vaginitis testing between July and August 2024. When using non-proprietary Σ-TRANSWAB collection methods, sensitivity and specificity values for the Aptima BV assay were 96.7 and 89.7% relative to Nugent score, and 89.9 and 90.6% for Seegene Allplex relative to Nugent score. Among ‘intermediate BV’ samples ( n =66), agreement between Seegene Allplex and Nugent score was 1.5%. Sensitivity and specificity values for the detection of CV were 88.6 and 90.8% for the Aptima CV/TV assay, and 90.2 and 93.7% for Seegene Allplex. Assay detection of TV could not be validated due to an insufficient number of TV-positive samples ( n =1). These findings were consistent with Aptima’s performance when using proprietary collection methods. Conclusion. Overall, the Aptima Vaginitis Panel demonstrated comparably high diagnostic performance to Seegene Allplex for the detection of BV and CV when using a non-proprietary sample collection method. TV prevalence was too low in this cohort to permit meaningful assay evaluation for this pathogen.
authors: Cécile Martaresche; Florian Scherrer

title: Evaluation of whole genome sequencing protocols and target-capture panels for detection of respiratory viruses in clinical specimens
abstract: Respiratory viruses are major contributors to global morbidity and mortality. When viral mutations compromise detection by conventional diagnostic assays, identifying cases and tracing transmission becomes challenging. Whole genome sequencing (WGS) improves on conventional diagnostics as it can detect viruses with novel mutations. This study evaluated the performance of the ePlex, a rapid multiplex polymerase chain reaction (PCR) assay (RMPA), an in-house real-time reverse transcription PCR assay (RT-qPCR) and WGS for detecting respiratory virus infections in clinical specimens. Sixty-one sequence libraries were prepared, and bait enriched from nasopharyngeal swabs, collected in 2021, which were negative for SARS-CoV-2 but positive for co-infections of respiratory viruses detected by the ePlex. An in-house bioinformatics pipeline enabled a metagenomic analysis approach to be compared with the ePlex and RT-qPCR. In most swabs, respiratory viruses were detected by WGS (average genome recovery: 85.9%) or RT-qPCR which concurred with the ePlex result, but as single viruses rather than co-infections. WGS recovered respiratory syncytial viruses (80%) and metapneumoviruses (70%) most often. This study demonstrates the power of WGS and bait capture in resolving the genomes of respiratory pathogens from limited clinical material. Detection of a single virus, rather than co-infections, in this instance could highlight the targeted nature of bait capture technology or competition between viruses during bait hybridization. The number of respiratory syncytial viruses detected (16/20) could be due to a spike in activity detected after the alleviation of non-pharmaceutical interventions in the COVID-19 pandemic.
authors: Daniel Kelly; Ketharani Yogananthan; Priya Subramaniam; Tiina Talts; Carmen F. Manso; Beatrix Kele; David Bibby; Mark A. Zuckerman; Jean Lutamyo Mbisa

title: Exploring phenotypic, nutritional and metabolic traits associated with early sexual development in young Nelore (Bos indicus) heifers.
abstract: This study explored the associations among phenotypic, reproductive, nutritional, and metabolic traits with early sexual development in Bos indicus heifers. A total of 443 prepubertal Nelore heifers (11.1 ± 0.07 mo old) were evaluated during a feedlot (automated feeders) period from day -70 to day 0. Parameters assessed on day -70 (beginning of the feedlot period) included body weight (BW), body condition score (BCS), presence of CL, uterine (UT) and largest follicle (LF) diameters, as well as blood collection for LC-MS/MS metabolomics (subset of 139 heifers). On day 0 (end of the feedlot period), all heifers were submitted to a timed artificial insemination protocol (TAI). In addition, on that day, ribeye area (REA) and rump fat thickness (RFAT) were assessed by ultrasound. Residual feed intake (RFI), average daily gain (ADG), and dry matter intake (DMI) during the feedlot period were calculated. Pregnancy diagnosis was performed on day 39 and heifers confirmed as pregnant were classified as early-conceiving (EC; n = 212), while those non-pregnant were classified as late-conceiving (LC; n = 231). Parameters evaluated on days -70 and 0 were compared between these groups. On day -70, no differences in BW (P = 0.30), BCS (P = 0.11), UT (P = 0.32) and LF (P = 0.39) diameters, and presence of CL (P = 0.98) were observed between groups. On day 0, no difference between groups were observed in BW (P = 0.46), BCS (P = 0.82), LF (P = 0.56) diameter, and REA (P = 0.19). However, EC heifers had greater UT diameter (P = 0.05), RFAT (P = 0.02) and presence of CL (P = 0.04). Additionally, although no differences between groups were observed in DMI (P = 0.15) and ADG (P = 0.40) during the feedlot period, EC heifers had higher RFI (P = 0.05) than LC heifers. Metabolomic analyses of samples collected on day -70 indicated a marked separation between LC and EC heifers, with an accuracy of 0.74. Significant pathways altered were alanine, aspartate and glutamate metabolism, TCA cycle, and pyruvate metabolism. In conclusion, none of the phenotypic traits assessed on day -70 reliably predicted early sexual development in heifers. By day 0, EC heifers demonstrated increased fat deposition and uterine development. Moreover, feed efficiency was negatively associated with early sexual development in yearling Bos indicus heifers. Metabolomic analyses revealed key changes in amino acids and energy metabolism and provided moderate predictive accuracy between EC and LC heifers. Collectively, the phenotypic, nutritional, and metabolic traits evaluated in this study contribute to a more integrated understanding of the physiological mechanisms underlying sexual development in Nelore heifers.
authors: Bruna Lima Chechin Catussi; Rubens Costa Pinto Silva; Adriano Santana Crozara; Bárbara Prestes de Castro; Angela Maria Gonella-Diaza; Lucas Oliveira E Silva; Pietro Sampaio Baruselli

title: Extracellular vesicle lipidomics liquid biopsy reveals systemic and tumor microenvironment metabolic reprogramming in ovarian cancer
abstract: Ovarian cancer is the most lethal gynecological malignancy, due to late-stage diagnosis, tumor heterogeneity, and lack of biomarkers for early detection. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) in plasma and ascites offer a minimally invasive source of tumor-derived information, yet their lipid composition and relationship to tumor heterogeneity remain poorly defined. We performed lipidomic profiling of EVs from plasma and ascites of high-grade serous ovarian cancer patients and from ovarian cancer and control cell lines to identify signatures of tumor progression and microenvironmental interactions. A lipid panel enriched in ovarian cancer EVs was evaluated in EVs and plasma across two independent cohorts (n = 146). Combined with CA125, this panel improved detection, particularly against benign adnexal masses, achieving an AUROC of 0.99 in the verification cohort in both formats. Ovarian cancer EVs preferentially accumulated triglycerides, including ether-linked species, whereas parental cells were enriched in phospholipids and ceramides. EV lipid signatures reflected tumor-associated metabolic reprogramming and captured tumor heterogeneity across cell models. These findings show that EV lipidomics from accessible biofluids offers a non-invasive window into ovarian cancer metabolism and candidate biomarkers for patient stratification and monitoring.
authors: Shikha Rani; Dominic Guanzon; Andrew Lai; Katherin Scholz‐Romero; Sarah Reed; Edita Ritmejerytė; Rohan Lourie; Naven Chetty; Kaltin Ferguson; Carlos Salomón

title: FORENSIC CLASSIFICATION OF GUNSHOT RESIDUE PARTICLES USING SEM-EDX AND MACHINE LEARNING
abstract: Machine learning (ML) is increasingly shaping forensic science by enabling more accurate and objective evidence analysis. This study applies ML algorithms to classify gunshot residue (GSR) particles using spectral data obtained through scanning electron microscopy with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (SEM-EDX). Conventional GSR identification relies on detecting characteristic inorganic particles containing lead (Pb), barium (Ba), and antimony (Sb), which point to firearm discharge residue. Twelve spectra were collected from four hand swabs taken during a simulated shooting scenario, alongside control samples that yielded no residue signal. The particles were analysed for elemental distribution and subjected to ML-assisted classification. A statistical framework combining probabilistic modelling with likelihood ratios (LRs) was then used to weigh the evidential strength of competing hypotheses. Results revealed marked differences in elemental composition across samples, underscoring the importance of rigorous statistical treatment rather than relying solely on visual or qualitative assessment. Three of the four swab classes offered strong support for GSR presence, yielding high LRs favouring the prosecution hypothesis. One sample, however, deviated from the model's underlying assumptions, illustrating how elemental signatures alone can be misleading if interpreted without appropriate methodological safeguards. Overall, integrating ML with probabilistic modelling offers a robust framework for forensic GSR analysis. Nonetheless, the findings highlight that methodological rigor cannot be sacrificed for computational convenience, and analysts should remain attentive to cases where statistical assumptions break down.
authors: Tolulope Bayode Abejide; Graham Souch; David Olayemi Alebiosu
