title: Factors Associated With Moderate‐to‐Severe Pain After Paediatric Laparoscopic Pyeloplasty: Implications for Nursing Care
abstract: BACKGROUND: Moderate-to-severe pain remains a clinically relevant concern after paediatric laparoscopic pyeloplasty and may interfere with early recovery. Identifying children at increased risk may support more timely and individualized perioperative pain management. AIMS: To investigate factors associated with moderate-to-severe pain after laparoscopic pyeloplasty in children and to inform targeted nursing and perioperative management strategies. METHODS: This single-centre retrospective observational study included children undergoing laparoscopic pyeloplasty. Postoperative pain was assessed at 2, 6, 12 and 24 h using either a Faces Pain Scale or the Face, Legs, Activity, Cry and Consolability (FLACC) scale according to age and communication ability. Moderate-to-severe pain was defined as a score ≥ 4 at any assessment within 24 h. Demographic, disease-related, surgical and perioperative variables were analysed. Multivariable binary logistic regression was used to identify factors independently associated with moderate-to-severe pain, and repeated-measures analysis of variance was used to assess changes in pain scores over time. This study was reported in accordance with the Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (STROBE) guidelines. RESULTS: Among 258 children, 65 developed moderate-to-severe postoperative pain, corresponding to an incidence of 25.2%. Multivariable analysis showed that age < 3 years, significant preoperative anxiety, operative time ≥ 120 min and the absence of a regional block were independently associated with moderate-to-severe pain. Sex, severe hydronephrosis and postoperative drainage tube placement were not independently associated with the outcome. Pain scores were highest at approximately 6 h after surgery, with significant group, time and group-by-time interaction effects. CONCLUSION: Moderate-to-severe pain is relatively common during the early postoperative period after paediatric laparoscopic pyeloplasty. Early risk identification, preoperative psychological support, appropriate regional analgesia and intensified pain assessment during the first 6-12 h may improve perioperative pain management. Prospective multicentre studies are warranted to validate these findings and develop clinically applicable risk-stratification strategies.
authors: Yueqin Xiang; Ruxia Min; Lianlian Ge; Lanzheng Bian

title: Factors Associated with Diagnostic Yield of Transbronchial Biopsy for Suspected Lung Cancer
abstract: Background: Transbronchial biopsy (TBB) is an important diagnostic approach for identifying peripheral lung lesions in suspected lung cancer patients. As is known, the lesion characteristics and radiological findings may influence its diagnostic yield. Therefore, this study aimed to identify factors associated with TBB diagnostic yield to help optimize patient selection and improve diagnostic success. Method: This cross-sectional study included 77 adults with suspected lung cancer who underwent TBB at Persahabatan Hospital between September and December 2024. Factors associated with TBB diagnostic yield, including tumor size, bronchus sign, and lesion location, were assessed. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was performed to determine the optimal tumor-size cutoff. A parsimonious multivariable logistic regression model including tumor size and bronchus sign was used to identify independent factors associated with a positive TBB result. Results: The overall diagnostic yield of TBB was 63.6%. In bivariate analysis, tumor size ≥2.95 cm and the presence of a bronchus sign were significantly associated with a positive TBB result. ROC analysis demonstrated modest discrimination for tumor size (AUC=0.693; 95% CI=0.562–0.824; P=0.005), with a cutoff of 2.95 cm yielding 87.8% sensitivity and 53.6% specificity. Lesions ≥2.95 cm had a higher diagnostic yield than lesions <2.95 cm (76.8% vs. 28.6%; OR=8.27; 95% CI=2.67–25.65; P<0.001). In multivariable analysis, tumor size ≥2.95 cm remained independently associated with a positive TBB result (aOR=6.33; 95% CI=1.91–20.83; P=0.002), whereas bronchus sign was not independently associated (aOR=0.36; 95% CI=0.07–1.77; P=0.206). Conclusion: Tumor size ≥2.95 cm was independently associated with a higher diagnostic yield of TBB in patients with suspected lung cancer. Tumor size may therefore be useful in identifying peripheral lung lesions more likely to yield a diagnostic transbronchial biopsy.
authors: Miraz Radhea Bagaskoro; Dicky Soehardiman; Ginanjar Arum Desianti

title: First Korean experience with shape-sensing robotic-assisted bronchoscopy integrated with mobile cone-beam CT: Results from the prospective ULSAN-ION study.
abstract: Shape-sensing robotic-assisted bronchoscopy (ssRAB) integrated with mobile cone-beam CT (mCBCT) has emerged as a promising platform for the diagnosis of peripheral pulmonary nodules (PPNs), with high diagnostic yield and low complication rates. However, no data have been reported in a Korean population. We evaluated the diagnostic yield and safety of ssRAB integrated with mCBCT in a Korean cohort. This prospective, single-center cohort (the ULSAN-ION study) enrolled patients undergoing ssRAB with integrated mCBCT from July 2025 to April 2026 (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT07057648). Diagnostic yield was assessed using the strict ATS/ACCP definition at the per-nodule and per-patient levels. A total of 111 patients with 140 PPNs were enrolled. Median age was 64.0 years (IQR, 55.5-69.5), and 51.4 % were male. Median nodule size was 14.0 mm (IQR, 10.0-19.2), and nodule morphology included solid (57.9 %), part-solid (28.6 %), and pure ground-glass opacity (13.6 %). A CT bronchus sign was absent in 70.7 % of nodules. mCBCT was performed in 88.6 % of nodules, with tool-in-lesion confirmation in 77.9 % and an overall tool-to-lesion rate of 99.1 %. Per-nodule diagnostic yield was 85.0 % (119/140) and per-patient diagnostic yield was 90.1 % (100/111). A malignant diagnosis was established in 75.7 % of patients, most commonly adenocarcinoma, and a specific benign diagnosis in 14.4 %. Pneumothorax occurred in 4.5 % of patients, with chest tube insertion required in 2.7 %. Airway bleeding (Nashville Grade ≥ 2) occurred in 1.8 %, with no Grade ≥ 3 events. This first prospective Korean experience demonstrates that ssRAB integrated with mCBCT achieves high diagnostic yield with an acceptable safety profile for PPN diagnosis.
authors: Ganghee Chae; Chul Park; Jin Hyoung Kim; Seung Won Ra; Kwang Won Seo; Yangjin Jegal; Hee Jeong Cha; Taehoon Lee

title: Frameless VarioGuide biopsy for pediatric brainstem lesions in the molecular era: diagnostic performance and workflow characteristics in a comparative single-center series
abstract: BACKGROUND: Molecular characterization has become essential for the diagnosis and treatment of pediatric brainstem lesions. While frame-based stereotactic and robotic-assisted biopsies are well established, comparative data on frameless VarioGuide biopsy for pediatric brainstem lesions remain scarce. This study evaluated the diagnostic performance, safety, and workflow characteristics of frameless VarioGuide biopsy compared with frame-based stereotactic and ROSA-assisted techniques. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed all pediatric patients (≤ 18 years) who underwent stereotactic biopsy of a brainstem lesion at a single tertiary neurosurgical center between 2016 and 2026. Patients were grouped according to biopsy technique (frameless VarioGuide, frame-based stereotaxy, or ROSA-assisted biopsy). Diagnostic yield, molecular diagnostic yield, complications, operative times, and workflow parameters were analyzed. RESULTS: Twenty-two pediatric patients met inclusion criteria. Six underwent frameless VarioGuide biopsy, nine frame-based stereotactic biopsy, and seven ROSA-assisted biopsy. Overall diagnostic and molecular diagnostic yields were 95%. Diagnostic and molecular diagnostic yields were 100% with VarioGuide, 89% with frame-based stereotactic biopsy, and 100% with ROSA-assisted biopsy, without statistically significant differences between groups (p = 0.62). Median operative times were similar among groups (32, 36, and 25 min, respectively; p = 0.28). However, preoperative setup time differed significantly, with the shortest duration observed in the VarioGuide cohort (40.5 min) compared with ROSA-assisted biopsy (64 min) and frame-based stereotaxy (112 min; p = 0.002). Despite the absence of intraoperative neuropathological assessment, all VarioGuide procedures yielded diagnostically and molecular-pathologically informative tissue. No procedure-related hemorrhage, infection, permanent neurological deficit, or procedure-related mortality were observed. CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory single-center cohort, frameless VarioGuide biopsy achieved high diagnostic and molecular diagnostic yields without permanent procedure-related morbidity and was associated with shorter preoperative setup time. These findings support further evaluation of frameless VarioGuide biopsy as a workflow-efficient approach for tissue acquisition in pediatric brainstem lesions.
authors: Sepide Kashefiolasl; Karsten Lachner; Christian Joerg Braun; Katharina Johanna Weber; Luciana Porto; Marcus Czabanka; Tobias Finger

title: From imaging enhancement to surgical autonomy: the evolutionary role of nanotechnology in AI-driven robotic surgery
abstract: Robot-assisted minimally invasive surgery provides stable visualisation and manipulation, but direct access to local tissue state remains limited. Lesion boundaries, mechanics, molecular activity and microenvironmental changes are often inferred from conventional feedback. This review evaluates how nano-enabled imaging, flexible and local sensing, and micro/nanorobotic intervention may extend signals and localised actions in robot-assisted procedures. We organise the evidence along an information-flow framework: signal acquisition, processing or computational interpretation, task-relevant state estimation, conversion into a decision variable or control-relevant input, and feedback-guided robotic action. Processing may involve calibration, signal processing, computational modelling, conventional machine learning, deep learning or artificial intelligence (AI)-based methods. The evidence reviewed is strongest for localised signal acquisition and supervised intervention. Selected forms of computational interpretation have been demonstrated, and localisation- or motion-derived geometric states enter feedback controllers in some systems. By contrast, biochemical, spectral, tactile and physiological states are usually displayed, analysed offline or returned through human-facing feedback; they rarely modify an online surgical controller. Closed-loop navigation in phantoms, surrogate-device studies and constrained navigation autonomy therefore represent partial control capabilities, not clinically relevant surgical autonomy. The principal missing transitions are robust validation of task-relevant tissue states, uncertainty-aware conversion of those states into control inputs, and safe action within realistic surgical workflows. Near-term clinical use is more likely to centre on bounded nano-enabled sensing or intervention modules embedded within supervised procedures. Progress towards bounded task autonomy will require reproducibility, material safety, workflow compatibility, explicit human supervision and prospective evidence of patient and task benefits.
authors: Jiahao Zhu; Shengcheng Tai; Zhihang Zhang; Ruicheng Wu; Dengxiong Li; Xiaodong Jin

title: Fully automatic airway segmentation in CT images via dual-stage neural network with topology-constrained centerline completion
abstract: Background: Precise segmentation of airways from computed tomography (CT) images is critical for pre-procedural planning in navigational bronchoscopy; however, existing methods often suffer from distal branch fractures and morphological losses due to slender diameters, low contrast, and noise. To address these limitations and achieve accurate, topologically complete airway segmentation, this study proposed a novel dual-stage neural network with topology-constrained centerline completion. Methods: A two-stage centerline-guided network (TSC-Net) was developed that innovatively combines centerline structural similarity (CSS) loss and centerline overlap rate (COR) loss. CSS loss maintains the continuity of airway tree structures by strengthening centerline morphological constraints, while COR loss enhances global centerline overlap to ensure branch integrity. Additionally, a topology-difference-driven fracture-region completion mechanism was adopted to adaptively repair the fracturedand misclassified areas. The model employs a residual UNet (ResUNet) backbone integrated with an atrous spatial pyramid pooling (ASPP) module to capture multi-scale contextual features and adopts a two-stage training strategy in which the encoder is frozen during stage 2 while the decoder is fine-tuned using dynamically adjusted loss weights. This strategy enables targeted optimization of discontinuous regions without compromising globally well-predicted areas. Results: Experiments on the Airway Tree Modeling Challenge 2022 (ATM'22), Lung Image Database Consortium and Image Database Resource Initiative (LIDC-IDRI), Extraction of Airways from CT (EXACT'09), and private datasets showed that TSC-Net achieved a Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) of 93.2%±2.1%, significantly outperforming SwinUNETR (92.9%±3.6%, P<0.05), nnUNet (91.2%±1.2%, P<0.05), and UNet (75.6%±4.3%, P<0.05). The tree-length detection (TD) rate reached 95.5%±4.2%, and the branch detection (BD) rate reached 92.6%±3.6%, both of which were significantly higher than those of all baseline methods (P<0.01). Moreover, the segmented distal branches exhibited continuous and smooth morphology. Conclusions: Overall, our method significantly enhanced both segmentation accuracy and distal branch integrity in automated CT-based airway segmentation through multi-dimensional feature enhancement, topological constraint optimization, and a dynamic completion mechanism. This method holds great promise for pre-procedural planning in robotic-assisted bronchoscopy by enabling accurate visualization of peripheral airways and facilitating navigation to distant pulmonary targets.
authors: Harmony Yuan; Yuan Cheng; Chengxi Yan; Jiangang Chen; Qian Ding; Ying Zhou; Minglei Yang
venue: Quantitative Imaging in Medicine and Surgery

title: Fulminant Emphysematous Hepatic Abscesses Due to Clostridium perfringens With Massive Intravascular Hemolysis: A Case Report
abstract: Clostridium perfringens is a gram-positive, anaerobic, gas-forming bacterium that can cause fulminant sepsis.Its alpha-toxin may induce massive intravascular hemolysis, and gas-forming hepatic infection with this organism often progresses to death within hours.An 80-year-old man presented to the emergency department with acute epigastric pain radiating to the back, tachycardia, hypertension, and fever.Triple-phase computed tomography demonstrated two gasforming hepatic abscesses in segments 7 and 8 with portal venous gas, while the gallbladder appeared normal.He developed a severe high anion gap metabolic acidosis, hyperkalemia, and indirect hyperbilirubinemia with a low haptoglobin and a rapid hemoglobin drop, consistent with massive intravascular hemolysis.Percutaneous drainage could not be performed because of rapid hemodynamic deterioration.He suffered a cardiac arrest with transient return of spontaneous circulation, followed by a second, fatal arrest two hours and 11 minutes after presentation.Blood cultures drawn at presentation grew C. perfringens, Enterococcus faecalis, and Serratia marcescens, and post-mortem examination with culture of the gallbladder wall identified the gallbladder as the primary source of infection.This case illustrates that gas-forming hepatic abscesses combined with unexplained hemolysis should immediately raise suspicion of C. perfringens sepsis and that a radiologically normal gallbladder does not exclude it as the source.Given the extremely compressed clinical course, early recognition and emergent source control are critical.
authors: Ritchie Mulleman; Annelies Truyen; Koen Monsieurs

title: GPU-resident Execution for Timing-predictable Sensor Processing Systems
abstract: Real-time embedded systems increasingly place GPU-accelerated processing of high-bandwidth sensor streams inside closed-loop systems, but the CPU (the host) remains the primary orchestrator of each iteration. The host observes sensor inputs, submits CUDA work, waits for completion, and commits actuation. This host-mediated path exposes the closed-loop end-to-end latency to I/O interrupts, host scheduler decisions, and CUDA API overheads even after common host-side mitigations such as GPU-memory RDMA or CPU core isolation. This paper presents GPU-resident Execution, a new execution model for real-time sensor processing pipelines that keeps I/O and GPU execution in a long-lived device-resident loop. Sensor inputs arrive in GPU memory, trigger GPU-side processing, and reach GPU-visible output endpoints without any host wakeups. We implement the model in the NVIDIA Holoscan C++ framework and provide reference components for building GPU-resident applications. We evaluate our system on NVIDIA GPUs and SoCs with inference, host-contention, multi-loop, and streaming camera workloads. On an industry-grade 1080p, 60 Hz real-time camera-to-display application, GPU-resident Execution reduces photon-to-display jitter from 4.83 ms to 0.66 ms (7.3x) relative to a CPU-driven GPU-memory RDMA baseline and reduces software-processing jitter from 1.70 ms to 0.01 ms (170x).

title: Genomic tracking of Campylobacter jejuni along poultry and pig value chains in Northeast India: Implications for food safety
abstract: Campylobacter jejuni is the predominant causative agent of human campylobacteriosis. A total of 864 samples (poultry cloacal swabs, chicken intestine, chicken meat, pig rectal swab, pig intestine, pork) were screened for the presence of C. jejuni using standard methods. A total of 27 isolates were confirmed with PCR with an overall occurrence rate of 3.13%. Highest isolation rates were from chicken intestine samples (9.72%), followed by pork (7.64%) and chicken meat (1.39%). Resistance levels were high towards nalidixic acid, tetracycline, ampicillin and ciprofloxacin. Multidrug-resistance and biofilm formation featured in 30.77% and 53.84% isolates, respectively. Genomic characterization identified the highest presence of T86I mutation in gyrA and cmeABC system. The isolates were abundant with important virulence genes such as cdtABC, wlan, neuABC and cstIII . The isolates belonged to diverse Penner serotypes and MLST types with ST 353 complex being the predominant clonal complex. Phylogenetic analysis indicated tendency of the genomes with similar ST/CC to cluster together and indicated wide genetic diversity . To the best of our knowledge, this serves as the first genome submission of C. jejuni from porcine sources of India. Further, this study underscores the need for exploiting modern technologies, including genomics, to study various food-borne pathogens.
authors: Arockiasamy Arun Prince Milton; Kandhan Srinivas; Heiborkie Shilla; Balusamy Dhayananth; Samir Das; G Bhuvana Priya; Sandeep Ghatak

title: Haematological alterations in dogs with canine distemper virus-associated respiratory tract infection in Guwahati, Assam
abstract: Canine distemper is a multisystemic viral disease of dogs in which the blood picture changes with the stage of infection and with secondary complications. This study evaluated the haematological alterations in dogs with respiratory tract infection associated with canine distemper virus (CDV) under field conditions in Guwahati, Assam, India. Twelve dogs formed two groups of six: dogs with respiratory signs that were positive for CDV antigen in a rapid immunochromatographic test of nasal and conjunctival swabs (CDV group) and apparently healthy dogs (control group). Haemoglobin (Hb), total erythrocyte count (TEC), packed cell volume (PCV), thrombocyte count, total leukocyte count (TLC), and differential leukocyte percentages were measured with an automated haematology analyser. Groups were compared by the independent samples t-test, with P < 0.05 considered significant. Dogs in the CDV group had significantly (P < 0.01) lower Hb (42.3%), TEC (32.3%), PCV (25.5%), and thrombocyte count (40.3%) than the control group, and all four values were below the canine reference limits. The TLC was significantly (P < 0.01) higher (46.2%), with higher percentages of granulocytes and monocytes and a lower percentage of lymphocytes. The absolute granulocyte (14.45 × 103/µL) and monocyte (1.68 × 103/µL) counts estimated from the group means exceeded the upper reference limits, whereas the estimated lymphocyte count (1.77 × 103/µL) remained within the reference interval. The results indicate anaemia, thrombocytopenia, and granulocytic leukocytosis with monocytosis in CDV-infected dogs and suggest that the fall in lymphocytes was relative and not absolute.

title: Health Care Teams Under Pressure: The Impact of Complexity on Team Cognition and Team Performance
abstract: Healthcare teams play a central role in delivering care to patients and their families. Teamwork has been shown to be directly related to clinical performance and patient outcomes, making it essential that these teams receive appropriate training, feedback, and assessment. These teams work in complex, dynamic environments characterized by changing team membership, time pressures, and large amounts of information that may be ambiguous, missing, or unknown. These characteristics make it difficult to fully capture team-level performance. Despite the critical role of healthcare teams, most approaches to measuring team performance are static, capturing what teams do rather than how or why performance emerges. This study investigated the dynamics of team cognition in complex, dynamic environments. Using a concurrent mixed methods design with a qualitative strand nested within the quantitative strand, this observational study addressed three questions: 1) What patterns exist in team communication and coordination behaviours, and how do these vary with team experience and case complexity 2) How does the rate of team cognition mediate the relationship between case complexity and team performance, 3) What insights do teams’ reflections and reflexive practices provide into the cognitive processes that shape their performance. Data were collected from video recordings of flight paramedic teams performing simulated scenarios, demographic surveys, reflective interviews, and performance scores. Lag sequential analysis (LSA) was used to identify significant patterns of behaviour, and mediation analysis was used to determine whether the rate of team cognition mediated the relationship between case complexity and team performance. Thematic analysis of the post-simulation interviews provided additional insight into the cognitive processes underlying team performance. Findings showed that communication is central to developing shared understanding. Teams relied on adaptive coordination to respond to the changing environment. Empirical evidence shows that behavioural sequences were observable, forming a part of paramedic clinical practice, and varying by team experience. These findings provide a preliminary perspective on team cognition and team performance in dynamic environments.
authors: de Vries, Ingrid

title: How exposed is work to robotics? Occupational, industry, and geographic measures
abstract: Exposure indices that map technical capabilities onto occupational abilities have become a standard tool for anticipating how AI may reshape work, but existing measures either cover software AI or proxy robotics through patents and installation data that reflect the industrial robots of past decades. We construct the first abilities-based exposure measures for robotics and physical AI, and the first to span occupations, industries, and geographies. Following the framework of Felten et al. (2018, 2021), we build a robotics capability taxonomy of 16 capabilities in eight domains from 78 academic, industry, and standards sources, use a large language model to score the relatedness of each capability to the 52 ONET work abilities, and aggregate to Robotics Occupational Exposure (ROE) for 774 occupations, Robotics Industry Exposure (RIE) for 250 NAICS industries, and county-level Robotics Geographic Exposure (RGE). We find that robotics exposure concentrates in physically intensive work such as construction, farming, transportation, and production, and in industries such as logging, mining, trucking, and warehousing. Unlike generative-AI exposure, ROE is higher in occupations with lower wages, lower education requirements, and less creative-ability content. Physical collaboration and assistance, terrain-based locomotion, grasping and handling, and task and functional reasoning move the exposure ranking most, yet no single capability carries the index. Because the measures capture technical relatedness rather than readiness, cost, or adoption, they should be read as an upper bound on where physical automation could affect work.
authors: Sebastian Sartor; Robert Seamans; Neil Thompson

title: Humoral Immunity and Variant Cross-Reactivity Following Asymptomatic and Symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 Infection and Vaccination in Young Adults (The ACE Cohort)
abstract: Abstract Purpose Asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection was a driving force of the COVID-19 pandemic, acting as a silent transmitter of the virus. The question of whether asymptomatic immunity differs from symptomatic immunity remains, as existing studies fail to recruit ‘well-defined’ asymptomatic individuals. Here, we conducted a longitudinal cohort study to evaluate humoral responses to infection and vaccination in asymptomatic predominantly young adults identified as part of the Asymptomatic COVID-19 in Education [ACE] cohort. Methods Asymptomatic testing services, located at three UK universities, identified asymptomatic adults who were subsequently recruited with age- and sex-matched symptomatic and uninfected controls. Blood and saliva samples were collected after SARS-CoV-2 Wuhan infection, and again after vaccination. Over 500 participants were recruited, and their IgG and IgA titres were measured in response to 5 Variants of Concern. Results Pre-vaccination, asymptomatic individuals exhibit significantly lower IgG responses to four of the tested variants; Wuhan, Alpha, Beta, and Delta, compared to symptomatic individuals; these differences diminished post-vaccination. In addition, there were key differences in terms of IgG cross-reactivity, where symptomatic individuals displayed stronger IgG cross-reactivity than asymptomatic and uninfected individuals, alluding to better protection from emerging variants. Individuals without prior natural infection displayed reduced IgG responses compared to symptomatic individuals, to all variants, post-vaccination. Despite their low IgG, salivary IgA levels in uninfected individuals were high, pre-vaccination. Conclusion This work demonstrates the requirement of vaccinations to enhance weaker IgG responses but also highlights that vaccines need to be constantly adapted to overcome viral evolution, particularly with more done to improve mucosal delivery options for respiratory viruses to enhance IgA responses.

title: Impact of Nasopharyngeal Swab Freezing Storage on the De-tection of Common Respiratory Viral Molecular Targets
abstract: Archived respiratory specimens are valuable for retrospective diagnostic studies, although long-term storage may affect viral RNA detection. This study evaluated nasopharyngeal swabs (NPS) stored at −80 °C for at least one year and retested using automated molecular assays with different multiplexing formats. Qualitative agreement with initial results and changes in cycle threshold (Ct) values were assessed, with discordant results investigated using an independent assay. SARS-CoV-2 showed the highest stability (positive percent agreement, PPA: 97.1–98.6%; mean Ct increase: 2.8–3.4), followed by respiratory syncytial virus (RSV; PPA: 88.4–97.1%; mean Ct increase: 1.75–4.50) and influenza virus (PPA: 80.0–92.9%; mean Ct increase: 5.48–7.92). Ct increases were significant for all viral targets. Differences across assay configurations suggested that assay formulation and target characteristics may influence post-storage detection. NPS aliquots stored at −80 °C remain useful for retrospective molecular testing, although target- and assay-dependent signal loss should be considered when interpreting results from archived specimens. title: In situ polymerized monolith tips for reproducible, format-flexible proteomic sample preparation applied to biofluids
abstract: Sample preparation increasingly sets the throughput and reproducibility of mass spectrometry (MS)-based proteomics. StageTips (stop-and-go extraction tips) and variants thereof have long been common implements to purify samples, and we recently extended the concept to solid-phase extraction capture (SPEC) tips, in which the entire digestion takes place in sub-microliter volumes. We replace the hand-packed bed with a monolith photopolymerized directly inside the pipette tip from a defined recipe (pSPEC), implemented here with strong anion-exchange (SAX) chemistry. A liquid-handling robot casts 384 tunable tips in minutes, at low cost and in any format, adding negligibly to the workflow's variance. Across biofluids, pSPEC added ∼20% more identifications than in-solution digestion of plasma and reached 3,500 protein groups from a single injection of healthy urine and 4,800 from saliva at 100 samples per day, depths usually requiring depletion or fractionation. The same light-cast approach should extend to single cells, affinity capture, and population-scale studies.

title: Integrated Microfluidic CRISPR-Based Diagnostic Device for Rapid Testing of HPVs.
abstract: Screening for high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) is a pivotal strategy for the prevention of invasive cervical cancer, particularly in resource-constrained settings. In this study, we developed a CRISPR-based compact automated real-time detection system, termed Ccard, for rapid testing of HPV16, HPV18, and the internal reference gene GAPDH through a streamlined workflow. A simple room-temperature treatment efficiently releases nucleic acids directly from swab samples, bypassing the need for extraction. The mixture was driven through the channels and loaded into the reaction chambers on the microfluidic chip by a vacuum pump. The lyophilized reagents in the reaction zone of the microfluidic chip were redissolved. The system subsequently performs a single-step RPA-CRISPR/Cas13a reaction, with real-time detection enabled by an Internet of Things device. The assay achieved detection within 30 min, with a limit of detection (LOD) of 5 copies/µL for both HPV16 and HPV18. Validation with clinical samples demonstrated high sensitivity (96.8% for HPV16 and 100% for HPV18) and 100% specificity. These results highlight the reliability, precision, and strong potential of the Ccard system for rapid testing of HR-HPVs.
authors: Tianci Wang; Lingyun Li; Yunxiang Wang; Yongjun Han; Teng Li; Chaoran Yu; Yufeng Lou; Zhen Rong; Kai Lin; Shengqi Wang

title: Integrity Detection and Characterization of Malicious Injections in RAVEN II
abstract: The increasing adoption of robotic systems in surgery, together with the expanding range of procedures they can support and the growing level of autonomy they provide, has substantially increased the complexity of surgical robots. As these systems integrate more sensors, controllers, communication interfaces, and model-driven control components, their attack surface continues to expand. A compromise of the integrity of a surgical robot can therefore cause unintended robot behavior and potentially threaten patient safety. In this paper, we characterize the detection boundary of malicious injections on RAVEN II using a public dataset that pairs the platform's telemetry with external high-resolution encoder ground truth. We identify three injection points spanning the command and observation paths and evaluate three injection patterns with increasing temporal dispersion. To capture different detection behaviors, we perform detection at two timescales: the window scale and the session scale. Rather than reporting detection rates at an arbitrarily chosen threshold, we quantify, for each injection point and injection pattern, the smallest end-effector deviation that can be resolved while maintaining an alarm rate acceptable for surgical operation. Our results show that detectability is strongly influenced by how the injected deviation is distributed over time. An abrupt step can be detected at deviations well below the 1 mm clinical tolerance, whereas the same overall deviation spread across a window or a session can remain hidden from single-window statistics. The open source code can be found at http://github.com/RAVENIIROS/RAVENIIIntegrity.
authors: Xingli Zhang; Diba Afroze; Fei Hu; Xiali Hei

title: Intracardiac echocardiography during invasive electrophysiological procedures
abstract: Intracardiac echocardiography (ICE) is an imaging technique that provides real-time, detailed visualization of intracardiac structures during various interventional procedures performed in the electrophysiology laboratory. Over the past decades, ICE has evolved beyond simply assisting with transseptal puncture, becoming an auxiliary tool in numerous aspects of cardiac interventions. This scientific statement offers a comprehensive, systematic overview of current applications of ICE across different clinical scenarios. The existing evidence regarding the benefits of ICE is primarily derived from observational studies, which complicates the formulation of definitive advice for its clinical use. Thus, this document aims to serve as a practical roadmap, emphasizing the key benefits of the technique. The document covers fundamental principles of ICE imaging, standardized views, its role in transseptal puncture, ablation of supraventricular and ventricular arrhythmias, reduction of procedural radiation, early detection and management of periprocedural complications, identification of infective endocarditis, and the role of ICE for endomyocardial biopsy and left atrial appendage occlusion procedures.
authors: Petr Peichl; Stylianos E. Tzeis; Marta Skowrońska; Dimitrios Asvestas; Jakub Marek Baran; Michela Casella; Rubén Casado-Arroyo; Matevž Jan; Josef Kautzner; Jens Erik Nielsen‐Kudsk; Péter Kupó; Andrej Pernat; Nándor Szegedi; Vedran Velagić

title: Intratumoral Therapeutic Injections for Lung Cancer: Current Evidence, Personalized Therapeutic Approaches, and Future Directions
abstract: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide despite significant advances in surgery, radiation therapy, targeted therapies, and immunotherapy. Although systemic therapies have improved outcomes across all stages of disease, treatment efficacy is often limited by inadequate intratumoral drug delivery, systemic toxicities, treatment resistance, and disease heterogeneity. Intratumoral therapeutic injections (ITIs), including intratumoral chemotherapy (ITC), have emerged as a promising locoregional therapeutic strategy designed to overcome these limitations through direct delivery of antineoplastic agents into tumor tissue. Advances in bronchoscopic technologies, particularly endobronchial ultrasound-guided transbronchial needle injection (EBUS-TBNI), robotic bronchoscopy, electromagnetic navigation bronchoscopy, and cone-beam computed tomography guidance, have expanded the feasibility of delivering therapeutic agents to central and peripheral pulmonary lesions. Most of the evidence for ITI comes from case reports, prospective or retrospective studies with small sample sizes, and non-randomized, single-arm clinical trials. While further evidence is needed, especially in the form of randomized controlled trials, the current literature shows promise in the areas of malignant airway obstruction and isolated mediastinal and hilar recurrence. Studies have also assessed the utility of novel formulations, including large surface area microparticle paclitaxel (LSAM-PTX). Potential future applications of ITI include use as neoadjuvant therapy, as part of combination therapy with radiation and immune checkpoint inhibitors, and in cases of oligoprogressive disease and medically inoperable tumors. Novel formulations, including large surface area microparticle paclitaxel (LSAM-PTX), sustained-release drug delivery systems, and the potential use of immunomodulatory agents, have further enhanced the therapeutic potential of local drug administration. Furthermore, advances in radiomics, artificial intelligence, computational drug distribution modeling, and biomarker-driven patient selection have positioned ITI within the broader framework of personalized cancer therapy. This review summarizes the biological rationale, technical approaches, clinical evidence, and future directions of ITI in lung cancer, emphasizing its evolving role as a precision therapeutic platform capable of providing effective cancer treatment alongside established therapeutic paradigms.
authors: Tatiana Maser; Moath Bani Salem; Osama Al Zoubi; Alexandria Iakovidis; Miguel Castro; Jingjing Chen; Pankit Patel; Karthik Vijayan; Hiren J. Mehta

title: Isolation and Identification of Microorganisms Associated with Automated Teller Machines in Calabar Metropolis
abstract: The metallic keyboards of automated teller machines situated within Calabar metropolis were investigated for microbial contamination due to their vast dermal contact by multiple users. Swab sticks soaked with normal sterile saline were used to collect specimens from the keypads. Isolation was done on nutrient agar and eosine methylene blue (EMB) for bacteria and Sabouraud dextrose agar for fungi using standard microbiological procedures. Identification of microorganisms was done using colonial, microscopic and biochemical characteristics. The results reveal that these machines that serve as cash dispensing device can be a potential disease dispensing machines as samples analyzed revealed bacterial isolates such as Staphylococcus spp (32%)), Bacillus spp (24%), Escherichia spp (20%), Pseudomonas spp (18%) and Salmonella spp (6%) while fungal isolates of the samples analyzed include microorganisms such as Rhizopus spp (56%), Aspergillus spp, (25%) and Penicillium spp (19%). These findings necessitate the need for adequate personal hygiene by users and frequent routine cleaning of these machines by the bank’s authorities is highly recommended.
authors: Chinyere Osondu-Anyanwu

title: Just-in-time volumetric imaging: Learning 2D-3D thoracic motion models during image-guided interventions
abstract: Despite two decades of innovation, cutting-edge bronchoscopic techniques still fail to yield clear diagnostic decisions in 30% of cases and miss malignancies in 20% of cases. Intraprocedural 3D imaging drastically improves both tool positioning and diagnostic yield. However, each 3D spin represents a static snapshot of an anatomy that is continuously evolving as the patient is ventilated throughout the procedure. Here, we propose just-in-time volumetric imaging, in which a patient-specific 2D--3D motion model is trained on pre-intervention scans before it is needed and then supplies volumetric images from single fluoroscopic projections during sampling. Given the inspiration-hold CBCT already acquired for navigation and an additional motion-inclusive CBCT, our optimization regime named VoxelMap-DualScan (VM-DS), solves a low-rank motion model by alternating least squares and then amortizes it into a projection encoder trained on synthesized projections with known motion, all within a 10-minute window. On eight held-out cases from the public DIR-Lab 4DCT dataset, VM-DS achieved a mean landmark target registration error of 2.8 mm, a structural similarity index of 0.95 and a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 37.7 dB. Accuracy was maintained when reducing the number of projections used for training from 227 to 23. Inference takes 1.5 ms per projection, making the framework suitable for real-time use during image-guided interventions. Code will be made available at https://github.com/Image-X-Institute/Voxelmap/tree/VM-DS
authors: Nicholas Hindley

title: LC−MS-Based Chlorine-Signature Query Engine Strategy for Automated Discovery of Phosphate-Containing Metabolites
abstract: Abstract Comprehensive profiling of phosphate-containing compounds (PCCs) in untargeted metabolomics remains challenging due to their high hydrophilicity, poor separation, and low stability, which hampers high-throughput screening from large-scale liquid chromatography−mass spectrometry (LC−MS) datasets. Herein, an LC-MS-based chlorine-tagging strategy integrated with a Chlorine Signature Query Engine (Cl-SQE) was established for the rapid identification of potential PCCs in complex matrices. The novel derivatization reagent, [5-(2-chlorophenyl)isoxazol-3-yl]methyl amine (ClXIMA), can react with phosphate groups on PCCs, such as nucleotides, sugar phosphates, glycerophosphates, and nucleotide sugars under mild conditions, thereby markedly enhancing reversed-phase retention and separation resolution. More importantly, the incorporation of chlorine, identifiable by its characteristic isotopic peak pattern, provides a unique digital signature in the mass spectra. Leveraging these features, Cl-SQE, a data mining program, was developed to systematically and automatically extract candidate PCCs from large-scale datasets. By applying this strategy to liver tissues from a mouse model of cholestasis, 318 potential ClXIMA derivatives were screened out, and 189 metabolites were identified or tentatively assigned. Statistical analysis revealed significant disturbances in nucleotide metabolism, addressing a critical gap in phospho-metabolomic profiling for cholestatic disease and revealing dysregulated nucleotide homeostasis as a potential feature of cholestasis-associated metabolic remodeling. Overall, this platform facilitates the discovery of PCCs in complex matrices and provides new insights into the pathogenesis of cholestasis and other clinical diseases.
authors: Xiaolin Chen; Yujie Li; Lanjia Ao; Xiqing Bian; H.K. Zeng; Na Li; Jian‐Lin Wu

title: Large Language Models for Automated AGREE II Quality Appraisal of Sepsis Clinical Practice Guidelines: A Methodological Comparative Study
abstract: Abstract Background Large language models (LLMs) show promise for automated clinical practice guideline (CPG) quality appraisal, but multi-model performance variability, domain-specific bias patterns, and computational efficiency remain poorly characterized. This study systematically benchmarked six LLMs against human expert consensus for AGREE II appraisal of sepsis CPGs. Methods We benchmarked six LLMs (Doubao-2.0, DeepSeek-V4, GPT-5.5, Gemini-3.1-Pro, Qwen-3.7, Mimo-V2.5) against a four-rater expert consensus (ICC = 0.829) for AGREE II appraisal of 11 sepsis CPGs (three runs per guideline; 198 assessments). Agreement was assessed by single-rater ICC(A,1), Pearson r, Lin's CCC, and Bland–Altman analysis; directional bias by FDR-corrected Wilcoxon tests. Results LLMs achieved moderate agreement with experts (ICC(A,1), 0.59–0.72; mean absolute error, 12.3%–17.3%), with score-range compression across models. Domain-specific bias was consistent: Applicability (D5) was the most under-scored (five of six models; median bias, − 25.0% to + 1.4%), whereas Rigour of Development (D3) tended to be over-scored (up to + 9.7%). Efficiency varied markedly: Mimo-V2.5 achieved the highest ICC (0.72), fewest tokens (68.3K), and fastest inference (15.0 s); Doubao-2.0 the lowest ICC (0.59) and slowest inference (130.2 s). Composite ranking (Mimo-V2.5 > Gemini-3.1-Pro > GPT-5.5 > Qwen-3.7 > DeepSeek-V4 > Doubao-2.0) was robust across weight schemes. Conclusions Contemporary LLMs achieve moderate agreement with human experts in AGREE II appraisal of sepsis CPGs but exhibit consistent domain-specific biases, particularly systematic under-scoring in Applicability. Performance does not scale with model size or general medical knowledge. LLMs are best positioned as triage and screening tools within a human–AI hybrid workflow rather than standalone evaluators.
authors: Tiantian Zhang; Xiaoming Zhang; Youji Zhu; Nuoyi Zhang; Liyin Zheng; Kaifeng Ye; Danping Wang

title: Large-scale characterization of the bovine virome reveals viral diversity and community patterns in Northwest China
abstract: Cattle play a critical role in global agriculture and food security while serving as hosts for diverse viruses with potential implications for animal and public health. To comprehensively characterize the bovine virome and its community patterns, we conducted a large-scale characterization of the beef cattle-associated virome in Northwest China using viral metagenomic sequencing. A total of 2,353 specimens, including nasal swabs, anal swabs, and serum, were collected from 794 cattle across 28 sites in Shaanxi, Gansu, and Ningxia, with nasal and anal swab specimens used for the metagenomic analyses. High-throughput sequencing identified viruses belonging to 14 phyla, 32 classes, 39 orders, 71 families, and 397 genera, revealing substantial viral diversity. Descriptive comparisons of the pooled libraries revealed differences in virome composition across geographic regions, farming systems, and sampling seasons, with the summer pool showing greater viral richness and contig abundance than the winter pool. Phylogenetic analyses revealed genetic relationships between several viral sequences detected in this study and viral lineages previously reported from humans and other animal hosts, raising hypotheses regarding broader host associations and potential cross-species transmission that require further investigation. Targeted PCR/RT-PCR screening and cell-culture-based virus characterization provided complementary validation of representative metagenomic findings and revealed frequent co-detection of multiple viral targets among the sampled cattle. Collectively, this study provides a large-scale characterization of the beef cattle-associated virome in Northwest China, expands current knowledge of viral diversity associated with beef cattle populations, and establishes a valuable resource for future virome surveillance, studies of viral evolution, and disease prevention.
authors: Lingling Jiang; Yunyi Kong; Gang Zhang; Pu Wang; Min Fang; Qiang Liu; Sinong Zhang; Yong Li

title: Limited efficacy of enrofloxacin against Mesomycoplasma ovipneumoniae infection in domestic lambs
abstract: Mesomycoplasma ovipneumoniae is an important respiratory pathogen in sheep that leads to pneumonia and reduced productivity, commonly upon co-infection with other opportunistic microbes. Whether M. ovipneumoniae infection can be successfully treated with antibiotics is unclear. Our pilot study evaluated the efficacy of enrofloxacin (Baytril ® ) for treating experimental M. ovipneumoniae infection in domestic lambs. Ten 3-month-old specific-pathogen-free lambs were randomly assigned to a treatment and an untreated control group. Lambs were inoculated with fresh nasal wash fluids from M. ovipneumoniae- positive sheep. After 4 weeks, the treatment group received enrofloxacin at 0.5 mg/kg in 200 mL of saline intranasally and 5 mg/kg subcutaneously on five consecutive days. Lambs were observed for an additional 4 weeks, with daily health scoring, weekly assessment of weight gain, and weekly nasal swab quantitative (q)PCR analysis for M. ovipneumoniae and Mannheimia haemolytica . Successful M. ovipneumoniae infection of all lambs was confirmed by qPCR 1 week after inoculation. While overall health scores and average daily weight gains were statistically similar between groups, enrofloxacin administration significantly accelerated the rate of body temperature decline over the post-treatment period ( P = 0.007). Interestingly, all treated lambs tested negative for M. ovipneumoniae by qPCR 1 week after treatment. However, there was a re-emergence of M. ovipneumoniae infection 2 weeks after treatment with 1/5 lambs testing positive, and 3/5 lambs tested positive 4 weeks after treatment. Co-infection with Mannheimia haemolytica was detected in all lambs, with a similar temporary suppression after enrofloxacin treatment. Endpoint tissue swab samples revealed variable qPCR detection of M. ovipneumoniae , with a trend for reduced infection of the lower respiratory tract in the treated lambs. However, middle ear swabs from all lambs tested qPCR-positive for M. ovipneumoniae , suggesting that the middle ear is a potential reservoir of this pathogen. Tissues collected after euthanasia showed reduced histopathological lung lesions in the enrofloxacin-treated group (Mann–Whitney U test, P = 0.032 ). Amongst four M. ovipneumoniae isolates recovered from the lung of one enrofloxacin-treated lamb, one isolate showed reduced susceptibility to enrofloxacin in vitro . Overall, our study showed that enrofloxacin treatment was only partially successful in reducing M. ovipneumoniae infection in domestic lambs.
authors: Sobha Sonar; Michael Throolin; Stephen Smith; Jonathon Sago; Eli T. Selong; Noah Adams; Jessica Dibbert; McKenna D. Quirk; Nathan J. Schaff; Helen Schwantje; Christian J. Posbergh; Diane Bimczok

title: Low-Cost IoT-Based Smart Blood Collection Bag Monitoring and Agitation System for Real-Time Hemovigilance
abstract: This paper presents the study, design, and development of a comprehensive, low-cost blood collection system. The proposed system is based on IoT technology and aims to improve the efficiency, safety, and standardization of blood donation procedures in clinical settings, while providing continuous monitoring, automated alerts, and centralized oversight. More specifically, the system consists of two components: the blood collection station and the information system. The blood collection station consists of two parts. The first part is a device that includes a load cell weighing unit which accurately measures the mass of a blood collection bag during collection. The device then continuously converts the measured weight into an estimated blood volume, thereby allowing for accurate monitoring of the progress of the blood donation. The second section consists of a mechanism for gently agitating the collected blood with the anticoagulant solution, with the aim of reducing the risk of clot formation during the procedure. The information system consists of a server that includes a database and web-based visualization software. The Wi-Fi protocol was used for data transmission. The heart of the system is a microcontroller that includes Wi-Fi connectivity and is responsible for collecting, processing, and transmitting data to the database. This enables simultaneous real-time monitoring of multiple blood collection stations through a central monitoring system. It can provide alarm notifications; for example, when the volume of collected blood reaches a predetermined threshold (e.g., 400 mL), the system can trigger both audible and visual alerts, ensuring an immediate response from medical and nursing staff. Through the visualization software, it is possible to monitor and record data, which can improve workflow coordination in blood donation centers and hospital settings. This approach achieves both a reduction in human error and the optimization of blood collection procedures.

Virtual Reality, Machine Learning, and Explainable Artificial Intelligence for pain management, objective pain assessment, and clinical decision support in vulnerable patient populations.To address the research questions defined above, the doctoral research pursues the following objectives: Objective 1: Virtual Reality for Pain Management and Rehabilitation To systematically evaluate the effectiveness, feasibility, and clinical applicability of Virtual Reality as a non-pharmacological intervention for pain management and rehabilitation, with specific emphasis on cancer-related pain and pulmonary rehabilitation.This objective further seeks to critically analyze and synthesize existing evidence in order to identify dominant technological trends, therapeutic strategies, methodological limitations, and research gaps in VR-based pain management studies.Particular attention is given to study design, outcome measures, levels of immersion, feasibility of clinical deployment, and realworld constraints, thereby establishing evidence-based directions for future VR research and clinical implementation.Objective 2: Machine Learning for Objective Pain Assessment To advance objective pain assessment methodologies by investigating Machine Learningbased approaches for facial image-and video-based pain intensity estimation, using state-ofthe-art deep learning techniques.This objective aims to systematically evaluate and benchmark different deep learning architectures, including convolutional, temporal, and transformer-based models, with respect to classification performance, robustness, generalization capability, computational efficiency,

title: Malaria-Associated Haematological Alterations Among Children Under Fifteen at Arthur Davison Children’s Hospital, Ndola, Copperbelt-Zambia
abstract: Background: Differentiating acute malaria from other non-malarial febrile illnesses presents a critical diagnostic and triage challenge in high-volume African pediatric referral centers. While general continental trends are well-documented, localized data mapping the precise cellular and hematological divergences across specific age groups remain limited. This study sought to quantify acute hematological alterations, compare pathogen-specific cellular signatures between malaria-positive and malaria-negative cohorts, and evaluate the relationship between host age and anaemia severity. Methods: An institutional, cross-sectional analytical study was conducted at Arthur Davison Children’s Hospital (ADCH) in Ndola, Zambia. A cohort of 200 febrile pediatric patients aged 0-15 years were enrolled. Screening for Plasmodium infection was performed using combined Pf/Pan RDT kits and gold-standard microscopic examination of Giemsa-stained peripheral blood smears. Comprehensive whole-blood profiles were processed within two hours of blood collection using a calibrated automated haematology analyzer (Sysmex XN series). Results: The institutional prevalence of laboratory-confirmed malaria was 18.0% (36/200 cases). Plasmodium falciparum monoinfection predominated, accounting for 88.9% (32/36) of positive cases, followed by P. malariae (8.3%) and P. ovale (2.8%). Early childhood cohorts experienced the highest vulnerability, with the 1–4 years age group harbouring 72.2% (26/36) of all cases and exhibiting the peak mean parasitemia density of 48,500 parasites/µL. Malaria-positive cohorts displayed profound cytopenias compared to malaria-negative cohorts, marked by a significant hemoglobin deficit (6.80 g/dL versus 12.56 g/dL; mean deficit of -6.06 g/dL) and depleted red blood cell counts (2.80 versus 4.71 × 10⁶/μL) secondary to accelerated hemolysis. Concurrently, absolute platelet counts were markedly lower in malaria cases (199.7 versus 314.4 × 10³/μL), indicating severe peripheral consumption. Conversely, the malaria-negative cohort exhibited a 1.97-fold increase in total white blood cell counts (13.40 versus 6.80 × 10³/μL), profiling a signature of marked leukocytosis suggestive of non-malarial bacterial or systemic infection mimics. Conclusions: Acute Plasmodium falciparum malaria drives severe, predictable hematological shifts in Zambian children, predominantly targeting toddlers aged 1–4 years with high-density parasitemia. The distinct physiological signatures identified profound anaemia and thrombocytopenia pairing with normal leukocyte counts, contrasted against the marked leukocytosis of malaria-negative febrile peers offer a robust diagnostic framework to improve emergency triage, accelerate targeted treatment, and optimize resource allocation in resource-limited tertiary care pipeline hubs.

title: Measles (rubeola) virus qualitative real-time reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction assay: development and clinical validation on an automated workflow.
abstract:
Introduction

Detection of Measles virus (MeV) RNA is an important method for confirming infection. This study described the clinical validation of a qualitative real-time reverse transcriptase-polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) assay for MeV detection.

Methods

A real-time RT-PCR assay was developed and validated using primers and probes previously reported in the literature. The assay was evaluated using reference materials, cultured virus, and previously tested clinical throat swab samples. An automated workflow was established for RNA extraction, RT-PCR amplification, and result reporting using robotic platforms and a real-time PCR instrument. The assay targets the measles nucleoprotein (N) and hemagglutinin (H) genes, with human RNase P gene used as an internal control.

Results

The MeV RT-PCR assay has a limit of detection of 500 genome copies per milliliter. The assay was tested against 85 different samples: 50 positive clinical samples and reference materials and 35 negative clinical samples or reference materials. All expected results were correctly identified, giving 100% sensitivity (50/50) and specificity (35/35). The assay showed 100% interassay and intra-assay reproducibility. No cross-reactivity was observed with other respiratory viruses or common bacterial and fungal pathogens.

Discussion

This automated measles RT-PCR assay demonstrated high accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and reproducibility.
authors: Yu L, Chen L, Dumas K, Weyandt N, Meyers M, Irwin P, Eitson JL, Schoggins JW, Park JY.

title: Metabolism of the scientific journal on domestic radiology
abstract: The purpose of this article is to present more fundamentally the natural metabolism of science and the scientific journal, partly using examples from radiology. The journal article is the main tool and practice of the researcher in converting personal knowledge into public knowledge for its verification and pragmatic realization. In national medicine and radiology, there is a problem of long-term preservation of knowledge (the work of scientists and state finances) and its accessibility against the backdrop of the emergence of new journals and their disappearance. If earlier there was a problem with the publication of articles due to the shortage of journals and the queue for publication, now there is a problem with the shortage of high-quality content articles. Virtually all significant results in the exact sciences (at least in the English-speaking world) can be found in the pages of just two journals: “Nature” and “Science”. Lotka’s law is mentioned in the aspect of the scientific literature citation system as a means of tracking the development of science. Attention is drawn to the formation of a new subspecialty – medical writers (since 1940). The replication crisis is described (possibly caused by human factors), a methodological crisis in which the results of many scientific studies are difficult or impossible to reproduce. The mobilization of science in the journal “Radiation diagnostics, radiation therapy” during the COVID-19 pandemic is considered using the example of articles “Low-dose radiation therapy for COVID-19 pneumonia”, “COVID-modulated emphysematous pyelonephritis against the background of severe course of oxygen-dependent covid pneumonia” та “Echocardiographic characteristics of complicated course of coronavirus infection in children (COVID-19) (review and portfolio)”. The bibliometrics of the journal “Radiology” (journal of the Radiological Society of North America.) are presented for comparison: the most viewed articles of 2021 and the most cited articles of 2021. It is demonstrated that the topic of the most cited articles of 2023 is artificial intelligence.
authors: Nikolay Kolotilov

title: Microbiological surveillance after automated reprocessing of gastrointestinal endoscopes in routine clinical practice: A prospective randomized microbiological surveillance study
abstract: Microbiological surveillance is used to monitor the quality of gastrointestinal endoscope reprocessing, but prospective data comparing automated endoscope reprocessor systems under routine workflow conditions remain limited. We conducted an exploratory, single-center, prospective randomized surveillance study of 222 endoscope-use episodes involving patient-used forward-viewing upper and lower gastrointestinal endoscopes. Endoscope-use episodes were allocated 1:1:1 to strongly acidic electrolyzed water, ozonated water, or peracetic acid using an Excel-generated random-number procedure (n = 74 each). Assigned reprocessing was performed after standardized bedside pre-cleaning and manual cleaning. Post-reprocessing samples were obtained from predefined external and internal sites. Surveillance success was defined as ≤20 colony-forming units per sample at all sampled sites and absence of predefined indicator organisms. Success was achieved in 67/74 (90.5%) strongly acidic electrolyzed-water episodes, 71/74 (95.9%) ozonated-water episodes, and 71/74 (95.9%) peracetic-acid episodes. Risk differences in surveillance success versus peracetic acid were -5.4 percentage points (95% confidence interval, -14.6 to 3.2) and 0.0 percentage points (95% confidence interval, -7.7 to 7.7), respectively. In exploratory post hoc non-inferiority analyses using a -5 percentage-point margin, non-inferiority was not demonstrated for either functional-water system. A -10 percentage-point margin supported ozonated water but not strongly acidic electrolyzed water. Post hoc scope-level sensitivity analyses were directionally consistent with the primary analysis and highlighted the influence of repeated failures in an individual physical endoscope. These findings should be interpreted as exploratory microbiological quality-assurance data, not as evidence of clinical infection risk or comparative clinical effectiveness. Study registration: University Hospital Medical Information Network Clinical Trials Registry (UMIN-CTR), UMIN000061627 (registered May 19, 2026; enrollment began November 8, 2024).
authors: Masayuki Kato; Hideki Hayashi; Nobuharu Hironaka; Masafumi Chiba; Takahiro Abe; Nana Shimamoto; Mamoru Ito; Masakuni Kobayashi; Kazuki Sumiyama

title: Microfluidic Extraction of Extracellular Vesicle-Associated Nucleic Acids for Downstream Molecular Analysis
abstract: Abstract Aim To develop a microfluidic workflow for extracting extracellular vesicle (EV)-associated nucleic acids (NAs) from biofluids, such as blood plasma and serum, for downstream molecular analysis. Methods Healthy serum and plasma samples were spiked with EVs obtained from Hec-1-A cells carrying defined mutations and characterized in accordance with MISEV guidelines. The spiked samples were then processed using either the standard centrifugation-based ExoGAG protocol or a microfluidic workflow. The latter combines ExoGAG mediated aggregation of EVs with mechanical entrapment of the resulting EV aggregates in a microfluidic filtration device (EVNA-chip). The retained material was washed and on-chip lysed to release its NA cargo. NAs were subsequently purified using a commercial silica column, producing an output suitable for molecular analysis through droplet digital PCR (ddPCR). Results The EVNA-chip recovery yield was 42.0 ± 4.28% and 38.1 ± 1.46% for double-stranded DNA (dsDNA) and microRNA respectively. The recovered dsDNA remained compatible with ddPCR detection of the KRAS p.G12D variant (c.35G>A) and with the assessment of MSI-associated alterations using BAT25, BAT26, NR21, NR24, and MONO27. The method was demonstrated for pilot cohort of patients with endometrial cancer. The RNA workflow supported reverse transcription and was demonstrated for the quantification of miR-X, a potential marker of Fabry disease, using patient samples and healthy controls. Conclusion Although recovery was lower than with the standard protocol, the centrifugation-free EVNA- chip workflow demonstrates the compatibility of the method with downstream NA molecular analyses and is advantageous for the development of an integrated, automated platform for EV-based liquid biopsy applications.

title: Microneedle Based Platforms for Glucose Monitoring: Current Status and Future Directions
abstract: Diabetes mellitus is a metabolic disease that requires continuous glucose monitoring to achieve glycemic control. However, current glucose monitoring technologies have many limitations and are often associated with adherence issues. Therefore, in this review, we considered some recent developments in biosensors using microneedles due to their non-invasive character and interstitial fluid measurement for real-time monitoring. The review highlights the use of nanomaterials in nanotechnology, the microfabrication methods, enzyme immobilization methods, and surface modification methods that lead to increased sensitivity and biocompatibility of the sensors. The review also emphasized the advances in clinical studies and the artifacts related to microneedle sensors, such as biofouling and signal drift. Moreover, the review specifically targeted the use of emerging technologies such as non-enzymatic sensing, multiplex biomarker detection, AI-based analysis, health monitoring, and a closed-loop insulin release system. The current review includes more than 100 peer-reviewed articles. It provides a thorough analysis of how microneedle-based biosensors can be considered a new approach for glucose detection that improves the quality of patients' lives. Collectively, all the recent advancements in microneedle-based biosensors have made them a new emerging platform for next-generation personalized medicine, along with a digital healthcare system.
authors: V. Sujan; Jobin Jose; Prachi Dwivedi; Naidulekha Aswani; Eyman Mohamed Eltayib

title: Mitigating lateral sensing blind spots: A dual-segment bronchoscopic robot with a bioinspired skin
abstract: Lateral force blind spots frequently trigger airway injuries during robotic bronchoscopy. Traditional sensing approaches lack fine spatial resolution, and single-segment robots suffer poor posture adjustment flexibility, worsening unmonitored tissue contact. We integrate a snake-scale-inspired 64-channel gradient piezoelectric film with a dual-segment manipulator to resolve lateral blind spots for secure bronchial navigation. The conformally wrapped sensor delivers fast (<10 ms), precise force detection ( R 2 > 0.98, RMSE < 0.145 N, CV < 2%) and filters bending pseudo-forces. The dual-segment design enables coordinated proximal-distal motion to avoid overcontact in tortuous lumens. Phantom and ex vivo porcine lung tests confirm real-time force localization, 5.0 N safety alarms, and autonomous tuning to keep contact forces below 3.0 N. This synergistic robot-sensor design supplies a translatable safety control strategy for flexible surgical manipulators.
authors: Qiqi Pan; Wenke Duan; Jingjing Luo; Lei Wang; Shijie Guo; Yongfei Feng; Hongbo Wang

title: Molecular detection of respiratory viruses from breath samples: Evaluation of nucleic acid extraction systems and PCR panels
abstract: Background Reliable and scalable molecular testing is essential for risk assessment and monitoring of respiratory viruses with epidemic or pandemic potential. The AveloMask Kit (Avelo) is a non-invasive sampling device that collects exhaled breath aerosols (XBA) using a high-performance filter, which can be released into a stabilizing buffer for nucleic acid preservation. Detection of viral nucleic acids in breath samples remains challenging, as viral loads are typically lower than in conventional upper-respiratory swabs. Therefore, optimizing extraction and polymerase chain reaction (PCR) workflows is critical to maximizing analytical sensitivity. Methods In this proof-of-concept study, we compared the nucleic acid extraction efficiency of ELITe InGenius® (ELITech) and QIAsymphony (Qiagen) automated platforms in combination with an in-house real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) panel and a commercial PCR panel (RespiFinder® 2Smart, Pathofinder). Using synthetic ribonucleic acid (RNA) standards, we determined the limit of detection (LOD) for severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), influenza A, influenza B, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) as a performance indicator for both extraction platforms and PCR panels. As proof-of-concept, we analyzed seven XBA samples from infected individuals, eight from healthy controls, and one from a person recovering from a cold. Results Our results demonstrate that ELITe InGenius and QIAsymphony provide comparable extraction efficiencies without negatively impacting downstream RT-qPCR. The combination of QIAsymphony and RespiFinder 2Smart achieved LODs below 100 viral copies/mL and detected all pathogens in clinical XBA samples (7/7) that were also detected in matched swabs. Conclusions These initial findings suggest the compatibility of high-throughput extraction systems and PCR panels with XBA samples collected using AveloMask and warrant further investigation of XBA sampling as a non-invasive method for respiratory virus detection.

title: Molecular epidemiology, seroprevalence and genetic characterization of bovine rotavirus in Qinghai yaks: first identification of G6P[5] genotype.
abstract: Bovine Rotavirus (BRV) is the main pathogen responsible for viral diarrhea in calves, which has a serious impact on the cattle industry and leads to economic losses. Therefore, this study aimed to fill the gap in the epidemiological research of yak-sourced rotavirus in Qinghai Province by investigating the infection rate and antibody positive rate of BRVA from yaks in Qinghai Province. We collected a total of 1,195 yak anal swab samples, 95 diarrheal fecal samples, and 834 serum samples from various cities and prefectures in Qinghai Province. The TaqMan probe method and indirect ELISA assay were used to detect and comprehensively analyze the infection rate of BRVA and the positive rate of serum antibodies in different cities and prefectures of Qinghai Province. Additionally, the key factors influencing virus transmission were explored in combination with epidemiological characteristics. The results showed that BRVA infections occurred to varying degrees in Xining City, Haidong City, Haibei Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, Huangnan Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, and Haixi Mongolian and Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture. The dominant genotype G6P[5] of the BRVA strains was first identified from yak populations in Qinghai Province. A total of 766 positive sera were detected by indirect ELISA, with an overall antibody positive rate of 91.85%. This study not only provided the latest epidemiological data of bovine rotavirus from yak populations in Qinghai Province, but more importantly, offered crucial data support for formulating targeted prevention and control strategies against BRVA in this region.
authors: Ying Huang; Yuan Han; Qiaorong Zhao; Deqing Yan; Xiaoling Zeng; Wanchao Xue; Changjiang Chen; Qing Liu; Zhi Li; Ru Meng

title: Monitoring of Clostridium botulinum in Poultry and Cattle Manure During Spreading Operations
abstract: Animal botulism mainly affects poultry and cattle, with risks of cross-contamination. This study aimed to evaluate Clostridium botulinum contamination in manure and soil following manure spreading on 13 clinically affected farms (10 cattle and three poultry) and 39 clinically unaffected farms (20 cattle and five poultry farms without any previous botulism outbreak, six poultry farms with a history of botulism and eight mixed poultry/cattle farms with an ongoing bovine botulism outbreak). Twelve manure samples, two swabs on a manure pile, 12 soil samples, and two boot swabs from fields were collected before manure spreading. Twelve soil samples and two boot swabs from fields were obtained after manure spreading. C. botulinum types C, D, C/D, and D/C were detected using real-time PCR after an enrichment step. On clinically unaffected poultry and cattle farms with no history of botulism, C. botulinum was detected in 1.4% and 1.8% of samples, respectively. Detection rates reached 8% on poultry farms with a history of botulism and 42.8% on poultry farms with ongoing bovine outbreaks. On clinically affected poultry and cattle farms, 34% and 18.9% of samples were positive, respectively. This study highlights the presence of C. botulinum in manure and soil and emphasizes the importance of biosecurity measures to prevent cross-contamination and disease recurrence.
